description: UNOS feature ledger (ADR-0203): the user-visible features and the planned changes, each with the steps that verify it. passes turns true only after every step passed as a user scenario: the tests in verified_by assert each step, the E2E specs on the local stand-in cover the steps in the web UI, and an entry whose steps make a host-level change (GLOSSARY.md) has also passed a device check and a re-check after a reboot of the deployed tree (ADR-0018). A pass also needs a reviewer in a fresh context who tried to refute the change, with each finding fixed or recorded (ADR-0017). A failing re-check, or a step that its tests do not assert as written, sets passes back to false. A pass changes only passes, verified_by and notes; changing a description or the steps, or dropping an entry, needs a new ADR that names the entry's id, and a changed entry lists that ADR in adr. supervisor/tests/test_feature_list.py compares the ledger with the one at the branch's merge base with main, where an ADR is new when its number is not in that base's docs/adr, and skips the comparison while that base has no ledger: until the ledger is merged into main neither a local run nor CI catches a dropped or reworded entry (ci.ledger-changes-checked). The feature-pass skill carries one entry per pass.

features.description: Issues on GitHub are triaged with the labels needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human and wontfix

GitHub deletes the head branch of a merged pull request by itself

features.description: Every command that an agent's Bash tool runs in the background is one call of timeout with a deadline of at most 2 hours
steps: A background command that is not one call of timeout, such as a wait loop, sleep 600 or make check > log 2>&1, is refused by the guard's rule background-deadline with one line that says what to write instead

One call of timeout with a deadline of more than 0 and at most 7200 s runs in the background: timeout 600 make check > log 2>&1, after cd DIR &&, with assignments and redirections, with the options -k and --kill-after, and timeout 900 bash -c with a loop inside the single quotes
A background call of timeout followed by ; && || | & or a newline, or with $(...), backticks or <(...) outside single quotes, is refused
A background deadline of 0, of more than 7200 s with the SIGKILL of -k, or that is not a literal duration is refused, and so are a signal of -s that may not end the command and --foreground
Commands in the foreground and the commands of the desktop app's terminal tool are not checked by the rule, and each of its denials adds a line to tmp/guard/denials.log
features.notes: Built 2026-11-11 (ADR-0335): the rule background-deadline of .claude/hooks/guard.py (check_background), which reads the line with the guard's own lexer. Tests first: on the guard of main 75 tests of supervisor/tests/test_agent_guard.py failed, the 53 refused cases of BACKGROUND_CASES, 17 checks of the messages, the 3 lexer cases of CASES, the docstring check and the denials log check. Step 1: the refused cases of BACKGROUND_CASES, the loop of 2026-11-10 among them, and test_a_background_denial_says_what_is_wrong; step 2: its allowed cases; step 3: its cases of operators and substitutions, also inside $((...)) and in unquoted heredocs; step 4: its cases of durations, -k, -s and --foreground; step 5: its foreground cases, test_the_terminal_tool_has_no_background_commands and test_a_background_denial_is_logged_like_the_others. The review in a fresh context (ADR-0017) found commands of the outer shell that the guard's lexer missed (substitutions inside $((...)), a heredoc delimiter <<$'EOF', a carriage return before #), signals of -s that do not end a command, --foreground, an unbounded -k, words of the command echoed in messages, a trailing ; refused, and gaps in the docs: all fixed, the lexer for every rule of the guard (four new cases in CASES). Kept as they are: a command that ignores SIGTERM runs on without -k (ADR-0335, Considered options), a redirection of a FIFO waits without a deadline, and the rule refuses the rare timeout forms 1e3, +60, --kill=10 and -vk 10, which GNU timeout takes. Not a host-level change: no device check.

features.description: The network, power, time zone, hostname, firewall, log, NFS and SMART actions read and change the host through src/host.py
steps: Setting the time zone or the hostname changes them on the host: timedatectl and hostnamectl on the host show the new values
Reboot, shutdown and their cancel act on the host
Firewall rules are the host's ufw rules, and NFS exports are the host's /etc/exports
Logs come from the host's journal, and SMART data from the host's smartctl
A test fails when one of these routers runs a host command without host.run_on_host
features.notes: Built (ADR-0416), except SMART: smartctl and the health router's SMART code are storage.hot-plugged-disks-smart's, so step 4's SMART half stays open here. The map of the host commands of the system, security, logs and NFS routers: the time zone (timedatectl) and the hostname (hostname; hostnamectl through PUT /network/hostname) already ran on the host (ADR-0331, test_system_time_zone.py, test_network.py); reboot, shutdown and their cancel are the power router's, on the host (ADR-0233, test_power.py); the logs' journalctl ran on the host (ADR-0257, test_logs_sources.py); NFS's exportfs and export files ran on the host (ADR-0321, test_nfs.py). Moved: ufw, which ran in the container, now runs on the host through src/host.py (security.host-firewall, test_firewall.py). Removed, without a caller (ADR-0207): GET /system/network (its own nsenter of ip and ethtool), GET /system/pcie (lspci, which the image lacks), GET /logs/files and /logs/file/{filename} (the container's /var/log) and DELETE /logs/clear/{source} (a placeholder); test_host_command_layer.py test_the_routes_that_read_the_container_are_gone and api.spec.ts 'GET ... is gone' answer 404. openssl, which reads and makes the certificates of the container's /data/certs and is no host command, runs through host.run_in_container, which takes input= for it (test_security.py, test_certificate_serving.py). Step 5: test_host_command_layer.py parses src/system/, src/security/, src/logs/, src/shares/nfs.py and exports.py, src/network/ and src/power/ and fails for a call of subprocess.run, Popen, call, check_call, check_output, getoutput or getstatusoutput (also imported by name), os.system, popen, exec*, spawn*, posix_spawn*, fork, asyncio.create_subprocess_*, pty, and for the text nsenter, also under another name of the module; it failed before the change (security/router.py 9 places, system/router.py 5). Its one exception, named in the test, is the UPS monitor's Popen of shutdown in power/router.py, which runs only outside a container (system.ups-monitoring). Host-level (GLOSSARY.md): passes after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214). Device check, by hand with the device-checks skill, never a shutdown: (1) `scripts/dev/api.py GET /system/timezone` answers what `scripts/dev/ssh.sh timedatectl show --property=Timezone --value` prints; PUT /system/timezone {"timezone": "Etc/GMT-3"} makes timedatectl on the host show Etc/GMT-3, and PUT with the zone of the first GET puts it back (each under `scripts/dev/sd.sh measure`). (2) GET /network/hostname answers `hostnamectl --static` of the host; PUT /network/hostname {"hostname": "unoscheck-name"} makes hostnamectl and GET /system/info show it, and PUT with the old name puts it back; `scripts/dev/check.sh` then reports smbd, wsdd2 and avahi-daemon active. (3) POST /power/reboot, then within the minute `busctl get-property org.freedesktop.login1 /org/freedesktop/login1 org.freedesktop.login1.Manager ScheduledShutdown` on the host names a reboot, and POST /power/cancel empties it; nothing reboots. Never POST /power/shutdown. (4) GET /logs/entries?source=journal&limit=5 lists the newest entries of `journalctl -r -n 5` on the host; GET /logs/files, /logs/file/syslog, /system/network and /system/pcie answer 404. (5) GET /shares/nfs lists the host's export files' entries and GET /shares/nfs-status names the host's NFS server. (6) The firewall: the device check of security.host-firewall. After the owner's reboot the same reads answer the host's values again, and GET /logs/entries?source=dmesg lists the new boot's kernel messages. Device check of cbe437c on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB in brackets): the time zone set to Etc/GMT-3 and back, timedatectl showing each (41.203, the device's daily logrotate, Armbian's log sync and dpkg-db-backup ran in that minute); the hostname set and back, hostnamectl and GET /system/info matching each time, smbd, wsdd2 and avahi-daemon active (0.273); a reboot scheduled, logind naming it, and cancelled, the boot id unchanged 70 s later (0.105); GET /logs/entries' 5 newest entries equal to journalctl's (cursors and messages), and the four removed routes answer 404 (0.062); NFS's export entries and server status equal to the host's (0.000); SMART of sda through Docker's node with health PASSED and a short self-test (the device check of storage.hot-plugged-disks-smart); the firewall as security.host-firewall's check. After a reboot from the API at 22:38 UTC (healthy by 22:41) the time zone, hostname, journal and dmesg reads matched the host again, and `scenario.sh all` passed in all 12 areas (23.426).

features.description: Every data path of the supervisor follows one setting, UNOS_DATA_DIR, so the backend runs outside its container without patched module constants
steps: UNOS_DATA_DIR=<dir> starts the supervisor with its database, secrets, state files, certificates and backups under <dir>
Host paths such as /etc/fstab keep settings of their own, and those that Samba or the kernel fix, such as /run/samba, stay as they are
scripts/standin/run_supervisor.py sets UNOS_DATA_DIR and patches no module constant
tests/test_standin.py finds no hard-coded /data path in supervisor/src
features.notes: Built 2026-11-19 (ADR-0419). supervisor/src/paths.py reads UNOS_DATA_DIR once, at its first import (unset or empty: /data; otherwise an absolute path of an existing directory, else DataDirError and no start) and alone names /data and makes paths in the data directory, each with its name of /data; the modules bind their names from it at their import, as they bound the literals (tests move them with monkeypatch; conftest.py sets UNOS_DATA_DIR to a read-only <the process's folder>/data before the first import, and no test changes it in its own process). Module constants replaced: audit/router.py AUDIT_FILE; backup/router.py BACKUP_DIR; health/router.py RAID_STATUS_FILE, SMART_HISTORY_FILE; notifications/router.py CONFIG_FILE, LOGS_FILE; offsite/service.py SETTINGS_FILE, SECRETS_FILE, STATUS_FILE, DATA_DIR (and MOUNTS_BASE from UNOS_MOUNTS_BASE_PATH); power/router.py CONFIG_FILE, UPS_CONFIG_FILE, WOL_FILE; scheduler/router.py TASKS_FILE, RUNS_FILE, SCHEDULED_BACKUP_DIR, BACKUP_KEYS_FILE, and DB_FILE from settings.db_path; security/router.py CERTS_DIR; storage/volume_usage.py HISTORY_FILE; updates/updater.py UPDATE_STATE_FILE, UPDATE_HISTORY_FILE, UPDATE_CONFIG_FILE, DB_FILE (settings.db_path, in place of DATA_DIR / 'unos.db' in two functions; DATA_DIR removed) and BACKUP_DIR from UNOS_UPDATE_BACKUP_DIR; config.py the defaults of db_path and app_catalog_path; main.py full_health_check reads settings.db_path. Host paths with new settings of their own (defaults as before, absolute or no start, set by nothing on the device): storage/pools.py FSTAB_PATH and FSTAB_BACKUP_PATH (UNOS_FSTAB_PATH), offsite/service.py MOUNTS_BASE (UNOS_MOUNTS_BASE_PATH), security/serving.py SERVED_DIR (UNOS_SERVED_CERTIFICATE_DIR), CADDY_TLS_HOST and CADDY_TLS_PORT (UNOS_WEBUI_TLS_HOST, UNOS_WEBUI_TLS_PORT), updates/updater.py BACKUP_DIR (UNOS_UPDATE_BACKUP_DIR). Step 1: test_data_dir.py starts the supervisor twice in child processes with UNOS_DATA_DIR naming two folders (the host settings name folders of the test): every data path lies in its folder with its name of /data (DATA_PATHS is the whole set), the database, the generated jwt_secret (0600) and the setup's audit entry are there, GET /health/full reads the database, the RAID status and the UPS settings there, and nothing else differs between the two starts; the values refused and the refused start; the compose files set no UNOS_DATA_DIR and mount the volume at /data. Step 2: the same starts put every host path where its own setting says, whatever UNOS_DATA_DIR is, and the settings default to the host's files (/etc/fstab, smb.conf, /etc/exports, /mnt/pools, /mnt, /served-certificate, /var/lib/unos/backups); /run/samba (Samba's folder, which smb.conf's [global] names), /proc/self/mountinfo and /proc/sys/kernel/hostname stay fixed, also under any UNOS_DATA_DIR. Step 3: run_supervisor.py sets UNOS_DATA_DIR and the host settings (stand_in_environment), no longer UNOS_DB_PATH or UNOS_APP_CATALOG_PATH; DATA_GLOBALS and HOST_FILE_GLOBALS are gone; it replaces functions only (the off-device copy's system-disk checks and S3 probe, Caddy's reload, and without /proc the file manager's mount table reader) and the login limiter's switch, which no setting may turn off on a NAS (test_standin.py test_the_stand_in_patches_no_module_constant); configure() refuses root and an earlier import of the supervisor; the fake unshare of fake_restic.py gives restic its state's hostname file in place of /proc/sys/kernel/hostname. Step 4: test_standin.py test_no_data_path_is_written_outside_the_paths_module (no /data literal and no path made from DATA_DIR; the apps' container paths of the catalog aside); READ_ONLY_PROBES is gone. install.sh's own UNOS_DATA_DIR (the host's /var/lib/unos, which only it read) is removed so that the name means one thing. Not host-level: compose sets no UNOS_DATA_DIR, the device keeps /data. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017); fixed: one source of the database's file (scheduler and updater took /data/unos.db), paths made from DATA_DIR caught, the tests' data folder read-only, the starts of test_data_dir.py kept off this machine's host paths, no mount table setting (it could turn the mount-point check off), absolute host path settings, the install test's targets, the compose check, root refused in configure(). The reviewer read step 2 as asking a setting for /run/samba too; it stays fixed (ADR-0419: Samba's own folder, written into smb.conf, not the supervisor's), and the lead reworded step 2 at the merge to say so, by ADR-0419. app_catalog_path (UNOS_APP_CATALOG_PATH) is read by no module: a legacy setting for an entry of its own. Device check 2026-11-19 of 15cf31d (mvp.batch-15, deployed 07:50 to 08:01 UTC: sync 6.215, build-supervisor 17.715, build-webui 21.367, up 6.465 SD MiB), before and after the reboot from the API at 08:21:50 UTC (all 7 containers healthy at 08:23:04): UNOS_DATA_DIR unset in the container, one mount at /data, the database open at /data/unos.db, jwt_secret mode 600 root and the audit log in /data/audit, as before (0.000 SD MiB); scenario.sh all OK after the reboot. Step 2 was reworded at the merge (ADR-0419): paths that Samba or the kernel fix stay as they are.

features.description: Changes to existing database tables ship as Alembic migrations
steps: alembic upgrade head on an empty database creates the whole schema
A change to an existing table comes with a revision, and the supervisor applies pending revisions at startup
A test runs every revision on a database made by the one before
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-21 (ADR-0444, which supersedes ADR-0022 and ADR-0319 in part): Alembic 1.20.1, the revisions in supervisor/src/migrations/versions, the baseline 0001 of today's schema with IF NOT EXISTS, init_db brings unos.db to the head first in the lifespan, in one SQLite transaction and without one at the head; no create_all in supervisor/src; a restore upgrades the backup's copy before the swap and refuses an unknown revision. Step 1: TestTheSchema test_an_empty_database_gets_the_whole_schema_at_the_head. Step 2: test_the_models_and_the_head_of_the_migrations_agree (the autogenerate diff is empty), test_the_tables_at_the_head_are_those_of_the_models (CHECK, collations), test_the_start_applies_a_pending_revision_to_an_existing_table, test_the_supervisor_upgrades_the_database_before_it_serves. Step 3: test_every_revision_runs_on_a_database_made_by_the_one_before, test_a_database_at_the_baseline_upgrades_to_the_head_at_the_start. Also: a database made by create_all is taken as the baseline with its tables unchanged (the dev device's), a table of an older layout stays and a warning names it, a failed upgrade changes nothing, a start at the head writes nothing, an unknown revision stops the start, the baseline's SHA-256 is pinned, the images ship the migrations, and a restore upgrades before the swap and refuses a failed upgrade or an unknown revision (test_backup_restore.py). The tests failed before the change. The deploy rebuilds the supervisor image from its pip layer on (a changed requirements.txt): hundreds of MB on the SD card once. passes waited for the deploy to show the dev device's database stamped and served: after the first start the supervisor's log has the INFO line 'unos.db was brought from the revision none (no migrations yet) to 0001', and a WARNING naming the tables whose layout is not the baseline's, which stay as they are; alembic_version holds 0001 and no other table changed (a RAM copy of the device's unos.db, read-only); GET /api/v1/health answers 200, a sign-in works with the existing accounts and GET /api/v1/auth/users lists them (scripts/dev/api.py); a restart of the supervisor logs neither line again. Passed 2026-11-21 on the dev device (0c7b84b9): the INFO line, and the WARNING named api_tokens, login_attempts, smb_state and users, whose layouts in a RAM copy differ only as create_all of January and an old ALTER TABLE left them (DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) in parentheses, users' totp_secret TEXT and totp_enabled INTEGER DEFAULT 0, smb_state of ADR-0319); the owner accepted them as they are ("yes, accept", in translation), where the notes had expected smb_state alone. alembic_version holds 0001; GET /api/v1/health 200, a sign-in and GET /api/v1/auth/users (2 users) work; after docker restart unos-supervisor (1.430 MiB on the SD card) neither line was logged again and health answered 200. The BPI-F3's unos.db was brought to 0001 with no warning.

features.description: The supervisor logs structured lines with level, logger and fields, and handlers log the exceptions they catch
steps: Every log line of the supervisor is one JSON object with time, level, logger and message
A handler that catches an exception logs it with its traceback before it answers
supervisor/src has no print() calls
features.notes: Built per ADR-0398: supervisor/src/logging_setup.py (JSON format, one configuration, UNOS_LOG_LEVEL, default INFO, libraries capped at WARNING), configured first in main.py. tests/test_logging.py runs the image's uvicorn command as a subprocess: every line is JSON, 20 health checks, the first-run setup, a sign-in and a read write no line, a wrong password one access line; secrets never reach a line at DEBUG; no print() in supervisor/src (the emergency CLI writes through _say); every broad except that raises an HTTPException logs its traceback. Device check (owner, not host-level): docker logs unos-supervisor after a restart and a sign-in (every line JSON, uvicorn's too; start lines only; a sign-in adds none; a wrong password adds one access line; no password, token or code), then the SD MiB of an idle minute with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure (expect 0.0 beyond the usual). Device check of 5412b79 on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB): every line of the supervisor's container log since its start parsed as one JSON object with time, level, logger and message (6 lines: uvicorn.error 4, src.shares.service 1, src.storage.pools 1), and the 7 since the reboot after it; a temporary regular user's sign-in added no line and a wrong password exactly one uvicorn.access line with 401; its password, session token and session key and the administrator's token were absent from the whole log (0.219, with the resource monitor's socket step); 600 s idle with no page open 0.086, the container log 2455 bytes before and after.

features.description: JSON state files are replaced atomically, and a file that cannot be parsed is kept and reported instead of reset
steps: A supervisor killed while it writes a state file leaves the old or the new content, never a partial file
A state file that cannot be parsed is renamed to <name>.bad and named in a warning, and the defaults are used
features.notes: Passed 2026-11-10 (ADR-0324; ADR-0325 and ADR-0326 supersede ADR-0240 and ADR-0260 for the key file and the notification files). Step 1: every JSON state file of the supervisor, 14 of them (STATE_FILES of test_state_files.py; a scan finds every module-level path of one in src in the table, no module that opens one of its paths with write_text, open and the like, and no literal path in a function), is written through state_files.replace_file: a temporary file next to it, renamed over it, synced first for the SMART history, the notification files and the key file. A process killed with SIGKILL before the rename leaves the old content, after it the new one, and a write that fails leaves no temporary file. Step 2: load_json renames a file that is not UTF-8, not JSON or no state of its kind to <name>.bad, names it in a warning and answers the defaults, unless a writer put a new file in place meanwhile, and every state file's loader uses it; the SMART history does so in the monitor's pass, while its endpoints keep their 500 (ADR-0235). Before the change, 10 of the 14 rename checks and all 14 checks of the .bad file failed. A fresh-context review found: a runs file that cannot be opened stopped the start, a task's run and the RAID check; a reader could set aside a file that a writer had just put in place; new syncs on the event loop; RAID gauges that went missing for a status without pools; and claims of the ADR and the records. Fixed: histories and caches read as none when they cannot be opened, the start and a run go on, renames take the path's lock and check the inode, only the files that an ADR wants durable are synced, the health outputs read the status as before, and the texts. Not host-level: the files are the supervisor's own state in its data volume.

features.description: Every time the API stores or returns carries its time zone
steps: Timestamps in API answers are ISO 8601 with an offset
The database stores times in UTC
The web UI shows times in the browser's time zone
features.notes: Built 2026-11-18 (ADR-0401, which supersedes ADR-0237 and ADR-0300). What a stored time without an offset means: UTC. The DATETIME columns (users, api_tokens, user_sessions, usernames_taken, two_factor_requirement, dashboard_layouts, login_attempts, smb_shares, smb_share_access, smb_accounts, smb_state, app_resource_limits) are SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP or written by db_now() of supervisor/src/times.py (datetime.utcnow() before): naive UTC, never altered (ADR-0319); the files of /data (the audit log, the update history and progress, the SMART history, the RAID status, the notification history, the scheduler's files, the backups' manifests) took naive datetime.now() of the container, whose clock is UTC, and new writes carry their offset (the audit log, the SMART history and the RAID status Z, as the API answers, so that an exported audit entry's hash can be computed again; the others +00:00); readers take a time without an offset as UTC (UtcText for the scheduler's and the notification history's text, stored_time_text for the SMART history, the RAID status and a restored backup's manifest). Answers: every datetime field of a model is UtcDatetime (Z), the str fields and plain dicts take utc_now()/from_epoch() with +00:00, the audit log answers AuditEntryView (its lines keep their text, so the hash chain holds) and compares instants in its filters, sorting, summary and clearing; its bounds take an offset (Z or +HH:MM). Changed forms: boot_time of /system/info (seconds since the epoch before), last_boot of /power/status (who -b before), a scrub's last_run (btrfs's ctime), a certificate's valid_from and valid_until (openssl's GMT text), a notification event's timestamp (a time, 422 otherwise). The one exception with another offset: a task's next_run, in the host's zone (ADR-0266). Docker's Created times pass as Docker answers them (RFC 3339, Z). Web UI: webui/src/lib/time.ts reads only a time with its offset and every page that writes a server time goes through it; the Audit Log page groups by the browser's day and sends From and To as the browser's day's first and last millisecond in UTC. Step 1: test_api_times.py (TestEveryAnswerCarriesItsOffset walks every GET of the API as an administrator in a process zone of UTC+05:45 with rows and files from before the change and fails for a time without an offset, the stats message; the source check of clock reads without a zone; every datetime field UtcDatetime; TestTimesOfTools), times.spec.ts (the JSON answers that the pages read, against the stand-in) and api.spec.ts (boot_time). Step 2: test_api_times.py TestStoredTimesReadBackAsUtc (old naive rows read back with their clock time in UTC; a new token stored in UTC whatever the process zone) and TestAuditLogAcrossTheChange (entries chained before the change keep their text and their chain, new ones continue it; bounds with offsets; exports; clearing). Step 3: times.spec.ts (the Users page in Asia/Kathmandu), audit.spec.ts (the timeline's times and days and From and To in Asia/Kathmandu), storage.spec.ts (a scrub's start), backup.spec.ts and language.spec.ts (a certificate's dates). Not host-level. The device check after the next deploy: GET /api/v1/system/info, /auth/users, /auth/tokens, /security/login-history, /audit/logs?limit=5 and /updates/history answer every time with its offset and the old rows with the same clock time as before (scripts/dev/api.py); GET /api/v1/audit/logs?limit=10000 shows every entry's chain ok across the entries written before and after the deploy; the Audit Log, Users and Storage pages in a browser outside UTC show the times in its zone. Review (ADR-0017, a fresh subagent): fixed the scheduler's runs and tasks and a restored backup's manifest from before answering naive text (UtcText, stored_time_text, now seeded naive in the walk), a time outside the calendar in UTC raising 500 (as_utc raises ValueError: 422, or a skipped audit line), old notification history entries with an event timestamp that is no time being dropped (kept without it), exported audit hashes that could not be computed again (new lines in the Z form; an old line's hash is over its time without the Z, tested), the walk's coverage (path values for a task's runs and a SMART history, naive SMART history and RAID status seeded, MIN_ANSWERED), the ADR's restatement of ADR-0237 and ADR-0300, the clock check's forms (datetime.datetime.now, now(tz=None), astimezone(), time.strftime), the audit page's datetime attribute (milliseconds), %2B in the user guide, and the verified_by list. Left: GETs that need the host, Docker or the network answer no 200 in the walk (/system/info, /power/status, the storage, snapshot, container and app routes); their models are checked by type (every datetime field UtcDatetime) and their producers by the clock check, and btrfs_time and openssl_time by TestTimesOfTools. ADR-0298 (proposed) still names ADR-0237, which ADR-0401 superseded: its acceptance would supersede ADR-0401's audit rules. Device check of 5412b79 on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB): GET /auth/users answered admin's created_at 2026-01-21T11:44:45Z and test's 2026-01-24T06:22:35Z (0.020); the 58 time-like fields of /system/info, /auth/users, /auth/tokens, /security/login-history, /audit/logs?limit=5 and /updates/history all carried an offset (0.016); /audit/logs?limit=10000 answered 2216 entries with no broken chain: 2031 ok, 4 of them written after the deploy, and 185 without a chain, the oldest, written before ADR-0328 (0.000); after a reboot 2218 entries, none broken (0.016).

features.description: The supervisor's OpenAPI schema describes every endpoint, its fields and its errors, with examples
steps: Every route of app.openapi() has a summary and a description
Every field of the request and response models has a description, and the models have examples
Each route lists the error statuses it answers
features.notes: Built 2026-11-19 (ADR-0417). Every route of supervisor/src sets summary= and has a description (its docstring, cut at \f before developer notes); every path and query parameter, every field of every model and the bodies without a model are described; every model of a request or an answer has an example that it takes as JSON; the 94 routes that answer a plain dict keep doing so (no response_model: it would validate and filter the answer) and document it with answer() of supervisor/src/openapi.py; the file and text answers (files and backup downloads, the Prometheus metrics) name their media type with the response_class they already returned. Errors: responses=errors(...) with the shared texts SIGNED_IN, ADMIN (main.py adds it to every router of _ADMIN_ONLY), BODY and RATE_LIMITED and texts of each route, from its code; the models ErrorDetail, Unprocessable (a 422 that a route lists itself) and RateLimited. Step 1: test_openapi.py test_every_route_has_a_summary_and_a_description, test_every_parameter_has_a_description. Step 2: test_every_field_of_every_model_has_a_description, test_every_request_and_answer_has_an_example, test_the_models_take_their_examples (also no key a model lacks, at any depth), test_no_example_holds_an_address_a_host_name_or_a_secret (documentation ranges, 10.0.0.0/24 and fd00::/64 for local-network fields, example domains, placeholders for secrets, query secrets and chat webhooks). Step 3: test_every_route_lists_the_error_statuses_it_answers derives from each route's code the statuses it must list (literal raises in the route, its dependencies and the src functions and __init__s they reach outside except handlers and outside tries whose handler keeps an HTTPException; 401/403 from the credential; 413 with a body; 429 with a rate limit; 400 or 404 for a path parameter) and fails for a route that lists none; the exceptions NO_ERRORS, NOT_ANSWERED and PATH_WITHOUT_NOT_FOUND carry their reasons and test_every_exception_is_still_needed fails for a stale one; TestTheChecks shows each check finding its defect on an app of defects. An API shape comparison of app.openapi() before and after (descriptions and examples stripped) found the paths, methods, parameters, bodies, success statuses and component schemas unchanged; only the four file or text answers' media types differ. Not host-level; the web UI has no generated types and is untouched. The device check after the next deploy: on the NAS, docker exec unos-supervisor python -c "import urllib.request; print(urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8080/openapi.json').read().decode())" answers the schema with the summaries and examples (docs/USER_GUIDE.md). Review (ADR-0017, a fresh subagent): fixed examples that the code refuses or cannot answer (NFS clients and SMB interfaces in documentation ranges, now 10.0.0.0/24 and fd00::/64; an encrypted backup's version in the list), an untrue login docstring (the step that asks for the second factor is not in the login history), the derivation's misses (Starlette's HTTPException, a class's __init__: the uploads' 422, now listed), example-check holes (an address before a full stop, bare host names, more secret keys, query secrets, chat webhooks), bodies without a model now with examples, nested unknown keys, stale exceptions, ADR ids in model docstrings (moved to comments), and texts of volume creation's audit, shares' 400/409/500, PUID/PGID, a backup's version, a task's last_run and last_status, certificate ids, SMB conflicts, widget ids, the trash and upload-leftover walks, a move's replace race, snapshot names and network interfaces. Left: the derivation is a floor (a helper's except handlers and methods other than __init__ are not followed; those statuses were listed by hand and reviewed by sampling); the plain-dict answers are documented by example only and no test compares them with the answers; the restore's example builds previous_database from settings.db_path at import (a /data literal would trip test_standin.py). Code weaknesses found and documented as they are, not changed: SelfSignedCertRequest.validity_days has no bounds; POST /containers answers 500, not 400, for a reserved name; UpdateConfig, NotificationConfig.events and PowerConfig.wake_on_lan are stored but nothing acts on them; a new scheduled task stores the last_run and last_status it is sent; the audit summary's days and the login history's limit take any integer. Device check 2026-11-19 of 15cf31d (mvp.batch-15, deployed 07:50 to 08:01 UTC: sync 6.215, build-supervisor 17.715, build-webui 21.367, up 6.465 SD MiB), before and after the reboot from the API at 08:21:50 UTC (all 7 containers healthy at 08:23:04): the device's schema has 270 operations, one per route, each with a summary and a description, and the schema checks of test_openapi.py find no problem in it (0.000 SD MiB); it differs from this tree's only in the restore example's previous_database, which is built from the database path at import.

features.description: The web UI is served only over HTTPS with certificates from Caddy's local CA and with security headers; plain HTTP redirects
steps: https://<host>/ loads with Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
API answers carry the same headers
http://<host>/<path> redirects to https://<host>/<path>
GET /api/v1/health still answers over plain HTTP
features.notes: The stand-in serves these headers through scripts/standin/front.mjs. Device check: 2026-11-05 (Phase 0 deploy, also after a reboot of that tree); the deployed tree changed since. Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC), from the device: https://127.0.0.1/ and /api/v1/health answer with Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, http://127.0.0.1/storage answers 308 to https://127.0.0.1/storage, and /api/v1/health answers 200 over plain HTTP.

features.description: Request bodies, WebSocket messages and login fields are limited before the credentials are checked
steps: An anonymous POST with a 2 MiB JSON body answers 413, and the body is not read
A signed-in 2 MiB JSON body answers 413, also when it is sent chunked
A WebSocket message over 64 KiB closes the socket
A login with a field over its limit answers 422, and audit entries store bounded fields only
File and backup uploads stream past 1 MiB under their own limits
features.notes: The limit is a middleware in front of every route (supervisor/src/request_limits.py); not host-level. Step 1: test_request_limits.py (test_content_length_over_the_limit_is_answered_413_without_reading, also for the login, test_content_length_over_the_limit_is_answered_before_anything_is_received, test_chunked_body_over_the_limit_gets_413, test_chunked_body_is_counted_and_reading_stops_at_the_limit, and test_a_real_server_answers_413_for_chunked_and_declared_bodies with both of uvicorn's HTTP parsers). Step 2: test_a_signed_in_client_gets_413_for_a_declared_and_a_chunked_body (a valid administrator token, GET /auth/me answers 200, then a declared and a chunked 2 MiB body each answer 413); the note that said it was missing was stale: note and test came in the same commit (2e4306d, 2026-11-07). Step 3: test_uvicorn_refuses_a_large_first_message_before_the_application_gets_it and test_both_images_limit_websocket_messages_alike (uvicorn's --ws-max-size in both images). Step 4: test_login_bounds.py. Step 5: test_request_limits.py (each upload's own limit) and test_upload_streaming.py (the uploads stream into their destination, and the server's memory does not grow); its tests of unnamed files run on Linux only (scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh) and concern files.upload, not the limits. Passed 2026-11-09.

features.description: Sign-ins and administrative actions are recorded in the audit log, which an administrator lists, filters and exports
steps: Sign in, create a user and delete it: GET /api/v1/audit/logs lists the three entries with user, action, time and client address
Filters by user, action and time narrow the list, and GET /api/v1/audit/logs/count counts it
GET /api/v1/audit/logs/export downloads the filtered entries
features.notes: Step 1: TestSignInAndUserManagementAreListed in tests/test_audit_log.py signs in, creates and deletes a user through the API and reads the three entries from GET /api/v1/audit/logs, newest first, with the user, the action, the time and the client address. Step 2: TestFilters and TestSearch filter by user, action, severity, time and text, at the edges of a day and of a second, on entries with microseconds as log_action writes them, and /logs/count counts the same entries; a bound covers the whole day, hour, minute, second or fraction it names, and one in another form or with a zone gets 422 (ADR-0237). Step 3: TestExport downloads the filtered entries as CSV and JSON, the same entries the list shows, and in the CSV a ' keeps a spreadsheet from reading a value as a formula, the user name of a failed sign-in included. Recorded today: sign-ins, users and their SMB access, shares, API tokens, recovery codes and the clearing of the log (docs/USER_GUIDE.md, Audit Log); storage, snapshots, containers, apps, backups, power, scheduled tasks, the network, and system settings write no entries yet (security.audit-admin-actions). Since ADR-0343 a user's own sign-out, password change and turning two-factor authentication on or off write entries too. Writing entries is tested in tests/test_login_bounds.py and tests/test_audit_log.py, the administrator-only routes in tests/test_authz.py. Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): no device check needed. The page is webui.audit-log-page.

features.description: Every administrative action and every change of a user's own sign-in is recorded in the audit log, not only sign-ins, users, shares and API tokens
steps: Creating and deleting pools and volumes, and creating, deleting and restoring snapshots, write audit entries with the user, the client address and the resource
Starting, stopping and removing containers, and installing and uninstalling apps, write audit entries
Creating, restoring and deleting backups, restarting and shutting down, and changing scheduled tasks, the network and the system settings write audit entries
A user's own password change and turning two-factor authentication on or off write audit entries
Every AuditAction value that the Action filter of the Audit Log page offers is written by the action it names, or is removed

The firewall's changes, clearing the login history, pools mounted, unmounted and imported, containers created, images pulled and removed, suspend, the power and UPS settings, the notification channels and the off-device copy's target and settings write audit entries that name what changed and never a secret
features.notes: A side finding of security.audit-log (ADR-0203): only the auth, shares, audit and emergency code called log_action (supervisor/src/audit/router.py), so POOL_*, VOLUME_*, SNAPSHOT_*, CONTAINER_*, APP_*, BACKUP_*, SYSTEM_*, SETTINGS_CHANGED, TASK_*, FIREWALL_*, SSL_CERT_UPLOADED and NETWORK_CONFIG_CHANGED were never written. Entries record real changes only (ADR-0320, which superseded ADR-0157; the adr list names ADR-0320 in its place). Step 4 is done (ADR-0343): POST /auth/logout, /auth/change-password, /auth/totp/enable and /auth/totp/disable write LOGOUT, PASSWORD_CHANGE, TOTP_ENABLED and TOTP_DISABLED (warning) after the change is committed, by the user, with the client address and browser and resource type user with the user name; a password change that also set Samba's password writes SMB_ACCOUNT_UPDATED too (ADR-0320). A refused attempt writes nothing, a sign-out only when it ended the session (end_session says whether), turning 2FA on or off only when its UPDATE, conditioned on the current state (and, to turn it on, on the secret its code was checked against), changed the row, a setup stores its secret only while 2FA is off, and an entry that cannot be written goes to the supervisor's log while the change still answers, as a sign-in (ADR-0251). Tested in tests/test_audit_own_account.py, which failed before the change. The secret conditions came later: test_a_setup_that_replaced_the_secret_meanwhile_keeps_2fa_off and test_a_setup_never_replaces_the_secret_of_2fa_turned_on_meanwhile failed before them (200, and 2FA on with the newer secret). Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): no device check needed for step 4. Step 4 on the dev device 2026-11-11 (by hand, tree 8ea5a08 before and after the reboot of 23:22 UTC, and main 405d318 after its deploy): a user made for the check had a refused change of its own password with a wrong current one (400, no entry), then changed its password, turned 2FA on and off with codes of two time steps, and signed out; the audit log held login_success, password_change, totp_enabled, totp_disabled and logout about the user, from its address and browser, and the entries of the run before the reboot were still there after it, the chain intact. Steps 1 and 2 are done (ADR-0350): POST and DELETE /storage/pools, POST and DELETE /storage/pools/{pool}/volumes, POST /snapshots/, DELETE /snapshots/{name} and POST /snapshots/restore, POST /containers/{id}/start, /restart and /stop and DELETE /containers/{id}, POST /apps/install, DELETE /apps/installed/{id} and POST /apps/installed/{id}/start, /restart and /stop write POOL_CREATED, POOL_DELETED, VOLUME_CREATED, VOLUME_DELETED, SNAPSHOT_CREATED, SNAPSHOT_DELETED, SNAPSHOT_RESTORED, CONTAINER_STARTED (a restart too), CONTAINER_STOPPED, CONTAINER_REMOVED, APP_INSTALLED and APP_UNINSTALLED after the change, by the administrator, with the client address and browser and the resource (types pool, volume, snapshot, container and app, which the Audit Log page names); removals and deletions are warnings. A refused or failed request writes nothing, a pool removal only when it unmounted the pool, dropped its fstab entry or removed its mountpoint (delete_pool says whether), a start only when the container was not running and a stop only when it was (Docker answers the others with a 304 that docker-py drops), and an entry that cannot be written goes to the supervisor's log while the change answers (audit_change of supervisor/src/audit/changes.py, which ADR-0351's routers use too). Tested in tests/test_audit_storage_and_apps.py: its tests of the entries failed before the change (no entry: assert [] == [...]); its tests of requests that write nothing pass either way and guard the real-change rule. Left open: mounting, unmounting and importing pools, creating containers and pulling or removing images on the Containers page have no AuditAction and are not audited, and two starts or stops of one container at the same moment can both write an entry (ADR-0350). The routes act on the host (GLOSSARY.md): the device check of steps 1 and 2 is still to be made. Step 3 is done (ADR-0351): POST /backup/create and /backup/upload write BACKUP_CREATED, POST /backup/restore/{filename} BACKUP_RESTORED (warning, with what it restored, written in the restore's own task so that a cancelled request keeps it) and DELETE /backup/{filename} BACKUP_DELETED, resource type backup with the file name; POST /power/reboot and /power/shutdown SYSTEM_REBOOT and SYSTEM_SHUTDOWN (warning, resource type host) as soon as shutdown +1 was accepted, a minute before logind acts, and POST /power/cancel the action it cancelled; POST /power/wol/{interface}/enable and /disable and POST /network/interfaces/{name}/down, /down/confirm and /up NETWORK_CONFIG_CHANGED (resource type network_interface); the scheduler's create, edit (the names of the fields that changed and, for a rename, the old name; never the command or the passphrase), toggle and delete TASK_CREATED, TASK_UPDATED and TASK_DELETED, and Run now the new TASK_RUN (resource type task with the task's name); PUT /network/hostname and PUT /system/timezone SETTINGS_CHANGED from the old value to the new (resource type host). All by the administrator, with the client address and browser, after the change and for a real change only (ADR-0320): a refused or failed request, a restore that restored nothing, a cancel with nothing pending, an Enable of an enabled interface, the same host name, zone or Wake-on-LAN state and a task saved unchanged write none, and that task edit and the deletion of a task that is not there no longer rewrite the tasks file (ADR-0214). An entry that cannot be written goes to the supervisor's log while the change still answers (audit_change of supervisor/src/audit/changes.py, ADR-0251, ADR-0343). The web UI names task_run and the resource types backup, host, network_interface and task. Tested in tests/test_audit_system_actions.py, which failed before the change (31 of its 47 tests: no entries, and the unchanged edit and unknown deletion found no entry of the task's creation either); tests/conftest.py keeps every test's audit log in its tmp_path. Not on the dev device yet: a reboot through POST /power/reboot whose system_reboot entry is still in the log after the reboot, and a restore, a task change and a time zone change with their entries. Suspend, the power and UPS settings that no page sets, the off-device copy and the notification settings are not audited (ADR-0351). Review fixes 2026-11-12: a request that failed part way writes its action with success false and what it did (ADR-0350, ADR-0351): pool_created after mkfs.btrfs (PoolFormattedError), pool_deleted after the unmount or the fstab drop (PoolPartlyRemovedError), container_stopped for an uninstall that stopped the app and could not remove it, network_config_changed for an Enable whose saved addresses could not all be restored (links.PartlyEnabled); POST /containers/{id}/restart refuses UNOS's own containers (404) as stop and remove do. Failed before: test_a_create_that_fails_after_formatting_writes_a_failed_entry, test_a_removal_that_fails_after_unmounting_writes_a_failed_entry, test_an_uninstall_that_stopped_the_app_and_could_not_remove_it_writes_a_failed_stop, test_an_enable_that_restored_part_of_the_addresses_is_in_the_audit_log_as_failed (no entry), test_a_system_container_is_not_restarted (200). A volume kept without its quota writes volume_created as failed (test_a_volume_kept_without_its_quota_writes_a_failed_entry failed before: no entry); the 409s of a create whose name leads to other subvolumes and a 500 of a failed removal of the new volume still write none (ADR-0350, Consequences). Device check 2026-11-12 (main 641f2a5, by hand, before and after the reboot from the API at 04:35:30 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 04:36:49; both containers healthy by 04:37:17)): a volume made, snapshotted, its snapshot and the volume deleted wrote volume_created, snapshot_created, snapshot_deleted and volume_deleted, and a second delete (404) nothing; a scrub task created, its hour changed (task_updated naming hour, no value; the same PUT again nothing), Run now (task_run) and deleted (task_deleted; a second delete nothing); the time zone set to Etc/GMT-3 and back (two settings_changed); a backup created and deleted (backup_created, backup_deleted; the 404 nothing); and the reboot through POST /power/reboot left its system_reboot entry (warning, resource host) in the log after the boot, the chain intact. Not on the device: pools (no spare disk), containers and apps (the owner's containers and image pulls are off limits), network interfaces and Wake-on-LAN. Step 5 is done (ADR-0359): of the AuditAction values that GET /audit/actions offers to the Action filter, firewall_rule_added, firewall_rule_deleted and ssl_cert_uploaded were written by nothing and are removed from the enum, the page's ACTION_NAMES and the audit catalog (the security router audits none of its changes, its firewall routes run ufw in the container, which has none, and an uploaded certificate is not served); every other value is written by the action it names (the table of ADR-0359). An entry's action is now the name as recorded (AuditEntry.action: str): an older entry whose action AuditAction no longer has is listed, counted, summed up, exported, found by the search and by the action filter, which takes any name exactly, and the chain holds through it; the page shows such an action as it comes. Tested in tests/test_audit_log.py: test_the_action_filter_offers_only_actions_that_the_server_writes (an AST scan of supervisor/src for AuditAction.<NAME>) failed before (assert ['firewall_rule_added', 'firewall_rule_deleted', 'ssl_cert_uploaded'] == []), and TestAnActionNoLongerWritten failed with the values removed and the old reader (the entry skipped, and 422 for ?action=firewall_rule_added; ?action=firewall_rule got 422 on main too); the damaged-lines test now uses a line without an action. webui/tests/audit.spec.ts 'offers only the actions the server writes, and shows an older action as recorded' failed before (the page named firewall_rule_added Firewall rule added). Left open: auditing the firewall's changes (on, off, rules, reset), the certificates' changes (upload, self-signed, delete) and clearing the login history (DELETE /security/login-history, which needs a resource type that the Audit Log page names): none writes an entry, and neither security.host-firewall nor security.custom-certificates tracks it (ADR-0359). Review fix 2026-11-12: log_action takes the action through AuditAction(action), so a name that AuditAction lacks raises ValueError and writes nothing (test_no_writer_takes_it failed before). Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): no device check needed for step 5; the device checks of steps 1 to 3 named above remain. Step 5 on the dev device 2026-11-12 (before and after the reboot from the API at 13:11:00 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 13:11:56; both containers healthy by 13:12:50)): GET /audit/actions offers neither firewall_rule_added, firewall_rule_deleted nor ssl_cert_uploaded, a listing or count filtered by one of them or by an unknown name answers 200 with no entries, and the chain of the listing is intact. Step 6 is done (ADR-0402, which supersedes ADR-0359 and closes the open items of the Consequences of ADR-0350, ADR-0351 and ADR-0359): the routes found by listing every POST, PUT and DELETE of the security, storage, containers, power, notifications and offsite routers that had no audit_change. POST /security/firewall/enable and /disable write firewall_enabled and firewall_disabled (warning) when the state changed, POST and DELETE /security/firewall/rules firewall_rule_added and firewall_rule_deleted, POST /security/firewall/reset firewall_reset (a reset now stops at the first failing ufw command and answers 500; one that failed after ufw's own reset writes it as failed), DELETE /security/login-history login_history_cleared (warning, with the count; none when nothing was cleared), POST /storage/pools/{name}/mount, /unmount and POST /storage/filesystems/{uuid}/import pool_mounted, pool_unmounted (warning; as failed when the host unmounted it and mounting again failed) and pool_imported (a mount of a mounted pool kept in the fstab and an unmount of a pool that is neither write none: mount_pool_changed and unmount_pool_changed say whether), POST /containers container_created (never the environment), POST /containers/images/pull image_pulled (only when the image is new or the reference moved: pull_image_changed) and DELETE /containers/images/{id} image_removed (warning), PUT /power/config and /power/ups/config settings_changed (resource power and ups, the field names with their values, the UPS user name and password by name only; neither request rewrites its file for unchanged settings any more), POST /power/suspend system_suspend (warning, written before systemctl suspend runs; a failing systemctl adds a second entry as failed), POST, PUT and DELETE /notifications/configs and PUT and DELETE /offsite/settings settings_changed (resource notification_channel and offsite; a channel or off-device settings saved as they were write none and no file; fields by name, values only of a channel's name and switch and of the off-device settings but never of a secret or an access key ID). All through audit_change, by the administrator, after the change, answering when the entry cannot be written; changed_fields of supervisor/src/audit/changes.py builds the details. The concurrent start or stop that wrote two entries is fixed: start_container and stop_container hold the lock of the container (_state_lock, keyed by Docker's ID) from reading its state to acting (test_only_one_of_two_changes_the_container failed before). The Action filter offers the 13 new values (pool_mounted, pool_unmounted, pool_imported, container_created, image_pulled, image_removed, system_suspend, firewall_enabled, firewall_disabled, firewall_rule_added, firewall_rule_deleted, firewall_reset, login_history_cleared), named in English and Russian with the new resource types firewall, firewall_rule, login_history, image, power, ups, notification_channel and offsite; the scan test of test_audit_log.py also names the ssl_cert_* values as security.custom-certificates's, which it neither requires nor forbids, and its older-action examples use legacy_example_action now that firewall_rule_added is written again. Tests: the four new files of verified_by, 46 of their 75 tests failed before (the rest guard requests that write nothing). Not audited still: the certificates (security.custom-certificates), notification tests and sends, Run now and the restores of the off-device copy. The firewall routes run ufw in the container, which has none (security.host-firewall): they are tested with a fake ufw and answer 500 on the device. Device check of step 6, to run after the deploy by the owner's request, safe on the device: (1) PUT /api/v1/power/config with the values it has (GET first, send them back): 200 and no entry; then change one value, such as shutdown_minute to 5: one settings_changed entry (resource power, "shutdown_minute (0 to 5)"), and put the value back: a second one. (2) A notification channel: POST /api/v1/notifications/configs with a webhook channel to https://hooks.example.invalid/x and a name of the check, PUT it unchanged (no entry), PUT it with enabled false (one entry naming enabled), DELETE it (a warning entry); no entry holds the URL. (3) PUT /api/v1/power/ups/config with {} when no UPS is set up: 200 and no entry (the defaults). (4) GET the audit log and see the entries of these steps with the user, the address and the resource, the chain intact; reboot from the API (POST /api/v1/power/reboot, the owner's action) and see that the entries are still there after the boot. Only if the owner agrees that the history may go: DELETE /api/v1/security/login-history?older_than_days=<more than the history holds> answers deleted_count 0 and writes nothing; with a smaller number it clears the attempts older than that and writes login_history_cleared. Must not run on the device: the firewall routes (they would act on a host that has no ufw in the container, and a reset or a disable could cut the owner's access), mounting, unmounting and importing pools (the owner's data), creating containers and pulling or removing images (the owner's containers and image pulls are off limits), suspend (the host would go to sleep), and the off-device copy's settings (the owner's repository). Review of step 6 (a subagent in a fresh context, 2026-11-18), no BLOCKING finding; fixed: the off-device settings were stored again though unchanged (now stored only when _change_made finds a difference; the test checks the files' mtimes), PUT /power/ups/config with the defaults created its file (now written only for a change), a container that Docker made and could not start left no entry (container_created as failed), the lock was one for all containers (now per container), a firewall switch took an unreadable ufw status for off (_ufw_is_active answers 500), a webhook's header names reached a channel entry (named as webhook_config.headers), a pull by digest could write a false image_pulled (the lookup falls back to images.get; test_containers.py's call count of images.get now looks at the last call, since a pull may look the reference up first). Left, recorded in ADR-0402: an Unmount that fails after the umount in the fstab or guard step and an off-device copy whose second file write fails write no entry, and the image that Docker pulls for a created container has none. Device check of f281749 on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB 0.305): PUT /power/config unchanged 200 with no entry; shutdown_minute changed and put back, two settings_changed entries naming it; PUT /power/ups/config {} with no UPS no entry; a disabled webhook channel to an .invalid host: its create one entry, an unchanged PUT none, a rename one, its DELETE one warning, and its URL, host and path in no entry; DELETE /security/login-history with older_than_days 36500 deleted_count 0 and no entry; each new entry with its user, client address and resource; 2332 entries, none broken. After a reboot from the API the entries were kept, and after scenario.sh all the chain held 2454 entries, none broken. Not run on the device: the firewall, mounts, container creates, image pulls, suspend and the off-device settings.

features.description: Audit entries are appended to the log one line each, off the event loop and with rotation, instead of rewriting the whole file
steps: Sign in 100 times: the audit log grows by 100 lines, and the bytes written before stay as they were
An entry is written in a worker thread, never on the event loop
A damaged line is skipped, and the other entries are still listed
The log rotates at its size limit and keeps a fixed number of old files, which GET /api/v1/audit/logs still reads

On the dev device, sign-ins append one line each to /data/audit/audit.jsonl without rewriting it (its inode and earlier bytes stay), and the SD writes of a sign-in are measured before and after the deploy (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)
features.notes: Device check on 2026-11-07 after the deploy: three sign-ins appended three lines of about 270 bytes, the file kept its inode and its earlier bytes, and GET /api/v1/audit/logs/count counted them. A sign-in wrote 0.156 to 0.168 MiB to the SD card, 0.172 to 0.195 MiB before with a small old log; the rest is the login history's SQLite commit (architecture.sqlite-write-cost). Step 5 was reworded by ADR-0224. Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): no reboot check needed. The old /data/audit_log.json was deleted on the device.

features.description: Each audit entry carries the hash of the one before, so an edited or removed entry is detected
steps: Every entry stores a hash over its content and the previous entry's hash
After an entry in the file is edited or deleted, GET /api/v1/audit/logs reports where the chain breaks
The chain continues across rotated files
features.notes: Builds on security.append-only-audit-log. Passed 2026-11-10 (ADR-0328). Step 1: every entry stores prev_hash, the hash of the entry before it, and hash, SHA-256 over the fields of its line but hash as canonical JSON, chained under the log's lock by _append_line, so the supervisor and the emergency command line make one chain. Step 2: GET /api/v1/audit/logs gives each entry its chain: broken for an edited entry, the entry after a removed, inserted or damaged one, the entry after one whose hash was made anew, and an entry without hashes after the chain; ok for the others; none for the entries from before the chain. The Audit page marks a broken one with "Chain broken" and why. The newest entries have no entry after them: the supervisor keeps the last entry it wrote or read at the log's end, and when that is gone or changed, a critical entry of the user system says so. Step 3: the first entry of each newer file links to the last entry of the file before it, and the oldest entry kept starts the chain, also after a clearing. TestHashChain and TestTheEndOfTheChain of test_audit_log.py (the 7 tests of TestHashChain failed before the change), and "an entry where the chain breaks is marked, with why" of audit.spec.ts. Not shown (ADR-0328): removing the oldest entries, and a chain written anew while the supervisor was stopped, as the hashes need no key. Not host-level.

features.description: The supervisor bounds the size of request headers and the number of open connections
steps: The upload throughput over 2.5 GbE is measured with the HTTP parser and limits chosen, and stays at today's level
A request whose header block is over the limit is refused
Connections over the limit are refused while the open ones keep working
features.notes: Built (ADR-0333): uvicorn runs with --limit-concurrency 128 in both supervisor images and the stand-in, src/websocket/events.py holds at most 64 open sockets and 16 waiting for their auth message (uvicorn's limit never refuses an upgrade), and Caddy's global servers block sets max_header_size 16KB. Step 2: test_deploy_scripts.py checks the Caddyfile's limit (the stand-in's proxy is Node's, with its default of 16 KB, so Caddy's 431 is a device check). Step 3: test_request_limits.py checks that both images pass the same limit, and a real uvicorn with a limit of 3 answers 503 while two other connections are open and 200 again once they are closed; TestSocketCaps of test_ws_auth.py refuses a socket past either cap before it is accepted, and counts sockets out when they close or fail to sign in. Step 1: the parser stays httptools and the limits do not touch request bodies; the measurement over 2.5 GbE needs a client on the LAN. Device check 2026-11-10 with main c1328ab and after the reboot of 22:01 UTC: uvicorn's command line on the host has --limit-concurrency 128, and through Caddy on the device a 12 KB header block got 200, a 22 KB one 431 over HTTP/1.1 (refused in HTTP/2's framing layer), a plain request 200. Step 1, measured from the workstation (10GBASE-T) to the device's 2.5 GbE port with scripts/dev/upload-speed.py, through Caddy and uvicorn's httptools into the pool: 256 MiB at 239 MiB/s (2.01 Gbit/s); 4 GiB three times at 90, 105 and 79 MiB/s, the write rate of the pool's 7200 rpm disk. No figure from before exists: the parser is the one of before, and these are today's level.

features.description: An administrator turns the host's UFW firewall on or off and adds and removes rules in System > Security
steps: Turn the firewall on in System > Security: ufw status on the host says active
Add a rule that allows a port from the LAN: the host's ufw lists it, and Delete removes it
The web UI, SSH and SMB stay reachable from the LAN with the firewall on
features.notes: Built (ADR-0416): the firewall is the host's ufw, run through src/host.py (src/security/firewall.py); ufw is in OPTIONAL_HOST_TOOLS, GET /security/firewall answers installed false without it and the card says to install the package, every change answers 409; with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local every firewall route answers 503 (the stand-in, the test stack). The rules are the host's, read from the ### tuple ### lines of /etc/ufw/user.rules and user6.rules in ufw's numbering; /data/firewall_rules.json is gone. Step 1: POST /security/firewall/enable saves the rules files and whether ufw was on in /run/unos/firewall, adds UNOS's rules (TCP 22, sshd's ports, 80, 443, 445, 5357 and UDP 3702, 5355 from each local network of SMB's hosts allow but the loopback, the IPv6 ones only with IPV6=yes), writes the marker, arms the transient timer unos-firewall-revert (120 s) and only then runs ufw --force enable; without the save or the timer nothing changes (500); unless POST /security/firewall/confirm keeps it, the timer puts the files back and turns ufw off (or reloads it after a rule change), keeping the FORWARD policies that ufw's stop would open (test_firewall.py TestEnable, TestRevert; test_firewall_scripts.py under sh and dash; firewall.spec.ts 'Enable asks first ...' and 'a change that is not kept ...'). Step 2: POST /security/firewall/rules runs `ufw allow in proto tcp from <source> to any port <port> comment <comment>` after checking each value, the rule is listed from the host's files, and DELETE /security/firewall/rules/{id} runs ufw --force delete <number> and checks that exactly that rule went (else the rules are put back); while ufw is on both arm the revert first, one change waits at a time (409), and UNOS's rules are not deleted (409) (TestRules; firewall.spec.ts 'a rule that allows a port from the LAN ...'). Step 3: UNOS's rules let the local networks reach the web UI, SSH and SMB before ufw goes on, and the revert undoes a change that cut them off; that they stay reachable on a real host is the device check's. Enable turns ufw's logging off unless it is off (its kernel log lines would reach the journal on the system disk while the NAS idles, ADR-0214). Every command runs under the host's timeout --kill-after=5 50 with LC_ALL=C; one the host does not answer leaves the armed revert to undo the change (test_an_enable_the_host_does_not_answer_is_left_to_the_revert). Enable is refused (409) for MANAGE_BUILTINS=yes, a DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY other than DROP, or no Docker chain in iptables' FORWARD (Docker's nftables backend), where ufw would cut the containers off; the revert of an Enable turns ufw off before it puts the files back, and puts back the FORWARD policies from before the Enable; a revert that fails leaves the file failed, which GET reports (revert_failed) and the card shows; GET reports reverting and client_local, and the Enable dialog warns a computer outside the local networks; SSH's ports come from ss and from sshd -T (ssh.socket); a rule that ufw would take as a new comment of an existing one is refused and put back; with IPV6=no user6.rules is not listed. Audit: firewall_enabled, firewall_disabled, firewall_change_kept (new), firewall_rule_added, firewall_rule_deleted and firewall_reset (test_audit_security_and_power.py). Not built: rules for outgoing or routed traffic from UNOS (the host's own are listed and can be deleted). Review (a subagent in a fresh context, 2026-11-18): fixed the two BLOCKING findings (a revert of an Enable that grepped ufw's translated status line, so on a host with another locale it left ufw on; an undo after a timeout that called the revert off while ufw could still be starting) and the RISK findings above (a failed revert reported as undone, a Reset that called the revert off before ufw's reset ran, MANAGE_BUILTINS and DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY unchecked, the FORWARD policies of Docker's nftables backend, ssh.socket's port, the asking computer outside the local networks, a comment-only update of UNOS's rule, the apps on the host's network that ufw filters over IPv4, a revert read while it runs, untested error paths). Left, with the reason: UNOS's rules come after the host's own, so an earlier deny of the host wins (documented; ufw's insert positions differ for IPv4 and IPv6, and reordering the host's rules is not UNOS's); the computer outside the local networks is warned, not refused (the web UI over IPv4 still reaches it, and a rule for it can be added first); a Disable while a revert runs is not refused (both run ufw; Disable is the safe direction); the AST check does not look into the argv of host.run_in_container; the ticking countdown has no live region, so that a screen reader does not read it every second (Keep is described by it); protocols other than TCP and UDP are shown as ufw names them. Host-level (GLOSSARY.md): passes after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214). The dev device has no ufw: the owner installs the package (ADR-0211) and sees `ufw status` say inactive. Device check, by hand with the device-checks skill, every API call through scripts/dev/api.py and every step under scripts/dev/sd.sh measure: (0) before the install, GET /security/firewall answers installed false and POST /security/firewall/enable 409; after it, record `iptables -S FORWARD | head -n 1` and `ip6tables -S FORWARD | head -n 1` on the host (Docker's DROP) and that `scripts/dev/check.sh` reports the IPv6 inbound filter loaded. (1) POST /security/firewall/enable answers changed true and revert_in near 120; on the host `ufw status verbose` says active with UNOS's 14 rules, `systemctl list-timers unos-firewall-revert.timer` lists the timer and /run/unos/firewall/pending holds its time. (2) Within the 120 seconds, from the workstation: `nc -vz -w 5 <the device's LAN IPv4> 443`, then 80 and 445, connect, `scripts/dev/ssh.sh true` signs in, and a listener that no rule lets in (`scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'timeout 100 python3 -m http.server 47123 --directory /dev/shm'`, which writes nothing) is not reached (`nc -vz -w 5 <ip> 47123` times out); only then POST /security/firewall/confirm: no unos-firewall-revert timer and no pending file is left, and the checks of (2) give the same; `scripts/dev/check.sh` passes. (3) POST /security/firewall/disable, then POST /security/firewall/enable without a Keep: about 125 seconds later `ufw status` says inactive, `journalctl -u unos-firewall-revert` shows the run, the FORWARD policies are as recorded in (0) and check.sh reports the IPv6 filter loaded. (4) POST /security/firewall/enable and keep it; POST /security/firewall/rules {"action": "allow", "protocol": "tcp", "port": "47123", "source": "<the workstation's LAN network>", "comment": "unoscheck"} answers revert_in; `ufw status numbered` on the host lists it and, with the listener of (2) running, the workstation's nc to 47123 connects; keep it; DELETE /security/firewall/rules/<its id from GET> removes it from `ufw status`, keep it, and nc times out again. (5) Leave the firewall on and kept for the owner's reboot; after it `ufw status` says active with UNOS's rules, the checks of (2) and check.sh pass and the containers are healthy; then POST /security/firewall/disable: `ufw status` says inactive and the FORWARD policies are as in (0). Whether ufw stays installed is the owner's call; its files keep UNOS's rules while it is off. Device check of cbe437c on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB in brackets): before ufw, GET says not installed and Enable answers 409 (0.020); ufw 0.36.2-9 installed by the check, inactive (62.664); with the firewall off, 443, 80, 445, ssh.sh and a listener on 47123 reached from the workstation; Enable armed the revert (119 s), ufw active with 14 UNOS rules, the timer and the marker present, 47123 blocked, access kept, Keep cleared the timer and the marker, check.sh OK (0.344); Enable without Keep: the revert turned ufw off 130 s after the request, `journalctl -u unos-firewall-revert` showing its run, no revert_failed (0.195); a rule for 47123 from the workstation's LAN listed, reached and kept, deleted, blocked and kept (0.137); on and kept across a reboot from the API at 22:38 UTC: active with the 14 rules 61 s after boot, access and check.sh OK, then Disable turned it off. That check found Disable putting back ufw's own FORWARD policies: IPv6's stayed DROP where it had been ACCEPT before the Enable. Fixed in 977b364 (ADR-0416: off4 and off6) and rechecked on the device on 2026-11-19 after its deploy (sync 0.457, build-supervisor 13.652, up 3.305): with IPv6's FORWARD policy put back to ACCEPT as found, Enable recorded DROP and ACCEPT, Keep left the record, Disable put back DROP and ACCEPT and removed it (0.156); an Enable without Keep was undone by the revert after 134 s with DROP and ACCEPT, no revert_failed and nothing left in /run/unos/firewall (0.219); access, the IPv6 filter and check.sh OK throughout. ufw stays installed and inactive on the device; after a reboot with ufw on, Disable falls back to the policies of ufw on (DROP), by design. Open: ufw on may block containers that reach the host's ports through host-gateway (Open WebUI to Ollama, Zigbee2MQTT to Mosquitto), not checked.

features.description: An administrator uploads a certificate or makes a self-signed one in System > Security, and the web UI is served with it
steps: Upload a certificate with its key and chain: it is listed with its names and expiry date
Browsers then get that certificate from https://<host>/
Deleting it returns the web UI to the certificate of Caddy's local CA
features.notes: Steps 2 and 3 are built (ADR-0404, which supersedes ADR-0357): POST /security/certificates/{id}/serve checks a stored certificate with cryptography (it parses, the key reads without a passphrase, belongs to it and is RSA of at least 2048 bits or EC on P-256 or P-384, which browsers take, its usages allow a TLS server, it is valid now, and each certificate of the chain is valid now, a CA when it says so and issued the one before it; one that expires within 30 days is served and marked), writes it with its chain and key into served.pem (0600, root's) of the volume served-certificate, which only the supervisor (read-write) and the web UI (read-only) mount, and runs `caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --force` with UNOS_TLS=served in unos-webui through docker exec; caddy_local_ca as the id serves the local CA again (UNOS_TLS=local, the file removed); deleting the served certificate serves the local CA first; a store under the served certificate's name is refused (409). A refusal of the checks answers 409 and reaches no Caddy; Caddy's refusal answers 502 and no Docker 503, and Caddy keeps what it served and the file is put back as it was (left as written when Docker did not answer in time, as Caddy may have loaded it); a delete of a certificate that Caddy serves reloads Caddy first. The web UI's command runs caddy validate with UNOS_TLS=served when the file exists and starts Caddy with the served certificate only when it passes, else with the local CA and one log line. webui/Caddyfile has the sites tls-local ({$UNOS_HOSTNAME:unos}, https://, tls internal) and tls-served (https:// only, the file as certificate and key), which import tls-{$UNOS_TLS:local} picks; the image build adapts both; ocsp_stapling off. The status and the listing say what a TLS handshake with webui:443 without SNI shows: served_by caddy_local_ca, stored_certificate or unknown, served_id, chosen_id and the SHA-256 fingerprint; each listed certificate has served, chosen and expires_soon, and its fingerprint is SHA-256. Serving what is served writes and reloads nothing, and the handshake that decides it is made under the lock. Audit entries: certificate_uploaded, certificate_generated, certificate_deleted and certificate_served (resource certificate, the id or caddy_local_ca). The card: the badge and HTTPS for browsers name the served certificate or Caddy's local CA, each stored certificate shows SERVED, NOT LOADED (chosen, but Caddy serves another) or NOT SERVED and EXPIRES SOON, Serve this certificate and Use Caddy's local CA ask in a dialog that warns that every browser will see a new certificate (and of the end date of one that expires soon) and shows the server's refusal, and the delete of the served one asks with its own text, in both languages (test_certificate_serving.py; TestServedCertificate of test_deploy_scripts.py and of test_standin.py; TestCertificateStatusNamesWhatIsServed; security.spec.ts serves, uses the local CA again and deletes the served one on the stand-in, whose front.mjs serves the served file while it loads; language.spec.ts; mobile-layout.spec.ts). Host-level (the web UI's container): it passes only after the device check below and its re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018); the stand-in runs no Caddy, no docker exec and no Caddyfile. Device check, after the owner's deploy of both images and the compose file (deploy.sh up recreates the containers with the new volume), each step wrapped in scripts/dev/sd.sh measure for its SD MiB: (1) scripts/dev/api.py GET /security/certificates/status answers served_by caddy_local_ca and chosen_id null; note its fingerprint F0. (2) scripts/dev/api.py POST /security/certificates/self-signed - with {"domain": "unoscheck<6 hex>.home.arpa", "validity_days": 30} on standard input; GET /security/certificates lists it, served false, with its fingerprint F1. (3) scripts/dev/api.py POST /security/certificates/custom_unoscheck<6 hex>.home.arpa/serve answers changed true and status served_by stored_certificate with fingerprint F1; through scripts/dev/ssh.sh, ls -ln of served.pem in the Mountpoint of docker volume inspect deploy_served-certificate shows mode -rw------- and owner 0. (4) From the workstation: openssl s_client -connect <the device's IPv4>:443 -noservername </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 prints F1 (no name, as a browser that opens the NAS by its address), and so does the same with -servername unos and with -servername other.example instead of -noservername; if the workstation's network filter still gets no data from the device's web ports (ADR-0198), run them on the device through scripts/dev/ssh.sh against 127.0.0.1:443 and say so. (5) The same serve again answers changed false and writes nothing beyond the API's own. (6) The owner restarts the web UI's container (docker restart unos-webui): docker logs unos-webui has no line 'the served certificate does not load', and step 4 prints F1. (7) The owner reboots the device: both containers are healthy, the status names stored_certificate, and step 4 prints F1. (8) A certificate with a chain, switched to directly: on the workstation, in a scratch folder, make a CA (openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -nodes -days 30 -subj '/CN=UNOS check CA' -addext basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE -keyout ca.key -out ca.crt) and a leaf for unoscheck<6 hex>-chain.home.arpa that it signs (openssl req -new -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -nodes -subj '/CN=unoscheck<6 hex>-chain.home.arpa' -keyout leaf.key -out leaf.csr; openssl x509 -req -in leaf.csr -CA ca.crt -CAkey ca.key -days 20 -extfile <(printf 'subjectAltName=DNS:unoscheck<6 hex>-chain.home.arpa\nextendedKeyUsage=serverAuth') -out leaf.crt), put leaf.crt, leaf.key and ca.crt as certificate, private_key and chain into one JSON body with python3, and send it on standard input to scripts/dev/api.py POST /security/certificates/upload -: it is listed with valid_until about 20 days ahead and expires_soon true (fingerprint F2). Serve it while the self-signed one is served: step 4 prints F2, and openssl s_client -showcerts shows two certificates, the leaf and the CA. The scratch folder is removed after step 9. (9) The start that cannot load the served file: the owner (root on the device) writes into served.pem in the volume's Mountpoint a certificate with the key of another (for example leaf.crt with ca.key, mode 600) and restarts unos-webui: docker logs unos-webui shows one line 'the served certificate does not load, Caddy's local CA instead: ...', step 4 prints F0, the status names caddy_local_ca with chosen_id the chain's certificate (the file holds its certificate), the card marks it NOT LOADED, and the web UI answers over HTTPS. (10) scripts/dev/api.py POST /security/certificates/caddy_local_ca/serve: served_by caddy_local_ca, step 4 prints F0, served.pem is gone.
