(11) Serve the self-signed certificate again (step 3), then scripts/dev/api.py DELETE /security/certificates/custom_unoscheck<6 hex>.home.arpa: the status names caddy_local_ca, step 4 prints F0, served.pem and the stored files are gone; delete the chain's certificate too. GET /audit/logs lists certificate_generated, certificate_uploaded, certificate_served (the certificates' ids and caddy_local_ca) and certificate_deleted. Review in a fresh context (2026-11-18), fixed: Ed25519 and P-521 keys (Caddy loads them, browsers fail the handshake) and certificates whose usages leave out TLS servers are refused; ocsp_stapling off; the handshake that decides a serve is made under the lock, an unchanged file is never written again, a reload that Docker did not answer in time keeps the file, and a delete reloads Caddy when Caddy serves the deleted certificate; unreadable extensions answer 409; the folder is synced after a rename. Left: a restore of the served file that itself fails (a full disk) answers 500 and can leave the file holding a certificate that Caddy does not serve, which the card then marks NOT LOADED and Use Caddy's local CA clears. Earlier history: before ADR-0404 stored certificates were only stored, and the status said so (ADR-0357). The gaps that the review of security.no-legacy-certificate-fixups found on 2026-11-10 are closed: openssl runs in a worker thread with a timeout of 10 s (read) or 60 s (generate), and a timeout answers 500 (TestOpensslRunsOffTheEventLoop); a store writes certificate, key and chain to temporary files (O_EXCL, O_NOFOLLOW, keys 0600) and renames them only once all are written, removing a stale chain, and stores, deletes and changes of the served certificate run in worker threads under one lock (TestCertificateFilesFollowNoLink, TestCertificateStoreIsAtomic, TestCertificateStoresAndDeletesDoNotMix); organization at most 64 printable characters and country two letters, 422 before openssl (TestSelfSignedSubjectValidation); a self-signed certificate is one whose issuer is its subject. The page still has no upload form: an upload goes through the API. Device check of 2026-11-12 (before ADR-0404): the status named caddy_local_ca, a self-signed certificate was listed as self_signed with served false, its key a regular file 600 root:root, a three-letter country was refused, and the delete removed both files. Device check of f281749 on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB in parentheses): the status caddy_local_ca, a stored certificate from before left alone; a generated self-signed certificate served (0.227): changed true, stored_certificate, served.pem -rw------- owned by 0, openssl s_client with no server name, with unos and with other.example all printed its fingerprint; served again: changed false, no entry, mtime unchanged; docker restart unos-webui (0.996): healthy, no 'does not load' line, the same certificate; kept across a reboot from the API. Then an uploaded leaf with its key and CA chain served over it (0.238), s_client -showcerts two certificates; a served.pem whose key does not match it, after a restart (1.102): exactly one 'does not load' line, the local CA served, the status caddy_local_ca with the leaf chosen and listed not served, HTTPS answering throughout; serving caddy_local_ca removed served.pem, and the deletes left the stored certificates as found (0.348); the audit log held the generated, uploaded, served and deleted entries and no key.

features.description: The certificate code keeps no special cases for files that older versions wrote
steps: The fix-ups for private keys that older versions left 0644 and for certificate names they stored without validation are gone from supervisor/src/security/router.py
Every stored certificate and key goes through the one current path: validated, and keys written 0600
tests/test_security.py passes without tests of the old cases
features.notes: Step 1: the fchmod of _write_private_key and the chmod before openssl, for keys that older versions left 0644, are gone, and so is the delete of any id inside CERTS_DIR, for names that older versions stored without validation (TestPrivateKeyMode test_no_key_mode_is_fixed_up). Step 2: an upload stores under the validated subject CN and a self-signed certificate under its validated domain; openssl prints the self-signed key and _write_private_key stores it like an uploaded one, 0600 whatever openssl's own file modes, and only after openssl succeeded, so a failure keeps the stored key (test_self_signed_key_file_is_0600, test_a_failed_self_signed_certificate_leaves_the_stored_key, test_uploaded_key_file_is_0600, test_a_new_upload_replaces_the_whole_key_file); the delete takes only the names that those two store (test_delete_refuses_an_id_that_names_no_certificate_name), and the listing shows only those, with the chain stored as <name>.chain.pem so that it is no certificate of its own (test_every_listed_certificate_can_be_deleted). Step 3: the tests of 0644 keys and of the name My NAS are gone. make e2e-local on main f3347fb, which holds the change, passed on the stand-in with E2E_CHROMIUM_PATH (670 passed, 16 skips on listed conditions): the web UI calls the delete and the listing. Passed 2026-11-10. Not host-level: the files are in the supervisor's data volume.

features.description: On a new installation the first visit creates the one administrator, and setup is refused afterwards
steps: Open the web UI of a new installation: /setup asks for the administrator's name and password
Create the account: the dashboard opens, signed in as that administrator
A second setup, also one sent at the same moment as the first, answers 400 and creates nobody
No default account exists before setup

features.description: A user creates API tokens for scripts, and a token can be disabled, expires and can be deleted

An expired token answers 401

features.notes: Step 1: TestApiTokenUse in test_authz.py creates a token with a name and a lifetime of 30 days: the answer holds it, GET /auth/tokens never does, and the database keeps only its SHA-256 (ADR-0239); TestApiTokenExpiry bounds the lifetime (ADR-0027). Step 2: a regular user's token gets 403 from the administrator-only APIs, and an administrator's token reaches them. Step 3: after POST /auth/tokens/{id}/toggle its requests answer 401 'API token is disabled' until it is toggled back; test_ws_auth.py refuses a disabled token at the WebSocket and closes a socket whose token is disabled. Step 4: a token whose expires_at has passed answers 401 'API token has expired', from the second after it. Step 5: TestApiTokenOwnership and TestApiTokenUse: another user, an administrator too, can neither list, toggle nor delete it, also with a token of their own. Steps 6 and 7 (ADR-0253, after the review of 2026-11-07): TestApiTokensAreManagedWithASession (a token, an administrator's too, gets 403 on create, toggle and delete, also of itself, and can still list; an invalid or disabled one keeps its 401) and TestApiTokenBounds (an empty, blank, 65-character or 900000-character name, other permissions than * and no name answer 422 and store nothing; the 101st token of a user answers 409, also for two requests at the same moment). api-tokens.spec.ts runs steps 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 and the name bounds against the stand-in's real supervisor; step 4 and the limit of 100 are backend-only, because the shortest lifetime is a day. features.description: A user sees the recent sign-ins of their account with the client's real address

features.notes: webui/tests/login-history.spec.ts on the stand-in's real supervisor, for a regular test user, with the browser in Asia/Kathmandu (UTC+05:45): a wrong password, then the right one. On the compose test stack that address is the test-runner's, and the spec also checks that it is not the proxy's (Caddy, the host webui). Fixed with it (ADR-0262): the times were answered without their UTC offset and shown hours off, the attempts of one second came in any order, and clearing the history counted its days in the server's local time. Step 1: test_two_factor_requirement.py TestTurningItOn (an administrator with 2FA and a current code turns it on with a grace period of 0, 1, 3, 7, 14 or 30 days, 7 by default; without own 2FA 409, a wrong or used code 400, an API token 403, a regular user 403, twice 409; the settings_changed entry of two_factor_requirement), TestTurningItOff and TestGracePeriod (during the grace period everything works and GET /auth/me answers by when; it starts at the later of the requirement's start and the account's creation); mandatory-two-factor.spec.ts on the stand-in: the card of System > Security turned on with 14 days and a code, then the sign-in of an account without 2FA lands on /two-factor-setup with the end of its grace period, Later reaches the dashboard and the Account page, the next sign-in asks again, and Stop requiring with a newer code ends it; an administrator without 2FA is told to turn it on first. TestARestoredRow (values that cannot be read, also aware times without a UTC, a missing table, tables of another layout, a start ahead of the clock: no request fails, and an administrator with 2FA turns it off) and TestARestore (a restore that turns it on or off, also from an older backup without the table, says so and audits it). mobile-layout.spec.ts walks the card and both states of the setup page. features.description: A user signs in with a hardware security key (WebAuthn) as the second factor
steps: On the Account page, register a security key
At the code step of the sign-in, touching the key opens the session
features.notes: Built 2026-11-18 on the workstation (ADR-0409); not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): a new table security_keys and the auth router, nothing on the host. Step 1: test_security_keys.py's TestRegistration and TestRegistrationChecks register ES256, EdDSA and RS256 keys of a software authenticator built on cryptography (supervisor/tests/webauthn_authenticator.py) through POST /auth/security-keys/register/begin, with the password, and /register/finish, and refuse every bent answer (type, origin, crossOrigin, RP ID hash, user presence, attested data, credential id, algorithm, CBOR that the bounded decoder refuses) and challenge (unknown, used, expired after 120 s, another user's, another session's, another origin's), an IP address (409), another page's Origin (403), an API token (403), an 11th key, a name twice and a credential id twice; security-keys.spec.ts adds a key on the Account page with Chromium's virtual authenticator (the WebAuthn domain of CDP) on the stand-in, after a wrong password kept the dialog. Step 2: TestSignIn: the code step offers only the keys of its own origin, a touch opens the session (Bearer and the session cookie), an answer works once, a forged Host cannot make a key work for another origin, a signature counter that goes backwards is refused and audited, and the login's 5 a minute counts the key's step; security-keys.spec.ts signs in with Use a security key at the code step, removes the key with the password, and the code step offers it no more; at https://127.0.0.1 the Account page says that keys need the NAS's name and the code step names where they work. TestWhatRemovesKeys: turning two-factor authentication off, deleting the user and reset-admin remove the keys; TestARestore: a backup's keys come back and pending challenges are forgotten; mobile-layout.spec.ts: the keys and both dialogs at 375 px and sideways, in both languages. Device check, by hand when the owner asks (it makes a temporary user and key and removes them), each step under scripts/dev/sd.sh measure: 1) scripts/dev/api.py POST /auth/users with a regular user unoscheck<6 hex digits> and a random password on standard input; 2) a minute later (the probe signs in 5 times, the login's limit per client, which api.py's relay at 127.0.0.1 shares), copy scripts/dev/security-key-probe.py into /dev/shm and run it there as root with python3 -I -B, the user's name and password as one JSON line on standard input, never on the command line: with the host's python3 (standard library only) and openssl it signs in, turns two-factor authentication on, makes an EC P-256 key in a folder of /dev/shm, registers it with Host and Origin unoscheck.invalid, signs in with it, sees the same answer refused, removes the key and sees the code step offer none, and removes its folder: every line PASS (TestTheDeviceProbe runs it against the API with the workstation's openssl); 3) scripts/dev/api.py GET /audit/logs: security_key_added, login_success 'Signed in with the security key ...' and security_key_removed of the user; 4) scripts/dev/api.py DELETE /auth/users/<id> --param username=<name>, and the probe removed from /dev/shm. A hardware key in a browser at the device's name, with Caddy's local CA trusted, needs the owner (a browser and a key at hand; the check never runs a browser): add it on the Account page, sign in with it at the code step, remove it. Review in a fresh context (2026-11-18, ADR-0017): nothing blocking; its risks were fixed (a test for each binding of a challenge, to the user's name, its origin, its RP ID and the request's origin, for the counter's compare-and-swap, and for a recovery code beside keys) and its nits too (the challenges behind a lock, as a restore clears them from its thread; a registration answered without reading the key again; the origin in security_key_removed; the sign-in page without WebAuthn; the page's challenge kept 50 s; the scripts' Host in the user guide; a name the account has refused before the touch). Left, with the reason in ADR-0409's Consequences: turning two-factor authentication off, which takes the app's code, removes the keys without the password, also with an API token, as before; and a registration refused after the touch leaves the credential in the authenticator. Device check of 09e792a on 2026-11-18 (0.469 SD MiB): a temporary regular user registered a key of the software authenticator, signed in with it at the code step and removed it (9 probe lines passed); the audit log holds security_key_added, the key's login_success and security_key_removed with no secret; the user and its files were removed after. A real hardware key in a browser is the owner's to try.

features.description: Signing out, a password change or an administrator's revoke ends a session on the server
steps: After sign-out, the session's token answers 401
A password change ends the user's other sessions
An administrator ends a user's sessions on the Users page
features.notes: Built (ADR-0329): a sign-in stores its session as a row of user_sessions (id = the JWT's jti), and authenticate_token accepts a session token only while its row exists and names its user (401 Session ended); the WebSocket re-check uses it too. Step 1: POST /api/v1/auth/logout deletes the caller's row, and the web UI's Logout calls it (webui/tests/auth.spec.ts: a copy of the token gets 401 afterwards; tests/test_sessions.py TestSignOut, also 400 for an API token). Step 2: a password change deletes the user's other rows in the commit of the new hash (TestPasswords; a refused change ends nothing); a password set by an administrator, the deletion of the user and reset-admin (test_emergency.py) end all of them. Step 3: POST /api/v1/auth/users/{id}/end-sessions?username= (administrators; 404, 409 for a reused id; audit entry user_updated) and the Users page's End sessions button (webui/tests/users.spec.ts Sessions: two sessions of a new user end, the administrator's stays). An ended session's live-data socket closes with 4401 (test_ws_auth.py). Database only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md).

features.description: The web UI keeps its session token out of localStorage
steps: After sign-in, localStorage holds no token
A reload keeps the session, or asks to sign in again, as the chosen design says
features.notes: Built (ADR-0397, superseding ADR-0009): the web UI's session token is in the HttpOnly cookie __Host-unos-session (Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, no Max-Age). POST /auth/login with cookie true sets it and answers no token, only session_key (an HMAC of the session id under the JWT secret), which the page keeps in its tab's sessionStorage and sends as X-UNOS-Session-Key and as key in a WebSocket's first message. A cookie counts only with the key of its session (401 otherwise, every route), so a server on another port of the NAS that the browser sends the cookie to (the catalog's Nextcloud serves HTTPS on 8443) cannot use it, and the cookie's token (marked cookie in the JWT) is refused as a Bearer token and in a WebSocket message. The cookie also counts only from the web UI's own origin: Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin when sent, Origin https://<Host> when sent and required for every method but GET and HEAD, else 403 (test_session_cookie.py walks every route); the cookie sign-in checks it before the password. Programs (scripts/dev/api.py, unchanged) sign in without cookie and get the token for a Bearer header. Logout sends the key, ends the session and deletes the cookie; one the NAS does not confirm leaves the session and the login page offers Sign Out Again. Tabs follow each other's sign-ins and sign-outs and hand the key to a new tab over the BroadcastChannel unos-session. The token that earlier versions left in localStorage is removed at each load. Step 1: session-cookie.spec.ts (no token in localStorage or sessionStorage, document.cookie without it, the login answer without a token, the cookie's attributes, an earlier version's token removed); first-run.spec.ts. Step 2, the chosen design: a reload keeps the session, and so does a new tab while another tab of the web UI is open; a new tab with none open asks to sign in again (session-cookie.spec.ts). No E2E spec reads a token from the page's storage (test_session_cookie.py TestNoTokenInWebStorage). Two reviews (ADR-0017). Fixed: the cookie alone was a full session for an HTTPS app on another port of the NAS's name (now the session key, and the cookie's token is no Bearer token); the token left in localStorage by earlier versions (removed at load); Sign Out Again could end a newer session (it ends only the unconfirmed one, forgotten at any sign-in); docs that said closing the browser always signs out. Left, with reasons: only Chromium runs the specs (Firefox and Safari send Origin with fetch and WebSockets per the Fetch standard: check them by hand once); a 401 to the sign-out counts as signed out, also for a cookie that another server replaced (nothing that the browser holds is that session then); a sign-out whose session had already ended leaves the dead cookie (logout answers 401 before it could delete it); the sign-out notice lives in the page's memory, so a reload of the sign-in page hides it; a tab that learns of another tab's sign-in only after a request of its own was refused, or a reopened tab with a stale key, goes to the sign-in page instead of asking the other tabs; the earlier versions' localStorage token is removed, not ended (its session expires within 24 h); scripts/dev/api.py does not redact session_key, harmless without the token, which it redacts; the Vite development server over plain HTTP no longer signs in. Database and web UI only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md). Device check of 991cb28 on 2026-11-17, through Caddy at https://127.0.0.1 as a temporary regular user: the cookie sign-in with a wrong Origin 403, with the right one 200 with session_key and no token, and the cookie __Host-unos-session HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ without Max-Age or Expires; /auth/me with the cookie and its key 200, without the key 401, cross-site 403, the cookie's token as a Bearer header 401; a PUT and a POST without Origin 403; the events socket with the key answered auth_ok and stats, with a wrong key it closed with 4401; Logout 200 deleted the cookie, and the old cookie and key then got 401; scripts/dev/api.py's Bearer sign-in 200 (SD MiB 0.145). Not on the device: Firefox and Safari.

features.description: An API token can be limited to reading, or to named areas of the API
steps: Create a read-only token: GET requests work and changes answer 403
A token limited to an area answers 403 outside it
features.notes: Database only, not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): the scope is the existing column api_tokens.permissions ("*" full, else "read" and the areas), checked in authenticate_token for every HTTP request and WebSocket (ADR-0392). Step 1: test_token_scopes.py TestTheSteps (an administrator's read-only token reads GET /auth/me, /auth/users, /auth/tokens, /audit/logs, /security/login-history and more; PUT /system/timezone, DELETE /audit/logs, POST /storage/pools and POST /notifications/test answer 403 "This API token can only read"; every change of the area auth and the restore of a backup 403 for every limited token; the backup download and the notification channels 403 as secrets) and TestEveryRoute (every route for 25 scopes, with a regular user's tokens that show the scope's own 403 or the role's, and with an administrator's tokens where the scope refuses, so that no handler runs; a full token is refused nowhere by a scope); api-tokens.spec.ts on the stand-in: the same through the API, and the Account page's dialog, which starts at read only in every area, makes a token whose GET works and whose change answers 403. Step 2: TestTheSteps (a token of audit reads and changes the audit log and answers 403 "This API token is limited to other areas of the API" for /auth/me, /storage/pools, /system/info and /security/login-history), TestEveryRoute (each of the 21 areas alone, read only in one area, two areas), TestWebSockets (the events socket only for every area, the container log socket for containers, the journal for logs, 4403 otherwise, also at the re-check after the stored scope changed); the spec: a token of Audit log and Storage made on the page reads the audit log and answers 403 for /auth/me, with the warning of the areas that run programs as root. Also: TestTheTable (the areas are the routes' prefixes, the kinds of the operations equal the test's own table, each concrete path takes its own template's kind, authenticate_token takes the operation as a required keyword), TestStoredValues and TestValuesThatCannotBeRead (restored values that are not a scope refuse the token everywhere and list it with scope_known false), TestARestore (the restore's warning counts them), TestTheApi (422 for permissions, unknown or repeated areas, a read_only that is not a JSON boolean; the audit entry names the scope). Open: the device check, through the API on the dev device: a read-only token and a token of one area made with a session, a few GETs and changes with each, and the SD MiB of the commits (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure). passes stays false until the lead's review. Device check 2026-11-17 (mvp.batch-8 at 320d3ec, deployed 2026-11-17 18:58-18:59 UTC; reboot from the API at 19:23:11 UTC (the boot of 19:24:4x, all containers healthy by 19:25:26); scenario.sh all after it: 187 steps passed, smart's sleep steps skipped while apps use the pool): with a read-only token GET /auth/me and /audit/logs 200, PUT /system/timezone 403; with an audit-only token /audit/logs 200, /auth/me and /storage/pools 403; both deleted (0.371 MiB; the tokens made and used on the device, never printed).

features.description: An API token's last use is stored at most once an hour, so automations do not write to the system disk on every request
steps: A script makes 100 requests with one token within a minute: last_used_at is committed at most once
GET /api/v1/auth/tokens shows a last use at most an hour old
On the dev device the requests of an automation write next to nothing to the SD card (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)
features.notes: Built 2026-11-07 (ADR-0252, which superseded ADR-0191): verify_api_token commits last_used_at only when it is empty or an hour old, and a commit that fails is logged and the request answered. Steps 1 and 2 pass: test_api_token_last_use.py (100 requests within a minute commit once, the next commit comes once the stored use is an hour old, GET /auth/tokens shows a last use at most an hour old, a request's own commit does not write a skipped last use, and a commit that fails at the UPDATE or at the COMMIT is rolled back and the request answered), test_ws_auth.py (the WebSocket's re-checks commit once; a handshake and a re-check whose commit fails still pass, and the socket stays open) and api-tokens.spec.ts on the stand-in (the last use the API shows stays as it is after more requests). Open: step 3, the device check after the deploy, with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure (ADR-0214): 100 requests within a minute with one API token, such as GET /api/v1/auth/me, write about what 100 requests with a session token write, plus at most one SQLite commit for the first (about 0.15 MiB, ADR-0224); before the change each of them committed. Database only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md). Device check 2026-11-17 (mvp.batch-8 at 320d3ec, deployed 2026-11-17 18:58-18:59 UTC; reboot from the API at 19:23:11 UTC (the boot of 19:24:4x, all containers healthy by 19:25:26); scenario.sh all after it: 187 steps passed, smart's sleep steps skipped while apps use the pool), step 3: 100 GET /auth/me with one token in 22.8 s wrote 0.062 MiB to the SD card (a 30 s idle 0.074), and GET /auth/tokens showed its last use at the first request.

features.description: Users can sign in while the disk that holds /data is full
steps: Fill the filesystem of /data, then sign in: the sign-in works
The audit entry that could not be written is reported in the log
features.notes: Built 2026-11-07 (ADR-0251): record_login_attempt rolls back a commit that fails with an OperationalError and logs the attempt as JSON, log_action logs an entry whose append fails with OSError as its JSON line, and login answers either way. test_sign_in_full_disk.py makes /data full by fault injection: SQLite's own 'database or disk is full' (PRAGMA max_page_count, login_attempts filled to its last page), the audit append failing with ENOSPC, and a commit failing at its end. Step 1: the sign-in answers a session token that GET /auth/me accepts, a wrong password 401, the password with a TOTP code its token, a wrong code 401. Step 2: the audit entry and the login attempt it could not write are logged at ERROR as JSON, with the user, the client address, the time (UTC for the attempt, whose row takes its time from the database) and the error; record_login_attempt rolls its session back, so that the caller can go on using it (TestRecordLoginAttempt). A recovery code does not sign in while its use cannot be stored: 500, and the code stays unused. Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md), and the dev device's /data is never filled for a check (ADR-0214). On a system disk full to the last block, the container's json-file log on the same disk can lose those lines too (ADR-0178).

features.description: Passwords are checked as given: the cut to 72 bytes kept for hashes of the passlib-era code is gone
steps: verify_password in supervisor/src/auth/utils.py checks the whole password, without cutting it to 72 bytes first
A sign-in with a password longer than 72 bytes fails like a wrong password, without a server error
New passwords longer than 72 bytes are still refused with 422, and the comment in supervisor/src/auth/schemas.py no longer points to old hashes
features.notes: Done 2026-11-09 (ADR-0315, which superseded ADR-0026). Step 1: verify_password encodes the password whole and answers False for one longer than 72 bytes before bcrypt, which matches no hash then, also not that of its first 72 bytes (test_auth.py TestPasswordHashing test_a_password_longer_than_72_bytes_matches_no_hash, which failed on the cut). Step 2: test_a_sign_in_with_a_password_longer_than_72_bytes_fails_like_a_wrong_one: an account with a password of 72 bytes signs in with it, and with one character more gets 401 "Incorrect username or password" (it signed in on the old code). Step 3: test_new_password_schemas_enforce_bcrypt_limit and test_authz.py test_new_passwords_longer_than_bcrypt_limit_are_rejected (422), and schemas.py's comments name the check as given. A hash of the passlib code for a password of at most 72 bytes still verifies (test_a_hash_of_the_passlib_era_still_verifies_its_password). Not host-level.

features.description: An administrator renames a user, and the user's SMB access follows the new name
steps: Edit a user and change the name: the user signs in with the new name, and the old one is refused
A user with SMB keeps it under the new name: Samba's account of the old name is removed, and the one of the new name is made with the password that the rename asks for
A new name that breaks the name rule, or exists in another case, is refused with the reason
features.notes: Built on the branch auth.user-rename (ADR-0368), not deployed yet. PUT /auth/users/{id} takes new_username with the current username; a user with SMB on needs a new password, the host account is renamed with usermod -l and keeps its uid, Samba's account of the old name is removed and the new name's made with the password, and the share access and smb.conf follow. Host-level (usermod, Samba's passdb, smb.conf): passes only after the device check and its re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). The check: scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb, whose steps rename the check's user with a new password (its open session ends, the marked host account keeps its uid and the files it wrote, pdbedit -L lists the new name and not the old), show the share's access and smb.conf's section under the new name with a signed session that writes, and sign the new name in to UNOS while the old one, tried with its old password, is refused by UNOS and by Samba (Samba's refusal only where the device has no guest share). smb_uid_names records each name of a renamed uid, so a backup made before or after the rename, restored after the user's deletion, keeps the uid (supervisor/tests/test_restore_accounts.py); usernames_taken bounds a regular user's login history by when the name was taken (TestRename). Not on the device: the refusals of the name rule, of a name in another case and of a name the host has, the busy account and the failed commit (supervisor/tests/test_smb_accounts.py TestRename), and the edit dialog (webui/tests/users.spec.ts on the stand-in). Device check 2026-11-12 (before and after the reboot from the API at 19:37:03 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 19:37:58; both containers healthy by 19:38:50), and after the deploy of the review fixes): scenario.sh smb passed its 32 steps each time (3.988, 3.812 and 3.691 MiB), with the rename of its user: its share and sign-in under the new name, the old name refused by UNOS and Samba.

features.description: The Storage page lists the host's disks with what UNOS knows about each
steps: Open Storage: every whole disk of the host is listed with model, size and serial
Each disk says whether it is the system disk, in use or holding data, and which pool it belongs to
When the disks cannot be listed, the page says why
features.notes: Proven here, 2026-11-07. Step 1: test_disk_safety.py TestDisksEndpoint (test_lists_every_whole_disk_with_model_size_and_serial: GET /api/v1/storage/disks lists every whole disk with model, size and serial, without the boot SD card and zram) and TestListDisks (hidden boot and virtual devices, a system disk on NVMe, a root shown as /dev/root, old lsblk); storage.spec.ts 'every disk is listed with its model, serial and size, and what uses it' (each row's device, model and serial, size, HDD or SSD, contents, mountpoints and status, on route fakes with the supervisor's texts). Step 2: TestDisksEndpoint test_each_disk_says_what_uses_it_and_which_pool_it_belongs_to (system, in use with its reason, holding data, the pool of a disk and of both members of a mounted pool) and TestListDisks (swap, md, wipefs signatures, a failed probe counts as data); the same spec shows the System, In use, Pool, Has data and Free badges with the reasons. Step 3: test_a_disk_list_that_cannot_be_read_answers_500_with_the_reason (500 'lsblk failed: <reason>') and the specs 'a disk list that cannot be loaded says why, and the pools are still shown' and 'a pool list that cannot be loaded says why, and the disks are still shown' (ADR-0271: each card says why instead of 'No disks found'). The steps only read the host (lsblk, findmnt, swapon and wipefs --no-act through supervisor/src/host.py), so they make no host-level change and need no reboot check; the device check was done on 2026-11-06. A sanity check after the next deploy: Storage on the device lists /dev/sda with its model, serial and size and the badge of the pool data's disk, and the SD card is not listed. Reviewed in a fresh context twice (ADR-0017), 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08: no finding left open for this entry.

features.description: An administrator creates a btrfs pool from free disks with a RAID profile, after typed confirmations
steps: Select free disks, a name and a profile: single, RAID0, RAID1, RAID1C3, RAID1C4 or RAID10, never RAID5 or RAID6
Create stays disabled until the pool name is typed, and for disks with data until the erase is confirmed
The system disk and disks in use are not offered, and a disk whose serial, WWN or size changed since it was selected is refused and the list reloaded
The new pool is mounted at /mnt/pools/<name> by UUID with a managed fstab entry and listed as healthy
features.notes: Not run on the dev device: it needs a spare disk. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator unmounts and mounts a pool, and a pool comes back mounted after a reboot
steps: Unmount a pool after the confirmation: it shows not mounted, and nothing can be written into its empty mountpoint, not even by root
Mount it again: the managed fstab entry (# unos-pool:<name>) is back, and the pool is healthy
Reboot the host: the pool is mounted before Docker starts, and the apps on it start
Unmount is refused while running apps keep data on the pool
features.notes: Built and proven here on 2026-11-07: storage.spec.ts 'Pool unmount, mount and removal (fake data)' on route fakes that change their pools as the supervisor does: Unmount asks first (Cancel sends nothing), POST /pools/<name>/unmount, then the card shows Not mounted, no fstab badge and no Scrub, Volumes or Unmount; Mount sends POST /mount and the card shows Healthy, Mounted at boot and its mountpoint again; the 409s of a pool that running apps or host processes use are shown in the dialog and the pool stays mounted. test_pool_persistence.py pins those 409 texts at the API (TestPoolEndpoints test_a_pool_that_running_apps_use_answers_which_ones, test_a_pool_that_host_processes_use_answers_409) and proves the host side on the fake host: the guard chattr +i, the managed entry removed and written again, the startup reconcile (TestUnmountAndDelete, TestMountPool, TestReconcile, TestAppChecksBeforeStart, TestLifespanRunsReconcile). Device check: 2026-11-05 (Phase 0 deploy: unmount, mount and a reboot of that tree); the deployed tree changed since. Device check 2026-11-08: every unmount of the pool data answered 409 "still in use outside the host ... so it was mounted again", also with every app stopped: systemd-resolved, -timesyncd, -udevd, -networkd, rsyslogd and -logind run with sandboxing in mount namespaces of their own, each with a copy of the pool's mount in a peer group of its own, which the host's umount does not reach; UNOS mounted the pool again, as designed. Built (ADR-0288): after the host's umount, the copies (the pool's filesystem by MAJ:MIN at its mountpoint with the host mount's root, in a namespace whose own root is the host's: the same MAJ:MIN and FSROOT at /, as systemd makes them for services) are unmounted with umount --namespace <pid>, never lazily; a namespace that has the pool mounted anywhere else (a container's bind mount), has it mounted at all while its root is its own (a container, also one that binds /mnt/pools or /mnt and so keeps the pool's mount at its mountpoint for its apps), or has another filesystem at its mountpoint together with a copy, is refused with 409 that names the process, and the pool is mounted again, as when a copy cannot be unmounted or the filesystem is still active after them. Tested in test_pool_persistence.py (the mount namespaces of the FakeHost: service copies, stacked copies, peers, an exited process, bind mounts, containers with the pool at its mountpoint, also while Docker cannot be asked, namespaces with roots of their own, a busy or hanging umount, lsns failing; the endpoints and their smb.conf applies; the texts of storage-fakes.ts), test_smb_integration.py (the shares stop being served) and storage.spec.ts ('an unmount refused while apps use the pool says why, and the pool stays mounted': a refusal for running containers, then for a mount namespace that has the pool mounted elsewhere, shown in the dialog while the pool stays mounted). Open: the device check after a deploy and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). With transmission stopped, Unmount data on the Storage page answers 200 and shows Not mounted, and GET /api/v1/storage/pools shows mounted false and persistent false; on the host, findmnt lists nothing at /mnt/pools/data, /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid> is gone (this decides), no line of /proc/*/mountinfo lists the pool's MAJ:MIN with the filesystem type btrfs (the field after ' - '; the number alone can belong to a tmpfs or overlay mounted after the pool's was freed), the supervisor's log has "Unmounted /mnt/pools/data in the mount namespaces of processes ..., which kept copies of its mount", lsattr -d /mnt/pools/data shows the i flag and touch /mnt/pools/data/x as root fails with 'Operation not permitted', and /etc/fstab has no '# unos-pool:data' marker. Should Unmount answer 409 that names a process of a sandboxed service as having the pool mounted at /mnt/pools/data, compare findmnt --task <pid> --mountpoint / -o MAJ:MIN,FSROOT with findmnt --mountpoint / -o MAJ:MIN,FSROOT on the host: copies are unmounted only where the two agree. Mount data: the marker and its entry are back, the pool is Healthy, and transmission starts. With transmission running, Unmount answers 409 that names transmission, and the pool stays mounted. After the owner's reboot the pool data is mounted at /mnt/pools/data before docker.service starts (systemd-analyze critical-chain docker.service lists mnt-pools-data.mount), and transmission runs. Report the SD MiB of each step. Device check 2026-11-08 after the deploy of main 533668a (the fix of ADR-0288): with transmission running, Unmount answered 409 naming it and the pool stayed mounted; with it stopped, Unmount answered 200, the supervisor unmounted a service's copy of the mount, and the host had nothing at /mnt/pools/data, no /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>, no '# unos-pool:data' marker, and touch in the mountpoint failed (Operation not permitted); Mount brought the marker back, the pool was healthy, and transmission started. After a reboot from the API the pool was mounted and transmission ran. Since ADR-0344 (storage.edge-cases), an unmount or removal of a mounted pool while Docker cannot be asked is refused with 503 before anything changes, so the mount-namespace check after the umount is no longer reached then.

features.description: Storage and the dashboard show each pool's health as the host reports it, and a degraded pool raises an alert
steps: A mounted pool without errors shows healthy
An unmounted pool shows not mounted, and one whose state cannot be read shows unknown, never healthy
Missing devices, error counters, a read-only mount and a filesystem that btrfs forced read-only are shown on the pool
Detach a device of a RAID1 test pool: within 5 minutes the RAID monitor marks it degraded and sends an alert that names the cause
GET /api/v1/health/raid-monitor/status shows the time of the latest check
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-05 (a healthy pool, also after a reboot of the Phase 0 tree). The degraded case needs a test pool on spare disks. Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): the pool data shows healthy and mounted read-write, and GET /api/v1/health/raid-monitor/status names its latest check (23:00:15 UTC, after the boot). Open: step 4, a degraded RAID1 test pool, which needs spare disks and was never checked on the device.

features.description: An administrator removes a pool from UNOS after typing its name, and its disks keep their data
steps: Delete asks for the pool's name, unmounts the pool and drops its managed fstab entry and empty mountpoint
The disks are not touched: the filesystem is listed again as an unmounted pool that can be mounted later
A pool that host processes or containers use is refused with 409
features.notes: Built and proven here on 2026-11-07: storage.spec.ts 'remove pool asks for its name, and the disks keep the pool to mount later' (the trash button 'Remove pool <name>', Continue, Remove Pool disabled until the exact name is typed, DELETE /pools/<name>, then the pool listed again as Not mounted with Mount, which mounts it again) and 'a pool in use is not removed, and the dialog says why' (the 409 in the dialog, the pool still mounted). test_pool_persistence.py: test_delete_forgets_the_pool_but_keeps_the_data (umount, the managed entry dropped, chattr -i and rmdir of the mountpoint, no mkfs or wipefs, listed again as unmounted and mountable), test_delete_keeps_a_non_empty_directory_guarded, test_delete_is_non_destructive, and the 409s at the API for containers and host processes (TestPoolEndpoints). The API takes no typed name: only the page asks for it (ADR-0035). Built: Remove Pool unmounts through the code of Unmount, so the copies that services with sandboxing keep in their mount namespaces, whose root is the host's, are unmounted with it, and a namespace that has the pool mounted anywhere else, or at all while its root is its own, like a container's that binds /mnt/pools, is refused with 409 (ADR-0288). storage.spec.ts 'a removal refused while the pool is in use says why, and the pool stays' shows that 409 in the dialog while the pool stays. test_pool_persistence.py tests the server: the managed fstab entry and the empty mountpoint dropped, the disks untouched and the filesystem listed again, the refusals while containers (also one whose namespace keeps the pool at its mountpoint), host processes or other mount namespaces use the pool; test_smb_integration.py its shares. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), on the device on a test pool of spare disks, not the pool data. Remove Pool (typing its name) answers 200; /etc/fstab has no '# unos-pool:<name>' line, /mnt/pools/<name> is gone, /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid> is gone (this decides), no line of /proc/*/mountinfo lists the pool's MAJ:MIN with the filesystem type btrfs (the field after ' - '; the number alone can belong to a tmpfs or overlay mounted after the pool's was freed), btrfs filesystem show still lists the filesystem, and the Storage page lists it as Not mounted; Mount mounts it again with its data and marker. With a container using the pool, Remove Pool answers 409 that names it, and the fstab entry stays. After the owner's reboot a removed pool is not mounted. Report the SD MiB of each step.

features.description: An administrator lists, creates and deletes the volumes of a mounted pool
steps: Open a mounted pool's Volumes dialog: the subvolumes in its top folder are listed, without snapshots
Create a volume with an optional quota: it appears at /mnt/pools/<pool>/<name>
Delete asks for the name; a volume that apps, Docker volumes, shares or NFS exports use is refused with what uses it
On a pool mounted read-only the dialog lists the volumes and says why they cannot change
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy). 2026-11-07: the Volumes dialog sends the optional quota, typed in GiB, in bytes and shows the 409 when quotas are not enabled (ADR-0243, which superseded ADR-0241; storage.spec.ts). Open: the device check of a create with a quota (the 409 while quotas are off on the pool data; once the owner enabled them, the limit on the new volume's quota group) and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Device check 2026-11-07 on the pool data: a volume with a quota was refused with the hint (409, quotas are off on data), the same volume without a quota was created at /mnt/pools/data/unoscheck, listed and deleted.

features.description: An administrator creates, lists, restores and deletes read-only snapshots, also on a schedule with a keep count
steps: On Snapshots, create a snapshot of a pool or a volume: it is listed with its time
Restore a snapshot: its content comes back as a new folder next to the original
Delete a snapshot
A scheduled snapshot task with keep count 3 keeps the three newest automatic snapshots and deletes no other
A scheduled snapshot of a pool that is not mounted fails with Pool <name> is not mounted
features.notes: Built 2026-11-07 (ADR-0243, which superseded ADR-0241): GET /snapshots/subvolumes lists each mounted pool and its volumes, read through src/host.py, a pool whose volumes cannot be read alone with volumes_error, and the Snapshots page picks one; times come in UTC with their offset, the names snap_, restore_ and auto_ take UTC, the list runs no du and needs its pool or volume, and create, restore and delete use dialogs. Create, restore and delete, the scheduled ones included, act on the folders they opened, through /proc/self/fd paths, and delete by subvolume id (ADR-0242). Asserted on fakes: steps 1 to 3 by test_snapshots.py and snapshots.spec.ts, steps 4 and 5 by test_scheduler_validation.py and scheduler.spec.ts. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step; it is also the first run of the real btrfs-progs with /proc/self/fd paths, subvolid-resolve and delete --subvolid: GET /snapshots/subvolumes lists /mnt/pools/data and its volumes; a snapshot of a volume and one of the pool are listed with their local time; restoring the pool's snapshot makes the volume restore_<time>, which the Volumes dialog deletes (a volume's copy stays undeletable in the web UI, storage.restore-copies-deletable); delete removes a snapshot; a snapshot task with keep count 3 run four times keeps three auto_ snapshots; a run while the pool is unmounted fails with Pool data is not mounted. Device check 2026-11-07 on the pool data: a volume was offered on Snapshots, snapshotted (listed with its UTC time), restored into restore_<time> with its content, and the snapshot deleted; a snapshot task with keep count 3 run four times kept the three newest auto_ snapshots and deleted no other (0.031 and 0.164 MiB on the SD card). Step 5 (a pool that is not mounted) is proven by test_snapshot_task_requires_mounted_pool: the only pool is in use by transmission.

features.description: An administrator scrubs a mounted pool, follows the progress and cancels it, also on a schedule
steps: Start Scrub on a mounted pool: the request returns once btrfs has started, and the API stays responsive
The pool shows the scrub's progress and, at the end, its result
Cancel stops a running scrub
A scheduled scrub task scrubs its pool, and fails without running btrfs when the pool is not mounted
A pool that is not mounted offers no Scrub button
features.notes: Built and proven here on 2026-11-07. Step 1: test_storage.py TestScrubStart (the request answers once btrfs returns, the scrub process still running), TestScrubOffTheEventLoop (worker threads, timeouts). Step 2: TestScrubStatus (btrfs-progs 6 output parsed: progress while it runs, finished, every error of the error summary summed, aborted, interrupted, never scrubbed) and storage.spec.ts 'Scrub (fake data)': Start Scrub, the progress bar 'Scrub progress' with bytes, percent, rate and duration, updated every 2 seconds, then 'Last scrub: No errors' with the start time; 'Last scrub: 13 error(s)' and the interrupted result (ADR-0272). Step 3: TestScrubStatus test_cancel_answers_the_cancelled_scrub and the spec 'cancel stops a running scrub, and the result says it was cancelled' (DELETE, followed while btrfs still reports running, then 'Last scrub: cancelled before it finished'). A status btrfs cannot report answers 500, not idle (test_a_status_that_btrfs_cannot_report_is_an_error_not_idle), and the card then says 'Could not read the scrub status' instead of a stale progress and still offers Cancel Scrub (spec 'a scrub status that cannot be read says why instead of a stale progress'); a start or cancel that btrfs did is answered running or aborted when the status read after it fails (test_a_start_or_cancel_whose_status_cannot_be_read). Step 4: test_scheduler_validation.py test_scrub_task, test_scrub_of_an_unmounted_pool_fails_without_btrfs, test_a_scheduled_scrub_is_recorded_when_btrfs_returns. Step 5: storage.spec.ts 'shows pool health and mount state' and the unmount spec (no Scrub on a pool that is not mounted). The 409 of the API for an unmounted pool is storage.scrub-needs-mounted-pool. Open, on the device, on the pool data: Scrub on the Storage page shows the progress moving and a result at the end ('Last scrub: No errors' on a healthy pool), Cancel Scrub on a second run shows 'Last scrub: cancelled before it finished', a scheduled scrub task's Run now is recorded as success, the API answers other requests meanwhile, and the SD writes of the run are measured (the scrub status lives in the /var/lib/btrfs tmpfs, ADR-0171); and the re-check after the owner's reboot (ADR-0018), after which the pool shows no last scrub result: the restart forgot it (ADR-0171). Device check 2026-11-08 after the deploy of main 1fdf802: a scrub of the pool data ran to the end in 19 s with 0 errors and its progress moving; a second scrub was cancelled (aborted). Right after the start, GET .../scrub still says idle for a moment. The re-check of 2026-11-09 (PROGRESS.md, Log) found step 2 failing on the device: for about 6 s after Start Scrub the API answered idle, Start Scrub's own answer too, until btrfs had recorded the new scrub, so the page stopped following a scrub that ran and offered Scrub again. Fixed by ADR-0313, which superseded ADR-0272: a scrub is running when btrfs prints its time left, also below "no stats available", and Start Scrub answers running when the status read right after it says idle (TestScrubStatus: the status of a scrub btrfs has not recorded yet, test_start_answers_running_before_btrfs_reports_the_scrub; 5.9 s of idle measured after a start); the copy of a disk replace, which the kernel runs as a scrub, is not shown as one when no record shows it (test_the_copy_of_a_disk_replace_is_no_scrub), and a cancel that btrfs did answers aborted when the status then says idle (test_a_cancel_before_btrfs_recorded_the_scrub_answers_aborted). Device check 2026-11-09 with main eceead5, ADR-0313 deployed: scripts/dev/scenario.sh scrub passed at 21:11 UTC and, after the reboot of 21:12 UTC (the boot of 21:14:01 UTC), at 21:17 UTC: Start Scrub answered running and so did the status right after it; the scrub of data ran 18 s, its bytes scrubbed growing from 0.42 to 1.28 GiB (1.27 after the reboot), and finished without errors; a second scrub, cancelled once btrfs had recorded it, ended aborted; a disabled scheduled scrub task's Run now said "Scrub started", and its scrub finished after 19 s, while one of a folder with nothing mounted on it failed with "Pool <name> is not mounted at <path>" (0.152 and 0.148 MiB; that no btrfs runs then is test_scheduler_validation.py test_scrub_of_an_unmounted_pool_fails_without_btrfs); the first step found the pool's last scrub idle both times (the smbconf check before it restarts the supervisor, ADR-0171); the whole check 0.555 and 0.543 MiB. The Storage page itself was not looked at on the device: its card is the E2E specs' on route fakes (ADR-0215), and the device check covers the API that the card reads. Since ADR-0314 the device check is scripts/dev/scenario.sh scrub: the start's answer, a scrub to its end with its bytes scrubbed growing, a cancel and a scheduled scrub's Run now, with each step's SD MiB; its first step names the pool's last scrub, which a reboot leaves none of (ADR-0171).

features.description: An administrator reads the SMART data of every disk the Storage page lists and schedules SMART tests
steps: On Storage or System > Disk Health, open a disk: its SMART attributes, temperature and overall health are shown
Disk Health lists the same disks as Storage, NVMe included, and disks without SMART data too
A partition or another device is refused as not a disk of this system
In System > Scheduler, a SMART test task offers the connected whole disks and keeps the disk of a task while it is disconnected
Run now records the run as success, failed or timed out
features.notes: Disk Health opens each disk's SMART data in a dialog, from what GET /health/disks returned (ADR-0235): health, temperature, power-on hours and cycles, serial, firmware, the last self-test (of the ATA or the NVMe self-test log), the ATA attributes with their status, and the SMART/Health Information log of NVMe disks (test_health_smart.py, health.spec.ts on route fakes). smartctl runs in the container (architecture.host-command-layer), and GET /health/disks runs it without -n standby, so opening Disk Health wakes sleeping disks (storage.disk-spindown). Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy: SMART data and a short test of the pool's disk). Open: the device check of the dialog (System > Disk Health on the device: the pool's disk /dev/sda opens with its attributes, temperature and PASSED; an NVMe disk, if one is connected, with its health log) and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Device check 2026-11-07 after the deploy of main cce0def: GET /api/v1/health/disks returned the SMART data of /dev/sda (WDC WD6400AACS: health PASSED, 33 C, 51832 power-on hours, 17 attributes, the last short self-test), and again after a reboot.

features.description: SMART attributes are recorded over time, and a rising count of reallocated or pending sectors raises an alert
steps: The SMART monitor records each disk's attributes at every pass
A rise in reallocated or pending sectors sends an alert to the e-mail and Telegram channels
GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends and /smart/predictions report the trend and a failure estimate per disk
features.notes: Proven here, 2026-11-07. Step 1: test_health_monitor.py TestSmartHistoryWrites test_every_pass_is_recorded_in_ram_where_the_endpoints_read_it (each pass adds the disk's counters, temperature and path, as /smart/history, /smart-monitor/status and /smart/trends report), test_health_smart.py test_the_monitor_checks_the_same_disks (every awake whole disk of Disk Health) and test_storage.py test_monitor_round_runs_in_a_worker_thread. The history is written only when a pass changes it and at shutdown (ADR-0269, ADR-0214): TestSmartHistoryWrites proves that passes that change nothing and a start that changes nothing write nothing, that a new disk, a counter, a path or an lsblk serial writes it at once, that a failed write is tried again and the alert still sent, and that the snapshots in RAM are written at shutdown. Step 2: TestSmartAlertChannels (a rise of the reallocated or of the pending sectors reaches every enabled e-mail and Telegram channel once, not a disabled one, with the title, message and recommendation) and TestSmartTrendAlerts (one alert per rise, again for a further rise, none after a snapshot without the counters, again for a rise after a drop, ADR-0270); TestSmartHistoryWrites test_a_pass_that_ends_after_the_shutdown_keeps_nothing_and_alerts_at_the_next_start (ADR-0269; an alert still being sent when the supervisor stops is cut off, as before); test_storage.py TestAlertsOffTheEventLoop (delivery off the event loop, bounded). Step 3: TestSmartTrendsEndpoint (GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends lists every tracked disk with its data points and rising counters, steady and removed disks included, the disks without a serial or with an empty one by path, the window of the last 24 values, ADR-0270) and test_smart_predictions.py (GET /smart/predictions: the failure estimate of each connected disk, ADR-0235). Only the ATA counters are recorded, so NVMe disks have none, and sleeping disks are skipped (smartctl -n standby). No host-level change. A sanity check after the next deploy: GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends lists the device's disks with data_points growing by one per hour, and /data/smart_history.json keeps its mtime across hourly passes (stat), so the hourly SD writes of the old monitor are gone (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure over a pass). Reviewed in a fresh context twice (ADR-0017), 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08; the findings were fixed except two, recorded in ADR-0269 and ADR-0270: an alert still being sent when the supervisor stops is cut off and not sent again (the monitor writes before it sends, as before), and a history that an older monitor stored under an empty serial is not continued under 'unknown'.

features.description: Disks whose SMART trend predicts a failure are marked replace soon on the dashboard and in Disk Health
steps: A disk with a predicted failure shows replace soon with the reason
The mark goes away when the prediction does
features.notes: GET /health/smart/predictions scores the SMART history as ADR-0235 fixes it (the rate over the last 24 snapshots; no prediction for NVMe disks or the shared 'unknown' history) and covers the disks connected now, found by the lsblk serial the monitor stores with each snapshot when it names one disk and one history, else by path. A counter is read from the snapshots that hold it, and the history file is written atomically; one that cannot be read answers 500. Disk Health marks a disk Replace soon by its serial, with the risk factors and the recommendation, and lists a prediction that matches no listed disk apart; the dashboard lists such disks for administrators and links to Disk Health; both say when the predictions cannot be read. Proven here, 2026-11-07: test_smart_predictions.py (the threshold, the window, snapshots without the counters, the disks covered, the mark going a day after the last rise, the history file), health.spec.ts and dashboard.spec.ts on route fakes, roles.spec.ts (no request for regular users); reviewed in a fresh context twice (ADR-0017), the findings of the second fixed on 2026-11-07. No host-level change, and no failing disk can be shown on the device. A sanity check there after the next deploy: GET /api/v1/health/smart/predictions answers 200 for the connected disks, new snapshots in /data/smart_history.json hold lsblk_serial, and the dashboard shows no mark and no warning.

features.description: The Snapshots page lists the copies that snapshot restores made, and deletes them
steps: Restore a snapshot of a volume: the copy restore_<time> is listed on the Snapshots page
Delete it there after the check that nothing uses it: the subvolume is removed by its subvolume id
The volume that held it can be deleted afterwards
features.notes: Until 2026-11-12 a restored copy inside a volume could be deleted nowhere in the web UI. Built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0358): GET /snapshots/copies?subvolume=<pool or volume> lists the copies that restores made right in a pool or a volume (a writable snapshot restore_<date>_<time>, its path checked byte for byte, Parent UUID set and not read-only), newest first with the time of the name, and DELETE /snapshots/copies/{name}?subvolume=... deletes one by btrfs subvolume delete --subvolid after the checks of a volume's Delete (running containers, SMB shares, NFS exports, the off-device copy; one function for both now, pools._refuse_used_subvolume), refusing anything else (400, 404, 409); the audit log gets snapshot_deleted. The Snapshots page lists the copies of the pool or volume chosen apart from its snapshots (name, path, time) and deletes them after a confirmation. The volume that held a copy can be deleted afterwards. Tests that failed before: supervisor/tests/test_restore_copies.py (no route: 405 for the list, 404 for the delete, and the volume's Delete stayed 409 with the copy inside), webui/tests/snapshots.spec.ts (7 tests: no Restored copies card, the Restore dialog's old texts), the volumes tests of supervisor/tests/test_dev_scenarios.py (the check made no snapshot or copy). The volumes scenario check (scripts/dev/scenario.sh volumes) has the steps: a snapshot of its volume, its restore, the copy listed and a subvolume on the host, its Delete refused while a share uses it, then done, and the snapshot and the volume deleted. Open: that device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Review fix 2026-11-12 (ADR-0358): a subvolume is taken for a copy only when each of Name, UUID, Parent UUID and Flags is a line exactly once in the whole output of btrfs subvolume show and the Name is the copy's; test_a_description_with_forged_or_other_names_is_not_taken and _is_refused (forged lines in a renamed name, its own Snapshot(s) line, another copy's name) failed before (listed; 200 deleted). Device check 2026-11-12 (the integration tree 8150936, before and after the reboot from the API at 13:11:00 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 13:11:56; both containers healthy by 13:12:50), and main b01cf92's tree 0a5294c after its deploy): scenario.sh volumes passed its 11 steps each time (1.516, 0.910 and 1.559 MiB): a snapshot of the check's volume, its restore making a copy in the volume (a subvolume on the host) listed with the volume's restored copies and not with its snapshots, the copy's Delete refused while a share uses it and naming the share, then deleting it also on the host, and the volume deleted after its snapshot.

features.description: Starting a scrub of a pool that is not mounted answers 409, and one helper starts every scrub
steps: POST /api/v1/storage/pools/<name>/scrub for a pool that is not mounted answers 409 and runs no btrfs command
The Storage page and scheduled scrubs start scrubs through the same helper
features.notes: Built 2026-11-09 (ADR-0311, which superseded ADR-0071): scrub_start of supervisor/src/storage/pools.py is the one start of a scrub, for the Storage page (pools.start_scrub, POST /api/v1/storage/pools/<name>/scrub) and the Scheduler's scrub tasks: it asks the host's mount table (findmnt) for a btrfs filesystem mounted at the pool's path and answers 409 without any btrfs command otherwise, also for a name that nothing is mounted for, then starts btrfs killed at its timeout (ADR-0290). Step 1: test_storage.py, TestScrubNeedsAMountedPool (the 409 and no btrfs with another pool mounted, and what counts as mounted on the fake host's mount table). Step 2: test_scheduler_validation.py, test_the_storage_page_and_scheduled_scrubs_start_through_one_helper, and test_scrub_of_an_unmounted_pool_fails_without_btrfs. Device check (ADR-0018) on 2026-11-09 with the runtime files of main 31ac73b, before and after the reboot of 18:41 UTC (the boot of 18:42:31 UTC), with the SD MiB of each step: POST .../scrub for a temporary folder /mnt/pools/unoscheck<hex> with nothing mounted on it answered 409 with the text of ADR-0311 (by ADR-0311, the old code answered 500 with btrfs's refusal on the ext4 root), and the folder was removed again (0.078 MiB each time); a Start Scrub of the pool data and a Run now of a disabled scheduled scrub task of it ("Scrub started") each started a scrub that btrfs reported running and that ran to its end after 18 to 19 s, Start Scrub's with 0 errors (0.035 to 0.125 MiB; cancelling one is a step of storage.scrub), and no task of the check was left. Since ADR-0314 these steps are scripts/dev/scenario.sh scrub.

features.description: A btrfs or smartctl command that hangs in the kernel no longer holds a worker thread after its timeout
steps: A scrub, stats reset or SMART test command that does not return is killed at its timeout, and its worker thread is free at once
The API answers the timeout, and later requests are served
features.notes: Built (ADR-0290, which superseded ADR-0289 after the review): btrfs scrub start, status and cancel (the Storage page and scheduled scrubs), btrfs device stats --reset, smartctl -t (POST /api/v1/health/disk/{device}/test and scheduled SMART tests), the reads of SMART data (Disk Health, the Storage page's SMART data and the hourly SMART monitor) and the btrfs subvolume show of the scheduler's snapshot cleanup (which had no timeout and now has 60 seconds) run through host.run_in_container. It starts the command in a session of its own; at the timeout it kills the command's process group with SIGKILL, leaves the wait for its end to a daemon thread and raises TimeoutExpired at once. It runs one run of a command at a time: a second run waits for the first and starts once it ended, and while a killed run is still stuck the command is not started but fails at once, logged once as "Not started", so a hung pool or disk keeps at most one stuck process of each command. A SMART test without an answer now says "smartctl did not answer within 30 seconds: <device> may not be responding" instead of "Command timed out"; a snapshot cleanup whose btrfs does not answer deletes nothing, and the snapshot task's run fails with "Snapshot <name> created, but old snapshots were not cleaned up: btrfs did not answer within 60 seconds. The pool may not be responding.". Step 1: tests/test_command_timeouts.py: TestRealProcesses (a timeout ends the command and the sleep it started, as nsenter starts its command, and no other process; a session of its own) and TestCommandsThatDoNotReturn (with fake processes whose wait never returns: the timeout raised at once, the process group killed, the wait left to a daemon thread, a stuck command not started again, a second run that waits for the first until it is killed and then starts nothing, a second run that starts as soon as the first answered); TestScrubStart of test_storage.py and test_a_scheduled_scrub_is_recorded_when_btrfs_returns of test_scheduler_validation.py run fake btrfs scripts through the real runner. Step 2: tests/test_command_timeouts.py through the API with one worker thread of each kind: POST, GET and DELETE /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub, POST /api/v1/health/raid/<pool>/reset-stats, POST /api/v1/health/disk/<disk>/test, GET /api/v1/storage/disks/<disk>/smart, GET /api/v1/health/disk/<disk> and GET /api/v1/health/disks answer the timeout, then serve the next request at once, and answer at once while the command is stuck; a scheduled scrub and SMART test fail with their message and free the scheduler's thread, a scheduled snapshot task whose cleanup gets no answer fails and keeps the snapshots, and the SMART monitor records the other disks; test_a_stats_reset_that_does_not_return_answers_500 of test_health_monitor.py; test_a_snapshot_task_whose_cleanup_btrfs_does_not_answer_is_recorded_as_failed of test_scheduler_validation.py (the run and the task's last status are failed). Because scrubs and SMART reach the host's pools and disks (a host-level change), the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214), were needed. On the dev device: POST /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub answers 200 within seconds, GET /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub then says running and `ps -o pid,sid,pgid,args` shows the scrub's btrfs process with its own session, and DELETE /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub cancels it; POST /api/v1/health/raid/<pool>/reset-stats answers 200; POST /api/v1/health/disk/<disk>/test?test_type=short answers started; GET /api/v1/health/disks, GET /api/v1/health/disk/<disk> and GET /api/v1/storage/disks/<disk>/smart answer with the disk's data; Run now of a BTRFS Scrub, a SMART Test and a BTRFS Snapshot task with a keep count records success; `docker logs unos-supervisor` has neither a "Killed" nor a "Not started" warning; and after a reboot the same. A process stuck in the kernel cannot be made on the device on purpose: that part is shown by the fakes only. Not covered: the Snapshots page's commands (run_cmd of src/snapshots/router.py, also the scheduled snapshot itself) still use subprocess.run, since they name their folders by descriptor numbers and their list would have to stop at the first btrfs that does not answer; the Storage page's scrub status polling does not wait for each answer, so on a hung pool its overlapping requests hold the default executor's threads for one timeout (docs/USER_GUIDE.md says so), after which the card says 'Could not read the scrub status' with the timeout (ADR-0272); the commands of host.run_on_host still run on, on the host, after their timeout, which frees the thread (architecture.host-command-layer). Device check 2026-11-11 (tree 8ea5a08, by hand, before and after the reboot from the API at 23:22:13 UTC on 2026-11-11 (the boot of 23:23:10; both containers healthy by 23:23:59)), the same both times: POST /storage/pools/data/scrub answered running in 0.5 s, ps showed 'btrfs scrub start /mnt/pools/data' alone in a session of its own (its sid and pgid its own, not the supervisor's), and DELETE cancelled it (aborted after 5 to 6 s); reset-stats answered ok; GET /health/disks, /health/disk/sda and /storage/disks/sda/smart answered with sda's data (WD-WCAUF0349104, PASSED); POST /health/disk/sda/test?test_type=short started a self-test that completed without error; Run now of disabled Scrub, Snapshot (keep count 1000) and SMART Test tasks recorded success ('Scrub started', 'Snapshot auto_<time> created', 'SMART test started') and their scrub and self-test ended without errors; the task snapshot was deleted again; docker logs of unos-supervisor held neither Killed nor Not started. SD MiB of the whole check 0.480 before and 0.591 after the reboot. A command stuck in the kernel cannot be made on the device on purpose: that part rests on the fakes, as above.

features.description: Storage operations stay correct with rare names, races and Docker states
steps: A subvolume renamed while the quota rollback guard runs is never taken for the new volume
Odd subvolume names, line breaks included, cannot confuse what UNOS reads from btrfs subvolume list
When Docker cannot be asked during an unmount, a Docker volume's mount of the pool is not taken for the administrator's own mount
Docker volumes are compared with bind folders after resolving symlinks and relative paths, also for third-party volume drivers
Whole disks named like xvdaa, sdaaa or dasda are accepted wherever they are listed
A failing subvolume list right after a volume create answers that the volume exists without its quota, and a create whose name was taken meanwhile names what is there
Renaming or moving a folder that is a bind mount answers 409, not 500
A folder delete stops at a mount or subvolume that appears below the folder while it is deleted
features.notes: Low-severity cases deferred in slice 1; each step can be a pass of its own. 2026-11-11: steps 3 and 7 fixed and tested with fakes; steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8 were open then (see 2026-11-12 below). Step 3 (ADR-0344, which supersedes ADR-0070): when Docker cannot be asked about the running containers or their volumes, Unmount and Remove Pool of a mounted pool answer 503 "Pool '<name>' was left mounted: Docker did not answer, ..." before anything changes (no umount, no fstab write, no unmount in a mount namespace); a pool that is not mounted is still removed without Docker. test_pool_persistence.py: test_without_docker_the_pool_stays_mounted_and_nothing_changes (a Docker volume's host mount of the pool, for unmount and remove), test_docker_volume_that_cannot_be_inspected_leaves_the_pool_mounted, test_without_docker_a_container_that_binds_the_pools_mountpoint_is_refused and TestPoolEndpoints test_unmount_and_remove_without_docker_answer_503_and_change_nothing failed before (the pool was reported unmounted, or unmounted and mounted again); they replace the tests of ADR-0070's unmount without Docker. Step 7: a rename, or a move within the pool, that rename(2) refuses with EBUSY (a folder that is a bind mount of another folder of its pool, whose st_dev is the pool's) answers 409 with the text of a delete of it, "'<name>' is a separate subvolume or filesystem (such as a snapshot or a mount point) and cannot be renamed (moved) in the file manager."; any other EBUSY of the file API answers 409 "In use by the system, for example as a mount point, so the file manager cannot change it" (it answered 500). test_files_security.py: test_a_folder_that_is_a_bind_mount_cannot_be_renamed_or_moved (EBUSY faked, the mount in the fake mount table) and test_any_other_entry_that_is_busy_is_a_conflict failed before (500 "File operation failed: <the text of EBUSY>"). Open for steps 3 and 7: the device check. A Docker that does not answer while the supervisor runs cannot be made safely on the device (a stopped Docker stops UNOS), so step 3 rests on the fakes. Step 7 on the device: on a test pool, bind-mount one folder onto another with mount --bind (on the owner's request), then Rename and Move of that folder in the File Browser answer 409 with that text and change nothing; unmount the bind mount afterwards. Report the SD MiB of each step. ADR-0348 (which supersedes ADR-0170): a move checks every item in the mount table before any is moved, so a bind mount among several items moves none of them (test_a_move_refuses_a_bind_mount_before_anything_is_moved failed before: the first item had moved), and a move that fails part way says how many items moved before it (test_a_move_that_fails_part_way_says_how_many_items_went_before failed before). A file that is a bind mount is looked up in the mount table whatever its st_dev, also before a move to another pool (test_a_move_refuses_a_file_that_is_a_bind_mount_with_another_st_dev failed before: the first item had moved, and to another pool the file had been copied and the answer was "In use by the system"). Not checked on the dev device yet: step 7 with a real bind mount (mount --bind on a test pool); step 3 cannot be made on the device safely. 2026-11-12: steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8 fixed and tested with fakes (ADR-0352, which supersedes ADR-0073). Step 1: the quota guard of a new volume takes as the newest id before the create the higher of the first line of `btrfs subvolume list --sort=-rootid` and the first level-0 line of `btrfs qgroup show --sort=-qgroupid`; a subvolume keeps its quota group 0/<id> while a rename takes it out of the list. test_volumes.py TestQuotaRollback test_a_subvolume_renamed_while_the_guard_reads_is_never_taken_for_the_new_volume failed before: with the swap after the create the renamed subvolume got the quota (200), with the swap when the quota failed it was deleted ("The volume was removed again."). Step 2: with the highest id first, a line that a name with a line break adds cannot raise the newest id; and every id the list gives a volume name is checked by the host's shell, which compares `btrfs inspect-internal subvolid-resolve <id>` with the name byte for byte (_VOLUME_PATHS_SCRIPT), for the list, a delete and the quota. test_a_name_that_forges_a_higher_id_costs_later_volumes_nothing failed before (409 "it was renamed or replaced right after it was created ... existed before it was created"), TestDelete test_a_name_that_starts_with_a_volume_name_and_a_line_break_is_another_subvolume failed before (the delete went to the id of "photos\nold", 257, not to 256) and test_such_a_name_alone_is_no_volume too ("photos" was listed). Two tests changed with it: test_forged_list_line_cannot_swap_volumes and test_a_forged_list_line_does_not_move_the_quota (renamed from test_a_forged_list_line_gets_no_quota) expected 409 and now expect the real volume deleted or limited, the forged id untouched; test_forged_list_line_cannot_redirect_the_delete no longer lists the phantom. Step 4: for an unmount, Remove Pool, Delete Volume and an import under an earlier pool's name, each Source of a container's mounts and each folder a local volume binds is made absolute (from /), resolved by `realpath --canonicalize-missing` on the host and located in the host's mount table (MAJ:MIN and FSROOT): it counts when it lies in the folder of the pool or volume (_containers_on). test_volumes.py TestVolumeInUse test_a_container_that_reaches_the_volume_another_way_keeps_it (symbolic link, relative link, relative device, device through a link, folder bound on the host, third-party driver) failed before (200, the volume deleted), and test_pool_persistence.py test_refuses_a_container_that_reaches_the_pool_through_a_link_or_another_mount (symbolic link, folder bound on the host; unmount and remove) failed before (DID NOT RAISE PoolBusyError: the pool was unmounted). Step 5: DISK_NAME_PATTERN also takes sdaaa, xvdaa, dasda, dasdaa and their partitions; lsblk still decides what is a disk. test_health_smart.py test_whole_disks_with_longer_names_answer_wherever_they_are_listed (GET /storage/disks/<name>/smart, GET and POST /health/disk/<name>), test_disk_safety.py test_creates_a_pool_on_a_disk_with_a_longer_name and test_scheduler_validation.py test_disks_with_longer_names_are_targets failed before with 400 "Invalid disk name format. Expected format like 'sda', 'sdb1', or 'nvme0n1'" (pool create: "Invalid device name format"). Step 6: a list or check that fails right after a create with a quota answers 500 "Volume '<name>' was created without its quota: ... Delete it and create it again.", and a create that btrfs refuses because something took the name meanwhile answers 409 "'<name>' already exists in pool '<pool>': <a folder|a file|a symbolic link|a subvolume> took the name while the volume was being created. Nothing was created." (stat --format='%i %F' on the host). TestCreateRaces test_a_failing_list_after_the_create_says_that_the_volume_exists_without_its_quota (500 "Listing the subvolumes of /mnt/pools/data failed: ...") and test_a_name_taken_after_the_check_is_a_conflict_that_names_what_is_there (500 "Creating volume 'documents' failed: ERROR: target path already exists: ...") failed before. Step 8: a delete for good of a folder (also Empty trash, the expiry and a move to another pool or volume) walks it on descriptors and checks each folder's st_dev and mount ID (/proc/self/fdinfo) before deleting anything in it (_remove_tree): a subvolume or mount that appears below the folder after the checks stops it with 409, which says that part of the folder was deleted before that. test_files_security.py test_a_delete_stops_at_a_subvolume_or_mount_that_appears_below_the_folder_while_it_runs (a subvolume, a bind mount) failed before: 200, the folder was deleted with the files of the new mount. Open: the device check, with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): on a test pool with quotas enabled, a volume created with a quota gets it (the real btrfs-progs with --sort=-rootid, --sort=-qgroupid and subvolid-resolve in the script); a subvolume made by hand with the name of a volume, a line break and more is not listed and does not stop the delete of that volume; a container that binds a symbolic link to a volume keeps Delete Volume from deleting it; SMART data of a disk only if one with a long name is attached. A mount that appears during a delete cannot be timed by hand: the fakes carry step 8. Accepted (ADR-0352): a stale quota group above every subvolume can make a create with a quota answer 409 after its id is given out again following a remount, and FUSE or network volume drivers are not recognized.
