Review fixes 2026-11-12 (ADR-0352): realpath runs under the host's timeout --signal=KILL 10; one that does not answer answers 500 before anything changes ("Pool '<name>' was left mounted: realpath did not resolve ...", "Volume '<name>' was not deleted: ..."); a list or check that does not answer after a create with a quota answers 500 "Volume '<name>' was created without its quota: btrfs did not answer within 120 seconds. Delete it and create it again." and keeps the volume. test_a_realpath_that_does_not_answer_leaves_the_pool_mounted, test_a_realpath_that_does_not_answer_keeps_the_volume and test_btrfs_that_does_not_answer_after_the_create_says_that_the_volume_exists_without_its_quota failed before. 2026-11-12: a realpath killed by timeout's SIGKILL reaches the supervisor as -9 (nsenter re-raises it); -9 now counts as a hang, as 124 and 137 do (the -9 cases failed before: 'exit status -9'). A btrfs qgroup limit that does not answer answers 500 "Volume '<name>' was created, but btrfs did not answer within 120 seconds while its quota was set: it may have no quota. Delete it and create it again." and keeps the volume (test_a_quota_limit_that_does_not_answer_says_that_the_volume_may_have_no_quota failed before). Device check 2026-11-12 (main 641f2a5, before and after the reboot from the API at 04:35:30 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 04:36:49; both containers healthy by 04:37:17)): a subvolume made on the host whose name holds line breaks and two forged list lines (one naming photos, one naming the next volume) showed no phantom volume, and the next volume made through the API was listed once with its path and deleted; GET /health/disks and /storage/disks list sda; scenario.sh volumes and files OK. Steps 1, 3, 4, 6 and 8 are races or failures that cannot be made on the device safely: they rest on the tests. Open on the device: step 7 with a real bind mount. Device check 2026-11-19 (main 9061fb0), step 7: a folder of a check volume of the pool data bind-mounted onto another on the host (mount --bind, 0.000 SD MiB): the files API's rename and move of the mount point answered 409, not 500, and the delete of a folder above it stopped at the mount; then umount and the folders and the volume deleted (0.059, 0.020, 0.016 SD MiB). Every step that can be made on the device safely has passed there; the races and failures rest on the tests.

features.description: Idle data disks spin down after a timeout set per disk
steps: Set an idle timeout for a data disk: it spins down after that time without access
The system disk cannot be given a timeout
Storage shows whether each disk sleeps, and reading SMART data does not wake it
features.notes: Built on 2026-11-15 (ADR-0378), a host-level change (ADR-0018): UNOS's udev rule /etc/udev/rules.d/90-unos-disk-spindown.rules and hdparm -S on the host. Step 1: PUT /storage/disks/{name}/spindown with Off or 5, 10, 20, 30 minutes, 1 to 5 hours (values hdparm -S expresses) runs hdparm -S under timeout and keeps one line per disk, matched by its serial, which udev runs at boot and when the disk is plugged in again; the rule is the setting's only home (no table), written only on a change, removed with its last line, audited as settings_changed of the resource disk (test_disk_spindown.py; storage.spec.ts: the Power column and the Idle Timeout dialog). Step 2: the system disk is refused with its reason (409), and so are a boot or virtual device and a partition (400), an NVMe disk, a disk without a serial a rule can match or with another disk's serial, and a host without hdparm, an optional host tool (ADR-0321): GET /storage/disks names the reason as spindown_problem. Step 3: each disk's power_state comes from hdparm -C on the host under timeout (CHECK POWER MODE alone: active/idle and idle are active, standby and sleeping standby, a failure or the timeout unknown; for an answer hdparm does not name, "unknown" with exit 0, as an EPC disk's idle_a, idle_b, idle_c and standby_y, smartctl -n idle -i -j in the container, which stops after CHECK POWER MODE without IDENTIFY: IDLE* active, STANDBY* and SLEEP standby, anything else unknown; one hdparm -C per disk at a time, and after one that timed out the disk is unknown at once, with no other started, until pgrep in the container finds it gone, as ADR-0290 bounds run_in_container), or, on a host without hdparm and for an NVMe disk, from smartctl -n standby -i in the container, whose IDENTIFY restarts an awake disk's standby timer; it is read first, and a sleeping disk is not probed with wipefs; the SMART reads of Storage and Disk Health run smartctl -n standby and answer standby / STANDBY (health.spec.ts); the Storage page asks for the pools and the filesystems found only once the disks answered (storage.spec.ts); every periodic disk access was audited and is shown standby-safe with every disk asleep: the SMART monitor (which also leaves alone a disk with an idle timeout that had no I/O since its last read, since IDENTIFY and SMART commands restart it (CHECK POWER MODE did not on the dev device's disk); its first pass after a start reads every awake disk, and a disk found asleep at its last pass is read once awake), the RAID monitor and the monitoring endpoints /health/prometheus and /health/full (now without a scan of the disks: btrfs filesystem show --mounted, whose exit 1 with nothing mounted means no pool, and lsblk), the trash expiry (hourly checks that ask only the disks of a pool whose pass is due and pass over one whose disks sleep; a pass put off remembers the sleeping disk and asks no disk of the pool again until the kernel counted a read or write on it, then that disk first) and the live statistics; and the host's smartd, which with Debian's smartd.conf asks every awake disk its power mode and SMART data every 30 minutes: install.sh turns it off once UNOS runs (stop_smartd, systemctl disable --now smartmontools), docs/INSTALL.md's Step 1 does so too, and uninstall.sh says how to turn it on again (test_deploy_scripts.py). The device check is scripts/dev/scenario.sh smart, whose steps read the SMART data of each disk (STANDBY for one that already sleeps), show the system disk (the boot SD card mmcblk1 on the dev device) refused a timeout with its reason, set sda's shortest timeout, wait for standby (at most six times 5.5 minutes, 1980 s, stopping at the first standby, which covers sda's own minimum of about 10 minutes for 5 now that its GET /storage/disks reads no longer restart the timer, and one more such minimum after an hourly SMART monitor pass that reads the awake disk during the wait, since in scenario.sh all the files and volumes checks use the pool just before; a disk still awake fails the step (a SKIP while apps use the disk to the end of the wait, ADR-0394), which says whether the kernel counted reads or writes on it meanwhile, and so names a command that restarts the timer or a longer minimum when it counted none), read SMART through both pages and show sda asleep with its I/O counters unchanged, and set the timeout of UNOS's rule again, or Off: no standby timer (hdparm -S 0) until sda's next power cycle, since ATA reads no timer back; on a host without hdparm, when UNOS's rule has none for sda but /etc/hdparm.conf sets one, and when sda has UNOS's timeout with its automatic offline data collection on and unrecorded (or a record without a timeout), the 6 idle-timeout steps (5 in the last case) are SKIPs with the reason (the dev device has hdparm now). Measured on the dev device on 2026-11-16 (sda WDC WD6400AACS-00G8B0 firmware 05.04C05 behind the JMB58x controller, smartd off, /proc/diskstats unchanged; hdparm -I: standby timer values spec'd by Standard, with device specific minimum): hdparm -S 60 (5 minutes) and -S 120 (10 minutes), each with hdparm -C every 60 s, both went to standby after 660 s, so sda raises a shorter timeout to about 10 minutes and CHECK POWER MODE does not restart its timer; hdparm -y put it in standby, and smartctl -n standby left it asleep (exit 2); -S 120 with smartctl -n standby -i every 3 minutes (in the supervisor's container) and hdparm -C every minute was still active after 840 s, so the earlier power read restarted the timer; with smartd active, a 20-minute timer did not run out in 22 minutes; and scenario.sh smart, whose GET /storage/disks reads every 330 s ran smartctl -i, failed with sda active after 990 s and 0 reads and 0 writes counted. Since the power read is hdparm -C (2026-11-16), the check's step finds sda standby at its read after about 660 s: "standby after 660 s (the timeout: 300 s)" on the dev device at 06:54, 13:42 and 19:21 UTC on 2026-11-16, and after 990 s in the run of 14:45 UTC, after a reboot (the device check at the end). Steps by hand beyond scenario.sh, with the device-checks skill, before and after a reboot: (1) scripts/dev/scenario.sh smart passes with the 6 idle-timeout steps PASS, not SKIP (first, after the deploy, save sda's timeout once on the Storage page or with api.py PUT, which turns its automatic offline data collection off and records it: until then the check SKIPs, since sda has UNOS's 20 minutes with the collection on, unrecorded), its wait step saying after how many seconds sda slept for its timeout of 300 s; (2) scripts/dev/api.py PUT /storage/disks/sda/spindown with {"minutes": 20}, then over ssh cat /etc/udev/rules.d/90-unos-disk-spindown.rules shows the line of sda's serial with -S 240, and udevadm test /sys/block/sda (a dry run) lists that line's RUN of /sbin/hdparm -S 240 for sda, which shows the rule matches the disk; (3) reboot (the owner), then GET /storage/disks shows sda's spindown 20 and, after 21 minutes without access, its power_state standby, which shows that udev applied the rule at boot; (4) GET /health/disks then answers sda STANDBY, and GET /storage/disks still says standby; (5) PUT {"minutes": 0} removes the file again, and its SD MiB are measured with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure; (6) with sda asleep, open the Storage page once, note sda's Power cell (Standby: it was read before the page's lists), and read GET /storage/disks a minute later: sda's power_state says whether the page's pool and import lists (btrfs filesystem show, which probes every block device) woke the disk of the mounted pool; record both in the PROGRESS.md log; (7) first record over ssh systemctl is-active smartmontools (read-only; the dev device was set up by hand, so smartd is as its installation left it); while it answers active, the owner turns smartd off as install.sh's stop_smartd does (systemctl disable --now smartmontools, a host-level change), since its reads every 30 minutes keep sda awake and the step would show nothing of UNOS's own checks: the step does not pass while smartd runs; then give sda 1 hour, leave it unused for 2.5 hours (the SMART monitor and the trash checks run hourly) and read GET /storage/disks: power_state standby shows that no periodic check of UNOS kept it awake; record smartd's state before the step, whether the owner turned it off, and the result in the PROGRESS.md log. Open: a disk plugged in again (USB) is the owner's to try; install.sh's stop_smartd is a host-level change that has not run on the dev device (install.sh has not run there at all, ADR-0376; smartd is off there since 2026-11-16, as stop_smartd leaves it, which step 7 records); the pages that list the pools (the dashboard, Storage, Shares, Snapshots, System > Scheduler) still read every disk when an administrator opens them (ADR-0378). Added on 2026-11-16 (ADR-0378): after a reboot sda stayed active for hours with -S 240 (UNOS's rule), -S 180 and even -S 120, with no read or write counted and no disk tool running on the host, while smartctl -c said its automatic offline data collection was on (status 0x84, suspended by an interrupting command from host; capabilities 0x7b; /etc/smartd.conf without -o on); after smartctl -o off and -S 120 it slept after 661 s, and the lead then restored it (smartctl -o on, hdparm -S 240). So a Save with a timeout, after hdparm -S, reads the disk's own automatic offline data collection (smartctl -n standby -i -c -j in the container, at most 30 s, ADR-0290; -i's smart_support marks an ATA disk without SMART or with SMART off, which runs none) and turns it off when it is on (smartctl -n standby -o off -i -c -j, whose JSON must show it off; one without a clear answer, killed or with no state read after it, is recorded all the same, since the drive may have taken it), recorded by a comment line of UNOS's udev rule after the disk's line; another timeout keeps the record, and Off turns it on again (-o on) only for a recorded disk; one off already, or without it (no switch; NVMe, SCSI/SAS), is left as it is and not recorded; a failure leaves the timeout set, logs it and answers a warning that the Storage page shows above the disks, and a rule that cannot be written puts it back as the old rule records it (on again for a record the change added, off again for one it removed) (test_disk_spindown.py, storage.spec.ts; the dialog says so in both languages, and that a scheduled scrub reads the pool instead: UNOS schedules no long SMART test yet, the Scheduler's SMART tests are short). scripts/dev/scenario.sh smart reads it first (smartctl -i -c -j through docker exec in the supervisor's container; fails when the rule records it off but it is on), proves it off and recorded after the Save, names it as the cause when the disk stays awake with no I/O, and leaves it as found, which its clean-up checks once more, naming what it left and the way back; a restore whose answer has a warning fails (test_dev_scenarios.py). Not confirmed: whether a drive keeps it off across a power cycle (the command is SFF-8035i's, which ATA/ACS was not found to define): sda kept it off across the dev device's reboots of 14:03 and 14:42 UTC on 2026-11-16 (read after the first boot, and the smart check's first step after the second), which need not have cut the drive's power; a power cycle of the drive itself was not measured. Added on 2026-11-16 (ADR-0378): deploy/uninstall.sh (remove_disk_idle_timeouts, right after the containers and the unos service stopped and before remove_files removes /opt/unos, where the script is), with the host's tools under timeout, runs hdparm -S 0 on each disk that a line of UNOS's rule names and smartctl -o on -c on each disk that a record names (the supervisor's container, whose smartctl UNOS used, is gone; -c reads the scans back, and only "Auto Offline Data Collection: Enabled." counts), then removes the rule and runs udevadm control --reload where udevadm exists, so a run stopped on the way finds the rule whole again; a disk whose scans stay off keeps its record: the rule is replaced by comments and those records, which udev ignores and read_rule takes as records without a timeout (a new installation's Off, or another run, turns them on where SMART is on on the disk), or removed all the same when that write fails; only the lines that read_rule takes as UNOS's count, read as udev reads a rules file without NUL bytes, which UNOS never writes (a line ends at \n or \r, only spaces and tabs around it; read_rule now reads it so too, with ASCII digits), compared with read_rule by a test in the C and a UTF-8 locale; the file is never run, a disk is found by its serial with lsblk -dnr -o NAME,TYPE,SERIAL and no other disk is touched; a rule that cannot be read, or holds a NUL byte (which bash would drop), stays; nothing stops the uninstallation, whose end names, with the exact command, what it could not undo (no hdparm or smartctl, a disk not attached or not alone with its serial, lsblk or a command that failed or did not answer, smartctl not showing the scans on), the rule left with records, and the lines edited by hand, for which nothing ran and which go with the rule, and says that the disks whose timeout it turned off have no standby timer until they restart (or until the boot that applies a rule it could not remove); confirm_uninstall lists it (test_deploy_scripts.py, test_disk_spindown.py). After a third review: smartctl's answer goes to a temporary file of mktemp, read once timeout has returned and removed, so that a smartctl that the kernel keeps past the KILL holds no pipe and the script goes on after 35 s per command at most (mktemp failing is named); the step runs before remove_files, so that a run stopped in it can run again; the script adds /usr/sbin, /usr/bin, /sbin and /bin after the PATH it was given (su without a dash keeps a user's PATH); a Ctrl-C or TERM while the disks are undone ends the uninstallation once the command running has ended (timeout keeps Ctrl-C from it, and bash went on), with the rule whole and the advice to run it again (exit 130 or 143); bash's Killed line is not shown; a temporary records file left by a killed run (the rule's name, then .unos-tmp. and a pid) is removed at the step's start, no file of another name; a disk with SMART off gets the command smartctl -s on -o on, which the script does not run; the records-only rule is 0644 also under umask 077 (test_deploy_scripts.py). After a fourth review: hdparm and smartctl get /dev/null as standard input and write their output and errors to the files of a temporary folder of mktemp -d, removed after the command (mktemp failing is named for both), so that one the kernel keeps past the KILL holds none of the script's files and a reader of its output (2>&1 | tee, ssh without a terminal) waits no longer; their errors are shown once they have ended; a HUP stops the step as Ctrl-C does (129), leaving no temporary folder, but after a dropped SSH session the next write to the closed terminal fails first, and set -e ends the script there with status 1, the rule whole as well (1040834); a run whose data volume is gone (a second run after a stop) makes no backup, which would be an empty archive; the end texts no longer say that a new installation's Off turns on the scans of a disk with SMART off (test_deploy_scripts.py). Not run on a host: only the stub tests of TestUninstallScript in test_deploy_scripts.py show it. Device check on 2026-11-16 (sda the pool's WD6400AACS, kernel 6.1.172; the SD MiB of each step in PROGRESS.md's Log): scripts/dev/scenario.sh smart failed its standby step on the first deployed tree, 57be517, in the run of 01:05 UTC (sda active after 990 s with 0 reads and 0 writes; the power read was smartctl -n standby -i then, and smartd ran), passed with 12 steps on 434d410 in the run of 06:54 UTC, and with 14 steps, those of the automatic offline data collection among them, on 5d79302 in the run of 13:42 UTC (after a Save of sda's 20 minutes had turned the collection off and recorded it), after the reboot of 14:42 UTC in the run of 14:45 UTC, and on the final tree cc9482e in the run of 19:21 UTC (the collection on, as found). Steps by hand: (1) as just said; (2) passed at 01:35 UTC: the rule's line of sda's serial with -S 240, and udevadm test listed RUN /sbin/hdparm -S 240 /dev/sda; (3) and (4) failed after the reboot of 07:17 UTC: sda still active after 22 minutes (the step read no I/O counts; from 07:44 to 08:13 UTC the kernel's counts since the boot stayed at 182 reads and 22 writes), which the measurements above traced to its automatic offline data collection, and passed after the reboot of 14:03 UTC, before which sda's own timer was turned off (hdparm -S 0) so that only the rule could set it: GET /storage/disks said spindown 20, the collection was still off and recorded, sda went to standby 1201 s after its last read or write (hdparm -C a minute apart), GET /storage/disks said standby, GET /health/disks STANDBY, and sda was still asleep after that read; (5) PUT {"minutes": 0} at 17:48 UTC removed the rule (0.309 MiB on the SD card) and turned the collection on again (on at 19:21 UTC); (7) smartmontools answered inactive and disabled (it was active and enabled at 01:04 UTC and was turned off during that night's timer measurements on sda; the step's systemctl disable --now changed nothing), sda got 1 hour at 15:17:52 UTC and was in standby at the step's one read at 17:47:55 UTC: nothing restarted its timer in the hour before that read, so no hourly check of UNOS (the SMART monitor, the trash checks) kept it awake, as the step asks; one read does not show that nothing woke it earlier in the 2.5 hours. Not run: (6), a look at the Storage page in a browser, which only the owner can do; it records whether the page's pool lists wake a sleeping disk, the matter that Open names and ADR-0378 accepts, and expects no result, so it is no condition of the entry's steps: step 3's SMART reads passed through the API, and the Storage page itself is the E2E specs' (storage.spec.ts), as the feature-pass skill's row of this entry says. The reboot checks ran on 5d79302; the final tree differs from it at runtime in read_rule's reading of lines that UNOS does not write (it reads the lines that UNOS writes as before, and udev, not read_rule, applies the rule at boot), the balance card's texts and deploy/uninstall.sh (no step of this entry), and passed scenario.sh smart after its deploy, without another reboot: the pass rests on the reboot checks of 5d79302. Passes since 2026-11-16: each step is asserted by the tests of verified_by (test_storage.py added: the SMART monitor's read of a disk in standby, smartctl -n standby, leaves it asleep and takes no snapshot; test_files_security.py: the trash expiry's checks of the pools that are due) and passed on the device before and after a reboot (ADR-0018). Added on 2026-11-17 (ADR-0394): with Immich, transmission and other apps on the pool the dev device's sda rarely sleeps, and scenario.sh all after the seventh batch's reboot failed only the wait step (active after 1980 s, 13 reads and 649 writes); the check now reads, before the wait and after each round, the disk's reads and writes and each running container's on it from its cgroup's io.stat (cgroup v2, through docker ps and inspect under timeout; also once more after the last power read), and a disk that the Storage page shows active after the wait is a SKIP that names them when, in the wait's last two rounds (660 s, longer than sda needs unused to sleep), the kernel counted reads or writes on it and containers other than UNOS's own (unos-*) did too, and UNOS's own did not; so is the next step, the SMART reads of the sleeping disk, and those reads are a SKIP when they find the disk awake after such a container used it; the step fails as before for a state other than active, no read or write in those 660 s (with the apps' use in the 660 s before named, after which a pass of the SMART monitor restarts the timer once), UNOS's own containers' use, reads or writes with no app's container counting any, counts that cannot be read, and any other failure of the SMART reads (test_dev_scenarios.py).

features.description: Storage shows how much of its quota each volume uses, and alerts at set levels
steps: The Volumes dialog shows each volume's use against its quota
Crossing 80, 90 or 95 percent sends an alert
A graph shows the use over time
features.notes: Built 2026-11-17 on the workstation (ADR-0387): GET /storage/pools/{pool}/volumes adds used, quota and usage (counted, inconsistent, quotas_off, unknown) from the kernel's quota groups in sysfs (/sys/fs/btrfs/<fsid>/qgroups/0_<id>: referenced, max_referenced, limit_flags; qgroups/inconsistent), and the Volumes dialog shows a bar and the use against the quota, the use alone without one, and the notes for quotas off (btrfs quota enable) and counts that need a rescan; each pass of the RAID monitor (5 minutes) reads the volumes of the mounted pools with quotas on, listing them again only after /sys/fs/btrfs/<fsid>/generation changed (and once more at the next pass), and reports a volume at 80, 90 or 95% of its quota as the problem volume_quota:<pool>/<id> (kinds volume_quota_80/90/95, an error at 95), alerted once per level crossed upward (Problem.stage) and left 5 points below a level, inconsistent counts changing nothing; one point per volume per hour for 30 days in RAM, with each volume's stage, written to /data/volume_usage.json only at shutdown, drawn by the dialog's Use over time (GET /storage/pools/{pool}/volumes/{name}/usage); the quota group 0/<id> that Linux 6.1 keeps after a volume's Delete is destroyed by the monitor once two of its lists found it without its subvolume and it counts nothing (ADR-0387). Tested on the workstation: test_volume_usage.py (sysfs and the FakeHost: the list, the levels, renames and deletes, the reads without commands, the history and its file), test_alert_events.py (the stage), volume-usage.spec.ts and the view of mobile-layout.spec.ts on route fakes; scripts/dev/scenario.sh volumes checks the list's use and the use over time of its volume with a quota of 1 GiB, or that the list says quotas are off. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), on the pool data, whose quotas were off on 2026-11-07. 1) With quotas off, scenario.sh volumes passes and its quota step says that the list says so. 2) The owner enables quotas (btrfs quota enable /mnt/pools/data on the host, then btrfs quota rescan -w /mnt/pools/data); /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>/qgroups/inconsistent reads 0 and /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>/generation a number (kernel 6.1.172); scenario.sh volumes passes with the volume made with a limit of 1 GiB and listed with its use against it. 3) By hand: a volume unoscheck<6 hex digits> with a quota of 104857600 bytes (POST /storage/pools/data/volumes), filled on the pool (not the SD card) with dd if=/dev/urandom bs=1M conv=fsync to 84, then 92, then 97 MiB, each followed by a wait for the next pass (at most 5 minutes and 30 seconds) inside scripts/dev/sd.sh measure: one alert each in the notification history (has used 84%, then 92%, then 97% of its quota, the last an error) and the banner's volume_quota_80, _90 and _95, the dialog's bar and its Use over time; files deleted down to 50 MiB: the problem goes at the next pass and nothing is sent; the SD MiB of each wait no more than the idle background. 4) Reboot check: with the volume kept at 50 MiB for one pass (one point), the owner's reboot; the supervisor's stop wrote /data/volume_usage.json, and afterwards GET /storage/pools/data/volumes/unoscheck<hex>/usage still lists the point from before the reboot. 5) Clean-up: DELETE the volume; at most two passes after btrfs dropped it, btrfs qgroup show /mnt/pools/data lists no 0/<its id>; the owner decides whether quotas go off again (btrfs quota disable /mnt/pools/data). Report the SD MiB of each step. Device check 2026-11-17 (the tree of mvp.batch-7 at 7cca7e9, deployed on 2026-11-17 at 12:48 UTC; a reboot from the API at 13:31:12 UTC (the boot of 13:32:28, both UNOS containers healthy by 13:33:21)), quotas off on the pool data at the start: (1) a volume without a quota listed as quotas_off, its usage endpoint too, and a create with a quota refused with 409 (0.039 MiB); (2) btrfs quota enable and btrfs quota rescan -w on /mnt/pools/data: qgroups/inconsistent 0, generation a number (0.000); scenario.sh volumes passed its 11 steps with the volume of 1 GiB listed against its quota (0.965); (3) a volume with a quota of 104857600 bytes filled with dd on the pool to 84, 92 and 97 MiB: after one pass each, one alert, volume_quota_80 and volume_quota_90 warnings and volume_quota_95 an error, in the banner's problems and the notification history, the list at 84.0, 92.0 and 97.0% (the waits 0.141, 0.535 and 0.148 MiB, the idle background); the 80% alert failed to reach Telegram (a ConnectTimeout of the device's network, recorded as failed), the others were sent; then a fresh file of 50 MiB in place of the fills (a truncate leaves btrfs's referenced bytes as they were): the problem went at the next pass and nothing was sent; (4) after the reboot /data/volume_usage.json was there, written at the stop (13:32:12, 306 B), and the usage endpoint listed the point from before the reboot. (5) failed: the DELETE left the volume's quota group, since Linux 6.1.172 refused btrfs qgroup destroy as busy right after every delete (the scenario runs had left 14 stale groups, 0/265 with the 1 GiB limit); it was destroyed by hand once btrfs subvolume sync and btrfs filesystem sync had run, and quotas were turned off. Fixed on the branch (68c5724, 9ecd228, b17889f, each reviewed in a fresh context; ADR-0387): the Delete leaves the group, and the monitor destroys a group that two lists in a row of one quota tree found without its subvolume once sysfs reads 0 for its counts. Re-checked with quotas on: 73f547a (the first version, which destroyed at the first list) destroyed a deleted volume's group 0/278 and the four groups that scenario.sh volumes left (0/279 to 0/282) at the next pass (0.387 and 0.070 MiB); 9ecd228 at 15:02 to 15:31 UTC: a deleted volume's group 0/283 read 0 and was still listed after the first pass, gone after the second (0.387), the groups that scenario.sh volumes (0.984) left, 0/284 to 0/287, gone after the second pass (0.117), a volume deleted right before a reboot from the API (15:22:55, the boot of 15:24:14) lost its group 0/288 by the second list after the start (0.184), no warning about quota groups in the supervisor's log, quotas off again and check.sh OK; b17889f, deployed at 15:31 to 15:32 UTC, at 15:32 to 15:43 UTC: quotas enabled again (0.266), a volume deleted, whose subvolume id 257 btrfs had given out again after the reboot (the highest live subvolume is 256), kept its group 0/257, reading 0, after the first pass and lost it at the second (0.234), no warning in the log; quotas off again (0.000), check.sh OK and deploy.sh status equal.

features.description: An administrator adds a disk to a pool or removes one, after typed confirmations
steps: Add a free disk to a pool: the pool grows, and its profile is kept
Remove a disk: its data moves to the other disks first, and a removal the profile cannot survive is refused
features.notes: Built 2026-11-18 (ADR-0411; host-level, so the device check and the reboot check of ADR-0018 apply). GET /api/v1/storage/pools/<name>/devices answers a mounted pool's disks (btrfs filesystem show --raw on the host under timeout --signal=KILL 60, since the container's /dev has only the disks of its start: devid, path, size, bytes allocated; model and serial from lsblk), each with why it cannot leave, its profiles (btrfs filesystem df -b, in the container) and the whole disks that can join it (disks.addable_problem: never a boot or virtual device, the system disk, one in use, mounted, swap, held by md, LVM or LUKS, or one with any btrfs filesystem, also another pool's that is not mounted or one only wipefs sees; a sleeping disk is not woken and has unknown contents). Step 1: POST .../devices with device (a whole disk, 400 for a partition), confirm_device (the path typed again, 400 otherwise), identity (path, serial, WWN, size, always, 422 without; 409 when the path now holds another disk), force (needed for data, which -f then erases) and contents (what the list showed: 409 when a disk with data now holds something else, as a sleeping disk listed with unknown contents) runs btrfs device add [--nodiscard for a pool without TRIM] <device> <mountpoint> on the host under pools._lock and pools.maintenance_lock; no conversion and no balance: the pool grows and keeps its profile; an NVMe drive on a SoC of NVME_NO_TRIM_SOCS joins no pool with TRIM (ADR-0370); audited as pool_disk_added before the pool is read for the answer, a btrfs that fails as failed (500). Step 2: POST .../removal with devid, device (still the devid's, 409 otherwise) and confirm_device runs btrfs device remove <devid> <mountpoint> in the transient unit unos-disk-remove-<pool> (systemd-run --collect --service-type=exec, RequiresMountsFor, TimeoutStopSec=10min, ExecStartPre truncate and echo of the devid, path and bytes allocated into /run/unos-disk-remove-<pool>.log), which survives a restart of the supervisor; refused with 409 and nothing run: the only disk, a profile other than single, dup, raid0, raid1, raid1c3, raid1c4, raid10, fewer disks left than the profiles in use need (raid1 with two disks), and too little space (devices.removal_problem, an estimate on the safe side: the bytes allocated on all disks plus 1 GiB per disk left must fit on the disks left for every profile in use, with each profile's chunks spread in equal shares over its width, raid0 and raid10 over every disk left (devices.raw_capacity), and the first chunk moved needs 1 GiB unallocated on as many disks left as the profile asks of a kernel before 5.15). GET .../removal: running while a disk has the size 0 (the kernel's btrfs_shrink_device), with the bytes left and those at the start from the log, else idle with finished or failed (btrfs's ERROR lines); the events socket sends {"type": "disk_removals"} while one runs; audited as pool_disk_removal_started. Both are refused (409) on a pool that is not mounted, is read-only or misses a disk, and while a scrub runs, a balance runs or is paused, or a removal runs; a balance's start and resume are refused while a removal runs (test_balance.py). Left as decided in ADR-0411: a scrub through the API or the Scheduler is not refused beside a removal (the kernel allows it; the card offers none), a removal cannot be cancelled from UNOS, a removal can still run out of space on its way in an uneven layout (btrfs keeps the disk with its data, and the card says it failed), and a removal stopped without an ERROR line of btrfs (systemctl stop, an OOM kill) shows no result. Review (fresh context, 2026-11-18): fixed the container's btrfs filesystem show, which does not see a disk attached after the supervisor started (now on the host), a space check that let raid10 on unequal disks and a raid1 pool right after an add pass, the audit of an add whose pool could not be read afterwards, a partition beside a mounted one accepted by the API, a sleeping disk's contents erased unseen, the erase checkbox kept between disks, and a removal that ends at once leaving the card stale. Tests: test_pool_disks.py (TestTheDisksOfAPool, TestAdd with the sleeping disk's contents, the partition and the audit before the read, TestWhatTheDisksLeftMustHold with raid10 on unequal disks and the first chunk's room, TestRemoval, TestRemovalsForTheEventsSocket), test_balance.py (test_a_balance_is_refused_while_a_disk_of_the_pool_is_removed), test_ws_auth.py (TestTheDiskRemovalsOnTheEventsSocket), storage.spec.ts 'Pool disks (fake data)' (the dev device's pool with its only disk that cannot leave and nothing to add, the typed path and the erase checkbox before Add Disk, a refusal kept in the dialog, a removal followed over the events socket until it ends with Add Disk, Remove Disk, Scrub and Balance disabled meanwhile, a running removal after a reload and a failed one, no add or removal beside a scrub, a paused balance or on a read-only pool), mobile-layout.spec.ts (the card's removal and both dialogs at 375 px in both languages). Device check by hand, touching no data (the dev device has one pool disk, sda of the pool data, and no spare disk), each step with its SD MiB (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure), after the deploy and again after a reboot: (1) scripts/dev/api.py GET /storage/pools/data/devices answers members [devid 1, /dev/sda, problem '/dev/sda is the only disk of the pool'], the profiles of btrfs filesystem df, candidates [] and removal idle without a result; (2) echo '{"devid": 1, "device": "/dev/sda", "confirm_device": "/dev/sda"}' | scripts/dev/api.py POST /storage/pools/data/removal - answers 409 'Refusing to remove /dev/sda: /dev/sda is the only disk of the pool', and scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'systemctl is-active unos-disk-remove-data; test -e /run/unos-disk-remove-data.log; echo $?' answers inactive and 1; (3) a POST /storage/pools/data/devices of /dev/sda (device and confirm_device /dev/sda, identity with the serial, WWN and size that GET /storage/disks lists for it) answers 409 '/dev/sda is a disk of the pool data already', and one of /dev/sdz with the same identity 400 '/dev/sdz is not a disk or partition on this system'; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'btrfs filesystem show /mnt/pools/data' still lists sda alone; (4) scripts/dev/api.py GET /audit/logs --param limit=20 has no pool_disk_added or pool_disk_removal_started entry; (5) on the Storage page of the device in a browser (the owner's: the agents do not sign in there), the card of data: Add Disk says No disk can be added, and Remove Disk lists /dev/sda as Cannot be removed with that reason, its Remove Disk disabled. Open: an add and a removal that move data on real disks (a spare disk, or the BPI-F3's SATA disks), a removal across a restart of the supervisor and across a shutdown of the host, and step (5): passes stays false until they ran. Device check of e5d531a on 2026-11-18, refusals only, before and after a reboot (0.027 SD MiB a run): the pool data lists its only disk /dev/sda as not removable with no candidates; its removal answers 409 (only disk) with the unit inactive and no log file; an add of its own disk answers 409 and of /dev/sdz 400; btrfs lists one device and nothing is audited. An add and a removal that move data wait for a spare disk, which the dev device lacks; the card's dialogs in a browser are the owner's. 2026-11-19: ADR-0429 (storage.nvme-trim-on-k1) removed the refusal of an NVMe drive on a SoC of NVME_NO_TRIM_SOCS and the --nodiscard of btrfs device add for a pool without TRIM: every disk is added with TRIM.

features.description: An administrator balances a pool and follows, pauses, resumes or cancels the balance
steps: Start a balance: the pool shows its progress and the estimated time left
Pause, resume and cancel act on the running balance
features.notes: Built 2026-11-15 (ADR-0379; host-level, so the device check and the reboot check of ADR-0018 apply: run on 2026-11-16, all but the Storage page's parts, at the end). POST /api/v1/storage/pools/<name>/balance takes {"usage": 1..99} (default 20: btrfs balance start -dusage=N -musage=N) or {"full": true} (--full-balance); supervisor/src/storage/balances.py runs start and resume on the host in the transient systemd unit unos-balance-<pool> (systemd-run --collect --service-type=exec, output appended to /run/unos-balance-<pool>.log after ExecStartPre emptied it), so that a restart of the supervisor's container, which kills its processes and with them a balance they run, neither stops nor hides it; the unit has RequiresMountsFor=<mountpoint> and ExecStop=-btrfs balance pause <mountpoint> with TimeoutStopSec=10min, so that a shutdown of the host pauses the balance, which the kernel resumes at the next mount, where systemd's SIGTERM would cancel it and delete it from the disk; status, pause and cancel are btrfs in the container (ADR-0290), a pause or cancel waiting 10 s for the chunk being moved (then pausing or cancelling). Refused with 409 and no btrfs: a pool not mounted as btrfs at its mountpoint, a read-only one, a running scrub, a balance that runs or is paused (one per pool), a resume of one that is not paused, a cancel while a pause waits for the chunk being moved and a pause while a cancel waits (the kernel pauses a balance with both requested, and both return 0: Linux 6.1.150 and later), a cancel of a paused balance of a read-only pool (EROFS); a pause or cancel asked again while the first waits answers the status, and a cancel that a pause from elsewhere beat answers paused, both without an audit entry; pools.scrub_start refuses a scrub, also a scheduled one, while a balance runs. The events socket sends {"type": "balances"} while one runs (webui.no-http-polling); the estimate comes from the chunks balanced since UNOS first saw it run. Audited: balance_started, balance_paused, balance_resumed, balance_cancelled. Step 1: test_balance.py TestStart (the unit's exact command, the filters, 422 for a limit outside 1..99 or with full, every 409, btrfs's refusal as 500, a balance with nothing to move, one the kernel does not report yet), TestStatus (btrfs-progs 6's status lines, the last result from the unit's output, in which a pause wins over a cancel printed with it and ExecStop's 'Not running' is no error), TestTheTimeLeft, TestBalancesForTheEventsSocket (also a balance that runs in the kernel, found by the first read of a supervisor that restarted); test_ws_auth.py TestTheBalancesOnTheEventsSocket; storage.spec.ts 'Balance (fake data)': the dialog's default of 20%, the progress bar 'Balance progress' with 'N of about M chunks balanced' and 'About N min left' from the events socket without a read, the result, a full balance only after its checkbox, a refusal kept in the dialog, a failed balance's error, no Balance on a read-only pool or beside a scrub, a read again after the socket connects again; mobile-layout.spec.ts (the card and the dialog at 375 px). Step 2: TestPauseResumeCancel (also a pause or cancel with nothing to stop, which btrfs-progs refuses with exit status 2 and 'Not running' for a pause, 'Not in progress' for a cancel: the status, no audit entry; a cancel while a pause waits and a pause while a cancel waits refused, a request asked again, a cancel that a pause from elsewhere beats, with FakeKernel following the kernel's pause-wins rule; a paused balance of a read-only pool) and the specs 'pause, resume and cancel act on the running balance', 'a pause that waits for the chunk being moved says so...' (Cancel Balance disabled while pausing) and 'a paused balance resumes only without a scrub, and is cancelled only on a writable pool'; a scrub refused while a balance runs: test_balance.py TestScrubAndBalance, test_scheduler_validation.py test_a_scheduled_scrub_fails_while_a_balance_of_its_pool_runs. Device check: scripts/dev/scenario.sh balance on the pool data (the HDD sda of the BPI-W3): a folder of the pool with 96 files of 128 MiB made with fallocate, every 8th kept (12 data chunks about 12% full, 1.5 GiB moved on the HDD, on the SD card only the empty folder of the 409 below /mnt/pools), Start Balance with 20% answered running and the unit active, a scrub and a second balance refused with 409, the chunks balanced with the time left, Pause (paused, the unit ended), Resume (the unit active again), Cancel (cancelled), the folder removed, the pool's last balance result the check's (cancelled) until the host restarts; test_dev_scenarios.py runs it on the fake NAS and shows that it fails for a balance of an unmounted folder that is not refused, a start that answers idle, btrfs outside the unit, a scrub beside the balance, no time left, and a pause, a resume outside the unit or a cancel that does not act, and that its clean-up waits for a pause that outlasts its step before it cancels. By hand, after scenario.sh balance and again after a reboot: (1) on the Storage page of the device, Balance of data with Every chunk and its checkbox: the card shows Balance in progress, the progress bar and the time left moving without a reload, Pause Balance shows Pausing after the chunk being moved with Cancel Balance disabled, then Balance paused with the note that a mount resumes it and that a paused full balance goes on only through the chunks less than 90% full, Resume Balance runs it again (the kernel log says 'balance: resume -dusage=90 -musage=90 -susage=90'), and once it ends the card says Last balance: finished with the chunks it rewrote; (2) start a full balance of data again and, while it runs, restart the supervisor (docker restart unos-supervisor): scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'systemctl is-active unos-balance-data' stays active, and once the API is healthy scripts/dev/api.py GET /storage/pools/data/balance answers running with its chunks, and the reloaded page shows it; (3) Cancel Balance: the card says Last balance: cancelled before it finished, and the audit log lists Balance started, Balance paused, Balance resumed, Balance started and Balance cancelled for pool data; (4) after the reboot (ADR-0018), GET /storage/pools/data/balance answers idle without a result (/run is gone) and no unit unos-balance-data is loaded (systemctl is-active answers inactive); (5) start a full balance of data again and, while it runs, System, Restart: after the boot the kernel log says 'balance: resume -dusage=90 -musage=90 -susage=90' (the unit's ExecStop paused it, and the kernel resumed it when data was mounted), no unit unos-balance-data is loaded, and GET /storage/pools/data/balance answers running while it goes on (Cancel Balance then ends it) and idle without a result once it has ended. Each step with its SD MiB (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure). Measured on the dev device on 2026-11-16 (kernel 6.1.172): a full balance of data started from UNOS (kernel log 'balance: start -d -m -s'), paused by the unit's ExecStop at a reboot ('balance: paused'), was resumed at the next mount as 'balance: resume -dusage=90 -musage=90 -susage=90' and ended a minute later after 4 block groups: on every resume (the kernel's at a mount and btrfs balance resume's, which Resume Balance sends) btrfs_balance() calls update_balance_args() (Linux 6.1 fs/btrfs/volumes.c), which gives each chunk type without a usage or usage-range filter that is not being converted usage=90, so a paused or interrupted full balance goes on only through the chunks less than 90% full; a balance with UNOS's usage limit (1 to 99) keeps its own. No behaviour change: the card's note of a paused balance and the full balance's warning, en and ru, docs/USER_GUIDE.md, ADR-0379 (edited in place, not merged yet) and CHANGELOG.md say so, with the way to rewrite every chunk again: cancel it and start a new full balance; storage.spec.ts 'pause, resume and cancel act on the running balance' and 'a full balance starts only once it is confirmed...' assert the two texts, and the by-hand steps (1), (2), (3) and (5) expect a resumed full balance with usage=90. Device check on 2026-11-16 (the SD MiB of each step in PROGRESS.md's Log): scripts/dev/scenario.sh balance passed its 11 steps in scenario.sh all from 01:05 UTC, after the reboot of 14:42 UTC in scenario.sh all from 14:45 UTC, and on the final tree cc9482e in the run of 19:21 UTC. Steps by hand, through the API and before the 90% finding, so (3) acted on the full balance of (2): (2) at 01:35 UTC a full balance of data kept running across docker restart unos-supervisor: the unit active, GET running with its chunks; (3) Pause (paused, the unit ended), Resume (running) and Cancel (idle, cancelled), and the audit log's newest balance entries balance_cancelled, balance_resumed, balance_paused and balance_started; (4) after the reboots of 07:17 and 14:03 UTC GET answered idle without a result and no unit unos-balance-data was loaded; (5) failed twice, then passed: after the reboot of 07:17 UTC the full balance (5 chunks, 2 balanced a minute before the reboot) was idle; after that of 14:03 UTC, with 20 GiB of zeros written into the pool first, it was idle too: the kernel log says that it ended at 14:04:32 UTC, about a minute after the boot (the device cycle's log kept no earlier kernel line of that boot), as the kernel's resume with usage=90, which passes over full chunks, ends it (the finding above; the reboot of 14:42 UTC showed that resume line); after that of 14:42 UTC, with 256 MiB files of which every second was removed (chunks about half full), the kernel log said balance: paused before the reboot and balance: resume -dusage=90 -musage=90 -susage=90 at the mount, no unit was loaded, GET answered running at 6 of about 31 chunks, and Cancel ended it (balance: canceled, and btrfs balance status found none); the fills were removed. Open: step (1) and the page's parts of (2) and (3) (the reloaded page, the card's Last balance) on the Storage page of the device in a browser, which only the owner can do (the agents do not sign in there as its administrator): passes stays false until then.

features.description: A disk attached after the supervisor started appears on the Storage page
steps: Attach a USB disk while UNOS runs: Storage lists it within a minute, without a restart
features.notes: Built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0360). Cause: GET /api/v1/storage/disks already ran lsblk at every request in the host's namespaces, which see the host's /dev, /sys and udev database (test_disk_safety.py TestDisksEndpoint test_a_disk_attached_or_removed_after_a_request_is_in_the_next_answer passed on the code before the change); the Storage page asked for its lists only when it opened and when Create Pool opened. The page now loads its lists again when the block devices that the stats stream /ws/v1/events names (disk_io.disks, from /proc/diskstats) changed and stayed the same for one message, not while a dialog is open but once it closes. Tests first: the two specs of storage.spec.ts Physical disks (a disk attached while the page is open is listed without a reload and a removed one goes; while a dialog is open the lists stay, and are loaded once it closes) failed on the page before the change, the attached disk never listed. Left: the device check, attaching a spare USB disk with the Storage page open, needs a spare disk (an owner action). SMART of a disk attached after the supervisor started still fails, since smartctl runs in the container whose /dev lacks the new node (ADR-0360 Consequences): storage.hot-plugged-disks-smart. Device check 2026-11-12 (before and after the reboot from the API at 14:45:53 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 14:46:49; both containers healthy by 14:47:40)): scenario.sh files and smb OK on the tree with the change; attaching a disk needs a spare one, an owner action.

features.description: The SMART data of a disk attached after the supervisor started can be read without a restart
steps: Attach a USB disk while UNOS runs: System > Disk Health shows its SMART data, runs its self-tests and the SMART monitor records it, without a restart of the supervisor
features.notes: Built 2026-11-18 (ADR-0414; host-level, so the device check and the reboot check of ADR-0018 apply). Cause (ADR-0360 Consequences): smartctl runs in the supervisor's container, whose /dev Docker fills once, when the container starts, so the node of a disk attached later was missing there: its SMART data, its self-tests and its snapshots of the SMART monitor failed with No such device until the supervisor restarted, while lsblk on the host listed it. Decision (ADR-0414): every smartctl goes through host.run_smartctl, which first makes the container's /dev/<disk> the host's whole disk from /sys/block/<disk>/dev (host.container_disk_node): a node with the host's number is left alone (no write, no log), a missing one is made and one with another number replaced (a block node, mode 0600, mknod under .<disk>.unos-new and renamed into place, in the container's /dev, a tmpfs), one INFO line per change, and never into a /dev on the filesystem of the host's /dev (/proc/1/root/dev, pid: host: a bind mount, or a supervisor on the host); a name of which the host has no whole disk gets no node and no smartctl (host.NoHostDisk: 400 with its text on Disk Health's endpoints); another OSError (a refused mknod) is host.DiskNodeError, which fails the read with its reason (500) and is logged once per disk. Nothing changes with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local, for another path and without /sys/block. run_in_container is unchanged (ADR-0290: a smartctl stuck in the kernel holds no worker thread, one run of a command at a time), and reading sysfs and making an inode send the disk nothing (ADR-0378: a sleeping disk stays asleep). No change to deploy/docker-compose.yml or to the container's privileges; considered and refused in the ADR: the host's /dev bind-mounted into the container (it would share the host's /dev/shm, /dev/pts and /dev/mqueue), smartctl on the host (the host's timeout cannot end one stuck in the kernel, so ADR-0290's bounds would need ADR-0378's pgrep machinery per command), a udev rule on the host. Tests: supervisor/tests/test_hot_plugged_smart.py (with FakeHost's container /dev: attach_disk, detach_disk, container_dev, nodes_made of test_pool_persistence.py). The web UI is unchanged: System > Disk Health lists the disk with its SMART data at its next load (opened, or its refresh button), which webui/tests/health.spec.ts shows for listed disks on route fakes; the stand-in has no smartctl. Device check (by hand, the device-checks skill, each command under scripts/dev/sd.sh measure <label> -- ...; after the owner's deploy of the supervisor, which changes no requirement, and again after the owner's reboot): the dev device's only data disk is sda, there at the start, so these steps show that it works as before and keeps Docker's node. (1) scripts/dev/ssh.sh docker exec unos-supervisor stat -c '%F %t:%T %a %G' /dev/sda prints block special file 8:0 660 disk (Docker's node; one of UNOS's would be 600 root). (2) scripts/dev/api.py GET /health/disk/sda: device /dev/sda, its serial and health_status PASSED (STANDBY when it sleeps, which leaves it asleep); scripts/dev/api.py GET /storage/disks/sda/smart answers its data (power_state standby with healthy null when it sleeps). (3) scripts/dev/api.py POST '/health/disk/sda/test?test_type=short' answers {"status": "started", "message": "Short test started on /dev/sda"} (it wakes the disk, as asked); after 3 minutes GET /health/disk/sda shows the test in self_test_status and last_test_result. (4) scripts/dev/api.py GET /health/smart-monitor/status: running true; GET /health/smart/history/<sda's serial>: newest no older than the supervisor's start (scripts/dev/ssh.sh docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' unos-supervisor), or, if sda slept at that pass, after the first hourly pass at which it was awake. (5) scripts/dev/ssh.sh docker logs --since <the start> unos-supervisor 2>&1 | grep -c -e 'in the container as the host' -e "container's node" prints 0. (6) step 1 again: unchanged. scripts/dev/scenario.sh smart covers steps 2 and 3 for every disk too (its smartctl -c of the data disk runs by docker exec, outside run_smartctl: with a USB disk attached, run it after Disk Health has read that disk). The owner's check with a USB disk, attached while UNOS runs (no pool on it needed): (a) scripts/dev/ssh.sh lsblk -dno NAME,TRAN,SERIAL lists it (sdX, usb), and before any read docker exec unos-supervisor ls /dev/sdX finds no such file (the cause); (b) System > Disk Health, opened or refreshed, lists it with its model, serial and SMART data (UNKNOWN only for a USB bridge that smartctl cannot pass through, which then also shows UNKNOWN after a restart of the supervisor); (c) the supervisor's log has one line Made /dev/sdX in the container as the host's disk 8:<minor>, and docker exec unos-supervisor stat -c '%F %t:%T %a' /dev/sdX prints block special file 8:<minor in hex> 600; (d) a SMART Test task for it in System > Scheduler, Run now: its run succeeds with SMART test started (or scripts/dev/api.py POST '/health/disk/sdX/test?test_type=short'); (e) within the hour, GET /health/smart/history/<its serial> has a snapshot of /dev/sdX; (f) detached and attached again, Disk Health lists it again with no new log line (an SCSI disk's number follows from its name); (g) docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' unos-supervisor is the same as before the disk was attached. Open: the owner's USB disk check. Device check of cbe437c on 2026-11-18: for sda, attached at boot, the container's /dev/sda is Docker's node (8:0, 660) before and after the reads, GET /health shows its SMART data with health PASSED, a short self-test completed without error, the SMART monitor runs and the history is fresh, and the supervisor's log has no node lines (0.043 in all); the same after a reboot. Not run: the USB disk attached while UNOS runs, which is this entry's step (the owner's).

features.description: An administrator creates an SMB share on a folder inside a pool that UNOS manages
steps: On Shares, Add SMB share offers only folders and volumes of managed pools, never a pool root, apps/ or .snapshots
A new folder is made as root:unos-smb 2770, only below folders that only root can change; below a pool root that others can write, the request answers 409 and names the chmod
A folder that overlaps another share is refused
The share is served at once: smbclient lists it for a user with access
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy: a share on an existing folder, and a new folder below the 0777 pool root refused). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb passed all 27 steps (the new folder 2770 root:unos-smb served at once, the pool's top folder and a folder inside a share refused), and GET /shares/paths offers the managed pool data only.

features.description: An administrator gives a user read-only or read-write access to an SMB share, and lowering it ends the user's open connections
steps: In the share's access list, pick a user who is not an administrator and a level
With read access the user lists and reads files over SMB, and writes are refused
With read-write access the user creates and changes files, and new files belong to the group unos-smb
Lowering the access during an open session makes the next write fail; removing it ends the tree connect
New users have no access to any share
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy: read and write over a signed session, a downgrade and a revocation during open sessions). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb passed all 27 steps (the access lowered to read and removed during open sessions: NT_STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED; without access NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED).

features.description: SMB refuses anonymous and wrong-password sign-ins while no share is guest-accessible
steps: An anonymous smbclient session is refused
A wrong password answers NT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE, never a guest session
With no guest share, server signing is mandatory and the guest-related globals are off
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb passed all 27 steps (a wrong password refused with NT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE, never as a guest, the null session refused, server signing mandatory without a guest share).

features.description: An administrator makes a share guest-accessible; guests read it and never write
steps: Check guest access for a share: the dialog warns, and so does the answer
An anonymous smbclient session lists and reads the share, and writes are refused
Removing the last guest share makes signing mandatory again
features.notes: The slice 2 device checks made no guest share. Device check 2026-11-11 with the device running main 96db310 (deployed at 15:16 UTC), from the scripts of the branch: scripts/dev/scenario.sh shares (run unoscheckc21bbe, 15:27:26 to 15:28:23 UTC, 2.941 MiB for the whole check, which passed 25 steps and skipped 1) found no guest share on the device (step 3, 0.000 MiB), then turned guest access on for its share with a PATCH: the answer carried the guest warning, GET /shares/smb-status named the share, and [global] had map to guest = Bad User, restrict anonymous = 1 and server signing = default, which testparm accepted (step 20, 0.176 MiB); an anonymous (null) smbclient session to the share listed it and read its file, and its write was refused with NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED, no file made (step 21, 0.000 MiB); Delete of that last guest share removed its section and kept the folder with its files (step 22, 0.199 MiB), after which [global] had server signing = mandatory, map to guest = Never and restrict anonymous = 2 again and the status named no guest share (step 23, 0.020 MiB). A null session's share list (smbclient -L) succeeded but named no share while the guest share existed ("SMB1 disabled -- no workgroup available" and no Disk line): restrict anonymous = 1 lets Samba's srvsvc refuse anonymous callers, which ADR-0339 records, superseding ADR-0098's text that the share list still works with it. features.description: An administrator gives a group of users access to an SMB share
steps: Make a group and add users to it
Give the group read or read-write access to a share: its members get that access, and new members get it too
features.notes: Built on the branch shares.group-access (ADR-0385), not deployed yet. A group is a row of UNOS's database (user_groups, user_group_members, smb_share_group_access), never a host group: smb.conf names each member whose SMB account is active in the lists of the shares the group has access to, with the higher of the member's own level and their groups' levels. /api/v1/groups (GET, POST, GET/PATCH/DELETE /groups/{id}, which take the group's name as the page saw it: 409 after a rename, which also raises the versions of the group's shares) and group_access in the share API; the Groups card of the Users page and the groups of a share's access picker and card. A member added gets the access at the save; a member removed, a lowered level or a deleted group closes the share's open connections (ADR-0103). A deleted or promoted user leaves every group, a renamed one stays under the new name; the reconcile purges stale rows; a backup holds the groups and a restore brings them back (the tables optional for older backups; a backup whose groups break the name rule or share a name is refused). test_share_groups.py proves the steps against the share fixture and, with the FakeSambaHost, a member's lists, the close-share at a removal and the deletion of the user; users.spec.ts and shares.spec.ts the pages on route fakes and a group made, renamed through its user and deleted on the stand-in. Host-level (smb.conf, Samba's access): passes only after the device check and its re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). The check by hand, with two users unoscheck<hex>a and b with SMB on and a share unoscheck<hex> without access of its own: a group with a, given read: testparm names a in valid users and nobody in write list, smbclient as a lists and reads and a put is refused (NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED), b is refused at the tree connect; the group given write: a's put works and the file gets the group unos-smb; b added to the group: b connects and writes without a change of the share; with b's session open, b removed: b's next command fails (NT_STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED) and a new connection is refused; a given read of its own beside the group's write: a still writes; the group deleted: valid users = root and available = no; getent group names no group of UNOS's and /etc/group, /etc/passwd and passdb are as before; then the share, its folder and the users deleted. After a reboot: a group with a member and write access made before it is listed by GET /groups and the member writes. Device check 2026-11-17 (the tree of mvp.batch-7 at 7cca7e9, deployed on 2026-11-17 at 12:48 UTC; a reboot from the API at 13:31:12 UTC (the boot of 13:32:28, both UNOS containers healthy by 13:33:21)), by hand with two temporary users with SMB on and a share without access of its own, 13:09 to 13:10 UTC, each step's SD MiB 0.000 to 1.168: the group made with the first user made no host group (getent group, /etc/group's digest unchanged); given read, testparm named the member in valid users and nobody in write list, the member listed and read and its put was refused (NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED), the other user was refused at the tree connect; given write, the member's put worked and the file got the group unos-smb; the second user added connected and wrote, the share's version unchanged; removed while its session was open, its next command failed (NT_STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED) and a new connection was refused; the first user's own read beside the group's write still wrote; the group deleted: valid users = root and available = no, /etc/group, /etc/passwd and pdbedit -L as before; the audit log had group_created, group_updated twice, group_deleted and share_updated with the group's access. After the reboot (13:34 UTC, 0.125 MiB): a group with a member and write access made before it was listed by GET /groups, testparm's write list named the member, and the member wrote over smbclient. Clean-up: group, share, folder and users deleted (1.480 MiB), the host's account files and passdb as before.

The macOS Finder sidebar lists the NAS
NetBIOS can then be turned off
features.notes: Built (ADR-0275): the rendered [global] turns NetBIOS off (disable netbios = yes, smb ports = 445) and keeps smbd's Bonjour registration on (multicast dns register = yes). install.sh: start_samba enables and restarts smbd and turns nmbd off (systemctl disable --now nmbd); configure_discovery writes /etc/avahi/avahi-daemon.unos.conf (Debian's avahi-daemon settings with use-ipv6=no and publish-aaaa-on-ipv4=no), the drop-in avahi-daemon.service.d/unos.conf (avahi-daemon -s -f that file) and the drop-in wsdd2.service.d/unos.conf (wsdd2 -4), reloads systemd, installs avahi-daemon with --no-install-recommends (no libnss-mdns, which would change the host's name resolution) and enables and restarts it, then wsdd2 the same way when apt-cache show finds the package. Without one (Debian 11, Ubuntu without universe) it warns and the installation goes on; a package that exists but does not install stops it, with apt-get's error. Both services answer over IPv4 only: a Mac would otherwise connect from a global IPv6 address, which hosts allow refuses, and wsdd2's TCP ports would listen on tunnels (ADR-0227). wsdd2 is a reserved account name: wsdd2.service runs as the dynamic user wsdd2, which a static account of that name would replace. uninstall.sh enables nmbd again when it restores smb.conf.original and keeps avahi-daemon, wsdd2 and UNOS's files of both, none of them in /etc/unos. docs/INSTALL.md (Step 5, Network Discovery) and docs/USER_GUIDE.md (Finding the NAS) describe it. Tests: test_smbconf.py (TestGlobal: the three lines in both [global] variants); test_deploy_scripts.py (TestInstallScript: smbd without nmbd on a first installation and a rerun; neither avahi-daemon nor wsdd2 among install_dependencies' packages, avahi-daemon without what it recommends; avahi-daemon's settings and drop-in and wsdd2's drop-in written and loaded before the packages are installed; a missing wsdd2 package lets the installation go on, a package that fails to install stops it with apt-get's error; the order of main; TestUninstallScript: nmbd enabled again with the restored file, the completion; TestInstallGuide: the manual installation's packages, commands and files are those of install.sh); test_smb_models.py (wsdd2 is reserved). Not built: scripts/dev/check.sh still expects nmbd to be active and checks neither wsdd2 nor avahi-daemon (device.check-network-discovery). Open: steps 1 to 3 need the dev device and a Windows and a macOS computer on its LAN. On the device, in this order: deploy the branch while nmbd still runs, since check.sh needs it until device.check-network-discovery is done (smbd reloads the new smb.conf; nmbd keeps running until it is stopped); then the owner's actions (ADR-0211): the commands of docs/INSTALL.md Step 5 after the nmbd line (the three files, systemctl daemon-reload, avahi-daemon without recommends, wsdd2, enabling and restarting both), systemctl disable --now nmbd, and systemctl restart smbd (smb ports applies only at a restart). From then on, until device.check-network-discovery, check.sh reports nmbd inactive: its only expected problem. The device check, once device.check-network-discovery lets check.sh answer OK, and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): test_smbconf_testparm.py passes with scripts/dev/bin/testparm; systemctl is-active smbd wsdd2 avahi-daemon answers active for each, and nmbd is inactive and disabled; ss -tulpn lists no socket on UDP 137 or 138 or TCP 139, smbd on TCP 445, wsdd2 on UDP and TCP 3702 (and on 5355 where systemd-resolved does not hold it) and avahi-daemon on UDP 5353, with IPv4 sockets only; on a Windows computer of the LAN, File Explorer's Network view lists the NAS, and opening it there asks for a UNOS SMB account and then lists the shares it may use (steps 1 and 3); on a macOS computer of the LAN, dns-sd -G v4v6 <name>.local answers IPv4 addresses only, the Finder sidebar lists the NAS under Locations, once, and connecting from there with a UNOS SMB account lists its shares, also from a Mac with a global IPv6 address where the LAN gives it one (steps 2 and 3). Device check 2026-11-08: install.sh's network discovery set up avahi-daemon and wsdd2 on the device (16 MiB on the SD card); the workstation's dns-sd lists the device's name as _smb._tcp at the device's name, also after a reboot; wsdd2 listens on UDP 3702; nmbd no longer runs. Open: Windows Explorer's Network view, with no Windows machine on the LAN.

features.description: An administrator chooses the network interfaces that SMB listens on
steps: Pick interfaces: smb.conf gets interfaces and bind interfaces only, and smbd listens only there
features.notes: Built (ADR-0391): the choice lives in the new table smb_bind_interfaces (one row per interface name; no row: every interface, as before, and smb.conf has neither line). With rows, the rendered [global] gets, right after hosts allow, interfaces = lo <the chosen names, sorted> and bind interfaces only = yes; the loopback is always bound (smbpasswd's default mode and the scenario checks' smbclient and smbpasswd -r reach smbd on 127.0.0.1, and smbd keeps a socket when no chosen interface is on the host). GET /api/v1/shares/smb-interfaces lists the host's interfaces from ip -j addr show through src/host.py (the host's network namespace), without the loopback and Docker's (docker0, br-*, veth*), with their addresses, state and whether they have a LAN address; point-to-point interfaces are listed but cannot be chosen (Samba skips them); it compares smbd's TCP 445 listeners (ss -H -l -n -t -p) with the choice and names each LAN address of a chosen interface without a listener and each listener outside the choice (restart_needed). PUT /api/v1/shares/smb-interfaces checks the names (the Linux interface name rule, not lo, not Docker's, at most 16, none point-to-point) and refuses with 400 a choice without an interface that is on the host, enabled, broadcast-capable and with a LAN address; a name not on the host is kept; [] (every interface) is always accepted, another choice is 503 while the host cannot be read. An apply whose interfaces or bind interfaces only line changes restarts smbd after testparm and the install (systemctl reset-failed smbd, timeout 60 systemctl restart smbd) instead of the reload: the open SMB sessions end, which the dialog says first with their number; a failed restart is a warning and a status problem and is retried at the next apply. POST /api/v1/shares/smb-interfaces/restart (Restart SMB on the page) restarts smbd for an address that came after its start. Rows are checked again when rendered (ADR-0144): invalid ones are left out with a status problem, and rows of which none is valid bind the loopback alone; GET /shares/smb-status names a choice of which no interface is on the host with a LAN address. wsdd2 and avahi-daemon do not follow the choice. The audit log records smb_interfaces_changed and smb_restarted. The Shares page's SMB tab has the card Network interfaces with the dialog and Restart SMB, in English and Russian. Not built: a scenario step of scripts/dev/scenario.py (the check is by hand, with the steps below). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214), on the dev device after the owner's deploy of supervisor and web UI (the check restarts smbd twice: the owner's open SMB connections end): (1) scripts/dev/sd.sh measure ss-before -- scripts/dev/ssh.sh "ss -H -l -n -t -p 'sport = :445'" shows smbd on 0.0.0.0:445 and [::]:445; scripts/dev/sd.sh measure get -- scripts/dev/api.py GET /shares/smb-interfaces lists enP4p65s0 with lan and offered true and the tunnel with offered false, no docker0, br-* or veth*, chosen [] and listening ["0.0.0.0", "::"]; note sha256sum /etc/samba/smb.conf. (2) echo '{"interfaces": ["enP4p65s0"]}' | scripts/dev/sd.sh measure choose -- scripts/dev/api.py PUT /shares/smb-interfaces - answers 200 with restarted true and no warning (or the same from Shares > SMB > Network interfaces > Choose interfaces). (3) the ss line of (1) shows smbd only on 127.0.0.1:445, [::1]:445, enP4p65s0's IPv4 address and its IPv6 addresses that are not link-local, none on 0.0.0.0, [::], 172.17.0.1, 172.31.254.1 or the tunnel's addresses; testparm -s --suppress-prompt on the device prints interfaces = lo enP4p65s0 and bind interfaces only = Yes, and PATH="$PWD/scripts/dev/bin:$PATH" make test TESTS=tests/test_smbconf_testparm.py TEST_WORKERS=0 passes, none skipped; on the device smbclient -N -L //172.17.0.1 fails with NT_STATUS_CONNECTION_REFUSED while smbclient -N -L //127.0.0.1 and //<enP4p65s0's IPv4> answer (any status but CONNECTION_REFUSED); GET /shares/smb-interfaces has no problem and restart_needed false, GET /shares/smb-status no problem, GET /audit/logs with action smb_interfaces_changed one entry. (4) after the owner's reboot: the ss line, testparm and GET /shares/smb-interfaces again (an IPv6 address that came after smbd's start is named there: record it and its Restart SMB), systemctl cat smbd shows network-online.target in Wants and After, and smb.conf has the same sha256 as before the reboot. (5) undo: echo '{"interfaces": []}' | scripts/dev/api.py PUT /shares/smb-interfaces - answers restarted true, the ss line shows 0.0.0.0:445 and [::]:445 again, smb.conf has the sha256 of (1), and scripts/dev/check.sh answers OK. Expected SD writes: about 0.1 to 0.3 MiB for each PUT (smb.conf, the database's write-ahead log, the audit line and smbd's start in the journal), about 0.02 MiB for each API read, nothing for ss and testparm. Device check 2026-11-17 (mvp.batch-8 at 320d3ec, deployed 2026-11-17 18:58-18:59 UTC; reboot from the API at 19:23:11 UTC (the boot of 19:24:4x, all containers healthy by 19:25:26); scenario.sh all after it: 187 steps passed, smart's sleep steps skipped while apps use the pool): PUT [enP4p65s0] answered 200 and restarted smbd (0.344 MiB); ss showed smbd only on the loopback, the LAN IPv4 and the port's global IPv6 addresses; testparm 'interfaces = lo enP4p65s0' and 'bind interfaces only = Yes'; smbclient refused on 172.17.0.1, answered on 127.0.0.1 and the LAN IPv4; no problems, one audit entry; test_smbconf_testparm.py with the device's testparm 22 passed, none skipped. After the reboot the same, smb.conf's sha256 unchanged and smbd's unit after network-online.target; then PUT [] restored 0.0.0.0:445 and [::]:445 and smb.conf's sha256 of the start (0.348).

features.description: A share can require encryption, serve Time Machine backups or show snapshots as Previous Versions
steps: Turn on encryption for a share: clients without SMB3 encryption are refused there
Turn on Time Machine: a Mac uses the share as a backup disk
Turn on Previous Versions: Windows lists the share's snapshots
features.notes: Built on the branch shares.per-share-protocol-options (ADR-0380), deployed to the dev device on 2026-11-16 (the device check at the end). Three options per share, off by default (encryption_required, time_machine, previous_versions of the share API), in the new table smb_share_options (a row only while one is on, deleted with its share in one transaction; orphans removed by the startup reconcile and the restore). Every share section states smb encrypt (required or default) and one vfs objects line; Time Machine adds fruit:time machine = yes, loads catia fruit streams_xattr in every section while a Time Machine share exists and gives [global] fruit:aapl = yes and fruit:nfs_aces = no; smbd announces _adisk._tcp itself for the Time Machine shares that are available, and a change of those (Time Machine on or off, a rename, the first access granted or the last one removed) restarts avahi-daemon after the reload (systemctl reset-failed, then timeout 60 systemctl restart, which waits for the job: a failure is a warning and a problem of GET /shares/smb-status until a restart works); Previous Versions add shadow_copy2 btrfs with shadow:mountpoint = the share's pool or volume and the names snap_/auto_<UTC time> (scheduled tasks snapshot pools only: a share in a volume lists the volume's snapshots of the Snapshots page), and turning them off closes the share's open tree connects, as turning encryption on does. Validated when stored (400: a guest share that requires encryption, Time Machine or Previous Versions without samba-vfs-modules, Previous Versions in a subvolume or file system of its own below the pool's top level other than a volume) and when rendered (left out, named by GET /shares/smb-status and by the share's not_rendered, which the card shows as a warning with the reason; a restored guest share that requires encryption is rendered without guests, and the restore turns its guest access off with a note). The import of an smb.conf that UNOS did not write keeps required encryption (of a section, or of [global] for every share) as the option with the access, superseding ADR-0086 (ADR-0380 restates its other rules), and Time Machine where fruit is loaded. Tests first: the 40 tests of supervisor/tests/test_share_options.py failed on main (no option rendered or stored), and on this branch its test of a hand-made option line in UNOS's own smb.conf until the import noted lines that UNOS does not render (smbconf.is_unos_option_line), and its two tests of a Time Machine share without access (available = no, which smbd does not announce) until smbconf.time_machine_shares left such sections out; the E2E test of webui/tests/shares.spec.ts found no option in the dialog; the smb check of supervisor/tests/test_dev_scenarios.py had none of the new steps, and passed with the fake NAS's defect advertise-fails (avahi-daemon not restarted, a warning of the answer) until its Time Machine step read the answers' warnings. The fixes of the two fresh-context reviews came test first too: the shrink of Previous Versions turned off, the blocking restart of avahi-daemon with its reset and status problem, the import of required encryption and of Time Machine from a file written by hand, the options of UNOS's own file only from the vfs objects line it composes, the note of another smb encrypt value in UNOS's own file, guest access of a share that requires encryption at the render and the restore, and not_rendered failed in test_share_options.py, test_share_import.py and test_smbconf.py before the change, and the smb check's new defects (adisk-unannounced, adisk-stays, encryption-keeps-sessions, encryption-everywhere, snapshot-other-names) failed it. So did the defect avahi-unreachable of a third check (busctl cannot ask Avahi once Time Machine is off, which the check read as no such service), until only Avahi's own answer for no such service (Timeout reached) counted as one. Host-level (smb.conf, avahi-daemon): passes only after the device check and its re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). The check: scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb, whose steps make a share of a folder in a new volume with Previous Versions on (shadow:mountpoint = the volume, testparm), record what smbd answers for the shadow copies of that volume before its first snapshot, without .snapshots (allinfo v.txt;
