any answer passes, and the step's PASS line shows it), list two snapshots of the volume that the check makes on the Snapshots page a second apart (it names them to the second) with the names it gives for a file the user wrote as @GMT-<their times> (smbclient allinfo), only the second after the first one's Delete, with the file, which the user overwrites after both snapshots, opening in it with exactly its bytes from before (get @GMT-<time>/v.txt into the SMB helper's folder in RAM, whose sha256sum there, run with smbclient's !, is the digest of the earlier bytes), and after the second one's Delete smbd refusing to open the file in either (an NT_STATUS error that is no status of a broken connection, session or tree connect, and ls in the same session lists the file afterwards) and allinfo listing none (no @GMT token, and no error but the one with which Samba 4.22's smbclient reports an empty list) while the volume keeps .snapshots, require encryption (open sessions of an SMB 2.1 smbclient and of an unencrypted SMB3 one end at the switch, a new SMB 2.1 smbclient refused with NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED, one with client smb encrypt = required served, the SMB 2.1 client served on the check's first share meanwhile and on this one again with the option off), turn Time Machine on (the one vfs objects line catia fruit streams_xattr shadow_copy2 btrfs, fruit:time machine = yes, the fruit lines of [global], testparm, an answer without a warning of a failed restart of avahi-daemon, and the share in the _adisk._tcp service that Avahi resolves under smbd's netbios name with busctl) and off (the service no longer names it; a busctl failure other than Avahi's answer for no such service fails the step), and delete the share and the volume. Steps by hand for the device check: 1. On the dev device, ls /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/samba/vfs/fruit.so /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/samba/vfs/shadow_copy2.so /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/samba/vfs/btrfs.so (scripts/dev/ssh.sh); if one is missing, the owner installs samba-vfs-modules (sudo apt install samba-vfs-modules, an owner action, ADR-0211) before the smb check, which otherwise fails at its Previous Versions step with the package named. 2. PATH="$PWD/scripts/dev/bin:$PATH" scripts/dev/sd.sh measure testparm -- make test TESTS=tests/test_smbconf_testparm.py: every combination of the options passes the device's testparm (skipped here, where no testparm is installed). 3. A Mac on the LAN: a share with Time Machine on and Read & write for a user with SMB on; System Settings > General > Time Machine > Add Backup Disk lists the share without a Finder connection first (the _adisk._tcp of smbd after avahi-daemon's restart); choose it, sign in, Back Up Now: the first backup completes. Turn Time Machine off: the share leaves that list. 4. A Windows computer on the LAN: a share with Previous Versions on, a snapshot of its pool or volume made on the Snapshots page; File Explorer > the share > a file > Properties > Previous Versions lists the snapshot's time, and Open shows the file as it was; delete the snapshot. 5. Re-check after a reboot: scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb passes again, and with a Time Machine share left on before the reboot the Mac's list of step 3 still names it (smbd registers it at its start). Not on the device: the dialog and the cards (webui/tests/shares.spec.ts on the stand-in), the refusals and the render-time checks (supervisor/tests/test_share_options.py). Check fix 2026-11-16: the first device run of scenario.sh smb failed at its Previous Versions step: after the snapshot's Delete, with no snapshot left, allinfo v.txt answered NT_STATUS_INVALID_NETWORK_RESPONSE getting shadow copy data. Samba 4.22's source puts the cause in smbclient, not in UNOS: for no snapshot smbd answers FSCTL_GET_SHADOW_COPY_DATA with the labels in 12 + 2 bytes (source3/modules/vfs_default.c, vfswrap_fsctl), and smbclient refuses any answer shorter than 16 bytes with that status (source3/libsmb/cli_smb2_fnum.c, cli_smb2_shadow_copy_data_fnum_recv), which allinfo prints and goes on (source3/client/client.c, do_allinfo). The step no longer rests on smbclient's reading of an empty list: two snapshots, the first one's Delete seen while the second is still listed and opens, the opens of both refused after the second one's Delete, and for the empty list only no @GMT token with no error or exactly that line (no_shadow_copies of scripts/dev/scenario.py). Test first: the fake NAS of supervisor/tests/test_dev_scenarios.py answers an empty list as Samba 4.22 does, names snapshots to the second of the device's clock and opens files in snapshots with get; the old step failed against it as on the device, and the new one passes and fails for the defects snapshots-unlisted, deleted-version-listed (a deleted snapshot still listed), deleted-version-opens (still opened) and snapdir-removed (.snapshots deleted with the last snapshot, which the fake answers with NT_STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST, an assumption then, which smbd's answer on the device for a volume without .snapshots later matched). A fresh check of the step found two gaps, closed test first: v.txt was never changed after the snapshots, so an open served from the live file passed (the fake NAS's new defect version-opens-live-file passed the check until the step overwrote v.txt after both snapshots and required the earlier line exactly in the version it opens), and any NT_STATUS error counted as a refused open, a dropped connection too (the new defect missing-version-drops-session passed until refused_open of scripts/dev/scenario.py left out the statuses of a broken connection, session or tree connect, TRANSPORT_STATUSES, and an ls in the same session had to list the file after the opens); docs/USER_GUIDE.md names smbclient's answers for no snapshot and for a pool or volume without .snapshots. A review of that fix found three problems, fixed test first: the version's bytes were judged by lines of smbclient's output, so a copy that held the earlier line and more bytes passed (the fake NAS's new defect version-extra-bytes passed the step, and so did version-line-contains-data, a line that only contains the earlier text, once the check was loosened to that text anywhere in the output), until the step compared the sha256sum of the copy that smbclient gets with the digest of the earlier bytes (sha256_digests of scripts/dev/scenario.py reads it past smbclient's prompts and the open line of the get, which the SMB helper's session test shows with a stand-in smbclient); docs/USER_GUIDE.md said that NT_STATUS_INVALID_NETWORK_RESPONSE means no snapshot, though a pool or volume with only snapshots of other names gives the same empty list, and it now says the list is empty; and it named NT_STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST for a pool or volume without .snapshots, which had been confirmed neither from Samba's source nor on the device: the guide then said only that none is listed, and the step that makes the share records allinfo's answer for the new volume before its first snapshot, so that the device check shows it (the fake's status for it was an assumption, which the device then showed; the step passes with any answer, which a test over four answers shows). Since the defect snapdir-removed failed the step only through that assumed status, the step also sees with stat that the volume keeps .snapshots after both Deletes: snapdir-removed passed it before, with smbd's answer for a volume without .snapshots taken as an empty list or as no error. Device check on 2026-11-16 (the SD MiB of each step in PROGRESS.md's Log): (1) fruit.so, shadow_copy2.so and btrfs.so are on the dev device; (2) test_smbconf_testparm.py with scripts/dev/bin first on PATH, so the device's testparm: its 19 tests passed, none skipped; scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb failed at its Previous Versions step on the first deployed tree, 57be517, in the run of 01:05 UTC (the check fix above), and then passed with its 37 steps, steps 18 to 21 this entry's, on 434d410 in the run of 06:54 UTC, on 5d79302 in the run of 13:42 UTC, before the reboots of 14:03 and 14:42 UTC, and after the reboot of 14:42 UTC in the run of 14:45 UTC; the shares code is the same in the four trees deployed. Step 18 recorded smbd's answer for a volume without .snapshots, NT_STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST getting shadow copy data, which docs/USER_GUIDE.md now names. Open: the steps by hand 3 and 4 and the Mac's part of 5, which need a Mac and a Windows computer on the LAN (the owner's): passes stays false until a Mac has made a Time Machine backup to a share and Windows has listed and opened a share's Previous Versions.

features.description: An administrator shares a volume as an iSCSI target with CHAP authentication
steps: Create a target from a volume with one LUN and CHAP credentials
An initiator with the credentials connects; one without is refused
Several initiators can be allowed
features.notes: Built (ADR-0418), not passing: it is host-level (the kernel's iSCSI targets) and waits for the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). shares/iscsi.py drives LIO through the host's configfs with three host scripts of src/host.py (the state read, the LUN files' check, the operations from standard input, so that no secret is on a command line); no host package. Step 1: POST /shares/iscsi/targets makes the sparse file <volume>/.unos-iscsi/<name>.lun (root, 0600, its folder root's 0700 and immutable), a fileio storage object (write-through, UNMAP on, the target's id as VPD serial), the target iqn.2003-01.org.linux-iscsi.unos:<name>.<8 hex> with authentication 1, generate_node_acls 0 and AuthMethod CHAP, LUN 0, portals on the host's LAN addresses only, and an ACL with the CHAP user and secret per initiator; the secret is generated or typed, stored in /data/iscsi_secrets.json (0600, synced, in no backup) and in the create's answer only (test_iscsi.py TestCreate; iscsi.spec.ts 'an administrator creates a target ...', 'a typed secret, mutual CHAP ...'). Step 2: the fake kernel's login of test_iscsi.py TestLogin lets in only an allowed initiator with the user and secret (and the mutual secret), and refuses no CHAP, a wrong secret and an initiator not allowed: a model of LIO's decision from what UNOS wrote, which the device check proves. Step 3: several initiators each get an ACL and log in, and a change of the list adds and removes ACLs (TestInitiators; iscsi.spec.ts 'a change of the initiators ...'). Also: the restore at every start, after a database restore and after a pool's mount, idempotent (no write and no log line when configfs is as it should be), removing UNOS's targets and storage objects that the database lacks and keeping others; a target without its secret, with a LUN file that is missing or not as UNOS made it, or whose pool did not mount is not served and the tab says why; CHAP turned off by hand is turned on again; the portals follow the host's addresses within 5 minutes (TestRestore); a pool that holds a LUN is not unmounted or forgotten and its volume not deleted (TestPoolAndVolume); a delete needs the name typed and names the sessions it ends (TestDelete; iscsi.spec.ts 'a delete ...'); UNOS's ufw rules let the local networks reach 3260 (test_firewall.py); the host scripts under sh and dash (test_iscsi_scripts.py). Device check (by hand, the device-checks skill; every step wrapped in scripts/dev/sd.sh measure <label> -- ..., its SD MiB reported; the expected numbers are estimates, not measurements): (0, owner, once) install the test initiator: scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends open-iscsi' (a package install, ADR-0211; a few MiB) and read the device's initiator name: scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'sudo cat /etc/iscsi/initiatorname.iscsi' (call it INIT; 0 MiB). (1) a volume: echo '{"name": "unoscheck1a2b3c"}' | scripts/dev/api.py POST /storage/pools/data/volumes - (about 0.1 MiB). (2) the target, with a test secret typed into a temporary body file of the workstation (mode 600, never on a command line): {"name": "unoscheck", "pool": "data", "volume": "unoscheck1a2b3c", "size_gib": 1, "initiators": ["INIT", "iqn.2026-11.org.example:unoscheck-second"], "chap_secret": "<12 to 16 characters>"}; scripts/dev/api.py POST /shares/iscsi/targets - < body: HTTP 201, served true, the answer's target.iqn is IQN and its portals hold LANIP, the device's LAN address (about 0.1 MiB: the database, the audit line, the synced secrets file; configfs is RAM, the LUN file is on the pool). (3) the host: scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'sudo cat /sys/kernel/config/target/iscsi/iqn.2003-01.org.linux-iscsi.unos:unoscheck.*/tpgt_1/attrib/authentication; sudo ls /sys/kernel/config/target/iscsi/iqn.2003-01.org.linux-iscsi.unos:unoscheck.*/tpgt_1/acls /sys/kernel/config/target/iscsi/iqn.2003-01.org.linux-iscsi.unos:unoscheck.*/tpgt_1/np; sudo ss -Htln sport = :3260; sudo lsattr -d /mnt/pools/data/unoscheck1a2b3c/.unos-iscsi; sudo stat -c "%s %b %a %u" /mnt/pools/data/unoscheck1a2b3c/.unos-iscsi/unoscheck.lun': authentication 1, both ACLs, the portal of the LAN address only (no 0.0.0.0, no 172.x of Docker), the folder immutable, the file 1073741824 bytes, few blocks, 600, root (0 MiB). (4) refused without the credentials: scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'sudo iscsiadm -m discovery -t sendtargets -p LANIP; sudo iscsiadm -m node -T IQN -p LANIP --login': discovery lists IQN, the login fails with an authorization failure (status 24) (small: open-iscsi's node records in /etc/iscsi). (5) in with the credentials: append to the device's /etc/iscsi/iscsid.conf, through standard input from a temporary file of the workstation (mode 600), the lines node.session.auth.authmethod = CHAP, node.session.auth.username = unoscheck and node.session.auth.password = <the secret> (scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'sudo tee -a /etc/iscsi/iscsid.conf > /dev/null' < file), then scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'sudo iscsiadm -m node -o delete -T IQN; sudo iscsiadm -m discovery -t sendtargets -p LANIP; sudo iscsiadm -m node -T IQN -p LANIP --login; lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,VENDOR,SERIAL': login successful, a 1G disk of LIO-ORG (call it /dev/sdX); GET /shares/iscsi lists INIT among the sessions (small). (6) a write and a read through the LUN: scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'sudo dd if=/dev/urandom of=/dev/shm/unoscheck.bin bs=1M count=16; sudo dd if=/dev/shm/unoscheck.bin of=/dev/sdX bs=1M oflag=direct; sudo dd if=/dev/sdX bs=1M count=16 iflag=direct | cmp - /dev/shm/unoscheck.bin; sudo dd if=/mnt/pools/data/unoscheck1a2b3c/.unos-iscsi/unoscheck.lun bs=1M count=16 | cmp - /dev/shm/unoscheck.bin; sha256sum /dev/shm/unoscheck.bin': both cmp silent; record the hash (about 0 MiB: the data goes to the pool). (7) the second allowed initiator and one not allowed: logout (iscsiadm -m node -T IQN --logout), put InitiatorName=iqn.2026-11.org.example:unoscheck-second into /etc/iscsi/initiatorname.iscsi (keep INIT), sudo systemctl restart iscsid, login: successful; the same with InitiatorName=iqn.2026-11.org.example:unoscheck-third: refused (authorization failure); then INIT back and iscsid restarted (small). (8) idle: logged in, scripts/dev/sd.sh measure idle -- sleep 600, compared with an idle interval before step 1: no more (the 5-minute check of the addresses only reads). (9) the reboot: logout, then scripts/dev/api.py POST /system/reboot; after it GET /shares/iscsi: served true, problem null; the supervisor's log has 'Applied the iSCSI targets: 1 served (unoscheck)'; ss lists the LAN portal; step 4's refused login, step 5's login and sudo dd if=/dev/sdX bs=1M count=16 iflag=direct | sha256sum equal to the hash of step 6; check.sh's SD writes since boot reported. (10) clean up: logout, sudo iscsiadm -m node -o delete -T IQN, the three lines out of iscsid.conf (sudo sed -i '/^node.session.auth.\(authmethod\|username\|password\) = /d' /etc/iscsi/iscsid.conf), echo '{"confirm": "unoscheck"}' | scripts/dev/api.py POST /shares/iscsi/targets/unoscheck/delete - (the folder .unos-iscsi goes with its last file), DELETE /storage/pools/data/volumes/unoscheck1a2b3c, no UNOS target left in configfs, no listener on 3260; the owner may purge open-iscsi. Review in a fresh context (ADR-0017), fixed: a folder made in an SMB share's setgid folder (now chmod 00700), the LUN files' scripts now work from the folder entered with cd -P and checked with pwd -P, one target that the kernel refuses no longer stops the others (each runs apart and is taken back whole), a volume that btrfs cannot check now leaves its served target as it is, a new secret ends the sessions (the ACLs are made anew), a change that the kernel does not take still answers its new secrets, a create's take-back runs each step, values starting with NULL are refused, tentative IPv6 addresses get no portal, a pool's mount serves its targets, and the 5-minute check runs only while a target is served. Left, with the reason: nothing ends the targets at the host's shutdown, so the pool powers off mounted after the last sync (ending them when the supervisor stops would end every session at each restart of it; a unit of the host is a follow-up, ADR-0418); the rule for 3260 comes with Enable or Reset of the firewall only (no older installations, ADR-0207); a restored database without a target leaves its LUN file and secret, and the name is then refused with 'choose another name'; the fakes model LIO, which the device check proves. Not checked on the device: the firewall's rule for 3260 with ufw on (a security setting, the owner's; test_firewall.py shows it), a Windows initiator, a pool that fails to mount at boot. Device check 2026-11-19 of 15cf31d (mvp.batch-15, deployed 07:50 to 08:01 UTC: sync 6.215, build-supervisor 17.715, build-webui 21.367, up 6.465 SD MiB), before and after the reboot from the API at 08:21:50 UTC (all 7 containers healthy at 08:23:04): the dev device's vendor kernel 6.1.172-vendor-rk35xx has CONFIG_TARGET_CORE=m and CONFIG_ISCSI_TARGET=m but builds no backstore (FILEIO, IBLOCK, PSCSI and USER not set): no target_core_file, GET answered kernel_support false; a create answered 500 at the modprobe and was taken back whole (no target, nothing in configfs or on 3260, no .unos-iscsi). Fixed (82346c1): a create on such a kernel answers 409 before anything is made. The owner's BPI-F3 (kernel 6.18.45-current-spacemit) has no LIO at all. Open: the whole device check, on a host whose kernel has LIO with its file backstore (another kernel: the owner's decision). Rechecked on the device after 82346c1's deploy (2026-11-19, 09:58 to 10:00 UTC: sync 0.527, build-supervisor 15.168, up 3.270 SD MiB; check.sh OK): a create answered 409 with NO_KERNEL_SUPPORT's text, no target, no folder, no module loaded, nothing audited (0.020).

features.description: An SMB user's password changes only through UNOS, so the password rule and UNOS's copy stay in step
steps: A password change from Windows (Change a password) aimed at the NAS is refused
The Account page stays the way to change it
features.notes: Built (ADR-0342, which supersedes the proposed ADR-0276; the owner delegated the choice, ADR-0013): UNOS's [global] has check password script = /bin/false in both variants (smbconf.global_settings), and so does the smb.conf that deploy/install.sh writes before the supervisor's first start. Samba runs that script for every password change that a client asks for over SAMR (Windows' Change a password, smbpasswd -r), once the old password is checked, and refuses the change with NT_STATUS_PASSWORD_RESTRICTION before it stores anything; root's smbpasswd -s -a, with which UNOS sets every Samba password, and pdbedit run no script, so activations, UNOS's password changes, the restore steps and the compensation of ADR-0124 work as before. Step 2: the Account page's Change Password (POST /auth/change-password) and an administrator's new password on the Users page stay the ways to change an SMB password, with the rules of ADR-0279 (test_smb_accounts.py TestPasswordChange, unchanged). Tests: test_smbconf.py TestGlobal (test_samba_refuses_every_password_change_of_its_own in both variants, and the pinned [global]); test_deploy_scripts.py test_first_install_refuses_samba_s_own_password_changes and the comparison of install.sh's file with render_config([]); test_dev_scenarios.py: the smb check's new step against FakeNas, its defects samr-change-accepted, samr-refusal-writes and samr-refusal-changes-password, the SMB helper's change mode against a stand-in smbpasswd (the passwords on standard input only) and how smbpasswd's answer is read. Device check (ADR-0018), done 2026-11-11 on tree 8ea5a08 before and after the reboot from the API at 23:22:13 UTC on 2026-11-11 (the boot of 23:23:10; both containers healthy by 23:23:59): the smb scenario check (scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb) before and after a reboot of the deployed tree, with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): its step after the new password signs in runs smbpasswd -r 127.0.0.1 -s -U <the check's user> on the device, the stand-in for Windows' Change a password, with the old password and a new one on standard input, and expects NT_STATUS_PASSWORD_RESTRICTION (Samba 4.22's smbpasswd prints MS-ERREF's description of it, "machine 127.0.0.1 rejected to change the password with error: When trying to update a password, this status indicates that some password update rule has been violated. For example, the password might not meet length criteria.", which the check reads by the phrase "some password update rule has been violated", as it reads the short "Error was : Password restriction." of older releases), passdb.tdb's time unchanged and the old password still signing in; its step 3 now also needs smbpasswd on the device. Not in the check: a Windows client. Step 1 is checked on the device only with smbpasswd -r, the stand-in for Windows' Change a password; no Windows client has tried it yet, so passes stays false until one does, an owner action, since the agent can reach no Windows machine (ADR-0342). On the device, testparm reads check password script = /bin/false from UNOS's smb.conf, and scenario.sh smb passed its 29 steps before and after the reboot (3.000 and 3.020 MiB): its step 21 got Samba 4.22's refusal, passdb.tdb unchanged and the old password still signing in. The review in a fresh context found that the step would have misread Samba 4.22's text; that was fixed before the device check. passes stays false until a Windows client has tried step 1.

features.description: A restore never gives two SMB accounts one uid, nor a uid that a user deleted before the backup had
steps: An archive whose smb_accounts holds two rows with one uid is refused
A uid handed out before the backup is never handed out again after the restore
features.notes: Step 1 built 2026-11-11 (ADR-0349): service.check_smb_tables (supervisor/src/shares/service.py), which a restore runs on the extracted database before the account snapshot and the SMB preparation, refuses an smb_accounts table that gives one non-NULL uid to two or more rows, with 400 "unos.db in the backup gives the uid <uid> to <n> SMB accounts", and nothing changes: no copy of the live database, no swap. UNOS's own table keeps uid UNIQUE, so only a crafted or edited backup holds such rows. test_backup_restore.py TestRestoredSchema test_two_accounts_with_one_uid_are_refused (uids 70001 and 70001: 400, the live database, smb.conf and the copies untouched, neither the snapshot nor the account rules run; 70001 and 70002, or no uids: restored) failed before: the restore answered 200. ADR-0349 records the rule, decided by the agent under the owner's delegation, and the option it rejects: clearing the uid of all rows but one, as ADR-0112 does for a uid that a live account holds, since neither restored row has the better claim. Step 2 built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0353, decided by the agent under the owner's delegation): the new table smb_uids (models.SmbUid) records every uid handed out on this NAS with the linux name it went to, and no row is ever deleted. An activation that allocates writes its row in the commit of the row's uid, before useradd, and allocates above every recorded uid whatever next_uid says (accounts._allocate_uid); the reconcile records each stale marked host account before step 6 removes it (step 5', so the first start of a new installation records the accounts that uninstall.sh kept); a restore reads the live table (snapshot_for_restore) and, in prepare_restored_accounts, a restored row whose uid no live account holds keeps it only when the record has no row for it or names the same linux name, else uid NULL, 'needed' and "SMB must be turned on again for X"; the backup's smb_uids is dropped whatever its layout and made anew with the live rows, the live accounts' uids and the restored rows' uids, and next_uid's floor lies above every recorded uid. A backup made before a deletion still brings the user back with the uid. Tests that failed before: test_restore_accounts.py TestWholePath test_the_uid_of_a_deleted_user[bob] (dave activated with 70000 and deleted; an archive giving 70000 to bob: "assert [] == ['SMB must be turned on again for bob']", bob kept 70000) and test_a_reinstall_records_the_kept_accounts ("assert 70000 is None"), TestHandedOutUids (snapshot, the rule for both kinds of database, the record of the restored database for a backup with its own record, none or another layout), test_backup_restore.py TestAccountStep test_the_uid_of_a_deleted_user_goes_to_no_restored_account (the real restore endpoint), test_smb_accounts.py TestCollisions test_an_activation_records_its_uid_before_useradd and test_a_recorded_uid_is_never_handed_out_again, test_smb_reconcile.py TestNextUid test_a_stale_marked_account_is_recorded_before_it_is_removed (all "no such table: smb_uids" before). Review fixes 2026-11-12 (ADR-0353, decided by the agent under the owner's delegation): reconcile step 5' records the stale marked accounts first, then every row with a valid name and uid, so the first start records the rows from before the table and later starts write nothing; begin_user_removal records the deleted row's uid when the table lacks it, in the deletion's transaction; a restore merges the backup's own smb_uids rows with a valid uid and name last, for the uids still missing (they can only reserve uids, and the old installation's backup after a reinstall brings back its deleted users' uids). Tests that failed before: test_smb_reconcile.py TestNextUid test_the_rows_are_recorded_once ("assert {} == {70000: 'alice', 70001: 'bob'}"), test_smb_accounts.py TestCollisions test_a_deletion_records_the_uid_the_record_lacks[missing], test_restore_accounts.py TestWholePath test_the_uid_of_a_user_activated_before_the_record (both cases: "assert () == ((70000, 'dave'),)"), TestHandedOutUids test_the_backups_own_record_joins_last, test_backup_restore.py TestAccountStep test_the_uid_of_a_deleted_user_goes_to_no_restored_account. Limits (ADR-0353): only uids whose user was deleted before the table existed (the dev device) are unknown; an uninstall deletes the record with the database until the old installation's backup is restored. Not checked on the device. Device check 2026-11-12 (main 641f2a5, before and after the reboot from the API at 04:35:30 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 04:36:49; both containers healthy by 04:37:17)): the database has the table smb_uids with its range check; the device has no marked SMB account now, so the backfill had nothing to record; scenario.sh smb, shares and restore OK (the restore check's activations, restores and deletions with the record). The crafted cases (one uid on two rows, a deleted user's uid in a foreign backup) rest on the tests.

features.description: The SMB status names the reason when smb.conf was replaced after UNOS's last apply
steps: Replace smb.conf by hand after an apply: GET /api/v1/shares/smb-status names the replaced file as a problem
features.notes: Built: after an apply that left UNOS's file in place, GET /shares/smb-status reads the live smb.conf and names a file without UNOS's header, or none, as a problem (ADR-0249). test_smb_integration.py replaces and removes the file after the startup apply, test_share_api.py (TestStatus) adds an unreadable file and the next change, and shares.spec.ts shows the problem on the Shares page. The step only reads: the status reads smb.conf through the /etc/samba bind mount with the function the activation check uses (ADR-0249), and changes nothing on the host, so it needs no device check. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017); its finding for this entry, ADR-0195 still listing the item as open, is fixed by ADR-0250, which supersedes ADR-0195.

features.description: Unmounting or forgetting a pool re-applies smb.conf, so its shares stop being served at once
steps: Unmount a pool with shares: smb.conf no longer serves them, and the Shares page lists them as not served
Mount it again: they are served again
features.notes: Built: create, mount, unmount and remove on the Storage page apply smb.conf before they answer, also after a failure (ADR-0248). test_smb_integration.py runs the real pool and SMB code on the fake hosts (unmount and mount, remove, a busy unmount and the mount of a mounted pool that write nothing, a failed apply, an unmount whose apply waits for smb_lock and runs with it held), test_pool_persistence.py (TestPoolEndpoints) checks which requests apply, and storage.spec.ts the Shares page after Unmount and Mount, with route fakes that also change the SMB status as the server does (test_share_api.py checks their texts). Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017), its findings fixed (ADR-0250 supersedes ADR-0195). Open: the device check (btrfs and Samba) and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018): with the share DATA served from /mnt/pools/data/shared, an account with access, transmission stopped and no SMB client connected, Unmount data on the Storage page: /etc/samba/smb.conf has no [DATA] section, smbclient -L lists no DATA, and the Shares page shows DATA as Not served and Pool not mounted; Mount data: smb.conf has the same [DATA] section again and the account opens DATA with smbclient. With an SMB client connected to DATA, Unmount answers 409 (busy) and smb.conf is unchanged. Report the SD MiB of each step. Device check 2026-11-08: blocked; unmounting the pool data is refused on the device (409) because systemd services' own mount namespaces keep copies of its mount (storage.mount-and-unmount). Device check 2026-11-08: unmounting the pool data took the share DATA out of smb.conf at once, and mounting it again served it again.

features.description: Every copy of foreign share sections and every import backup is kept, not only the latest
steps: A second foreign section event keeps the first copy of smb.conf.unos-replaced
Several import backups are kept, each with its date
features.notes: Built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0362, which supersedes ADR-0085, ADR-0092 and ADR-0309). Each smb.conf with share sections that UNOS did not render gets a copy of its own before an apply, /etc/samba/smb.conf.unos-replaced-<UTC time YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_ffffff>, and each live smb.conf that the import finds without UNOS's header an import backup /etc/samba/smb.conf.unos-import-backup-<UTC time>, unless one of the newest 10 copies of its kind has exactly these bytes (only regular files count); a copy is hard-linked to its name and never replaces a file, and after it the copies of its kind beyond the newest 10 are deleted, never the new one (smb.keep_copy, smb.COPIES_KEPT). The status problem names the new copy and the earlier ones, newest first, until the supervisor restarts; the import report names the import backup and the earlier ones; deploy/uninstall.sh lists the import backups oldest first. Asserted on fakes: step 1 by test_share_apply.py (TestReplaced: a second event keeps the first copy, the newest 10, a clock set back, a failed copy; TestSmbHelpers) and test_share_api.py (TestStatus); step 2 by test_share_import.py (TestCopy: an earlier import backup stays beside the new one, each with its time, the newest 10) and test_deploy_scripts.py (the uninstall's list). The smbconf scenario check (scripts/dev/scenario.py) refuses to start beside 9 replaced copies, edits smb.conf by hand twice, takes the one new name after each apply as its copy, expects the first copy to keep its bytes and to be named on the Shares page as an earlier copy and the earlier copies to stay, and deletes only its two copies (test_dev_scenarios.py). Open: the device check, scripts/dev/scenario.sh smbconf after a deploy of these runtime files, on the owner's request (ADR-0304), and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214). The device's undated /etc/samba/smb.conf.unos-import-backup of the earlier single copy is neither listed nor deleted (ADR-0207): renaming it to the dated form, or deleting it, is the owner's call. Device check 2026-11-12: the integration tree d149c3a before and after the reboot from the API at 14:45:53 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 14:46:49; both containers healthy by 14:47:40), scenario.sh smbconf (15 steps then: its copy beside the earlier ones, named on the Shares page; 2.988 and 2.477 MiB) and smb OK; after the review's fixes, main a9adcb1's tree 2bb76a8, scenario.sh smbconf OK with 17 steps (3.469 MiB): two hand edits, the first copy kept with its bytes beside the second and named on the Shares page as an earlier copy, both deleted again; smb OK (29 steps). The two-copy steps ran after the deploy of the fixes, without another reboot; the copies are files in /etc/samba that a reboot keeps.

features.description: Samba's own writes to the system disk are reduced: daemon logs in RAM, and no passdb write for a retry of a replaced password or a sign-in of a locked account
steps: On a host whose /var/log is on the system disk, smbd and nmbd log to /run/samba with a small size cap

A failed SMB sign-in of an existing account writes nothing to passdb.tdb while the account is locked or when it retries one of the account's two previous passwords, and any other one writes the account's count of failures, of which the fifth locks it; such a retry writes once when it sets a count older than 5 minutes back to 0 (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)
features.notes: Built (ADR-0277, ADR-0278). Step 1: the rendered [global] has `log file = /run/samba/log.samba` and `max log size = 100` on every host, since RAM cannot be told from the system disk reliably (zram shows as a block device with ext4) and where /var/log is in RAM the file was in RAM already; one file for smbd, nmbd and the smbd of each client, without %m, so that clients add no files to /run. deploy/install.sh writes the same file. Tests: test_smbconf.py (TestGlobal), test_deploy_scripts.py; test_smbconf_testparm.py needs the device's testparm. Step 2: the account reconcile reads `pdbedit -P "password history"` at every start and sets it to 3 only when it differs, so that a wrong password that is one of an account's two previous passwords skips Samba's passdb write (test_smb_reconcile.py TestPasswordHistory and TestConsistent, against samba_fake.py). A password enters the history only when it is set while the policy is 3 (ADR-0278): an account whose password was set before, as every SMB account on the dev device, has an empty history, so its first change after the deploy does not spare retries of the password it replaced, and only its second change does. ADR-0159 and ADR-0278 took every other wrong password to write passdb.tdb once; measured on the device on 2026-11-09, none does while Samba's lockout policy is 0 (ADR-0310), so step 2 holds as written; limiting repeated failures is shares.smb-login-protection (ADR-0280). Unthrottled SMB sign-ins are an accepted risk (ADR-0280). Device check (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): test_smbconf_testparm.py passes against the device's testparm (scripts/dev/bin first on PATH); after the deploy, the reconcile's audit entry says "Set Samba's password history to 3 (it was 0)" once and `pdbedit -P "password history"` prints 3, and the next start reads it without setting it; after the apply's reload, /run/samba/log.samba exists and /var/log/samba/log.smbd and log.nmbd do not grow while clients connect, fail to sign in and Samba reloads; with an SMB account activated after the deploy, or one whose password was changed once after the deploy, change its password through UNOS, then scripts/dev/sd.sh measure around a sign-in with the password just replaced shows about 0 MiB and passdb.tdb's mtime unchanged, and a sign-in with a wrong password that the account never had leaves it as well while no lockout counts failures (ADR-0310); the same after a reboot. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): ADR-0278 and the device check above now say that a password enters the history only when it is set while the policy is 3, and ADR-0281 lists the whole [global] with the lines of step 1, superseding ADR-0087. Device check 2026-11-08: smb.conf has log file = /run/samba/log.samba, max log size = 100, log level = 1 auth_audit:2 and logging = syslog@2, and testparm accepts it. Device evidence of 2026-11-09: the smb area of scripts/dev/scenario.sh all, with the runtime files of main 12483dd, at 07:43 UTC and, after the reboot of 12:22 UTC, at 13:58 UTC passed its steps 3 (Samba runs UNOS's smb.conf with a password history of 3), 19 (the replaced password refused, passdb.tdb's time of change as before) and 23 (log file = /run/samba/log.samba, max log size = 100, and /var/log/samba's logs did not grow); its step 21 (a password the account never had, refused; 0.000 MiB at 13:58 UTC) did not look at passdb.tdb then. Measured at 14:24 UTC, after that reboot only (ADR-0310): with bad lockout attempt 0 and password history 3, four sign-ins with passwords a temporary account never had and one with its replaced password each left passdb.tdb's modification time as it was, at 0.000 to 0.016 MiB each; the account was deleted again (1.496 MiB for the whole measurement). GET /audit/logs with the search "password history" answered one entry, "SMB startup reconcile: Set Samba's password history to 3 (it was 0)" of 2026-11-08 04:02 UTC: every start since read the policy without setting it. Since 2026-11-09 the smb check's step with a wrong password compares passdb.tdb's modification time, and its step 3 expects bad lockout attempt 0 (a fresh-context review had found that the step compared nothing). That check passed on 2026-11-09 with the runtime files of main 31ac73b, in scripts/dev/scenario.sh all from 18:25:55 UTC and, after the reboot of 18:41 UTC, from 18:43:12 UTC: its step 3 read no lockout and a password history of 3, and its steps 19 (the replaced password) and 21 (a password the account never had) each left passdb.tdb's time of change as it was, at 0.016 and 0.000 MiB both times. Not checked on the device, and no longer asked for: setting a previous password again through UNOS, which smbpasswd as root does without the history's check (ADR-0278); neither the entry's steps nor the smb check, reviewed on 2026-11-09, name it. Description and step 2 reworded on 2026-11-10 by ADR-0334 (shares.smb-login-protection), which supersedes ADR-0310: Samba's lockout now counts each failed sign-in but a retry of one of the two previous passwords, which writes the account's passdb entry, and a locked account writes nothing until its lock ends. passes is false until the smb scenario check, whose step with a wrong password now expects passdb.tdb to change and whose lockout step expects the refused sign-in of the locked account to leave it as it was, passes with the lockout before and after a reboot (ADR-0018). Device check of the reworded step 2, 2026-11-10 with main bcc4eff, before and after the reboot of 22:01 UTC: the smb scenario check's step 19 (a replaced password leaves passdb.tdb as it was), step 21 (a wrong password changes it, as Samba counts it) and step 22 (a locked account's sign-in leaves it as it was) passed both times.

features.description: On a host whose smbd is confined by AppArmor, a share on a new folder is served without a restart of smbd
steps: An ADR decides how, once such a host is supported: for example update-apparmor-samba-profile, then apparmor_parser -r, after every change of share paths
On a test host whose smbd runs under an enforced Samba profile, create a share on a new folder: smbd serves it at once
On a host whose smbd is unconfined, such as the dev device, UNOS runs no AppArmor tool and changes no profile
features.notes: The dev device cannot check step 2: a read-only check on 2026-11-07 found AppArmor enabled in the kernel, no AppArmor utilities, no smbd or samba profile loaded, and smbd unconfined (ADR-0162).

features.description: SMB safeguards that existed only for a rollback to an older release are removed, or kept by an ADR
steps: SMB changes are audited with actions of their own; the rule to use only actions an older release knows is gone
An ADR decides whether the startup purge of SMB rows and the copy of foreign share sections still guard against restored databases and hand edits, and code kept only for rollbacks is removed
The tests of the removed paths are removed with them
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-10 (ADR-0320, which supersedes ADR-0157). Step 1: SMB changes are audited with actions of their own: smb_account_updated (a user's SMB account), smb_shares_imported (the import), smb_reconciled (the startup reconcile), smb_restored (the SMB state after a restore) and share_permissions_repaired (Repair permissions), and the NFS exports with nfs_export_created and nfs_export_deleted; the rule to use only actions an older release knows is gone, as the audit loader skips a line it cannot read and keeps the rest; the web UI names every action in English and Russian (test_smb_startup.py, test_smb_accounts.py, test_share_import.py, test_backup_restore.py and test_nfs.py expect the new actions and failed before; test_share_repair.py expects share_permissions_repaired and runs on Linux only; test_audit_log.py checks the names); ADR-0321 supersedes ADR-0292 for the NFS actions. Step 2: ADR-0320 keeps the startup purge of SMB rows (ADR-0137) and the copy of foreign share sections (ADR-0092), which guard restored and hand-edited databases and smb.conf files; their remarks on older releases in the comments of auth/router.py and shares/accounts.py are gone, and no code served a rollback alone. Step 3: no test served a removed path. Open: test_share_repair.py on Linux (scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh), which needs the supervisor's root filesystem in the device's /dev/shm, gone since the reboot of 2026-11-09; making it again (docker create and export) is an owner action. Not host-level: the audit log is the supervisor's file. 2026-11-19: the supervisor image's root filesystem made again in the device's /dev/shm (1.477 SD MiB, the command that scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh prints), and test_share_repair.py passed on Linux: 68 passed.

features.description: Repeated failed SMB sign-ins are slowed down or locked out, and SMB-bound passwords on a list of common passwords are refused
steps: After repeated failed SMB sign-ins, further attempts from that client or for that account are refused for a while (a rate limit or a lockout)
A password on a list of common passwords is refused with the reason when SMB is turned on with it, and when a user with SMB changes to it
features.notes: Step 2 built (ADR-0279): constants.smb_password_problem refuses a password whose casefolded form is a line of supervisor/src/shares/common_passwords.txt (about 1450 passwords compiled for UNOS, each of at least 8 characters) with "SMB passwords must not be common passwords: this one is on the list of passwords that attackers try first", after the rules of length, size and control characters, wherever SMB-bound passwords are checked. UNOS checks only the passwords that it gives to Samba: Samba's own password change (SAMR) took a common password without UNOS until shares.password-changes-only-through-unos made Samba refuse every such change (ADR-0342), so step 2 holds for every change; and an account that got its password before the list keeps it until its next change. The password that goes back to Samba when the user's own password change fails after smbpasswd ran (ADR-0124) is checked without the list, so that such an account keeps SMB (test_smb_accounts.py TestCommitFailureAfterSmbpasswd and TestSmbpasswdTimeout, test_smb_models.py). Tests: test_smb_models.py (the rule in any case, the order of the rules, the format of the list), test_smb_accounts.py TestCommonPasswords (creating a user with SMB creates nothing; an administrator's and the user's own activation; the password change of an active account by the user and by an administrator; users without SMB keep any password; the text of the E2E fake), users.spec.ts 'creating a user with SMB and a common password is refused with the reason, and creates nobody' (stand-in, the real server) and 'a common password is refused for SMB, and the dialog shows why' (route fakes), account-smb.spec.ts 'turning SMB on with it is refused with the reason and how to go on' (stand-in, the real server) and 'with SMB on, a common password is refused with the reason and nothing changes' (route fakes: the stand-in has no Samba, so no account is active there). Step 2 changes nothing on the host. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): a failed change away from a common password that an account got before the list now puts it back instead of turning SMB off, and ADR-0279 names the two exceptions above. Step 1 built (ADR-0334, which supersedes ADR-0280 and ADR-0310; the owner delegated the choice): the startup reconcile keeps Samba's account policies "lockout duration" 5 (minutes), "reset count minutes" 5 and "bad lockout attempt" 5 beside "password history" 3 (accounts.ACCOUNT_POLICIES, ensure_account_policy): pdbedit -P reads each at every start and pdbedit -P -C sets one only when it differs, the threshold after the two times; a policy that cannot be read or set is a problem of the reconcile, and the others go on. Samba then counts each failed sign-in of an account but a retry of one of its two previous passwords (ADR-0278), locks the account at the fifth, and for 5 minutes refuses every sign-in of it, the right password too, with NT_STATUS_ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT, writing nothing to passdb.tdb meanwhile; each counted failure writes the account's passdb entry, which changes step 2 of shares.samba-runtime-writes (ADR-0334). Tests: test_smb_reconcile.py TestLockout and TestPasswordHistory against samba_fake.py, which knows the policies with Samba's defaults; test_restore_accounts.py. Device check (ADR-0018), not run yet: the smb scenario check (scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb) before and after a reboot of the deployed tree, with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): its step 3 reads the four policies, its step with a wrong password expects passdb.tdb to change, and its last step that signs in expects 5 wrong passwords in a row to lock the check's account, so that the right password is then refused with NT_STATUS_ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT and passdb.tdb stays as it was; the check deletes the account while it is locked (test_dev_scenarios.py). Not in the check, which does not wait for them: the end of the lock after 5 minutes and a count that starts again after 5 minutes without a failure. Accepted with ADR-0334: anyone on the LAN who knows a username can keep its SMB account locked. The threshold is set only when both times are UNOS's: when one cannot be read or set, the lockout stays as it was and the reconcile says why (test_smb_reconcile.py TestLockout). Turning a user's SMB off and on again ends a lock. Device check 2026-11-10 with main bcc4eff: scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb passed its 28 steps at 21:59 UTC (3.895 MiB) and again after the reboot of 22:01 UTC (3.418 MiB): step 3 read the four policies (history 3, lockout duration 5, reset count minutes 5, bad lockout attempt 5), step 21 a wrong password that changed passdb.tdb (0.305 MiB), step 22 five wrong passwords that locked the account so that the right one was refused with NT_STATUS_ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT, leaving passdb.tdb as it was (0.133 MiB); pdbedit -P read the same policies after the reboot.

features.description: Failed SMB sign-ins are logged with the client and the account, so that a client that keeps failing can be found
steps: A failed SMB sign-in is logged through Samba's auth_audit class, with the client's address and the account name
An administrator finds these lines in System > Logs and sees which client keeps failing
features.notes: Built (ADR-0277). Step 1: the rendered [global] has `log level = 1 auth_audit:2`, `logging = syslog@2` and `debug timestamp = no`: Samba logs a failed sign-in in its class auth_audit at level 2 and a successful one at 3, the syslog backend takes level 2, and the other classes stay at level 1 (test_smbconf.py TestGlobal); deploy/install.sh writes the same (test_deploy_scripts.py), and ADR-0281 lists the whole [global] with these lines, superseding ADR-0087. Step 2: the source Samba of System > Logs (smbd.service, nmbd.service) lists these lines newest first as notices, and its search finds them by `Auth:` or by a client's address (test_logs_sources.py TestFailedSmbSignIns, against the fake journal; logs.spec.ts 'failed SMB sign-ins: Samba lists them, and a search shows the client that keeps failing', with route fakes: the stand-in has no journal); docs/USER_GUIDE.md (Logs) says how. Device check (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): test_smbconf_testparm.py passes against the device's testparm; after the deploy's apply reloaded Samba, a sign-in with a wrong password (for example smbclient on the device against 127.0.0.1 as the account test) adds one journal entry of smbd.service with priority notice that starts with `Auth:` and holds `status [NT_STATUS_WRONG_PASSWORD]`, the account and `remote host [ipv4:127.0.0.1:`; a successful sign-in adds none; GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=samba&search=Auth: lists the entry and System > Logs shows it; Samba's other messages come without their header line; the same after a reboot. Device check 2026-11-08: a failed SMB sign-in (smbclient with an account that does not exist) was logged by auth_audit with the account, the status and the client's address, and GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=samba&search=<account> found it. `test_smbconf_testparm.py` against the device's testparm (Samba 4.22.6), 2026-11-08: its logging test expected a `log level` line and `debug timestamp = no`; the dump of `testparm -s` shows no `log level` line, not even for a debug class that Samba lacks, and names `debug timestamp` `timestamp logs`, so of `log level` testparm checks only the parameter's name, never its classes or levels. The test now asserts `timestamp logs = no` beside the log file, its size limit and the syslog level, and all 11 tests pass there (0 MiB); the level of auth_audit rests on test_smbconf.py. Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC), from the journal of the smb scenario check's run at 23:03 UTC: its account's two wrong passwords each added one entry of smbd.service with priority notice that starts with `Auth:` and holds `status [NT_STATUS_WRONG_PASSWORD]`, the account and `remote host [ipv4:127.0.0.1:`; its successful sign-ins added none, so auth_audit logs at level 2, not 3; no smbd message of that run has a header line; and GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=samba&search=<account> lists both entries.

features.description: Repair permissions runs as a background job, so a large share is repaired in one run that the page follows live
steps: Start Repair permissions on a large share: the request answers at once, and the job runs until the share is done, without the 240 s limit of a request
Shares shows the job's progress and its end over the WebSocket, without polling
One repair runs at a time: a second start while one runs is refused
features.notes: Built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0363, which supersedes ADR-0155 and ADR-0006): POST .../repair-permissions answers 202 at once with the job running and walks in a daemon thread of its own until the share is done, stopped (DELETE on the same path, 202; 409 when no repair of that share runs) or 24 hours have passed (repair.TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS; no entry limit); a second start of any share while one runs answers 409 "A permissions repair is already running". The walk reports its counts about once a second, and /ws/v1/events sends administrators {"type": "repair"} with the running job and then its end, which GET then answers as the share's last run; the Repair dialog shows the counts and Stop repair, the share's card says Repairing permissions, and the page reads the shares again at the end, without polling. Backend tests: test_share_repair_job.py, test_ws_auth.py (TestTheRepairOnTheEventsSocket); the walk's stop and progress and the endpoints on real folders are Linux-only tests of test_share_repair.py, not run on macOS. E2E: webui/tests/shares.spec.ts on the stand-in. Host-level (it changes files on the pools): done only after the device check and a reboot check (ADR-0018). Open on the dev device: scripts/dev/scenario.sh shares, whose Repair step now expects the 202 answer running and waits until GET names the run's end, with each step's SD MiB; a second start and the stop cannot be shown there, since the check's share is repaired in moments; a repair of a large share, followed on the Shares page and stopped there, is a check by hand. Review fixes 2026-11-12: the events socket sends administrators the repair right after auth_ok, null when none has run, and the web UI keeps it (null too), so a restart no longer leaves a dead repair showing; a share deleted, renamed or moved stops its repair, and the last result is kept by share id; a stop of the supervisor stops the repair and waits up to 5 s for its audit entry; the end is published only after the audit write; the walk re-reads the mount table with each progress report. Device check 2026-11-12 (the integration tree b9aaea5 before and after the reboot from the API at 19:37:03 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 19:37:58; both containers healthy by 19:38:50), and main 7827340's tree 5deee90 after its deploy): scenario.sh shares passed its 25 steps and skipped the ACL one each time (3.945, 3.227 and 4.004 MiB), its Repair step answered 202 running and GET then named the run's end. The Linux-only tests of test_share_repair.py did not run: scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh needs its rootfs in the device's RAM again (an owner action).

features.description: The parser of /etc/exports reads every line form that exportfs accepts and leaves the lines UNOS did not write as they are
steps: Tests give the parser of supervisor/src/shares/exports.py every line form of exports(5): comments, continuation lines, quoted and escaped paths, several clients on one line, default and per-client options
Each line is read as exportfs reads it, or reported as unreadable and left in the file unchanged
Adding or removing an export changes only the lines that UNOS wrote
features.notes: Built: exports.py ports the reader of nfs-utils 2.8 (support/nfs/xio.c, getexportent and parseopts of support/nfs/exports.c). test_nfs.py gives it every line form and checks where exportfs stops reading a file; with the fake host it checks that an add or a delete changes only the lines that UNOS wrote, those exactly in its form (a line written by hand into UNOS's file is listed but never deleted), keeps every other byte, and changes nothing while a file has a line that exportfs cannot read (ADR-0292). Not passing: step 2 is checked only against the port's own expectations, and step 3 writes a host file, a host-level change (ADR-0018); the real sh, od and atomic write ran only on macOS. Open, on the device after the owner installed nfs-kernel-server and deployed: GET /shares/nfs compared with `exportfs -v` for hand-written lines of /etc/exports and of /etc/exports.d (continuations, quotes, several clients, '-' options), and a line that exportfs cannot read named with its file and line; an add and a delete keep every other line of /etc/exports.d/unos.exports byte for byte (sha256 of the file without UNOS's line, before and after), the host's dash and GNU od included; then the same after a reboot. Device check 2026-11-19 of 15cf31d (mvp.batch-15, deployed 07:50 to 08:01 UTC: sync 6.215, build-supervisor 17.715, build-webui 21.367, up 6.465 SD MiB), before and after the reboot from the API at 08:21:50 UTC (all 7 containers healthy at 08:23:04): a fresh check volume with the hand-written /etc/exports.d/unoscheck.exports: GET /shares/nfs equal to exportfs -v (6 pairs), the unreadable line named with its file and physical line 7 (exportfs's own message says 6, as its counter skips comment lines), an add refused with 409 while that line is there; without it an add and a delete kept every other byte of unos.exports; after the reboot the same comparison, and an add and a delete kept the rest of unos.exports byte for byte (sha256 equal, also to before the reboot) with the hand-written file unchanged; then the file deleted, exportfs -ra, the volume deleted (0.016 to 0.387 SD MiB a step). The earlier check of 9061fb0 that day, before and after its reboot, gave the same.

features.description: An administrator installs an app from the catalog onto a chosen mounted pool
steps: On Apps, the catalog lists the apps by category, with search
Install asks for the pool, and only mounted pools are offered
The app's data folders are made inside that pool, with no '..' and no symlinks, and placeholder secrets are refused
The installed list shows the app with the host folders it uses, and warns about data outside mounted pools
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (transmission reinstalled with its login on the pool data). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): GET /apps/installed lists transmission with the same host folders on the pool data as before the reboot, its container runs again, and GET /apps/catalog lists 70 apps by category. The stand-in has no Docker: the catalog cards are skipped there.

features.description: The transmission app installs only with a web login, and its RPC refuses requests without it
steps: Installing transmission without USER and PASS is refused
With both, the container gets them, and its web UI and RPC answer 401 without the login
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (the RPC answered 401 without the login). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): transmission's RPC answers 401 without the login.

features.description: An administrator starts, stops, restarts and uninstalls installed apps, and a start first checks that the app's data is on a mounted pool
steps: On Apps > Installed, Stop and Start an app: its state follows
An app whose pool is not mounted does not start, and the answer says which pool to mount
Uninstall removes the container and keeps the app's data
features.notes: Built (ADR-0256): start, restart, stop and uninstall act only on containers with the unos.app label (400 for another container, 404 for an unknown one); stop and uninstall run in a worker thread (ADR-0254); uninstall removes the container without its volumes and leaves the data folders. TestStopAndUninstall and TestStartChecks (the 409 names the pool) prove the steps against a fake Docker, and the Installed apps tests of webui/tests/apps.spec.ts the Installed tab with route fakes (the stand-in has no Docker). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). On the device: Stop and Start of transmission on Apps > Installed change its state; with the pool data unmounted (an owner action), Start is refused with the message that names the pool 'data'; Uninstall of an app installed for the check removes its container and leaves its folders under /mnt/pools/data/apps. Device check 2026-11-08: Stop and Start of transmission through Apps > Installed changed its state. Open: the start of an app whose pool is unmounted, which waits for unmounting to work on the device (storage.mount-and-unmount). Device check 2026-11-08: Stop and Start of transmission changed its state, and starting it while the pool data was unmounted was refused (409) with the folder that is not on a mounted pool. Open: Uninstall, not run on the owner's transmission. Device check 2026-11-19 (main 9061fb0), after the reboot from the API at 05:57:39 UTC: Uninstall of Linkwarden and of Paperless-ngx, installed for the check, removed their containers and networks and kept their folders under /mnt/pools/data/apps (Linkwarden 1402 entries before and after; Paperless-ngx 30 before and 27 after, its database db.sqlite3 and generated file kept: UNOS's uninstall deletes no file of an app, and the three were the app's own files of its run), each with app_uninstalled in the audit log (2.145 and 2.141 SD MiB). With the checks of 2026-11-08 every step has passed on the device.

features.description: An administrator manages Docker containers and images: lists them, starts, stops and restarts containers, reads their logs live, and pulls and removes images
steps: Containers lists every container with its state, and filters by state
Start, Stop and Restart act on the container
The logs of a container stream live over the WebSocket
Images lists the images; pull adds one, and remove deletes one that no container uses
features.notes: Built (ADR-0255): the Images tab of the Containers page lists, pulls and removes images, never forced. The server refuses an image that a container uses, running or stopped, with 409 naming the containers; otherwise it removes each tag of the image and then the rest, because Docker deletes an image with more than one tag by its ID only when forced (TestImageRemoval, against a fake that refuses as Docker's classic image store does). The drawer's Logs tab follows /ws/v1/logs/{id} with the first-message auth instead of polling the HTTP log; each line carries Docker's timestamp, and the server closes with 1000 when the log ends or cannot be read (TestTheLogSocketClosesWhenItsLogEnds, under a real uvicorn). On the stand-in (no Docker), webui/tests/containers.spec.ts covers every step with route fakes and page.routeWebSocket, with the ends of a stream (1000, 1011, 4403, 4401) and the view of the newest 500,000 characters. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). On the device: Containers lists transmission with its state and the state filter Running keeps it; Stop and Start change its state; its Logs tab shows its last lines with their times and a new line live without a reload, and after a Stop from the drawer says that the log stream ended; Images lists lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission and alpine; Pull of a small image (an owner action, ADR-0211, with its SD writes) adds it, a second tag of it (docker tag, an owner action) shows in its row, and Remove deletes the image with both tags; Remove of the transmission image is refused with the answer that names the transmission container. Device check 2026-11-08: Containers listed transmission as running, Stop and Start changed its state (exited, running), and the Images view listed the host's 7 images. Pulling and removing an image were not run there: a pull writes the whole image to the SD card.

features.description: An administrator sets memory and CPU limits for an app's container
steps: Set a memory limit and a CPU quota for an app: docker inspect shows them
The app's page shows its use against the limits, and crossing one sends an alert
features.notes: Built 2026-11-17 on the workstation (ADR-0390); host-level, as Docker's containers get the limits and their use is read from the host's cgroups (ADR-0018). Per container: PUT /apps/installed/{container}/limits (memory_limit in bytes and cpu_limit in CPUs, both required, null for none) sends Docker's update (Memory and MemorySwap the same, CpuPeriod 100000 and CpuQuota), at once and without a restart, reads the container again (a limit that Docker discarded with a warning answers 409, what it applied is kept), and keeps the limits in the new table app_resource_limits for the app's next install, which creates each container with its own (an uninstall keeps them); bounds: memory from 64 MiB to below MemTotal and, when set or lowered on a running container, at least its use now (memory.current without inactive_file, plus memory.swap.current) with a margin of 10%, at least 32 MiB, refused with 409 when its cgroup cannot be read; CPU from 0.1 to the host's CPUs in hundredths (GET /apps/limits); a CPU limit set with docker update --cpus (NanoCpus) is shown and not changed (409); removing a CPU limit sets CpuQuota -1, removing a memory limit sets Memory to twice MemTotal and MemorySwap -1 (Docker cannot unset a container's memory limit), shown as none; audited as app_limits_changed. Every 30 s one pass (src/apps/usage.py, in the lifespan) asks Docker for its summary list of the running unos.app containers and its oom events since the last pass, and reads memory.current, memory.stat, memory.max, memory.swap.current, cpu.stat and cpu.max of each container's cgroup through /proc/1/root/sys/fs/cgroup (system.slice/docker-<id>.scope, or docker/<id>); GET /apps/installed answers each container's resources (limits from HostConfig, memory_used without inactive_file, cpu_used in CPUs, sampled_at); problems of the source apps: app_memory (90%, cleared below 80%), app_cpu (90% of the CPU limit averaged over 5 minutes, cleared below 70%) and app_oom (an error from Docker's oom event, kept an hour after the last), each alerted once. The Installed tab's cards list each container's use against its limits with bars, and a Limits dialog. Tested on the workstation: test_app_limits.py (the fake Docker's update, list and events, fake cgroup files), apps-limits.spec.ts and the dialog's view of mobile-layout.spec.ts on route fakes; reviewed in a fresh context, its findings fixed (ADR-0390). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), on the dev device (a BPI-W3, 8 GB, 8 CPUs, Docker with cgroup v2, Immich and transmission installed), each command under scripts/dev/sd.sh measure <label> -- with its SD MiB reported; the changes of limits, the docker exec and the reinstall at the owner's word (ADR-0211). (1) After the deploy: scripts/dev/check.sh (OK, unos-supervisor within its CPU budget with the 30 s passes, ADR-0374); scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup; docker info --format "{{.CgroupDriver}} {{.CgroupVersion}}"' prints cgroup2fs and systemd 2; scripts/dev/api.py GET /apps/limits answers memory_max the host's MemTotal in bytes and cpu_max 8; after a minute, GET /apps/installed answers memory_used and cpu_used for immich, immich-database, immich-redis, immich-machine-learning and transmission, each memory_used within a few MiB of scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker stats --no-stream --format "{{.Name}} {{.MemUsage}} {{.CPUPerc}}"', and no limits. (2) Set: echo '{"memory_limit": 1073741824, "cpu_limit": 2}' | scripts/dev/api.py PUT /apps/installed/immich-database/limits - answers 200; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker inspect -f "{{.HostConfig.Memory}} {{.HostConfig.MemorySwap}} {{.HostConfig.CpuPeriod}} {{.HostConfig.CpuQuota}} {{.HostConfig.NanoCpus}} {{.State.StartedAt}}" immich-database' prints 1073741824 1073741824 100000 200000 0 and the StartedAt from before (no restart), and with d=/sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/docker-$(docker inspect -f {{.Id}} immich-database).scope, cat $d/memory.max $d/memory.swap.max $d/cpu.max prints 1073741824, 0 and 200000 100000; GET /apps/installed lists memory_limit 1073741824 and cpu_limit 2.0 for immich-database, GET /audit/logs the entry app_limits_changed, and Immich stays healthy (pong on 2283). A limit below immich-database's use plus its margin (memory_used + 10%, at least 32 MiB) answers 409 and changes nothing. Expected SD writes: under 0.2 MiB per change (Docker's hostconfig.json and config.v2.json of the container, the database row, the audit line, the API call). (3) Crossing without harm, in transmission (its own processes stay below the limit; the owner runs the docker exec): read its memory_used U from GET /apps/installed (about 20 MiB) and set its memory_limit to 100663296 (96 MiB, above U + 32 MiB); the owner runs scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker exec transmission sh -c "(head -c $((88 - U))m /dev/zero; sleep 75) | tail > /dev/null"' with U in whole MiB, which holds about 88 MiB (92%) for 75 s: within 30 s GET /notifications/logs has one warning alert 'transmission is near its memory limit' (the health banner shows it in a browser), and once the command ended it is gone at the next pass with nothing sent. Then the OOM: the owner runs scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker exec transmission sh -c "tail /dev/zero > /dev/null"', whose tail the kernel ends at the limit (the largest process of the cgroup, not transmission-daemon); scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker events --since 5m --until "$(date +%s)" --filter event=oom --filter label=unos.app' shows the oom of transmission and its cgroup's memory.events oom_kill 1; within 30 s GET /notifications/logs has one error alert 'transmission ran out of memory', and transmission still runs (RestartCount as before) and its web login answers; then its limits null. (4) Remove: echo '{"memory_limit": null, "cpu_limit": null}' | scripts/dev/api.py PUT /apps/installed/immich-database/limits -: docker inspect prints Memory twice the host's MemTotal in bytes, MemorySwap -1 and CpuQuota -1, its cgroup's cpu.max max 100000 and memory.max that number or max; record memory.swap.max (Docker may leave 0 until the container's next start, ADR-0390); GET /apps/installed lists no limits. Set it again to 1 GiB and 2 CPUs for (5) and (6). (5) Reinstall (the owner's): uninstall transmission with a limit of 256 MiB set, then install it again (its login values, ADR-0219): docker inspect transmission shows Memory 268435456 again and the install's audit entry ends with the limits kept for it. (6) Reboot check after the owner's reboot: check.sh OK; docker inspect immich-database still prints 1073741824 1073741824 100000 200000, its cgroup's memory.max and cpu.max as in (2), GET /apps/installed lists the limits and, after a minute, the use of every running container; scripts/dev/sd.sh measure idle -- sleep 600 shows no more than the idle background (the passes write nothing). Clean-up: the limits removed again with null, or kept at the owner's word. Device check 2026-11-17 (mvp.batch-8 at 320d3ec, deployed 2026-11-17 18:58-18:59 UTC; reboot from the API at 19:23:11 UTC (the boot of 19:24:4x, all containers healthy by 19:25:26); scenario.sh all after it: 187 steps passed, smart's sleep steps skipped while apps use the pool): cgroup v2 with systemd; the use of Immich's four containers and transmission matched docker stats within 0.1 MiB; immich-database at 1 GiB and 2 CPUs: docker inspect and its cgroup files as set, no restart, audit entry, Immich pong (0.254); 85 MiB answered 409 (at least 118 MiB); transmission at 96 MiB with about 88 MiB held 75 s: the warning at 19:15:24, gone after; a tail killed by the OOM killer alone (exit 137), Docker's oom event, oom_kill 1, transmission still running, the error alert at 19:18:05. Removing a memory limit of a running container failed with 500 (Docker 29.9 with runc 1.5 keeps the swap limit for MemorySwap -1 and refuses the memory limit above it): fixed in 7f5dd29 (a swap limit twice the new memory limit; the fake Docker refuses -1 as the device did), deployed at 20:2x UTC, and both removals then answered 200 with Memory 2x and MemorySwap 4x MemTotal, no restart (0.297, 0.227). After the reboot the limits were still in docker inspect and the cgroups, and GET /apps/installed showed limits and use. Not run: the reinstall with a limit, since transmission's image tag floats and its install pulls.

features.description: When Docker does not answer, the app and container pages and their API say so with 503
steps: Stop Docker on a test host: the container and app endpoints answer 503 with the reason, and the pages show it
features.notes: Passed 2026-11-10 (ADR-0323). The test host is the stand-in, which has no Docker socket: on the dev device a stopped Docker stops UNOS with it. The containers API answers 503 "Docker is not available: <docker-py's reason>" on every route when Docker cannot be reached (no socket, a refused or broken connection); the Apps API does so for the first request of each route to Docker (the listing, the lookup of an app, the name check of an install), and an operation that fails after it keeps its 500 "Failed to ..." (ADR-0254, ADR-0256). A read timeout and an error that Docker answers keep their status (TestADockerThatDoesNotAnswer of test_containers.py and test_apps.py; 41 of its first tests failed before). On the stand-in, api.spec.ts finds the 503 and the reason for GET /containers, /containers/images and /apps/installed, which skipped there before, and the "Containers without Docker (stand-in)" specs of containers.spec.ts find the reason alone on the Containers tab (no counts, search, empty list or Create button), on its Images tab and, with the 503, on the Apps page; both skip on the test stack. A fresh-context review found the step met for a Docker that is down, and: the tab's shared error variable, which the Create dialog cleared, a broken stream or chunked answer that gave 500, a read timeout of a long stop called unavailable, an error answer to the version query called unavailable, the Apps API's operations, which ADR-0254 and ADR-0256 keep at 500, the API checks on the test stack against ADR-0215, an Apps-page spec that passed before, and overstated records. All fixed as ADR-0323 says; left: the Apps page's empty texts under the error (apps.catalog-without-docker) and the dashboard, which does not show the 503. Not host-level: it changes the answers, not the host's containers.

features.description: The code for apps that older versions installed under /mnt/pools/default is gone
steps: The checks and messages for apps without a pool label, whose data is in /mnt/pools/default, are removed from supervisor/src/apps and supervisor/src/health
The web UI's types and texts for them are removed
tests/test_apps.py passes without the cases of older versions
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-10. Step 1 (ADR-0318, which supersedes ADR-0039): supervisor/src/apps no longer counts a catalog pool volume outside the pools base as data, only what lies under the pools base as configured or with symbolic links resolved (test_data_under_a_pools_base_reached_through_a_link_is_checked), and the start of an installed app has one 409 for data that is not on a mounted pool, which names the pool that the folder lies on (TestStartChecks test_the_answer_names_the_pool_that_holds_the_folder, which failed before: the answer named the install's pool); the 409 for apps without a pool label, whose data was in /mnt/pools/default, is gone, and so are the comments of apps/schemas.py and health/router.py on them (test_no_code_for_apps_of_older_versions, which failed before). Step 2: AppStorageWarning shows only the warning of a pool that is not mounted; the texts systemDisk and systemDiskTitle of the apps catalog and the comments of webui/src/lib/api/apps.ts on older versions are gone, and both fakes of apps.spec.ts that showed the warning are apps whose pool is not mounted. Step 3: the tests of an app under /mnt/pools/default and of an override outside the pools base are gone; test_apps.py passes; 2026-11-12: the last test comment on app data of older versions (test_pool_persistence.py, test_only_btrfs_pools_are_monitored) now names a folder under the pools base that is not a pool. Open: host-level (GLOSSARY.md: the host's containers): on the dev device, an app installed on a pool whose pool is not mounted is listed with its folders outside the pools and its start answers the 409 that names the pool, with the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), as for apps.manage-installed.

features.description: Docker calls of the containers API run off the event loop, so a slow pull or stop does not hold up other requests
steps: While an image is pulled, or a container is stopped, removed or listed, GET /api/v1/health and other requests are still answered
Every Docker call of supervisor/src/containers/router.py runs in a worker thread, as start and restart already do
A test with a Docker call that blocks shows another request answered meanwhile
features.notes: Built (ADR-0254): every route of supervisor/src/containers/router.py, and the stop and uninstall of the Apps API, call Docker in a worker thread, each request within the client's 60 s timeout (a pull has no deadline). TestDockerCallsOffTheEventLoop checks every route of the router; TestRequestsAnsweredWhileDockerBlocks shows, under a real uvicorn, GET /api/v1/health and GET /api/v1/apps/catalog answered while a pull, a stop, a removal or a listing blocks in a fake Docker. Open, because Docker containers are host-level (GLOSSARY.md): the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), in which GET /api/v1/health answers within a second while the device pulls an image (an owner action, ADR-0211) and while transmission is stopped from the Containers page. Device checks 2026-11-19: on 9061fb0, GET /api/v1/health timed once a second answered within 0.047 s while Paperless-ngx's images were pulled (177 samples), 0.040 s during Linkwarden's (140) and 0.048 s while transmission was stopped and started through the containers API, every answer 200; on 15cf31d after the reboot from the API at 08:21:50 UTC, transmission stopped and started again: the slowest of 20 answers 0.062 s, none over a second, transmission running after (3.977 SD MiB).

features.description: An app can be installed to run in the SMB group, so that it can use a share's folder
steps: Install offers to run the app in the SMB group, which sets its PGID to 70000 (unos-smb)
Such an app reads and writes the share folder it was given; an app installed without the option still cannot
features.notes: Built (ADR-0274): the install option run_in_unos_smb, the checkbox "Run in the group unos-smb" of the app's details, exists for the apps of linuxserver.io images with a pool folder outside {pool}/apps (can_run_in_unos_smb) and adds PUID 80000 (SMB_APP_UID, no other app's user), PGID 70000 and UMASK 007 to the container's environment; other images ignore PUID and PGID, and the option is refused for them and for apps with only their own data. PUID and PGID are no longer environment values (400), and the Environment tab shows them read-only. An install refuses a folder that is, lies inside or holds a share's folder without the option; with it, a share's folder is mounted, and a read-only folder may hold shares, but never a folder inside a share, a share's folder for the app's own data or a writable folder that holds a share. A snapshot folder (.snapshots), the trash (.unos-trash) and folders in them are refused for every app. GET /apps/installed says whether an app runs in the group (runs_in_unos_smb, from its container's PGID), and the Installed tab and the details show it. TestRunInUnosSmb, TestShareFolders, TestInstalledApps and TestConstants prove the environment, the refusals and the list against a fake Docker, and the unos-smb tests of webui/tests/apps.spec.ts the form and the installed view with route fakes (the stand-in has no Docker). Not covered: a share made later on the folder of an app outside the group is not refused (ADR-0274). Open, because Docker apps and share folders are host-level (GLOSSARY.md): the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).
