On the device: install a linuxserver.io app (for example syncthing) without the option, then uninstall it (its data stays). Install it again with the option and its data folder set to the folder of a share: it starts, its /config belongs to uid 80000 after the start, and docker inspect shows PUID=80000, PGID=70000 and UMASK=007. Inside the container its user (abc, uid 80000) lists and reads the share's files and creates a file and a folder there, which get the group unos-smb with 0660 and 2770, and an SMB user with write access changes that file. Record the owner, group and mode of the share's folder after the app's first start: root or uid 80000 with the group unos-smb and 2770 passes, any other owner (such as uid 1000) or mode fails. The same install without the option is refused with 400 before any image is pulled, and so is one that sets PUID through the API. The Installed tab shows Runs in the group unos-smb for the app. Uninstall the app afterwards; its data stays.

features.description: The App Store shows the app catalog when Docker does not answer
steps: With Docker down, Apps lists the catalog and says that the installed apps cannot be loaded
On the stand-in, which has no Docker, the catalog-cards test of webui/tests/appstore.spec.ts runs instead of being skipped
features.notes: webui/src/routes/apps/+page.svelte loaded the catalog and the installed apps in one Promise.all, so a failure of either hid both. Passed 2026-11-10 (ADR-0327): the page loads them each on its own, with a state each, lists the catalog as soon as it came, and shows a count only from a load that succeeded. Step 1: on the stand-in, whose supervisor answers GET /apps/installed with 503 (ADR-0323), the Apps page lists the catalog, says "The installed apps could not be loaded: Docker is not available: ...", gives only the number of apps available, and its Installed tab has no count and no "No apps installed" (containers.spec.ts, "the Apps page lists the catalog and says that the installed apps cannot be loaded"); with the answer held on a route fake, the catalog is listed meanwhile (appstore.spec.ts, "the catalog does not wait for the installed apps"). Step 2: "should show app cards in catalog" of appstore.spec.ts runs on the stand-in without its skip. Both of the first checks failed before the change. A fresh-context review found both steps met, and: the catalog still waited for Docker's answer under one loading flag; counts of 0 during a refresh; a spec that matched the tab with its count; an unnamed catalog error; and the record. All fixed. Not host-level.

features.description: An administrator creates a configuration backup, encrypted with a passphrase if wanted, and downloads it
steps: In System > Backup & Restore, create a backup: it is listed under a unique name, also when two are made in the same second
With a passphrase the backup is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and named .tar.gz.enc
Download saves the file with the session, and a download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page
A backup that cannot be created, deleted or downloaded is reported on the page

features.description: An administrator uploads a backup file, and malformed or hostile archives are refused before they are stored
steps: Upload a .tar.gz backup: it is checked in one streaming pass and then listed
Upload an encrypted .tar.gz.enc backup: it is stored as uploaded_<date>_<time>.tar.gz.enc and checked when it is restored
A plain backup named .tar.gz.enc, a corrupt archive and a file over 64 MiB are refused and leave nothing behind

features.description: An administrator restores a backup, an encrypted one with its passphrase, and the configuration comes back
steps: Restore a backup made in the web UI: users, two-factor settings, API tokens and shares come back
An encrypted backup restores with its passphrase and is refused without it
A restore that does not fit into the RAM-backed /tmp answers 507 and changes nothing
A second restore while one runs is refused
features.notes: The SMB side of a restore is shares.restore-keeps-smb-with-proof. A restore renders smb.conf from the restored database and reconciles the SMB accounts (supervisor/src/backup/router.py), a host-level change (GLOSSARY.md): Device check of 2026-11-11 (PROGRESS.md): a configuration backup put into the backup list from an off-device copy, and an encrypted backup with its passphrase, each restored with "success" (database and smb_config), with the users, SMB shares, API tokens, smb.conf and Samba's passdb users the same before and after; the refusals without the passphrase and with a wrong one are steps of scripts/dev/scenario.sh backups, which passed before and after the two reboots that followed. Steps 3 and 4 (507 for a restore that does not fit, a second restore refused) are shown by the tests only.

features.description: A scheduled backup task makes backups and keeps only the newest N scheduled ones
steps: Add a backup task with retention 3 in System > Scheduler
Each run stores auto_backup_<date>_<time>.tar.gz.enc, complete before it is listed, and two runs at once both succeed
The fourth run deletes the oldest scheduled backup and never a manual one
features.notes: webui/tests/scheduler.spec.ts makes a backup task with Keep Count 3 in the form on the stand-in and runs it four times (Run now): each run stores one auto_backup_*.tar.gz.enc, the fourth deletes the oldest, and the Backup & Restore tab lists the three newest and the manual backup. The backend tests check that a backup is listed only once complete and that two runs at once both succeed. Not host-level: the backups stay in the supervisor's /data. Device check: 2026-11-06 (two scheduled backups at once), before scheduled backups were encrypted (ADR-0325).

features.description: Backups of the configuration and of the pools' data are copied off the device and restored from there
steps: On System > Backup & Restore, Save and test of a copy target, a folder on a disk mounted below /mnt or an S3-compatible store with its keys, with the password typed twice (at least 12 characters), opens the copy repository with restic or makes it when none is there; a folder on the system disk, a wrong password and a store out of reach are refused with the reason, and nothing is saved

The repository password and the S3 secret key are kept only in /data/offsite_secrets.json, mode 0600: in no answer of the API, settings or status file, log line, configuration backup or argument of restic

A task of the type offsite_copy, or Run now, copies the configuration archive and the chosen pool folders without their snapshots and trash, removes the snapshots beyond the retention, checks the repository with a share of its data and tests the restore of the configuration; a step that fails fails the run with restic's message and is alerted as a task problem, files that vanished while restic read them are a note, files that cannot be read fail the run once every step ran, and a run while another copy runs is skipped as a success

The page shows the last copy with its files, check and restore test, and the snapshots; Restore configuration puts a snapshot's configuration into the backup list, and Restore files restores a snapshot or one of its folders into a new folder of a pool without overwriting anything
features.notes: Built (ADR-0337): restic in a layer of its own of the supervisor image; supervisor/src/offsite/ with the settings in /data/offsite.json, the secrets in /data/offsite_secrets.json (0600) and the last copy and restore in /data/offsite_status.json; the copy's steps unlock, the configuration from standard input, the folders, forget with --prune, check and the restore test, for the Scheduler's task type offsite_copy and Run now; the restores of the configuration into the backup list and of files into a new folder restored-<UTC time> of a pool; the section Off-device copy of System > Backup & Restore. restic is not installed on the workstation: the backend tests and the local stand-in run the fake of supervisor/tests/fake_restic.py, so restic itself runs first on the device. The test stack skips the E2E main flow: its image has no restic, and its pools share the filesystem of its data volume, which the copy refuses as the system disk. The dev device ran e663f14 with the real restic 0.18: scenario.sh offsite OK (12 steps), and a copy, Restore configuration and the regular restore of that backup left the users, shares, tokens, smb.conf and passdb the same. The review in a fresh context (ADR-0017) of e663f14 found 13 points, each fixed with a test that failed on e663f14 (PROGRESS.md, 2026-11-11): the folders held open while restic runs and the Storage page's refusal to unmount or remove a pool in use, --retry-lock 10m and snapshots --no-lock, the rule for exit status 3, Run now of a task as a task of the scheduler, check --with-cache for s3, the whole disks instead of filesystems, --host unos, and smaller ones. On 8fef386 the device check found that Save with an S3 store out of reach held its request and the lock of the module for restic's 10 minutes: Save and a run now connect to an S3 store first (10 s) and refuse one that does not answer, and Save's restic commands end after 120 s. A second review of 8fef386 led to a UTS namespace and host name of its own for each restic (restic tests a lock of its own host name with SIGHUP to its PID), one copy repository per installation, check --no-cache, the refusal of a disk target whose disks cannot be found, md and device-mapper partitions followed to their members, the refusal of Delete Volume while a copy uses it, and Forget removing staged secrets files. A last review with three lenses and two refuters for each finding found eight more, fixed in c926016: SIGTERM before SIGKILL so that a stopped restic removes its lock, python -B for the host-name step, the disk rule when the disks of /mnt or /data cannot be found, and Delete Volume atomic with a copy, with smaller test and doc points. Device checks of 2026-11-11 (PROGRESS.md): scripts/dev/scenario.sh offsite OK on e663f14, 8fef386, f4ecd22 and c926016 (12 steps each); Save and test refused a folder on the system disk, an S3 store out of reach (within a second since 38a6da5) and a wrong password; a copy before the reboot of 12:52 UTC and one after it, with both copies' snapshots listed; scenario.sh all (101 steps) before and after two reboots. Not run on the device: a copy to a real S3 store and to a second disk, for want of a store and a spare disk; the S3 path runs against the fake restic in the tests.

features.description: Off-device copies also go to a second NAS over SFTP or to a restic REST server
steps: On System > Backup & Restore, an SFTP target (host, user, folder, with its host key pinned) or a REST server with its credentials can be saved and tested as the copy target
Copies, their check and restore test, and the restores run to it as to a disk or an S3 store
features.notes: Built (ADR-0422): the kinds rest and sftp of supervisor/src/offsite/. REST: https:// only, its user and password only in restic's environment (RESTIC_REST_USERNAME, RESTIC_REST_PASSWORD), the certificate checked by the system's roots, a CA certificate or the SHA-256 fingerprint of the server's own certificate, which Save reads, compares and keeps for restic's --cacert. SFTP: no ssh in the supervisor image and no new image layer: restic's -o sftp.command runs the host's /usr/bin/ssh (openssh-client, an optional host tool) through nsenter into the host's mount and network namespaces, with a fixed argv, a key pair that UNOS makes (POST /offsite/sftp-key; the private key only in /data/offsite_secrets.json and, per command, a 0600 file of the tmpfs) and the host key pinned at the first test and refused when it changes until a save trusts the new one. Not host-level: nothing on the host changes (ssh only reads; its files are in the container's tmpfs), so the entry needs no reboot check. restic is not installed on the workstation: the backend tests and the stand-in run the fake restic, which plays both servers; restic 0.18 and the host's ssh meet a real REST and SFTP server first in the device check below. Device check (by hand with the device-checks skill, without the owner's second NAS), after the deploy, on a device where GET /offsite/settings says configured false and no Scheduler task copies (as scenario.sh offsite requires). P: the pool's mount point (the one scenario.sh offsite picks); A: the device's LAN address (the first of scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'hostname -I'). Measure steps 2, 4, 5, 9 and 10 with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure <label> -- <command> and report their SD MiB. Secrets are made on the device in /dev/shm (umask 077) and piped into scripts/dev/api.py ... - from there, never on a command line. (1) On the device: mkdir /dev/shm/unoscheck-rest P/unoscheck-rest P/unoscheck-src (with two small files); in /dev/shm/unoscheck-rest: openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -nodes -days 1 -subj /CN=A -addext subjectAltName=IP:A -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem; openssl rand -hex 24 > password; openssl rand -hex 24 > repo-password; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'cat > /dev/shm/unoscheck-rest/server.py' < scripts/dev/restic-rest-server.py; nohup python3 -I -B server.py --listen A:18443 --root P/unoscheck-rest --cert cert.pem --key key.pem --user unoscheck --password-file password > log 2>&1 & echo $! > pid. (2) Save and test: a python3 -I -c on the device prints the body {kind rest, endpoint https://A:18443, prefix unoscheck, username unoscheck, tls fingerprint, certificate_sha256 from openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256, rest_password and password read from the two files, sources [P/unoscheck-src]} into scripts/dev/api.py PUT /offsite/settings -: 200, has_rest_password, P/unoscheck-rest/unoscheck/config made; the same with another rest_password answers 400 with 401 Unauthorized and keeps the settings. (3) POST /offsite/run, then GET /offsite/status until running is null: last_copy success, check passed, restore_test passed, files_new 2. (4) GET /offsite/snapshots: a configuration and a data snapshot; restore-configuration puts offsite_<time>.tar.gz into the backup list (delete it again); restore-files of the source into pool P gives both files byte for byte. (5) A new certificate (stop the server, openssl req again, start it): Run now fails at the step settings naming both fingerprints, and the server's log shows no request of it. DELETE /offsite/settings. (6) SFTP: mkdir -m 700 /dev/shm/unoscheck-sftp and mkdir -m 755 P/unoscheck-sftp (root:root, the chroot); ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f /dev/shm/unoscheck-sftp/host1, and host2; an sshd_config there with Port 18022, ListenAddress A, HostKey /dev/shm/unoscheck-sftp/host1, PidFile /dev/shm/unoscheck-sftp/sshd.pid, AuthorizedKeysFile /dev/shm/unoscheck-sftp/authorized_keys, PermitRootLogin prohibit-password, AllowUsers root, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, UsePAM no, StrictModes no, ChrootDirectory P/unoscheck-sftp, ForceCommand internal-sftp, Subsystem sftp internal-sftp, AllowTcpForwarding no, X11Forwarding no; /usr/sbin/sshd -f /dev/shm/unoscheck-sftp/sshd_config -E /dev/shm/unoscheck-sftp/sshd.log. (7) POST /offsite/sftp-key; python3 -I -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "scripts/dev"); import api; print(api.DeviceApi().get("/offsite/settings").json()["sftp_public_key"])' | scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'cat > /dev/shm/unoscheck-sftp/authorized_keys' (api.py's printed answers redact it). (8) Save and test with {kind sftp, host A, port 18022, username root, path /repo, host_key_fingerprint from ssh-keygen -lf /dev/shm/unoscheck-sftp/host1.pub, password from /dev/shm/unoscheck-rest/repo-password, sources [P/unoscheck-src]}: 200, host_key_fingerprint is host1's, P/unoscheck-sftp/repo/config made. (9) Run now as in (3), and (10) the snapshots and both restores as in (4). (11) Restart sshd with HostKey host2: Run now fails at the step unlock with Host key verification failed; a PUT of the same settings answers 400 with host1's fingerprint and Trust; with trust_new_host_key true it answers 400 without a host_key_fingerprint and 200 with host2's (ssh-keygen -lf host2.pub), and Run now succeeds. (12) No secret in a log: docker logs --since <start> unos-supervisor and journalctl --since <start> hold neither password (grep -c -F -f of both files gives 0). (13) Clean up: DELETE /offsite/settings, kill both servers by their pid files, remove /dev/shm/unoscheck-*, P/unoscheck-rest, P/unoscheck-sftp, P/unoscheck-src, the restored-* folders and the offsite_ backups. Not checked on the device by this entry: a real second NAS, and a REST server's CA mode, whose probe the backend tests show against a local TLS server and whose --cacert against the fake. The review in a fresh context (ADR-0017) found no blocking point; its risks were fixed with tests (ADR-0422): trusting a changed host key needs its fingerprint, a fingerprint given beside a kept pin is compared with it before restic runs, a dropped key type gets the Trust hint, ssh starts with env -i (restic's environment holds the password), a pinned certificate's validity and names are checked as Go checks them, and the CA probe is tested against a local TLS server. Left: the device check's log scan covers the two passwords and not the private key, which the backend tests' log capture covers. No scenario.sh area was added: one needs the fake device of supervisor/tests/test_dev_scenarios.py to play every call and helper of it. Device check 2026-11-19 of 988bf19 (mvp.batch-16, deployed 14:1x UTC: sync 4.562, build-supervisor 15.062, build-webui 20.875, up 5.719 SD MiB; check.sh OK), before and after the reboot from the API at 14:41:15 UTC: the device had no off-device copy (configured false) and has none again. REST: a temporary restic REST server on the device's LAN address with a self-signed certificate and its folder on the pool; saved and tested with the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint (a wrong password answered 400 naming 401 Unauthorized and kept the settings); Run now: copy, check and restore test passed, 2 new files; two snapshots; a configuration restore listed and deleted; a file restore byte for byte; a new certificate refused at the pin before any request reached the server; settings deleted (0.016 to 0.211 SD MiB a step). SFTP: a second sshd on port 18022 with its own host key and a chroot on the pool; UNOS's key pair, its public key installed; saved and tested with the host key's typed fingerprint; Run now with check and restore test; both restores byte for byte; a changed host key failed the copy ('Host key verification failed'), the same settings answered 400, trusting without its fingerprint 400, with it 200, and the copy passed again; no password in the supervisor's log or the journal; settings deleted, both servers stopped, everything of the check removed (0.023 to 0.324). The check's own scripts/dev/restic-rest-server.py refused restic 0.18's POST without a Content-Length with 411; fixed with a test (a chunked body, or none). Not run: the REST server's CA mode (the tests' real TLS server covers it), a second NAS of the owner's.

features.description: A restore checks and extracts the archive in one streaming pass instead of decompressing it into /tmp first
steps: The peak use of /tmp during a restore is at most half of what it is today
A restore still refuses every archive it refuses today
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-12 (ADR-0364). A restore reads the backup in one pass over its gzip stream, the pass of the upload check (_read_archive in supervisor/src/backup/router.py), encrypted backups after their decryption in memory as before, and writes only unos.db to /tmp, as it comes; the manifest is read into memory, scheduled_tasks.json only noted, and the SMB preparation keeps its rollback journal in memory. Step 1: test_a_restore_holds_at_most_half_as_much_in_tmp_as_before (plain and encrypted) measures the files in TMPDIR after every call that returns in the restore's thread, for a backup with a database of about 4 MiB: it failed on the code before with 8,540,791 bytes (the decompressed archive, the extracted files and the SQLite journal) against at most 4,257,827, half of the decompressed archive plus the files extracted from it, and now holds the database alone. Step 2: every refusal test of test_backup_restore.py passes unchanged, with the same answers (a member whose data would end past MAX_TAR_BYTES is still a corrupt archive for a restore, as for the decompressed archive, ADR-0364), and so do test_backup_upload_check.py and test_backup_files.py; test_a_database_cut_short_or_refused_after_it_leaves_nothing_in_tmp covers the database extracted before a refusal. The 507 test lost its decompression phase, which no longer exists: a /tmp that is too small now fails at unos.db. scripts/dev/scenario.py restore_check needs no change (its restores answer as before). Open: not host-level; on the dev device after a deploy, scripts/dev/scenario.sh restore and backups must still pass, and neither measures the peak of the container's /tmp, which a step of the restore check sampling df /tmp in the supervisor container during its restores could show. Review fix 2026-11-12: _scan_members refuses a regular file whose name, after at most one leading ./, is not its normalized path (unos.db/. passed as unos.db and failed with EISDIR, 500): test_a_file_whose_name_is_not_its_plain_path_is_refused and the upload cases file-named-as-a-folder and manifest-named-as-a-folder failed first (ADR-0364). Device check 2026-11-12 (before and after the reboot from the API at 19:37:03 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 19:37:58; both containers healthy by 19:38:50), and after the deploy of the review fixes): scenario.sh restore passed its 20 steps (7.648, 7.367 and 7.262 MiB; one run right after a deploy measured 48.664 MiB, 35.5 of them in its read-only step 2, the deploy's own writes still going on, and a run on the idle device right after it 7.262 MiB), and scenario.sh backups its 8 (0.406 and 0.383 MiB).

features.description: Backups refuse files that are not backups at upload, and take the host's pool entries of /etc/fstab
steps: A gzip file that is not a backup, uploaded as .tar.gz.enc, is refused at the upload instead of failing at the restore
A backup takes the pool entries of the host's /etc/fstab, or no fstab at all, never the container's file
features.notes: Built 2026-11-11 (ADR-0345, which takes up the two backup cases of ADR-0167). Step 1: an upload named .tar.gz.enc whose bytes are gzip data to their end (header, deflate data, CRC-32 and length, zero padding allowed, or more than MAX_TAR_BYTES decompressed without an error) is refused with 400 "This file is not an encrypted backup: it is an unencrypted gzip file", and nothing is stored (_refuse_plain_archive and _is_gzip of supervisor/src/backup/router.py); a plain backup still gets "This backup is not encrypted: upload it as .tar.gz". test_backup_upload_check.py test_gzip_data_named_as_encrypted_is_refused_at_the_upload (gzip that is no tar, a tar without a manifest, a cut tar, zero padding after the stream, more than the decompression limit) failed before: each was stored and answered 200; test_an_encrypted_backup_whose_salt_starts_like_gzip_is_accepted guards the other side (an encrypted backup whose random salt starts with gzip's header is kept). Step 2, no fstab at all: no backup reads /etc (Create Backup, encrypted backups, the archive of the off-device copy, backup tasks); BackupConfig and the web UI's type lose include_pools and include_network, which only added the container's fstab and netplan files; a restore ignores the fstab and netplan members of a backup that still holds them, unextracted and without the warning "fstab is included in the backup but is not restored automatically." test_backup_files.py test_a_backup_holds_neither_fstab_nor_netplan failed before (the backup by hand held fstab and netplan, read from the container's /etc), test_backup_restore.py test_restore_database_and_shares failed before (the fstab and netplan warnings), and so did the accepted case fstab-and-netplan-of-an-older-backup of test_backup_upload_check.py (400 "fstab in the backup archive is too large"); test_scheduler_validation.py test_a_backup_task_stores_encrypted_backups allows no fstab in a backup task's backup. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0345 supersedes ADR-0166 after it; USER_GUIDE and CHANGELOG say that only gzip data to its end is refused). Device check 2026-11-11 (tree 8ea5a08, before and after the reboot from the API at 23:22:13 UTC on 2026-11-11 (the boot of 23:23:10; both containers healthy by 23:23:59)): scripts/dev/scenario.sh restore named the members of its backup by hand (manifest.json, unos.db) and of its scheduled one (manifest.json, scheduled_tasks.json, unos.db), neither with fstab or netplan, and passed its 20 steps (7.332 and 7.574 MiB); an upload of a gzip of a tar named .tar.gz.enc answered 400 "This file is not an encrypted backup: it is an unencrypted gzip file" and left the backup list and the backups folder as they were (0.082 MiB), also on main 405d318.

features.description: The backup API has no include_ options that select nothing
steps: BackupConfig of POST /api/v1/backup/create and the web UI's type have no include_users, include_apps, include_scheduler or include_notifications, and the manifest of a new backup names none of them
Create Backup, encrypted backups through the API, the off-device copy and backup tasks make the same backups as before: the manifest and the database, and for a task also the scheduled tasks
features.notes: Built 2026-11-12 (ADR-0355). Step 1: BackupConfig of supervisor/src/backup/router.py has only encrypt and passphrase, and the BackupConfig type of webui/src/lib/api/backup.ts only encrypt and passphrase (the Backup tab sends an empty body, as before). _collect_backup_content takes encrypted instead of the config: the manifest of Create Backup, of encrypted backups through the API and of the off-device copy's archive is version, created, hostname and encrypted, without the config that named the options and would now only repeat encrypt. A request that still sends an include_ option is answered as before (pydantic ignores unknown fields; ADR-0207, no compatibility for API clients). Step 2: the members are unchanged (manifest.json and unos.db; for a backup task also scheduled_tasks.json, whose manifest never named the options). Backup tasks never carried the options: ScheduledTask ignores unknown keys (pydantic's default), so a task stored with them, also in a config object, loads and runs, and the next write of the tasks file (the record of its run) leaves them out; no migration. An older backup whose manifest config names the options (also include_pools and include_network) uploads and restores: only a JSON object is required of manifest.json. test_backup_files.py test_backups_have_no_include_options (a request with the four options, an encrypted backup, the off-device archive, a backup task stored with the options and run, an older backup uploaded and restored) failed before with: AssertionError: assert {'encrypt', '... 'passphrase'} == {'encrypt', 'passphrase'}, Extra items in the left set: 'include_notifications', 'include_scheduler', 'include_users', 'include_apps'. No E2E spec: the web UI's change is a type that no code sends. Device check 2026-11-12 (main 641f2a5, before and after the reboot from the API at 04:35:30 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 04:36:49; both containers healthy by 04:37:17)): a backup made through the API held manifest.json and unos.db, its manifest exactly version, created, hostname and encrypted (false), and it was deleted again; scenario.sh backups and restore OK (the restore of a backup made moments before, and the scheduled task's backup).

features.description: Restores take only backups whose database holds the shares, and the import of shares from an old backup's smb.conf is gone
steps: Restoring a backup whose database has no share tables is refused with a clear message
The path that imports shares from the archive's smb.conf for such backups is removed with its tests
Backups stop carrying a copy of smb.conf, unless an ADR keeps it
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-10 (ADR-0319, which supersedes ADR-0040, ADR-0077, ADR-0139, ADR-0142 and ADR-0143). Step 1: a restore checks the four SMB tables of the extracted database and creates none; one that lacks them is refused with 400 and nothing changes (TestNotAuthoritative test_a_backup_without_the_smb_tables_is_refused, which failed before: the tables were created and the shares imported). Step 2: the import of the archive's smb.conf is gone, with the source 'backup' and smb_state.pending_import_conf; a database without the import marker imports the live smb.conf, never with guest access (test_the_smb_conf_of_an_older_backup_is_not_read, test_the_shares_of_the_live_file_are_imported, test_guest_access_is_not_restored), and its tests are gone or read the live file. Step 3: no backup, manual or scheduled, carries smb.conf, and BackupConfig has no include_shares (test_a_backup_holds_no_smb_conf and test_a_backup_task_stores_encrypted_backups, with the host's smb.conf in place, which failed before for scheduled backups; test_a_backup_restores_the_shares_of_its_database); a restore ignores an smb.conf in an archive, and a database of the previous layout, with pending_import_conf, restores (test_a_database_of_the_previous_layout_restores). The web UI's BackupConfig has no include_shares either. Host-level (GLOSSARY.md: the smb.conf that a restore leads to). Device check of 2026-11-11: scripts/dev/scenario.sh restore (ADR-0341), run from the workstation against the device running main 96db310 (deployed at 15:16 UTC), 15:38:59 to 15:39:58 UTC, OK in 20 steps, 7.207 MiB on the SD card in all; a first run at 15:13 UTC, before the step of the database copies, passed its 19 steps (7.504 MiB), and its two copies of the database were removed by hand afterwards (0.070 MiB). A restore of the first, with the check's share and its access for two SMB users in place and nothing changed since, answered "success", database and smb_config, and kept the shares and smb.conf byte for byte (the same sha256), with the users, API tokens, SMB host accounts and Samba's accounts (0.484 MiB). Re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), 2026-11-11, scripts from main d6e98c0 against the device running main 96db310 (the runtime of d6e98c0 differs only in a docstring of supervisor/src/shares/smbconf.py): scripts/dev/scenario.sh all OK before the reboot (19:19:48 to 19:25:58 UTC, 146 steps passed, 1 skipped) and after it (the reboot asked from the API at 19:25:58, the boot of 19:26:54, check.sh OK at 19:28; 19:28:15 to 19:34:35 UTC, 146 steps passed, 1 skipped): scenario.sh restore OK, 20 steps, 7.215 MiB before and 7.117 MiB after, both backups without smb.conf and the first restore keeping smb.conf byte for byte each time.

features.description: Scheduled backups are encrypted, because they hold the users' two-factor secrets
steps: A backup task encrypts what it stores with AES-256-GCM and a passphrase, as a manual backup with a passphrase is (.tar.gz.enc)
A scheduled backup restores with that passphrase and is refused without it
features.notes: A backup task needs a passphrase, which no answer of the API and no file holds; the device keeps the key derived from it in /data/scheduled_backup_keys.json, mode 0600 (ADR-0325). The stand-in runs a backup task and restores its backup with the passphrase (webui/tests/backup-restore.spec.ts). Not checked on the device: the RAM a run takes there, and that backup tasks made before ADR-0325 fail until a passphrase is set.

features.description: A user browses the pools and downloads files in the file manager
steps: Open Files: it starts in the pools directory, and .. goes up
Open a folder and click a file's name: the file downloads with the session
A download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page
Paths outside the pools are refused, and symlinks are shown but never followed
features.notes: Step 3: files.spec.ts 'a download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page' (added on 2026-11-07, after a review found the step unasserted).

features.description: A user uploads files into the open folder, and a file appears only when it is complete
steps: Upload files into the open folder: they are listed once complete
Each upload goes to the folder that was open when it started
A refused, failed or cancelled upload leaves nothing, and so does a supervisor stopped in the middle
Bad folders, bad names and form part headers over 8 KiB are refused before any data is written

Select items, choose Copy or Move, open the destination and choose Copy here or Move here

features.description: The file manager never deletes, renames or moves volumes, other subvolumes or mount points
steps: Deleting, renaming or moving a volume answers 409 and changes nothing
Deleting a folder with a subvolume or a bind mount below it answers 409 and deletes nothing
A volume can still be copied
