features.description: Uploads time out when the client stops sending, and hidden upload files left on filesystems without O_TMPFILE are cleaned up
steps: An upload whose client stops sending is cut off after a read timeout, and its space is freed
Hidden .unos-upload-<hex> files left by a stop, on filesystems without O_TMPFILE, are found and removed with the owner's consent
features.notes: Step 1 done (ADR-0347): request_limits.receive_upload waits at most UPLOAD_IDLE_TIMEOUT (120) seconds for each chunk of the body, for file manager and backup uploads alike; then it answers 408 "The upload timed out: the client sent nothing for 120 seconds" with Connection: close, and the upload's discard frees its file. A client that keeps sending, however slowly, is not cut off. Tests: the stops_sending and keeps_sending tests of test_upload_streaming.py (ASGI and through uvicorn). Device check 2026-11-11 (tree 8ea5a08, before and after a reboot, by hand through Caddy on the device): an upload that sent its part head and 1 MiB of a declared 4 MiB, then nothing, its connection open, had its unnamed file in the folder held until 119 s after the last byte and gone at 120 s, and nothing of it was left (no file, no hidden .unos-upload-* file, no descriptor); a small file uploaded at once after it was stored; each step wrote 0 MiB to the SD card. Caddy passed the 408 only when the client sent 1 KiB more, at 151 s, and then at once (ADR-0347, Consequences). Step 2 done (ADR-0354, which supersedes ADR-0167, whose cases are all decided now): the supervisor looks for hidden .unos-upload-<16 hex> regular files in every folder below the pools directory (also on mounts there; not in .unos-trash or .snapshots; without following symlinks), once UPLOAD_LEFTOVER_AGE (600 s) after each start (first_upload_leftover_check in the lifespan, a warning in the log only when it finds some) and on POST /api/v1/files/upload-leftovers/check; GET /api/v1/files/upload-leftovers lists them with path, size and modified as the check found them, without touching the disks; DELETE /api/v1/files/upload-leftovers removes the given paths for good after checking every one through its folder's descriptor (400 for another name, 409 for a non-file, an upload in progress or a change in the last 10 minutes), looks at each file again right before its unlink (one replaced or written since is left alone), and drops what is gone, refused or left alone from GET's list. The walk goes at most 64 folders down (deeper folders are named among the problems) and remembers only the roots of mounts (_mount_roots), not every folder. Uploads in progress: _FileUpload puts each hidden name into the in-memory _uploads_in_progress before creating the file and takes it out in discard(). The File Browser shows a notice (region "Leftovers of interrupted uploads") with their number and size and Remove…, whose dialog lists them and asks first (Cancel focused). Tests: test_upload_leftovers.py (also a supervisor killed mid-upload into a folder without unnamed files, whose file the next check finds and the removal removes), the routes in test_authz.py, the first check in test_lifespan.py; E2E: "offers to remove the hidden files of interrupted uploads, and asks first" and "after a refusal, the dialog lists the leftovers that are still to remove" of files.spec.ts on the stand-in, and the notice and dialog in mobile-layout.spec.ts. Not yet checked on the dev device: a vfat or exfat disk mounted below a pool, a supervisor restart in the middle of an upload into it, the check 10 minutes after the start, the removal, and the SD MiB of the check (expected 0). A leftover whose folder was replaced by a symbolic link or a file since the check leaves the list, and the others are removed (test_a_leftover_whose_folder_was_replaced_since_the_check_leaves_the_list failed before: 403 or 400). Device check of step 2, 2026-11-12 (main 641f2a5, by hand, before and after the reboot from the API at 04:35:30 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 04:36:49; both containers healthy by 04:37:17)): in a folder of the pool, a hidden .unos-upload-<16 hex> file of 1 MiB changed 20 minutes before, a fresh one and a plain file; POST .../check and GET listed the old one alone with its size and time; DELETE of the plain file answered 400, of the fresh one 409, of both hidden files 409, and removed nothing; DELETE of the old one removed it alone; 0 MiB on the SD card. A real leftover from a filesystem without O_TMPFILE (a vfat or exfat disk) was not made: no spare disk. The check by itself ran 10 minutes after the supervisor's start on the device (started 04:40:56 UTC, checked 04:50:59), finding nothing and no problem.

features.description: Folders made with New Folder and files uploaded in Files inside a share are writable for the share's SMB users without a Repair
steps: Create a folder and upload a file in a share's folder in Files: they get the group unos-smb with group write (2770 for the folder, 0660 for the file)
An SMB user with write access to the share changes the file and creates entries in the folder at once
Outside share folders the File Manager creates entries as before
features.notes: Built (ADR-0273): New Folder and Upload give the new entry 2770 or 0660 when the folder it is made in is setgid, of the group unos-smb with group rwx and nothing for others (_share_folder in supervisor/src/files/router.py); the group comes from the folder, and elsewhere new entries keep what the umask leaves. A new folder that cannot get 2770 is removed again, or the answer says that it stays private, since Repair permissions skips private folders. Copy, and a Move to another pool or volume, into a share folder give the copies the share's modes (files.group-writable-copies-and-moves-in-shares, ADR-0396); a Move within a pool or volume keeps them. Steps 1 and 3 are asserted by test_files_security.py, test_upload_streaming.py and test_share_api.py (TestFileManagerInAShareFolder) with the runner's gid as the SMB group, and step 3 in the web UI by files.spec.ts ('outside share folders, a new folder and an upload give the group no write access'); the stand-in cannot give a folder gid 70000. The unnamed upload file (O_TMPFILE) is checked on Linux only: scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_upload_streaming.py -k share_folder (both share-folder upload tests, each unnamed and hidden). The device check, and again after a reboot (ADR-0018): in the folder of a share that UNOS created (2770 root:unos-smb) and that gives an active SMB user Read & write, create a folder and upload a file in Files: stat -c '%a %U:%G' shows 2770 root:unos-smb and 660 root:unos-smb. That user then, over SMB (smbclient), overwrites the file and puts a file into the new folder, without a Repair. A folder and an upload made in Files in a pool's top folder, which is never a share's folder, show 755 and 644 root:root (a volume that is shared and was repaired is a share folder: there they get 2770 and 660). Device check 2026-11-08: New Folder in /mnt/pools/data/shared made the folder 2770 with the group unos-smb. The rest is the scenario checks' (the feature-pass skill's table): scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb (step 10: New Folder and Upload in a new share's folder give 2770 and 660 root:unos-smb; step 11: over SMB the share's user changes the uploaded file and puts a file into the new folder) and files (steps 3 and 4: 755 and 644 root:root outside share folders) passed with the runtime files of main 12483dd at 07:43 UTC on 2026-11-09 and, after the reboot of 12:22 UTC, at 13:58 UTC (ADR-0018), as with main 78769b4 on 2026-11-08 before and after its reboot (22:33 and 23:03 UTC).

features.description: Items that Copy, or Move from another pool or volume, put into a share in Files are writable for the share's SMB users without a Repair
steps: Copy a file and a folder into a share's folder in Files: the copies get the group unos-smb with group write (folders 2770, files 0660, or 0770 for files their owner may run, as Repair permissions gives them)
Move a file and a folder from another pool or volume into a share's folder: they get the same modes
An SMB user with write access to the share changes the copied and moved items at once
Outside share folders Copy and Move keep the modes of the items, as before
features.notes: Built (ADR-0396): Copy, and a Move to another pool or volume (rename(2) answers EXDEV: a copy, then the delete), into a share folder (_share_folder in supervisor/src/files/router.py, as ADR-0273 decides it: setgid, the group unos-smb with rwx, nothing for others) give every copy the mode of constants.share_entry_mode, which Repair permissions uses too: folders 2770, regular files 0660, or 0770 when their owner may run them, through the whole copied tree; the group comes from the setgid folder. Private entries (no group or other bits) keep their modes, and what is in a private folder is copied as outside shares, as Repair leaves them; symbolic links stay links, and nothing is followed. Each copy is private (0600, 0700) until it is complete and then gets its mode through its descriptor (_copy_entry); in a share folder, a folder that another one replaced between the copy's mkdir and its open (whoever can write the share folder can rename one there) is refused with 409 before anything is copied into it or its mode changed (_open_new_folder), and a copy's mode comes from the source that was opened (fstat), so a private entry renamed over the source keeps its mode. A copy that stops part way answers the error (507, 403) and leaves the item whose copy stopped private, which an administrator deletes in Files, and a move deletes its source only after a complete copy. ACL entries are neither copied nor changed: a copy gets the destination's default ACL, and its group bits become the mask. A Move within a pool or volume stays a rename that keeps the owners and modes, also into a share (Repair permissions gives them the share's); outside share folders Copy and Move keep the modes as before. Steps 1, 2 and 4 are asserted by test_files_security.py (the section 'copies and moves into share folders') and test_share_api.py (TestFileManagerInAShareFolder, the folder of a new share) with the runner's gid as the SMB group, the modes by test_smb_models.py (TestConstants), and step 4 in the web UI by files.spec.ts ('outside share folders, Copy and Move keep the permissions of the items', on the stand-in only); the stand-in cannot give a folder gid 70000. The default ACL test is Linux-only: scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_files_security.py -k default_acl. Step 3, and steps 1, 2 and 4 with the real group, need the device check (host-level: it changes modes on the pool), and again after a reboot of the deployed tree (ADR-0018), with the scenario checks of the feature-pass skill's table: scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb, steps 12 to 14: in the folder of the check's new share (2770 root:unos-smb, its user with Read & write), Copy of cp.txt and cpd/ (with cpd/i.txt) from a new volume unoscheck<run>m, where stat -c '%a %U:%G' shows 644, 755 and 644 root:root, gives 660, 2770 and 660 root:unos-smb; Move of mv.txt and mvd/ (with mvd/i.txt) from that volume, another subvolume, gives the same and leaves the volume without them; then the share's user over smbclient overwrites cp.txt, mv.txt, cpd/i.txt and mvd/i.txt and puts n.txt into cpd and mvd, without a Repair; the volume goes with the clean-up. scripts/dev/scenario.sh files: step 6, Copy and a Move within the pool keep 644 root:root; step 13, Copy of a volume keeps the modes of its entries; step 14, a file and a folder moved from the volume into the check's folder keep 644 and 755 root:root. The smb check now also compares the pool's volumes with its baseline. The notes of files.group-writable-entries-in-shares, which the review found stale, were set right at the merge. Device check of 991cb28 on 2026-11-17: scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb 40 of 40 (steps 12 to 14 passed, SD MiB 0.020, 0.000 and 0.000) and files 17 of 17 (steps 6, 13 and 14 kept the modes) before a reboot from the API at 23:24:54 UTC, and scenario.sh all after it (every area passed, smart's two sleep steps skipped while apps use the pool, ADR-0381); scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_files_security.py -k 'default_acl or share': 42 passed.

features.description: Items deleted in the file manager can be brought back for a while
steps: Delete items in Files: they go to the trash of their pool or volume, and their folder no longer lists them
On the Trash page, restore deleted items: they are back where they were, and a name that is taken there again is refused
They are gone for good only after a set time, 30 days after their deletion, or when an administrator empties the trash or deletes them from it
features.notes: Built 2026-11-07 (ADR-0259, which filled in the steps for the trash it chose; step 3 keeps the original guarantee: the Delete dialog offers no Delete for good before the server refused the move): Delete in Files moves items into <pool>/.unos-trash or <pool>/<volume>/.unos-trash with one rename, a private folder (mode 0700) per item with the item and its origin; a trash that someone else made first is made the supervisor's with mode 0700 before it is used, one that cannot be made so is refused (409), and only private folders in a trash count as its entries; every item is checked before any is moved (also bind mounts on the way, from the mount table), and one that fails after others went answers with how many went; the Delete dialog offers Delete for good (?permanent=true) only after a 409 or 507 refusal of the move, and after any refusal it holds only the items still in their folder, with the focus on Cancel; GET /files/trash, POST /files/trash/restore (every item checked first, also that its folder is on the filesystem of its pool or volume and below no mount point), DELETE /files/trash and POST /files/trash/empty; trash_expiry_loop in the lifespan, at the start and once a day; the name .unos-trash is hidden, refused and left out of copies, every share section vetoes it and it cannot be shared; on the Trash page each checkbox is labelled with the item's name, folder and deletion time. Asserted on this machine: step 1 by test_files_security.py (the trash tests, volumes and deeper subvolumes through st_dev fakes, trashes of other owners through fakes of st_uid, bind mounts through the mount table fake) and files.spec.ts ('deletes the selected items', 'Delete offers no Delete for good until the trash has refused the items', the keyboard test and the two refusal tests of the Delete dialog); step 2 by the test_restore_ and test_a_restore_ tests and files.spec.ts ('the Trash page lists deleted items, and Restore puts them back where they were', 'a restore is refused while the name is taken again, and the item stays in the trash', 'the Trash page tells items of the same name apart by where and when they were deleted'); step 3 by test_deleted_items_are_deleted_for_good_30_days_after_their_deletion, test_an_administrator_deletes_items_for_good_or_empties_the_trash, test_a_trash_that_others_can_change_is_made_private_and_what_they_put_there_is_no_entry, the expiry loop tests, test_lifespan.py and files.spec.ts ('the Trash page deletes items for good, and Empty trash deletes everything', 'Delete offers no Delete for good until the trash has refused the items'). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step: every share section of the rendered smb.conf has veto files = /.snapshots/.unos-trash/ and testparm takes it; a file and a folder deleted in /mnt/pools/data/shared land in /mnt/pools/data/.unos-trash (mode 0700) and Restore brings them back; a file deleted in a volume lands in that volume's .unos-trash through the real btrfs rename, not in the pool's, and comes back; a .unos-trash that a user other than root made in a volume with mode 0777 is root's with mode 0700 after the next listing (the real fchown, which the tests fake); a file in a snapshot or in the restored copy of a volume's snapshot answers 409 (no trash) and, after that refusal, Delete for good removes the latter; smbclient lists no .unos-trash in the share of a volume; a delete, a restore and an expiry pass write 0 MiB to the SD card; after a reboot the items are still listed, and an entry renamed to a time 31 days back is gone after the pass at the start. The backend tests ran on macOS (renameatx_np, and APFS takes only UTF-8 names): scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_files_security.py runs them with renameat2 across two folders and restores a name that is not UTF-8. roles.spec.ts keeps regular users off the Trash page. Whether the Delete dialog should offer Delete for good before a refusal is the owner's decision (ADR-0259, Considered options). Device check 2026-11-08 after the deploy: a file deleted on the pool data and in the share's folder went into /mnt/pools/data/.unos-trash (mode 700, root), came back with Restore, and went for good from the trash; every share of smb.conf has the trash's veto line and testparm accepts it. Device check 2026-11-11 of the rest (tree 8ea5a08, by hand, before and after the reboot from the API at 23:22:13 UTC on 2026-11-11 (the boot of 23:23:10; both containers healthy by 23:23:59)): in a new volume, a file deleted went into the volume's own .unos-trash (700 root:root) with one rename (same st_dev and inode), not into the pool's, and Restore brought it back; a file in a read-only snapshot of the volume answered 409 (no trash) and Delete for good of it was refused; a .unos-trash that nobody made in the volume with mode 0777 was root's with mode 0700 after the next listing (the real fchown); a delete, a restore and an expiry pass each wrote 0 MiB to the SD card; an item kept across the reboot was still listed with its origin, deletion time and inode, and came back with Restore, and an entry renamed to 31 days back was gone after the supervisor's pass at its start (the container started at 23:23:23, after the boot; the check's own comparison with the API's boot_time failed only because that time moved with the clock's correction after the boot). scenario.sh files passed its 16 steps before and after the reboot, also on main 405d318.

features.description: The dashboard shows live CPU, memory, network and disk I/O over the WebSocket, and the storage overview
steps: Open the dashboard: the stats arrive over the WebSocket, and the CPU, memory and network values change with them, without HTTP polling
The storage widget shows the pools with the health the API reports
features.notes: Built: /ws/v1/events sends the stats every 2 seconds (ADR-0363), and the dashboard's five stats cards (CPU, Memory, Network, Disk I/O, Temperature) show each message; the storage widget shows each pool with the health that GET /storage/pools reports (ADR-0036), read when the page loads and on Refresh. Fixed with ADR-0388: the Disk I/O card was missing, though the message carried disk_io. The network of the message was the supervisor container's own (psutil reads /proc/net/dev in the container's network namespace): the dashboard and the Resource Monitor showed the traffic of the container's eth0, and System > Network, which matches the rates by name, showed it on a host port named eth0 and no live rates on a host whose port has another name. It is now the host's, from PID 1's /proc/1/net/dev (links.parse_net_dev, which GET /network/stats shares) over the interfaces that System > Network lists (not lo, dummy0, docker0, veth* or br-*, links.is_hidden). The disk rates came from psutil's totals over every device of /sys/block (zram, loop, device mapper, md; LUKS and LVM twice) and now count the physical disks only, those with a device in /sys/block, from the one read of /proc/diskstats that also lists the block devices for the Storage page. Each rate is the sum of the interfaces or disks that both samples have (never negative, and a device that comes adds no counters at once), over the monotonic clock, and none for the first sample after a gap of more than 10 s (the average since the dashboard was last open was shown as the current rate). Regular users get the network's rates without the host's interfaces, which are System > Network's (ADR-0030). Gone from the message: the interfaces' ipv4, speed and is_up (the container's), and the totals of bytes, packets and operations and each block device's counters, which no page read. Step 1: dashboard.spec.ts 'the stats cards follow each stats message of the socket, and nothing polls the API' (a fake socket sends three messages, the CPU, memory, network and disk I/O cards show each, and the page sends no request to the API while page.clock runs a minute; it failed first on the missing Disk I/O card, and it fails for a setInterval that loads the page's data again), 'the stats cards show the stats messages of the server as they arrive' (the stand-in's own socket: the cards show each of three messages, no API request between them), 'the stats cards write sizes, rates and the temperature with their units', 'shows the dashboard in Russian' and 'a regular user sees the dashboard in Russian' (the stand-in's socket sends a regular user no interfaces, and the Network and Disk I/O cards show rates); websocket.spec.ts (the socket's sign-in and the order of its messages); test_ws_stats.py (the host's interfaces from PID 1's /proc/net/dev and never psutil's view of the container, the hidden interfaces left out, psutil's interfaces with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local, interfaces and disks that come, go or start again, the physical disks only with zram, loop, dm and md devices and partitions left out and one read of /proc/diskstats, the monotonic clock, a sample after a gap, an unreadable file logged once, the message's shape; they failed first on the container's view, psutil's totals, the wall clock and the gap's average); test_ws_auth.py TestTheInterfacesOnTheEventsSocket (the interfaces for an administrator, none for a regular user or for an administrator who is no longer one, the shared sample unchanged; it failed first for the regular user); test_webui_polling.py (no setInterval of the web UI reaches the API, ADR-0365). Step 2: dashboard.spec.ts 'storage widget shows the health the API reports' (not mounted, degraded, error, unknown and healthy pools of the fakes) and 'storage widget follows the health the API reports for each pool' (a pool healthy, then degraded with a device missing, then not mounted, at each Refresh, beside one that stays healthy). mobile-layout.spec.ts: the dashboard with its five cards fits a phone in both languages. Open: the check on the device, as the stand-in has no network namespace apart from the host's and no /sys/block of a NAS (ADR-0215): with the dashboard open, a copy to a share over SMB shows its rate on the Network card (received) and on the Disk I/O card (Write) within a few seconds, the Disk I/O card stays near 0 while only zram is written (Armbian's /var/log), the rates of System > Network follow the host's `cat /proc/net/dev`, and the supervisor's log has no "The host's network counters cannot be read". Device check 2026-11-17 (mvp.batch-8 at 320d3ec, deployed 2026-11-17 18:58-18:59 UTC; reboot from the API at 19:23:11 UTC (the boot of 19:24:4x, all containers healthy by 19:25:26); scenario.sh all after it: 187 steps passed, smart's sleep steps skipped while apps use the pool): an administrator's socket listed only enP4p65s0 (docker0, br-*, veth*, lo hidden), its counters equal to the host's /proc/net/dev, its rates following a 40 MiB transfer (19.6-20 MiB/s), disk read peaking at 89.9 MiB/s for a 256 MiB read of sda, zram writes not counted (0.035 MiB); a temporary regular user's socket had interfaces [] with the rates (0.145); no 'network counters cannot be read' in the log; the same after the reboot (0.020, 0.121, 0.016).

features.description: The API has no stats endpoints that no page calls and that report the supervisor container's network instead of the host's
steps: GET /api/v1/monitor/network and GET /api/v1/monitor/disk-io are removed, with /monitor/history/network, /monitor/history/disk-io and the network and disk_io of /monitor/all, which only they fill
GET /api/v1/system/stats is removed, and scripts/dev/api.py names another path in its usage
test_authz.py and webui/tests/api.spec.ts no longer name them, and the stats message of /ws/v1/events stays the one source of live stats
features.notes: Found by the review of system.dashboard on 2026-11-17 (ADR-0388, Consequences): no page calls these endpoints (webui/src asks for no /monitor/ path, and test_ws_stats.py test_the_web_ui_keeps_no_unread_stats_code checks that no client asks for /system/stats). supervisor/src/monitor/router.py reads psutil in the supervisor container's network namespace: /monitor/network answers the container's interfaces with ipv4, speed and is_up, and rates over the wall clock that turn negative when the clock is set; /monitor/disk-io answers psutil's totals over every device of /sys/block, zram, loop, device mapper and md included, over the wall clock; supervisor/src/system/router.py's /system/stats answers the container's network counters. Today only webui/tests/api.spec.ts and test_authz.py name them, and scripts/dev/api.py's usage and test_dev_scripts.py use /system/stats as a sample path against a fake. The rest of the monitor router (/cpu, /memory, /processes, /history/cpu, /history/memory) has no page caller either: the pass decides, with an ADR, whether it goes too. Built: the five routes and the network and disk_io of /monitor/all are removed with their samplers and history buffers (the rest of the monitor router stays: no ADR decided it); /system/stats too, and scripts/dev/api.py, the device-checks skill and test_dev_scripts.py use /system/info as the sample path. Asserted by test_authz.py (404 for each route, /monitor/all without them) and test_ws_stats.py test_nothing_asks_for_the_removed_container_stats_endpoints (no webui/src, webui/tests or scripts file names them). No ADR: ADR-0388 and ADR-0207 decided it. Device check of 991cb28 on 2026-11-17, before and after a reboot: /monitor/network, /monitor/disk-io and /system/stats answer 404, /monitor/all only cpu, memory and timestamp, /system/info 200 (SD MiB 0.020). Left from the review: ADR-0388, ADR-0346 and ADR-0006 still describe the removed routes as they were when decided.

features.description: System > Resource Monitor shows CPU, memory, network and disk I/O with their history, and the process list
steps: Open System > Resource Monitor: CPU, memory, network throughput and disk I/O are shown
The time range buttons change the history shown
The process list shows the running processes with their CPU and memory use
features.notes: Built with ADR-0399. The history: supervisor/src/monitor/history.py takes a sample every 10 s in a loop of the lifespan, also while no page is open, and keeps the averages since the last sample of the host's CPU (busy share of /proc/stat's times), network (the interfaces that System > Network lists, /proc/1/net/dev) and physical disks (/proc/diskstats with /sys/block), as the stats message reads them (ADR-0388), and the memory in use at the sample, on a clock that counts a suspend (CLOCK_BOOTTIME), for one hour (360 points) in RAM only: nothing is written, a failing sample is logged once, a restart starts it empty. GET /api/v1/monitor/history (administrators) answers the points with their ages on the monotonic clock; MonitorTab.svelte reads it once when it opens and adds each stats message of /ws/v1/events, no timer (ADR-0365), but not the message the store held at the opening nor one whose new sample_seconds is 0 (the first sample after a gap, whose rates and CPU share are 0), which the cards still show. The time range buttons 5 min (default), 15 min and 1 hour change what each of the four charts draws, with the peak of the range under each and the range in each chart's accessible name. The process list: the host's ten processes that use the most CPU (pid: host, apps' containers included), with PID, name (never the command line), CPU share, resident memory and the effective user as the host's /etc/passwd names it (read through /proc/1/root/etc/passwd when it changed; the container's /etc/passwd named host accounts wrongly or not at all), and regular users' sockets now get no processes and no block device names (the finding of system.dashboard's review). The CPU share of the stats message was of the time since the last sample of the same worker thread (psutil keeps cpu_percent's last reading per thread); it is now of the time since the last sample. Removed: /monitor/cpu, /memory, /processes, /history/cpu, /history/memory and /all, which no page called. Step 1: monitor.spec.ts 'the live stats in English' (each card's values from a fake socket's message, the process table's columns and rows), 'the stand-in' (the real supervisor's history answers 200 and the tab shows the processes of its own socket); test_monitor_history.py (the averages, the host's devices only, devices that come, go or start again, a gap, an hour kept and nothing written, a failure logged once, the loop in a worker thread, the API: 200 to an administrator, 403 to a regular user, 401 without a session, the removed routes 404); test_ws_stats.py (the CPU share in any thread, the message's shape). Step 2: monitor.spec.ts 'the time range buttons change the history shown' (a fake history with points 30, 10 and under 5 minutes old: each range shows its own peak in every card and names its span), 'each stats message extends the history, which the tab reads once' (one request, the peak follows the messages, a message of sample_seconds 0 adds no point), 'the message that the store held when the tab opened is no point of the charts'; the range test also checks the lines drawn (their points' x and y, and the break where points are more than 30 s apart). Step 3: monitor.spec.ts (name, PID, user, CPU and memory of each process), test_ws_stats.py (the host's users, a changed and an unreadable passwd, the machine's own users with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local, the ten read in full only), test_ws_auth.py (a regular user's socket has no processes and no block devices, also after a demotion). In Russian: monitor.spec.ts 'in Russian' and mobile-layout.spec.ts. Every new test failed first: the spec's six on the old tab (no cards' headings, range buttons, peaks or history), the backend ones on the old events.py (the users came from the container, the CPU share was 0 in a new thread, the regular user got processes and disks) and on the missing history module. Host-level (it reads the host's /proc): it passes only after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), by hand with the device-checks skill, read-only, each step with its SD MiB: (1) at least 30 s after the supervisor is healthy, scripts/dev/sd.sh measure history -- scripts/dev/api.py GET /monitor/history: HTTP 200, interval_seconds 10, points oldest first about 10 s apart, the newest under 20 s old, cpu_percent and memory_percent within 0 to 100, every rate 0 or more; the newest memory_percent within 3 points of what scripts/dev/ssh.sh free -b gives as (total - available) / total; (2) a read of a file of 1 GiB or more of the pool, scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'dd if=<file> of=/dev/null bs=1M count=1024 iflag=direct', then the GET again: a point after it has disk_read_rate above 10 MiB/s, and the SD card counts no MiB for it; (3) the owner opens System > Resource Monitor as an administrator in a browser: the cards show values, the charts lines, 5 min, 15 min and 1 hour change them, and the process table lists the host's processes (smbd, dockerd, the apps' processes) whose users, for the same PIDs, are those of scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'ps -eo pid,user:32,comm --sort=-%cpu | head -15' (uids without a name on the host as numbers); (4) scripts/dev/sd.sh measure idle -- sleep 600 with no page open: no more MiB than before this change (the sampler writes nothing), and scripts/dev/check.sh: UNOS within its CPU budget (ADR-0374); (5) after an hour of uptime, step 1's GET has 360 points, the oldest about 3590 s old; after the owner's reboot, steps 1 to 4 again, the first GET within 20 s of the supervisor's health answering no or one point. Review (fresh context, ADR-0017): no blocking finding; fixed: a read of the history while the sampler appended could answer 500 (copied first), ages after a suspend (CLOCK_BOOTTIME, and only the last hour answered), a false zero point at every opening (sample_seconds), the charts' lines unasserted, the CPU test blind to guest and iowait, the memory called an average in the docs, a passwd uid of non-ASCII digits, a device step's 10 s bound. Left: 'nothing is written' is asserted in the backend only as no file in the working folder (the device step measures the SD card), and the tab shows its charts only once a stats message has arrived (at most 2 s). Left open: the device check. Before this pass the E2E spec checked the tab's headings only, and no backend test covered the monitor API. Since ADR-0388 (2026-11-17) the stats socket's network is the host's interfaces that System > Network lists, read from /proc/1/net/dev, not the supervisor container's. Device check of 5412b79 on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB): /monitor/history answered a 10 s interval, points 10.0 to 10.1 s apart, the newest 2.6 s old, memory 17.9% against the host's free -b 17.9 (0.000); a 1 GiB file on the pool written at 80 MB/s (0.055) and read with iflag=direct at 92 MB/s (0.000) raised disk_read_rate to 65.7 MiB/s, then deleted; the administrator's events socket's 10 processes matched ps on all 10 PIDs, and a regular user's socket carried stats without processes or block device names; 600 s idle 0.086 with the container log unchanged and the supervisor at 1.3% of a core; after a reboot from the API (0.020) 0 points when the health answered and 6 a minute later, and 63 points after scenario.sh all with memory within 0.1 of the host. Not run: an hour's 360 points (the smbconf scenario restarts the supervisor: 638 s of uptime at the end) and the tab's range buttons in a browser.

features.description: The dashboard shows the host's CPU temperature, and the API lists every sensor
steps: The dashboard's Temperature card shows the temperature of the host's CPU
GET /api/v1/system/temperatures lists each sensor group with its readings
A host without sensors shows that none are available
features.notes: The code is done (ADR-0346): src/system/sensors.py chooses the CPU's or SoC's sensor by its name (coretemp Package id 0, k10temp Tdie else Tctl, cpu_thermal, soc_thermal, package_thermal; '-' read as '_'), else the first group, for both /system/stats (cpu_temperature) and the stats message (cpu.temperature); tests/test_system.py TestDashboardTemperature, and dashboard.spec.ts shows the card with a temperature and N/A without one, through a fake socket (the stand-in has no sensors). Device check 2026-11-11 (tree 8ea5a08, before and after the reboot from the API at 23:22:13 UTC on 2026-11-11 (the boot of 23:23:10; both containers healthy by 23:23:59)): GET /system/stats answered cpu_temperature 44.384 and 43.461, the RK3588's soc_thermal as sysfs read it at the same moment (/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon0/temp1_input, 44.4 and 43.5 to 44.4 C), and no temperatures field; GET /system/temperatures listed the 7 thermal groups (soc, bigcore0, bigcore1, littlecore, center, gpu, npu), each within a degree of sysfs; 0.000 MiB on the SD card. The card renders that value, as dashboard.spec.ts shows through a fake socket; the stand-in has no sensors (step 3).

features.description: System > Network shows the host's interfaces, DNS, gateway, routes and connections, and an administrator brings an interface up or down
steps: Open System > Network: each interface is listed with its addresses, state and speed
DNS servers, search domains, the gateway and the routing table are shown
Bring an interface down and up again: its state follows on the host
features.notes: Built (ADR-0245): every command of the network API runs on the host through src/host.py. GET /network/interfaces lists each interface's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, its operational state, whether it is enabled, and its link speed from the host's sysfs; VLANs (eth0.100) are listed and changed like the others; the routes are the IPv4 and IPv6 tables; DNS reads all of resolvectl's servers and leaves out its fallback servers; a failed request answers 500 with the host's message (a host that does not answer in time: "the host did not answer within N seconds"), and the page shows it. The tab is built from the UI components and tokens. Disable and Enable follow ADR-0244 (system.network-disable-confirmation). The fake-host tests and the E2E spec (route fakes: the stand-in has no host network) pass. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): System > Network on the dev device lists its NICs and the Hurricane Electric tunnel with the addresses, states and speeds that `ip addr` and `cat /sys/class/net/<if>/speed` show on the host, and the DNS servers, search domains, gateway and routes of `resolvectl status`, `ip route` and `ip -6 route`; Disable and Enable of a NIC that does not carry the connection, and carries no VLANs (ADR-0246), follow on the host (`ip link`). The live rates on the page still come from the supervisor container's interfaces, matched by name (system.dashboard). GET /system/network, which no page called and which duplicated GET /network/interfaces with ethtool speeds, is removed (ADR-0416). Device check 2026-11-07: GET /api/v1/network/interfaces showed enP4p65s0 at 2500 Mb/s with its IPv4 and IPv6 addresses; DNS (10.1.1.1), the gateway and the routes were shown; the VLAN enP4p65s0.99, added for the check and removed after it, went down and up again on the host through the API. Since ADR-0388 (2026-11-17) the stats socket's network is the host's interfaces that System > Network lists, read from /proc/1/net/dev, not the supervisor container's.

features.description: An administrator sets the host's name and time zone
steps: Set the hostname in System > General: hostnamectl on the host shows it
Set the time zone: timedatectl on the host shows it, and scheduled tasks follow it
features.notes: Built (ADR-0331): GET and PUT /api/v1/system/timezone and GET /api/v1/system/timezones run timedatectl on the host through host.run_on_host_async (tests/test_system_time_zone.py: the host's zone and list, a change on the host, an unknown zone refused with 400, a failed change with timedatectl's message, Unknown without timedatectl); the hostname is set through PUT /api/v1/network/hostname, which runs hostnamectl on the host and answers 500 when it fails, and GET /network/hostname and GET /system/info read it with hostname on the host, also after a change (test_network.py); the container's PUT /api/v1/system/hostname and the bind mount of /etc/hostname are removed. Zones with digits, '+' and '-' (Etc/GMT-3) can be set, and an option or a path never reaches timedatectl. System > General's card Name and time zone sets both (webui/tests/system-general.spec.ts on route fakes, in English and Russian: the PUT bodies, the confirmation, the host's message on a refusal and the old zone kept). Device check 2026-11-10 after the deploy of main e6a44d5: GET /api/v1/system/timezone answered the host's Etc/UTC and /timezones its 598 zones; PUT Etc/GMT-3 made timedatectl and /etc/localtime on the host and GET /api/v1/scheduler/timezone show it (0.082 MiB), PUT Etc/UTC put it back (0.074 MiB), and --help was refused with 400; PUT /api/v1/network/hostname unoscheck-name made hostnamectl and /etc/hostname show it and GET /network/hostname and /system/info answered it at once (0.172 MiB), and the old name was put back (0.094 MiB), with smbd, wsdd2 and avahi-daemon active afterwards. Re-check after a reboot 2026-11-10 with the card deployed (main 70dfec4): the zone Etc/GMT-3 and the hostname unoscheck-name set through the API before the reboot of 20:15 UTC were still the host's after it (timedatectl, /etc/localtime, hostnamectl, /etc/hostname) and the API's (GET /system/timezone, /scheduler/timezone, /network/hostname, /system/info); both were put back, and smbd, wsdd2 and avahi-daemon restarted to take the old name again.

features.description: An administrator reboots, shuts down or suspends the host, cancels a pending shutdown, and turns Wake-on-LAN on
steps: Reboot and Shutdown in System > Power ask for confirmation, then act on the host one minute later
Cancel stops a pending reboot or shutdown
Turn Wake-on-LAN on for an interface: ethtool on the host shows it, and the Power tab says that a magic packet starts a host that is off only where the board keeps the network card powered
features.notes: Built (ADR-0233): reboot, shutdown, cancel, suspend and Wake-on-LAN run on the host through src/host.py; GET /api/v1/power/pending reads logind's ScheduledShutdown, and Cancel runs shutdown -c only while something is pending; the Wake-on-LAN choice per interface is kept in /data/wol_config.json and set again at each start of the supervisor; with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local (the stand-in, the test stack) every power endpoint answers 503 and runs nothing; POST /system/reboot, /system/shutdown and /system/cancel-shutdown are gone. System > Power shows each answer, the pending action with its Cancel button, and the interfaces with their MAC address and an on or off button; Suspend asks first too. Proven on a fake host and with route fakes only: every step acts on the host, so the entry passes after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), and reboots of the dev device are owner actions (ADR-0211). The device check must show: Reboot in the tab makes busctl get-property org.freedesktop.login1 /org/freedesktop/login1 org.freedesktop.login1.Manager ScheduledShutdown name reboot one minute ahead, and the host reboots then; Cancel empties it and nothing happens; Shutdown powers the host off a minute later; Turn on for the board's NIC makes ethtool <nic> on the host show Wake-on: g, a magic packet from a second machine on the LAN starts the host after a shutdown (whether the NIC and the board support it is unknown), and after a reboot ethtool still shows g. The host needs ethtool; the startup check names it when it is missing. The UPS monitor still shuts down only outside a container (system.ups-monitoring). Device check 2026-11-07: Wake-on-LAN on and off through the API showed Wake-on: g and d in ethtool on the host; a reboot was pending one minute later and Cancel stopped it; a reboot from the API rebooted the host (back after 114 s, with the pool mounted, Samba, the share and the containers up). Magic packets from the workstation did not start the dev device after a shutdown: its board cuts the network card's power (ADR-0247).

features.description: With NUT configured, System > Power shows the UPS state, and UNOS shuts the host down on low battery
steps: Configure the UPS: the battery charge, the runtime and the state are shown
On battery below the set level, UNOS sends an alert and shuts the host down
Test connection names a failure
features.notes: Safety fix 2026-11-12 (ADR-0356): GET and PUT /api/v1/power/ups/config answer has_password, never the NUT password; a PUT without a password (absent, null or empty) keeps the stored one, one without a username removes it, a password without a username is refused (400); /data/ups_config.json is written with mode 0600 and only on a change, and a damaged one is logged without its values; a file of another mode, and its .bad, get 0600 when the monitor starts. upsc runs on the host through src/host.py under timeout(1), off the event loop (OPTIONAL_HOST_TOOLS: nut-client), with ups_name, host and port checked. While the host has no upsc, GET /power/ups/status answers available false with the reason "The host has no NUT client: upsc was not found. Install the package nut-client on the host", POST /power/ups/test 503 with it, GET /power/ups/list an empty list with it as error, and GET /power/ups/monitor/status available false with it; the monitor then shuts nothing down, writes nothing and logs the reason once. Values with decimals are read, each on its own: one that is no number is null and the UPS stays available, and no reason holds a value (review fix 2026-11-12; the decimal tests and the 0644 test of test_ups.py failed before). supervisor/tests/test_ups.py checks this on a fake host, and the API part of steps 1 and 3 there. The web UI has no UPS page. Open: steps 1 to 3 (no UPS on the dev device; NUT is an owner install), the page in System > Power, the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). UNOS does not use the NUT username and password yet. In the supervisor container the monitor never shuts the host down (step 2): it starts the shutdown only when is_in_container() is false, and /.dockerenv makes it true (supervisor/src/power/router.py). Device check of the safety fix 2026-11-12 (before and after the reboot from the API at 13:11:00 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 13:11:56; both containers healthy by 13:12:50), and after the deploy of the review fixes): GET and PUT /power/ups/config answer has_password and never the password, a PUT without one keeps it, a password without a username is refused (400); ups_config.json is 600 root:root on the host and the password is in no answer, no docker log or journal line and no audit entry; with no upsc on the host GET /power/ups/status answers available false with the reason naming nut-client; the settings were put back and the file, which did not exist before, removed. Steps 1-3 stay open (no UPS, NUT not installed: owner actions).

features.description: The host shuts down, and wakes, at the times set in the power settings
steps: Set an auto-shutdown time: the host shuts down then
Set a wake time: the host wakes then (rtcwake)
Idle shutdown turns the host off after the idle time
features.notes: Built (ADR-0407): supervisor/src/power/schedule.py, a loop of the lifespan with a pass a minute, acts only on what an administrator turned on in the power settings (all off by default and in a damaged file), and nowhere with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local (the stand-in, the test stack: GET /power/schedule answers 503, PUT /power/config refuses settings that act with 503). Step 1: a daily shutdown at a time on the host's clock (scheduler.router.schedule_zone, ADR-0266; the skipped and the repeated times of daylight saving time), announced 11 minutes before as the problem shutdown_scheduled (health banner and every notification channel, ADR-0332, shown until the host goes down), issued one minute before its time as POST /power/shutdown issues it (shutdown -h +1 through host.py, ADR-0233; audited as system_shutdown by system), only 10 minutes after its announcement, never over a pending reboot or shutdown, and not again that day after a Cancel; postponed (problem shutdown_postponed) while a running job runs (a run of a scheduled task or one due in the minute that began or the next 2 minutes, a backup by hand, a restore, an app install, the off-device copy, a permissions repair, an update of UNOS, a btrfs scrub, balance, replace or device removal, also with btrfs's own options, or the kernel's balance or replace thread) or while the wake is on and the RTC does not hold its alarm, announced again when nothing holds it and issued 10 minutes later, dropped 6 hours after its time or when a wake time passes while it waits, skipped when the next wake comes within 10 minutes; a system clock set by more than 2 minutes starts the schedule over from the new time. Step 2: a daily wake by the RTC /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm, read and written through host.run_on_host (sh -c with fixed scripts); the RTC takes it when rtc0 and its wakealarm exist and its clock is within 5 minutes of the system clock, else GET /power/schedule names why and PUT /power/config refuses the wake with 409 (nothing stored); PUT arms it before storing (500 when the RTC keeps no alarm, and clears it when the settings cannot be stored), each pass keeps it at the next wake time (also after it fired), turning the wake off clears it (or only stores the change on a host that lost rtc0 or its wakealarm), and with the wake off the RTC is left alone; a wake less than 10 minutes after the shutdown is refused with 400. Step 3: the idle shutdown after 20 to 1440 idle minutes, announced 10 minutes before (problem shutdown_idle); the host is not idle while a signed-in WebSocket of the web UI is open, logind has a session other than a per-user manager, ss shows an established connection to port 445, 139 or 2049, a running job runs, or a disk other than the boot SD card or eMMC moved more than 1 MiB a minute; what cannot be read counts as use; the idle time starts again after each use, at each start of the supervisor and when the wake time passes; after an announcement that use withdrew, the next comes an hour later at the earliest. GET /api/v1/power/schedule (administrators, read only) answers the zone, the next shutdown, its state and holds, the next wake with the RTC's answer and alarm, and the idle state with its findings; System > Power's card Shutdown and wake schedule edits and shows them in English and Russian. Nothing is written at a pass (RAM only; the settings file only on a PUT that changes it), and a pass logs only a change. Proven on a fake host and a fake clock (supervisor/tests/test_power_schedule.py) and with route fakes and the stand-in's refusals (webui/tests/power.spec.ts); every step acts on the host, so the entry passes after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Device check, by hand; it never shuts the dev device down, and a real shutdown and wake are the owner's, because the board may not power on from its RTC: (0) BEFORE the deploy, scripts/dev/api.py GET /power/config must show auto_shutdown, auto_wakeup and idle_shutdown false (a file stored when these settings did nothing is acted on from the first start: PUT them false first); (1) keep the settings: scripts/dev/api.py GET /power/config; (2) on the host, ls /sys/class/rtc/rtc0 and cat /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/since_epoch /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm, and GET /power/schedule: wake.rtc answers available, or the reason that matches what the host has; (3) with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure, PUT /power/config with auto_shutdown at the time 23 hours 50 minutes from now on the host's clock, auto_wakeup 6 hours after it, idle_shutdown on with 1440 minutes (on a host whose RTC cannot wake it, PUT answers 409 with the reason of step 2: then PUT without auto_wakeup); (4) GET /power/schedule: timezone the host's, shutdown.next that time and state planned, wake.next and wake.rtc.alarm the same instant, which cat /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm shows in seconds since the epoch, idle.idle false with the check's own login_session among idle.found; GET /power/pending answers nothing pending; (5) after two minutes the same answers, nothing pending, one docker log line of the supervisor saying the wake alarm is set and none per minute, and the SD MiB of the two minutes; (6) PUT /power/config with the settings of step 1: wakealarm on the host reads empty, GET /power/schedule shows the shutdown, the wake and the idle shutdown off. A check stopped before step 6 puts the settings back at once (a shutdown armed in step 3 would come in 23 hours 50 minutes, announced in the banner 10 minutes before, and Cancel shutdown stops it). After the owner's reboot, steps 2 to 6 again. The owner's own trial: a shutdown time a few minutes ahead and a wake 15 minutes after it, to see the announcement, the shutdown and whether the board powers on from its RTC. Left to system.ups-monitoring: the UPS monitor's own low-battery shutdown, which still never runs in the container. Review (ADR-0017, fresh context) fixed: a task due in the decision minute now holds the shutdown; a postponed shutdown is dropped when a wake time passes, and announced again before it comes; an update of UNOS, a btrfs replace or device removal and btrfs commands with global options hold it; the announcement stays shown until the host goes down; a clock set by NTP or by hand starts the schedule over; the idle announcement is not repeated within an hour after use withdrew it; the wake can be turned off on a host that lost its RTC; an alarm set for settings that could not be stored is cleared; the card names the browser's zone of the plan. Left as they are: the card reads the plan when the tab opens and after a save only (no polling, ADR-0365; the banner follows the announcements live); a damaged settings file leaves an alarm set before in the RTC (one wake); a SMART self-test running in a disk holds nothing. Device check of 09e792a on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB), arming and putting back only: a PUT of the power settings with a wake far ahead armed the RTC (wake.next equal to rtc.alarm and to /sys/class/rtc wakealarm) and logged nothing, the loop logged nothing a minute (two minutes cost 0.016 to 0.066 MiB with the check's own calls), the alarm stood across a reboot from the API, and the settings were put back off with wakealarm empty (0.195 to 0.281 a run). The real shutdown at a set time or when idle, and the wake by the RTC, are the owner's to see.

features.description: System > Logs shows the host's journal, kernel messages and log files, with filters and search
steps: Pick a source and a severity: the entries are listed, newest first
Search highlights matches and shows markup in log lines as text
The filters are comboboxes named by their labels
features.notes: Built (ADR-0257, ADR-0258): every source is a part of the host's journal, read with one journalctl command on the host through src/host.py, newest first (--reverse --lines=<limit>), off the event loop: System Journal (all of it), Kernel (--dmesg), Docker (docker.service), Samba (smbd.service, nmbd.service), Authentication (the syslog facilities auth and authpriv) and Cron Jobs (cron.service); UNOS Supervisor and Web Server are no longer sources. journalctl runs under the host's timeout(1) (`timeout --kill-after=5 30`), which ends it on the host after 30 seconds, and at most two reads run at once, on a pool of threads of their own. In every source a severity lists that level and the more severe ones and the time range applies, and the search is journalctl's literal, case-insensitive --grep, so it finds the newest matches of the whole range; a search without a match (status 1 without output) lists no entries. The output is split at \n alone, so an entry with U+2028 stays one entry. The tab shows the entries in the answer's order, says newest first, shows the times in the browser's time zone, sends a new limit with its request, shows only the answer of its newest request, shows an error instead of the list, and Auto and Search wait for an answer that is still coming. Step 1: tests/test_logs_sources.py (TestSources: each source's command and its entries, newest first; TestSeverity: every level in every source; TestTimeRange; TestEntries, with U+2028, the host's timeout and two reads at a time off the default executor; TestErrors, with a journalctl that reads too long ended on the host; TestValues, TestRoles; the old routes' test left with them, system.no-legacy-log-endpoints) and logs.spec.ts 'pick a source and a severity: the entries are listed, newest first', 'the limit and the time range reach the server with the request they change', 'Auto asks again every 5 seconds, but not while an answer is still coming', 'a late answer for the source picked before does not replace the entries of the one picked last' and 'an error of the server is shown instead of the entries of the request before'. Step 2: logs.spec.ts 'search highlighting shows markup in log lines as text', 'a search asks the server: the matches it lists are highlighted, and no match says so' and 'Search waits while an answer is still coming', and TestSearch (with a search that finds nothing) and TestEntries for the server. Step 3: logs.spec.ts 'filters are comboboxes named by their labels'. Not built: the log files of the description. GET /logs/files and /logs/file/{filename}, which read the supervisor container's /var/log and had no view, are removed (ADR-0416): which of the host's files the API may read as root is a later decision. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): on the dev device, for each of the six sources, GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=<source>&limit=20 answers 200 with the host's entries, newest first (timestamps descending), the same entries as `journalctl -r -n 20` with the source's matches on the host (a 200 also shows that the host runs journalctl under its timeout(1)); ?source=dmesg&priority=warning lists only the levels emerg to warning; ?since=1 hour ago only the last hour's entries; ?search=<a word of an older entry>&limit=5 finds it, and a word no entry has answers 200 with no entries (journalctl --grep's status 1 on no match); System > Logs lists the same; after a reboot Kernel lists the new boot's messages. Device check 2026-11-08 after the deploy: journal, dmesg, docker, samba, auth and cron each listed their entries newest first. Open: the same after a reboot. After the reboot of 2026-11-08 the journal was listed newest first again.

features.description: An administrator adds e-mail, Telegram and webhook channels (generic, Discord, Slack) and sends test notifications
steps: In System > Notifications, add an e-mail channel: the mail server's certificate is verified, also with SMTPS on port 465, unless the channel allows a self-signed one
Send a test: the message arrives, or the error is named
Telegram and webhook channels work the same way
The history lists the notifications sent
features.notes: System > Notifications adds e-mail, Telegram, webhook, Discord and Slack channels; a test shows under its channel whether it was sent or the error, and the history lists tests, POST /notifications/send and the monitors' alerts, newest first (ADR-0326). The certificate check of ADR-0045 (STARTTLS, SMTPS on port 465, the self-signed opt-out) came in from commit bbb773b of the branch smtp-verify-tls, which stays unmerged. test_notifications.py delivers to a local mail server (STARTTLS and SMTPS; trusted, self-signed and wrong-host certificates; a relay that takes mail without a login; the Date and Message-ID it receives) and a local webhook receiver, and fakes Telegram's API; its API tests also let the writes of the channels and the history fail as on a full disk, wait as on a busy SD card, and come two at once; notifications.spec.ts drives the tab with route fakes, and one of its tests sends through the stand-in's own supervisor to a mail server that is not there. Not a host-level change. No real mail server, Telegram or webhook service has been reached: that needs the owner's accounts, and Telegram from the dev device is system.telegram-from-the-device.

features.description: Problems reach every enabled notification channel and show as a banner in the web UI
steps: A pool not mounted or degraded, a failed SMART test, scrub errors, low space and a missed task each send one alert to every enabled channel, webhooks included
The web UI shows a health banner until the problem is gone
An alert is sent once per problem, not at every check
features.notes: The RAID monitor reports the problems of the managed pools (not mounted or no disk found, degraded, read-only after an error, 90% and 95% full), the SMART monitor those of the disks (health FAILED, a failed self-test), and a check every 5 minutes those of the scheduled tasks (last run failed, a missed run); each is alerted once through every enabled channel, webhooks included, while it lasts, and again after a restart of the supervisor, since the list is kept in RAM (ADR-0332). Scrub errors reach the devices' error counters, which make the pool degraded. Administrators see the list as a banner above every page until it is empty. Device checks (PROGRESS.md, 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11): a failed task's alert went once to every enabled channel (a webhook and Telegram) while the problem lasted, again at the first check after a reboot (10:19:51 UTC), and a task whose time fell while a reboot stopped the supervisor was alerted as missed (13:03:29 UTC); the dev device's real pool and disk raised no problem. Open: the kinds that need a fault or spare disks on the device, a pool not mounted or degraded, a failed SMART test, scrub errors and low space, as storage.pool-health's step 4; the tests show them.

features.description: Telegram alerts reach their chat from the dev device's network
steps: A Telegram, webhook, Discord or Slack request that connects nowhere from the supervisor's container goes once more, the same request, from the host's network with the host's curl, and arrives
A request that reached its service is never sent again: an HTTP answer of any status, or no answer in time after the request was sent, ends the send
The bot token, a webhook's URL and its headers reach curl only on its standard input: never on its command line, in an error text, the history or the log
An answer counts the same on both paths, and a send that fails both ways names both attempts, or a host without curl, in the test's answer and in the history
Both attempts end within the channel's time, 15 seconds for Telegram and 30 for the others, and within an alert's 60 seconds
A test notification to a Telegram channel arrives from the dev device
features.notes: Built (ADR-0336, which supersedes the proposal ADR-0046; neither IPv6 for the compose network nor e-mail instead): the HTTP channels send each request from the container with a connect timeout of 5 seconds, and only when httpx raises ConnectError or ConnectTimeout (no TCP or TLS connection, so the request was not sent) once more from the host's network through host.run_on_host_async: curl with fixed options on its command line (--disable first, --globoff, --max-time with what is left of the channel's time, --proto =https,http, --config -, the status after the body) and the request as its config on standard input (url, request, header, data-raw, each value quoted with its escapes, UTF-8 as it is). A request with a NUL character or a header that httpx would not send is not sent from the host. The bot token, a webhook's URL with its path and its header values are replaced by *** in what httpx, curl and the services say; Telegram's answer counts as a delivery with HTTP 200 and "ok": true on both paths. curl joined HOST_TOOLS (deploy/install.sh installs it). E-mail is unchanged. Tests first: 42 tests of test_notifications.py's TestFromTheHostsNetwork (against FakeHost's curl of test_pool_persistence.py, which reads the config as curl does, and one through the real curl of the machine to a local receiver) failed on the code before, and so did 4 older tests that the decision changes: Telegram's connect timeout is 5 of its 15 seconds, and a webhook's refused connection is tried from the host as well. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): the headers that curl reads differently, a webhook's key named by its path alone, short values garbling errors, curl's time after a slow TLS handshake and a captive portal's page as Telegram's error were fixed with tests that failed first; the host's attempt in asyncio's default thread pool and a loopback URL that names the host stay, with the reasons in PROGRESS.md (2026-11-11). A host-level change: it sends from the host's network. Device check (main 53396c0, 2026-11-11, PROGRESS.md): a test notification to the owner's Telegram channel answered "sent" at 09:12:52 UTC and was recorded as delivered at 09:12:58, after the container's 5 s connect timeout and the host's curl, and the owner confirmed it arrived. After the reboots of 10:19 and 12:52 UTC the first alerts of the start, "Task ... failed" at 10:19:51 and "Task ... missed its run" at 13:03:29, reached Telegram the same way.

features.description: An administrator schedules a custom shell command
steps: Add a custom task with a command in System > Scheduler: it runs at its schedule
Its output and exit status are recorded with the run
Regular users can neither see nor create such tasks
features.notes: The command runs with /bin/sh as root inside the supervisor container. A run records the exit status and the last 16 KiB of standard output and error together; a command is stopped after 24 hours, and every process of its session ends with it, also those that timeout or job control put in process groups of their own (ADR-0267). A run that a stop of the supervisor cuts off is recorded as failed, at an orderly stop or at the next start (ADR-0268). Step 1: the stand-in's E2E test makes a custom task in the form and runs it (Run now); test_the_scheduler_runs_a_custom_task_at_its_time drives the scheduler loop on a fake clock, since the stand-in runs no background loops. Step 3: the scheduler router is administrator-only (test_scheduler_validation.py, test_authz.py), and roles.spec.ts shows that a regular user gets neither the tab nor the API. On the device, the hour of a run follows the host's time zone: the device check of system.scheduler-time-zone.

features.description: Editing a scheduled task keeps its last run, and every field of the task form is named by its label
steps: Edit a task that ran: its last run and last status stay
Every control of the task form is reached through its label
features.notes: The task form keeps its native controls, each named by its label through a for/id pair; the passphrase fields of backup tasks are Input components (ADR-0325).

features.description: Scheduled tasks run at the times of the host's time zone
steps: Set the time zone, add a task for 03:00: it runs at 03:00 local time, also across a change of daylight saving time
features.notes: Built (ADR-0266): the scheduler reads the host's zone through host.run_on_host (where /etc/localtime links below zoneinfo/) at each pass and answer, and keeps the zone read last while the host cannot be asked, follows its clock with fixed rules for the changes of daylight saving time, and answers next_run with the zone's offset and run times in UTC with +00:00; GET /api/v1/scheduler/timezone names the zone, and the Scheduler tab shows it. The changes of daylight saving time are checked on a fake clock (test_scheduler_time_zone.py); the stand-in's host is the workstation. Open: the device check. Set the zone on the host with timedatectl set-timezone (the web interface cannot yet: system.hostname-and-time-zone); then GET /api/v1/scheduler/timezone must name it, a daily task's next_run must carry its offset, and a custom task made for a minute ahead on the host's clock must start in that minute (its run's started_at, read in that zone); after a change of the zone, within a minute the next_run follows it. The same after a reboot (ADR-0018). Device check 2026-11-08: with the host's zone set to Europe/Moscow by timedatectl, GET /api/v1/scheduler/timezone answered Europe/Moscow; the zone went back to Etc/UTC.

features.description: GET /api/v1/health answers without a session, for monitors and the containers' health checks
steps: GET /api/v1/health answers 200 without a token
Successful health checks stay out of the supervisor's access log; failed ones and all other requests are logged
features.notes: Over plain HTTP it is Caddy's rule: security.https-local-ca.

features.description: An administrator token reads the full health report and the Prometheus metrics
steps: GET /api/v1/health/full with an administrator token reports the database, Docker, the pools and the monitors
GET /api/v1/health/prometheus answers metrics in the Prometheus text format, with the pool count
Both answer 401 without a token and 403 to a regular user
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-05 (health/full, also after a reboot of the Phase 0 tree). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): GET /api/v1/health/full answers healthy with the database, Docker, storage and RAID ok (UPS not configured), GET /api/v1/health/prometheus the metrics with unos_storage_pools 1, and both answer 401 without a token; the 403 to a regular user is asserted by the route matrix of test_authz.py.

features.description: An administrator installs an update and rolls it back from System > Updates, or lets UNOS install updates by itself
steps: System > Updates shows the current version and the latest release
Install Update backs up, installs the release, checks its health and rolls back on failure
Rollback returns to the version before
With automatic install on, a new release is installed at the configured interval
features.notes: Built 2026-11-21 up to the release installer (ADR-0443); passes stays false until the owner decides it, a release exists and the dev device checks it. Fixed first, the cause: the backup before an update is copy_database (SQLite's backup API, with the commits still in unos.db-wal, one file with the rollback journal) into in-app-<time> of UNOS_UPDATE_BACKUP_DIR, which deploy/docker-compose.yml now mounts from the host's /var/lib/unos/backups (mode 700, newest 3 kept), and a rollback puts it back through the open database with the restore's _replace_database after _verify_database and _verify_page_size (test_update_install.py TestTheBackupHoldsTheLastCommits; on the base code the backup lost the commit still in the log). Step 1: the tab as before (updates.spec.ts). Step 2: the images first (up to an hour), then the backup, the switch (up to 700 s) and a health check of 300 s every 3 s, each check cut off at the deadline, for a known installed version older than the release; a failed switch or a release that does not answer is rolled back with the backup's database and the version before, and the history says failed (TestInstallUpdate, the spec's install and failure tests). Step 3: Rollback, offered while the newest backup is of the update to the version that runs, puts its database back with the restore's post-restore step, starts the version before and waits for it (TestRollback, the spec's rollback test). Step 4: automatic_install_loop in the lifespan installs a newer stable release once next_automatic_check has come, an interval after it was turned on or after the last look (TestAutomaticInstall, the spec's automatic install test). Also: jobs start as asyncio tasks (BackgroundTasks ran create_task in a worker thread), the progress is written once a step and sent over /ws/v1/events, an interrupted job is failed at the next start, a restore is refused while an update runs and the reverse, POST /updates/reset, the tarball download, git and docker compose in the container, UNOS_INSTALL_DIR and the settings nothing read are gone. Open, for the owner (ADR-0443): (1) where a release's images come from while GHCR has none (CI off, ADR-0230; building them on the device writes hundreds of MB to the SD card, ADR-0214); (2) how the supervisor replaces its own container, since the process that runs the update is in one of the containers it replaces (a unit on the host, a helper container, update.sh with a tag, or another way). Until then src/updates/installer.py's Undecided refuses Install Update, Rollback and the automatic install with that reason, and the tab names update.sh. Then: an installer that fills the seam, a release tag, and the device check of an install, a failed install's rollback and a Rollback, before and after a reboot (ADR-0018): host-level through the compose mount.

features.description: Until the in-app updater works, System > Updates offers no Install or Rollback and points to update.sh
steps: System > Updates shows the current and the latest version, and no Install Update or Rollback button
The tab names sudo /opt/unos/deploy/update.sh as the way to update
features.notes: The supervisor image carries its version: UNOS_VERSION, git describe --tags --always of the checkout that deploy/install.sh or deploy/update.sh built; update.sh fetches its branch with the tags in its history, so a release tagged after the install was cloned names the images (ADR-0234). The tab shows it, the latest release on GitHub or that none is published, and names sudo /opt/unos/deploy/update.sh; Install Update, Rollback, the update progress, the history and the settings left it, while their routes stay until system.in-app-updater. General shows the same version. Proven with route fakes and in the scripts' sandbox only, so passes stays false until the dev device shows its version: scripts/dev/deploy.sh, which builds the device's images, does not pass UNOS_VERSION yet, so System > Updates and General read unknown there. Missing: that script change (the owner's), then a deploy after which GET /api/v1/updates/current on the device (scripts/dev/api.py) and both tabs name the deployed tree's version. Device check 2026-11-07: after deploy.sh passed git describe of the tree to the build, GET /api/v1/updates/current answered the version (cce0def-dirty), and GET /api/v1/updates/check that no release is published.

features.description: The logs API has one entry endpoint for every source; the old dmesg and journal endpoints are gone
steps: GET /api/v1/logs/dmesg and /api/v1/logs/journal answer 404
GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=dmesg and ?source=journal serve them
No caller in webui/src uses the old paths
features.notes: Removed 2026-11-09 from supervisor/src/logs/router.py, as ADR-0257 foresaw. test_logs_sources.py TestOneEntryEndpoint: step 1, the old paths answer 404 and read no journal (they answered 200 before the removal); step 2, GET /logs/entries with source dmesg and journal and their filters reads them; step 3, no file of webui/src names them.
