features.description: An administrator bonds interfaces, tags VLANs and manages bridges
steps: Create a bond (LACP or balance-rr) of two interfaces: the host uses it
Add a VLAN on an interface or a bond
Create a bridge for containers
features.notes: Built (ADR-0424), not yet checked on the device. UNOS makes bonds, VLANs and bridges only where systemd-networkd keeps the host's network and NetworkManager does not run (GET /network/virtual-interfaces answers supported false and the manager, every change 409; NetworkManager and ifupdown hosts are left open, see below); with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local every route answers 503. Each interface is networkd's own .netdev and .network (05-unos-<name>.*), each port a 04-unos-<master>+<port>.network, and a VLAN's parent a 04-unos-<parent>.network that holds the parent's own settings (copied from the file networkd applied to it, without its [Match]) and the VLAN= of its VLANs, because a drop-in of netplan's Name=e* file would attach the VLAN to every card; the .netdev's '# unos:' line lists the interface's files, and UNOS lists and deletes only those. Live files in /run/systemd/network, kept ones in /etc/unos/netdevs, which the host's unit unos-netdevs.service (Before=systemd-networkd.service) copies back at boot: a change that is not kept never outlives a reboot. Step 1: POST /network/virtual-interfaces/bonds (LACP 802.3ad with layer3+4 hashing, or balance-rr; MIIMonitorSec=100ms) of 2 to 8 wired cards; a bond that takes the card of the default route or of the asking computer's route takes over that card's network sections, its MAC and its DHCP lease's IAID (test_virtual_interfaces.py TestBonds, test_an_lacp_bond_of_the_uplink_takes_its_settings_and_waits_to_be_kept). Step 2: POST .../vlans, ids 1 to 4094 (422 otherwise), on a card or a bond that networkd manages (TestVlans, test_a_vlan_on_a_bond, test_the_parents_file_holds_every_vlan_of_it_and_goes_with_the_last). Step 3: POST .../bridges of 0 to 8 ports (cards, bonds, VLANs), STP off (TestBridges). Validation: names (1 to 15 characters, none the host has, none reserved), MTU 1280 to 9216, addresses (none, DHCPv4 without gateway, routes and DNS, or 1 to 4 static ones without a gateway), a port in no other bond or bridge, without VLANs, without a disable of ADR-0244 that waits, and without addresses of its own unless it is the one protected port whose settings are taken over (two protected ports: 409), no second VLAN of an id on a parent, a parent file with drop-ins refused and the host's own VLAN= lines of the parent kept (each in TestBonds and TestVlans). The revert: a change that touches a protected interface (the default routes' and the asking computer's, with their parents and ports) records its ops, writes the marker and arms the transient timer unos-netdevs-revert (120 s) before it changes anything (without them nothing changes, 500), and the host undoes it unless POST .../confirm keeps it (TestRevert: not kept, kept, a reboot before the Keep, one change at a time, a failed or unanswered step undone at once or left to the timer, whose marker becomes undoing so that no Keep takes a change that failed; networkd's result checked: the interface, its ports' master, a VLAN's parent and id, a bond's mode, no link in networkd's failed state). A VLAN on the uplink waits to be kept too, unlike the entry's brief: networkd applies the parent's settings again for it, which drops and asks again for the uplink's DHCP lease. A change that touches nothing protected (a bridge without ports or of other cards, a VLAN on another card) is kept as soon as networkd made it (verified for 20 s). DELETE .../{name} removes an interface UNOS made (409 for one it did not make, one with VLANs on it, a bridge's port). Roles: administrators only (TestRoles, test_authz.py). Audit: network_interface_created, network_interface_deleted, network_change_kept. The host scripts run under sh and dash in test_virtual_interfaces_scripts.py; the page's card, its dialogs, the countdown and Keep in webui/tests/network-virtual.spec.ts, the dialogs at 375 px in mobile-layout.spec.ts. Deviations from the brief, decided in ADR-0424: a VLAN on the uplink arms the revert too, and the kept files reach networkd through UNOS's unit unos-netdevs.service from /etc/unos/netdevs, not from /etc/systemd/network, so that no unkept change outlives a reboot. Review in a fresh context (ADR-0017): its blocking finding (the parent's copy dropped the host's own VLAN= lines and drop-ins) and its risks (a failed change that could be kept, verification of the VLAN id, the bond's mode and networkd's failed state, RequiredForOnline=no, two protected ports, a port's own addresses, the boot unit's copy order, multipath default routes, a disable that waits) are fixed with tests; left as it is: a write without a revert that the host does not answer is undone at once, which is safe because every command runs under the host's timeout --kill-after=5 30 and has ended when the supervisor's 40 seconds are over. Left open: NetworkManager hosts (Raspberry Pi OS, desktops, Armbian's standard images) and ifupdown hosts (Debian's own server install) get no bonds, VLANs or bridges from UNOS; deploy/uninstall.sh removes /etc/unos with the kept interfaces (they last until the next reboot) but leaves unos-netdevs.service, which does nothing without its folder; a Docker macvlan network on a card that becomes a port is not seen. Device check (host-level; ADR-0018), by hand with the device-checks skill, every API call through scripts/dev/api.py, every step under scripts/dev/sd.sh measure <label> -- ... with its SD MiB recorded (expected: the reads 0, a change that is not kept only networkd's journal lines, a kept one a few KiB more for /etc/unos/netdevs and, once, the unit), the LAN checks being, from the workstation, `nc -vz -w 5 <the device's LAN IPv4> 443`, then 80 and 445, `scripts/dev/ssh.sh true` and `scripts/dev/check.sh`: (0) read only: `scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'systemctl is-active systemd-networkd NetworkManager networking; networkctl list --no-pager; networkctl status enP4p65s0 --no-pager; ip -br addr; ip route show default; ip -6 route show default'` shows networkd active, NetworkManager not, and enP4p65s0 configured by netplan's 10-netplan-*.network (if NetworkManager runs or networkd does not, stop: the device cannot check the entry); GET /network/virtual-interfaces answers supported true, no interfaces, enP4p65s0 protected; record its addresses and default routes. (1) a bridge without the uplink: POST /network/virtual-interfaces/bridges {"name": "unoscheckbr", "ports": []} answers revert_in null; `ip -d link show unoscheckbr` is a bridge; /run/systemd/network and /etc/unos/netdevs hold 05-unos-unoscheckbr.netdev and .network; `systemctl is-enabled unos-netdevs.service` says enabled; enP4p65s0's addresses, default routes and Network File as in (0); the LAN checks pass. (2) a VLAN on the uplink, not kept: POST .../vlans {"parent": "enP4p65s0", "vlan_id": 3999, "name": "unoscheckvl"} answers revert_in near 120; `ip -d link show unoscheckvl` is VLAN 3999 on enP4p65s0; `networkctl status enP4p65s0` names /run/systemd/network/04-unos-enP4p65s0.network; /etc/unos/netdevs has none of its files; `systemctl list-timers unos-netdevs-revert.timer` lists the timer; the LAN checks pass within the 120 seconds (if the device's address changed, stop and tell the owner); no Keep: about 125 seconds later GET lists no unoscheckvl and revert_in null, revert_failed false, `ip link show unoscheckvl` fails, enP4p65s0's Network File is netplan's again, `journalctl -u unos-netdevs-revert` shows the run, its addresses as in (0), the LAN checks pass. (3) the same VLAN, kept: the POST of (2), the LAN checks within 120 seconds, then POST .../confirm answers its change; no timer and no /run/unos/netdevs is left; /etc/unos/netdevs holds 05-unos-unoscheckvl.netdev and .network and 04-unos-enP4p65s0.network; check.sh passes. (4) a bond of the uplink alone, the dev device having one card: POST .../bonds {"name": "unoscheckbd", "mode": "802.3ad", "ports": ["enP4p65s0"]} answers 422 and {... "ports": ["enP4p65s0", "unoscheckbr"]} 409 (a bridge is no bond's port); no timer, no file and no interface appear. A real bond needs a second card: the owner's, with a USB network adapter (enx...): POST .../bonds of enP4p65s0 and it (802.3ad on a switch with LACP, or where the switch has none, 802.3ad still carries traffic on one port; not balance-rr on one unmanaged switch), revert_in near 120, the LAN checks within it, not kept and undone as in (2); again and kept; after a reboot bond0 has both ports and enP4p65s0's address; DELETE it, kept, and after a reboot enP4p65s0 is netplan's again. (5) the reboot (POST /power/reboot, as the earlier checks, or the owner's): after it GET lists unoscheckbr and unoscheckvl present, `ip -d link show` has both, enP4p65s0's Network File is 04-unos-enP4p65s0.network with its addresses and default routes as in (0), `journalctl -b -u unos-netdevs.service` shows its run before systemd-networkd's start, `systemctl status systemd-networkd-wait-online` did not wait for unoscheckbr or unoscheckvl (no 120-second timeout in `systemd-analyze blame`), the containers are healthy and the LAN checks pass. (6) cleanup: DELETE .../unoscheckvl answers revert_in near 120 (its parent is the uplink), the LAN checks, POST .../confirm; DELETE .../unoscheckbr answers revert_in null; /etc/unos/netdevs is gone, unos-netdevs.service is disabled and its file removed, enP4p65s0's Network File is netplan's, neither interface is listed by `ip link`; after a second reboot GET lists none and enP4p65s0 is as in (0). Device check 2026-11-19 of 988bf19 (mvp.batch-16, deployed 14:1x UTC: sync 4.562, build-supervisor 15.062, build-webui 20.875, up 5.719 SD MiB; check.sh OK), before and after the reboot from the API at 14:41:15 UTC: systemd-networkd active, NetworkManager not, the uplink enP4p65s0 on netplan's file. A bridge unoscheckbr without ports: no revert, kept at once, files in /run and /etc/unos/netdevs, uplink unchanged (0.289); VLAN 3999 unoscheckvl on the uplink not kept: revert_in 119, undone after 131 s by unos-netdevs-revert (0.047); the same VLAN kept after the LAN checks (0.207); a bond of the uplink alone 422, with the bridge as a port 409 (the VLAN on the uplink refused first); with both kept and a failsafe unit armed, the reboot: the uplink's addresses and routes as before, both interfaces back, unos-netdevs.service before systemd-networkd, wait-online 4.959 s; then the VLAN deleted (kept after the LAN checks) and the bridge: nothing of UNOS's left; every LAN check (443, 80, 445, SSH) OK after every change. UNOS leaves an empty /etc/unos after the last interface goes. Open: step 1, a real bond, which needs a second network card (the owner's, a USB NIC).

features.description: Disabling a network interface asks for confirmation and turns the interface back on by itself unless the change is confirmed
steps: Disable an interface in System > Network: a dialog names the interface and warns that the connection to UNOS may drop
Unless the change is confirmed from the page within a set time, the interface comes back on by itself
A confirmed change stays after that time
features.notes: Built (ADR-0244, ADR-0246): Disable asks in a dialog that names the interface and warns that the connection may drop. POST /network/interfaces/{name}/down saves the interface's addresses and routes in /run/unos/network on the host, arms the transient systemd timer unos-network-revert-<if> (60 seconds) and only then disables it; it refuses (the interface stays enabled) when the state cannot be saved or the timer cannot be armed, and (409) for an interface that carries VLANs without loose binding, which the kernel turns off and on with it. The page counts down, the newest countdown first and with the focus on the countdowns, and offers Keep (POST .../down/confirm); a Keep whose host command fails or does not answer in time answers from the marker on the host. Without Keep the timer turns the interface back on with its saved addresses and routes, also when the supervisor restarts. When the page's time runs out it looks again 5 seconds later and reports what it finds: back on, still counting on the host (countdown and Keep again), still off with nothing waiting (a revert that could not turn it on, or a Keep elsewhere: reported, with Enable), gone from the host, or not readable. Wherever UNOS finds the interface on again (Enable, Keep), it discards the saved state, unless the revert is restoring it. The fake-host tests, the tests of the host scripts under sh and dash and the E2E spec pass. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): disable a NIC that does not carry the connection and wait: after 60 seconds `ip link` shows it up again, `ip route` and `ip -6 addr` show its default route and IPv6 addresses again, `journalctl -u unos-network-revert-<if>` shows the revert and /run/unos/network/<if> holds no pending file; disable it and press Keep: it is still down after 60 seconds, `systemctl list-timers` lists no unos-network-revert timer, and Enable brings back its routes; disable it, press Keep, turn it on on the host (`ip link set dev <if> up`) and send `POST /network/interfaces/<if>/up`: it answers 200 and /run/unos/network/<if> holds no saved files; disable the NIC that carries the web UI: the page reaches UNOS again within about a minute; after a reboot every interface is up. Whether the dev device's network manager turns a kept disable back on by itself is unknown until then. Device check 2026-11-07 on the VLAN enP4p65s0.99 (the device has one NIC, which carries the connection): disabled through the API it was down on the host with revert_in 59, came back on by itself after 60 seconds, and a disable that was kept stayed down after 70 seconds; no revert timer was left (0.082 MiB on the SD card).

Hide a widget, and show it again
features.notes: Built 2026-11-17 on the workstation (ADR-0395); not host-level. Per user on the server: the new table dashboard_layouts and GET, PUT and DELETE /api/v1/auth/me/dashboard-layout (every signed-in user, own layout only; ids of widgets as ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$, once each, 1 to 64, hidden a boolean, else 422; the server knows no widget catalog; a stored value that is no valid layout reads as the default), written only for a real change and audited as dashboard_layout_changed; the row goes with its user. Customize shows a toolbar per widget: a drag handle (HTML5 drag and drop), Move up and Move down (keyboard and phone, focus kept, a live region), Hide; Hidden widgets with Show, and Reset to default. Unknown ids in a stored layout are ignored, missing widgets come last. Tested: test_dashboard_layout.py, dashboard-layout.spec.ts (drag and reload, keyboard, hide and show, reset, unknown ids, save and load failures, only the user's changes reach the API, Russian, a regular user in two browsers) and the phone view in mobile-layout.spec.ts. Dragging with a finger is not supported by design: the buttons are the touch alternative. Reviewed in a fresh context: no BLOCKING finding; fixed: stat cards' equal height, Refresh while a save runs, focus after Hide, Show and Reset, a failed save announced, the drag spec's exact order. Left: two concurrent identical PUTs may both write and audit (last writer wins, harmless); the wide widgets' two-column rows begin at 1280 px, so 1024 to 1279 px shows one per row (disclosed in ADR-0395); the Alert component has no live-region role, so the failed save is announced through the page's status region. Device check of 991cb28 on 2026-11-17: the default {"widgets":[]}; a PUT 200, read back, one dashboard_layout_changed entry (SD MiB 0.070); the same PUT again wrote nothing and no entry (0.000); the layout survived a reboot, and DELETE gave the default with one entry. With auth.token-storage the dashboard's Refresh without a session gets a 401 for each of its two requests (roles.spec.ts).

The navigation folds into a menu

The cause: webui/src/routes/audit/+page.svelte showed the entry's details, where supervisor/src/auth/router.py writes the token's name ("Created API token: <name>", "Deleted API token: <name>"), and its user and address without breaking. Both steps: the view "Audit Log with long names" of webui/tests/mobile-layout.spec.ts, at 375 x 812 in English and in Russian, serves three entries as the server writes them (route fakes, ADR-0189): the token's creation and deletion and a failed sign-in with a name of 128 characters (MAX_USERNAME_CHARS of supervisor/src/audit/router.py), each from a full IPv6 address and with a browser; it waits for each entry and checks that neither the document nor an element scrolls sideways and nothing is cut off at the side. features.description: The check that the balance dialog fits a phone held sideways does not depend on timing: it passes when mobile-layout.spec.ts runs alone and in the full run
steps: Find why 'On a phone held sideways › Dialog: balance a pool fits the screen' of mobile-layout.spec.ts fails when the spec runs without the other specs, though it passed in two full runs of make e2e-local
Fix the cause, in the page or in the test, without a retry
The test passes ten times in a row alone, the spec passes with audit.spec.ts, with which the test failed before, and make e2e-local passes the test
features.notes: Found on 2026-11-17 while webui.audit-log-long-token-name was built: the test failed 10 times of 10 alone (scripts/standin/e2e.sh tests/mobile-layout.spec.ts --grep 'held sideways.*balance a pool' --repeat-each 10), also 3 times of 3 alone with the spec and the Storage page of main, and in a run of mobile-layout.spec.ts with audit.spec.ts, but passed in two full runs: once Every chunk (full balance) was chosen, the dialog's title had a viewport ratio of 0. The cause is in the test, not in the page: Select's list flies in for 150 ms (in:fly), and the view clicked its option at once. Playwright 1.57's click found the option moving on its first try and on its retries after 0 and 20 ms; the try that finds it at rest forces scrollIntoView by its number (none, end, center, start, in turn), and the fourth, after a wait of 100 ms, forced block 'start': the option went to the top of the dialog's overlay, which, 375 px high with a dialog of 452 px, scrolled to its end, 109 px, before the tap, and kept that when the warning and the confirmation made the dialog 604 px high. The page scrolls the overlay only on the keyboard's moves through the list, and a finger scrolls nothing there. On the other views the overlay does not scroll at that point (at 375 x 812 the dialog fits), and no other view chooses an option. How many tries the list takes to rest depends on timing: a click that comes once the list rests, as under a heavy load, scrolls nothing, the likely reason for the passes in the full runs; on main 5623bc1 a full run with Playwright's log (DEBUG=pw:api) failed the test the same way, the overlay at 109 px after the fourth try (840 passed; security.spec.ts's 'a failed reload of the certificates shows no stale list' failed too, outside this change). Fixed in the view's steps: settled() of mobile-layout.spec.ts waits until the list has no animation of its own left (Element.getAnimations(); Svelte keeps the finished animation until its transition ends), and the first try then taps the option without scrolling, as a finger does. Not done: scrolling the title back into view after the tap, which would also hide a page that scrolls its overlay. Step 3: with the change the test passed 10 times of 10 alone, mobile-layout.spec.ts with audit.spec.ts passed (174 tests), and make e2e-local passed (842, 14 skips on listed conditions); after the review's wording changes the three views of the balance dialog passed 10 times each alone. features.description: The web UI can be shown in another language, Russian first
steps: The Account page offers English and Russian
Every text of the web UI comes from a catalog with both
features.notes: First of two phases (ADR-0287). Built: the lookup and the stores of webui/src/lib/i18n/ (one catalog per area with English and Russian halves, plural forms by Intl.PluralRules, the choice kept in this browser as unos-locale, <html lang> after it, Russian by default for a browser set to Russian, dates in the browser's format when it is of the page's language and else day first on a 24-hour clock), the Language card of the Account page, and the texts in both languages of the navigation and the frame (+layout.svelte, the tabs of the System page), the login and setup pages, the Account page (SecurityTab.svelte with RecoveryCodes and SmbAccessCard; the firewall's and the certificates' values through maps from the server's values to keys, a certificate's openssl dates in the page's language) and the shared components of src/lib/components/ui. Step 1: webui/tests/language.spec.ts switches an administrator's Account page to Russian and sees the navigation and the page change at once, stay Russian after a reload and on the login page after signing out, and go back to English; switches a regular user's Account page to Russian, also after a reload; shows the firewall's and the certificates' values in both languages; and checks that a browser set to Russian starts in Russian and that an English page in it writes dates day first. Step 2 is not done: the .svelte files listed in webui/scripts/i18n-untranslated.txt still show English texts, and the second phase translates them one area at a time, each taking its files off the list. make frontend runs webui/scripts/i18n-check.mjs (supervisor/tests/test_i18n.py), which fails, in a .svelte file that is not listed, for text between tags, a user-facing attribute or prop, and every string literal of a script or a markup expression that is not code (compared or looked up, a key, a class, a name, a path; a literal exempted with i18n-ignore and its reason); for a listed file with nothing left to translate; for a key that no catalog has; and for a catalog whose ru half differs from the en half. It cannot see a text that the code puts together from data at run time, a single lower-case word in a script, or a .ts module, so the empty list is necessary, not sufficient: passes stays false until the list is empty and a walk through every page in Russian, by a reviewer in a fresh context, finds no English text other than the server's messages. Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): no device check needed. Second phase, apps: the App Store (src/routes/apps/+page.svelte and src/lib/components/apps/) takes its texts from catalog/apps.ts, names each category with the label of its category list (AppCategory.svelte) and writes the sizes of the pools in the number format and the units of the page's language; webui/tests/apps.spec.ts shows the catalog, the details of an app and the installed apps in Russian. The names, descriptions and variables of the apps and their memory recommendations stay in English, as the server's app catalog has them, so the walk of ADR-0287 still finds English there. ADR-0291, proposed to the owner and not yet decided, would count them with the server's messages and keep the category list's labels on the English cards (Smart Home, AI & LLMs and Downloads, where they said Home Automation, Ai and Download); refused, the cards get keys of their own with their former words, and the app catalog needs a translation before this feature passes. Second phase, the dashboard and Files: the dashboard (src/routes/+page.svelte and its widgets, the containers' states through a map) and Files with its trash, with the units of their sizes, rates and times from their own catalogs and the numbers' decimal point kept (ADR-0297); dashboard.spec.ts ('shows the dashboard in Russian', with the stats cards of a fake stats socket, and a regular user's) and files.spec.ts ('shows Files and the trash in Russian', 'Files and the trash count, size and date their items in Russian') show them in Russian, with the counts in their plural forms, the sizes, rates, times and dates that the code puts together at run time, while the server's messages stay English; dashboard.spec.ts 'the stats cards write sizes, rates and the temperature with their units' keeps their English. Left for one change across the areas (ADR-0297): formatBytes and formatBytesPerSecond of src/lib/stores/stats.ts still write English units, which the translated Images tab of the Containers page shows in Russian too; and the App Store writes numbers with a decimal comma (ADR-0291), the dashboard and Files with a decimal point. The check of the texts does not see either, so the walk of ADR-0287 has to. Translated in phase B: System > Notifications and System > Network (NotificationsTab.svelte and NetworkTab.svelte, catalogs notifications and network), off the list; webui/tests/notifications.spec.ts and webui/tests/network.spec.ts check each tab in Russian (its texts, plural forms, the server's values through maps of keys, a channel's events by their names, dates, and the link speeds and the live traffic of the stats stream in the page's units and number format), and the values that ip and ss print in the Network tab's tables stay as they come (ADR-0295); supervisor/tests/test_notifications.py checks that the English half of the notifications catalog names and describes the server's events word for word. formatBytes and formatBytesPerSecond of webui/src/lib/stores/stats.ts still write English units on the pages that use them. Second phase, the System tabs Resource Monitor, System Logs, Disk Health and Power Management and the Audit Log page: they take their texts from the catalogs monitor, logs, health, power and audit, and the server's values through maps (log sources, levels and time ranges; SMART states, attribute states, NVMe fields and the units of a disk's capacity; audit actions, severities and types of resource). The Resource Monitor writes its sizes, rates and percentages, and Disk Health a disk's capacity, in the number format of the page (a decimal comma in Russian) and its units, as the Network tab does. Each spec of these pages has a test in Russian, and test_logs_sources.py, test_audit_log.py and test_health_smart.py tie the maps to the server's log sources, audit actions and types of resource, and disk capacities. On a Russian page the Audit Log names actions and resources in Russian, but its search finds them by their English words only, as the page says when a search finds nothing, while ADR-0237 has the search find them as the page shows them: ADR-0298, proposed to the owner and not yet decided, would make that exception, and until then ADR-0237 stands and this feature does not pass with it; refused, the Russian page names them by ADR-0237's English words, or the search also finds the names of the page's language. Second phase, shares: the Shares page (src/routes/shares/+page.svelte and src/lib/components/shares/, the SMB state badge that the Users page shows too) takes its texts from catalog/shares.ts, also those that texts.ts and access.ts held, among them the page's own copies of the server's answers, shown before anything is sent (a pool's top level or apps/ as the folder, the guest warning), whose English stays the server's word for word; GET /shares/paths answers each location's name instead of an English label, and the forms write its kind in the page's language (ADR-0300); the time of a repair run follows $intlLocale; the sentences around a share's name or a folder's path (the two deletion dialogs, the folder of a share that is not served) are translated in parts (ADR-0296). webui/tests/shares.spec.ts shows in Russian the SMB tab with its share cards, the dialog of a share that is not served, the dialog of a new share with the access picker and the SMB states, Repair permissions with a run and its counts, and the deletion of a share, and webui/tests/nfs-exports.spec.ts the NFS tab with its exports and clients and the dialogs of an export, and both read the sentences in parts whole in English and in Russian; the server's messages, a share's import notes and the reason a share is not served stay in English. Done 2026-11-08: webui/scripts/i18n-untranslated.txt is empty, and npm run i18n (make frontend) finds no text outside the catalogs: 1782 keys in English and Russian over 55 .svelte files. Step 1: webui/tests/language.spec.ts; step 2: the check and the Russian test of each page's spec.

features.description: Pages that show changing data get it over the WebSocket, never by polling the API
steps: Container details, System > Logs, Storage and System > Updates update without setInterval polling
A test fails when a component fetches the API from setInterval
features.notes: Built: no page polls the API. Container details stream their log over /ws/v1/logs/{id} (ADR-0255, apps.containers-and-images: containers.spec.ts 'the log of a container streams live over the WebSocket'), and UpdateTab.svelte asks only on Check again (updates.spec.ts). System > Logs' Auto follows the host's journal over /ws/v1/journal (ADR-0366): the socket takes the values of GET /api/v1/logs/entries in its URL, sends the newest entries as that request answers them, then each new entry of the source, level and search from a `journalctl --follow --lines=all` on the host that starts --after-cursor= the newest entry it sent (or --since=@<the second it read at> when it sent none) and that HostStream.stop ends with its process group when the client leaves or its access is revoked (host.stream_on_host); errors send {"type": "error"} and close with 1000. The Storage page follows a running scrub over /ws/v1/events (ADR-0367): storage/scrubs.py keeps each pool whose scrub was seen running (the scrub API's answers, a status read's failure, the Scheduler's start), an administrator's events socket asks for a read of the scrubs that run at most every 2 seconds without waiting for it, and sends {"type": "scrubs"} whenever they change; nothing is read while no administrator is connected, and a read that a request answered meanwhile is dropped. Step 1: test_ws_auth.py TestTheJournalSocket, TestTheJournalSocketsErrors and TestTheJournalSocketsRoles (against test_logs_sources.py's FakeJournal, which follows from a cursor or a time), test_host_tools.py (the stream of a real local command, a forked child ended with the group, a line over the limit dropped), TestTheScrubsOnTheEventsSocket, test_storage.py TestScrubsForTheEventsSocket and test_scheduler_validation.py test_scrub_task; logs.spec.ts 'Auto follows new entries over the journal socket and never asks the API again' (page.clock runs a minute with no request) and 'Auto stops when the journal socket ends, and says why'; storage.spec.ts 'Scrub (fake data)' on a fake events socket (one status read at the load, none while a minute passes). Step 2: a static check, webui/scripts/polling-check.mjs, run by test_webui_polling.py (ADR-0365), not a spec that fakes timers: it reaches every component and every state, also those no spec brings about, and runs in make test; it failed on LogsTab.svelte, storage/+page.svelte and the countdown of NetworkTab.svelte, which reads the interfaces once when its time has run out and is exempted with polling-ignore. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). On the device: System > Logs with Auto shows a line that `logger -t unos-check` writes on the host within a few seconds without a reload, also with the search unos-check, and after Auto is turned off or the tab is left no journalctl --follow is left on the host (pgrep -af 'journalctl --follow'); a scrub started on the Storage page, and one of a Run now of a scheduled scrub task, shows its progress growing and then its result without a reload, and no GET of the scrub status follows the page's load (the browser's network view). scripts/dev/scenario.sh scrub could check the scrubs messages of /ws/v1/events while its scrub runs. Review fixes 2026-11-12: after the events socket drops and connects again, the Storage page reads each mounted pool it shows running or unreadable (storage.spec.ts 'after the events socket connects again, the page reads each scrub it shows running or unreadable' failed first). The polling check follows exported functions of src/ .ts modules and fails a timer that changes a store or a variable an API-reaching $: statement reads (TestOtherModules, TestWhatATimerChanges; gaps in ADR-0365). Deployed 2026-11-12 (main 7827340) and checked on the device around the reboot from the API at 19:37:03 UTC on 2026-11-12 (the boot of 19:37:58; both containers healthy by 19:38:50) with the shares, restore, smb and backups scenarios; the pages' live data is shown by the E2E specs on the stand-in (ADR-0215).

The web UI waits for the supervisor's health check, which gets 10 minutes of start period
The health checks carry no credentials
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (scripts/dev/deploy.sh up: both containers healthy). Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): both containers healthy after the boot (step 1). Step 2 holds for docker compose up only: at boot dockerd's restart policy (unless-stopped) starts both containers at once, the web UI 34 ms before the supervisor, and the web UI's first health check failed (23:00:14 UTC) before it turned healthy, so after a reboot the web UI did not wait for the supervisor's health check. Since 2026-11-09 the web UI's command waits for the API before Caddy starts, whoever starts the container (ADR-0307; the owner left the choice to the agent). Device check of 2026-11-09 (01:18 UTC, scripts/dev/deploy.sh up webui): the web UI recreated with that command, healthy after 6 s, Caddy its PID 1; busybox's wget of the image takes its options. Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-09 (ADR-0018, 78bb5b8 on the device, the boot of 07:17:13 UTC): dockerd started both containers at once again, and the web UI's command logged one wait, `waiting for the supervisor's API: wget: can't connect to remote host (172.31.254.3): Connection refused` (07:17:06, by the clock before timesyncd set it at 07:17:28); Caddy's first line came at 07:17:34.27 UTC, after the supervisor's `Application startup complete` at 07:17:32.78, so step 2 holds also at boot, as Caddy waiting for the health route that the supervisor's check requests (start period 600 s). Both containers healthy with no restart and check.sh OK (step 1); both health checks request /api/v1/health without credentials (step 3); Caddy is the web UI's PID 1.

features.description: The Dockerfiles pin their base images by digest
steps: Every FROM line names its image by tag and digest (name:tag@sha256:...)
Dependabot proposes the digest updates

A supervisor build on the dev device, after the linux/arm64 image of its base's tag has moved upstream, starts from the pinned base in its build cache: it pulls no base and does not run apt-get or pip again
features.notes: The pins (ADR-0305) are the digests the dev device held on 2026-11-08: python:3.11-slim@sha256:65bd3d9f... in its build cache, the base of deploy-supervisor:latest, and caddy:2-alpine@sha256:f2b257f2..., the base of deploy-webui:latest; node and the Playwright image take the registry's digests of that day. That day the registry's python:3.11-slim named sha256:07d48240..., with the same linux/arm64 image (sha256:31afb5c0...) and only riscv64 rebuilt, so an unpinned build would still have reused the cache. Step 1: TestBaseImages in supervisor/tests/test_deploy_scripts.py. deploy.sh build-supervisor says before the build whether the pinned base is on the device (test_deploy_sh_build_supervisor_says_whether_its_pinned_base_is_on_the_device). Not yet checked: step 2 (the first Dependabot pull request that moves a digest: its cooldown counts from the tag's last push) and step 3 (a deploy once python:3.11-slim names an arm64 image other than sha256:31afb5c0...: build-supervisor says the base is on the device, every step of the build is CACHED, and the SD writes stay in single MiB). Deploy of main 78769b4 on 2026-11-08: build-supervisor said the pinned base is on the device (layers of the build cache pulled from sha256:65bd3d9f...), COPY requirements.txt, pip install and COPY src/ were CACHED and nothing was pulled (6.094 MiB on the SD card); build-webui built the final stage from the pinned caddy image on the device with --pull=false (18.539 MiB). Whether the tag's arm64 image had moved upstream by then was not checked, so step 3 stays open.

features.description: The supervisor's /tmp tmpfs fits boards with 1 GB of RAM
steps: The tmpfs size follows the owner's choice: 25 percent of RAM, or a lower fixed cap with a lower backup size limit
Backups and restores within the limit still work on a 1 GB board
features.notes: The owner's choice (delegated) is a lower fixed cap, ADR-0406: /tmp is size=192m in both compose files, and a backup's database is limited to 48 MiB, the archive and the decompressed tar to 64 MiB; a database over the limit is refused before it is copied, with the limit in the message (413 for Create Backup), and uploads and restores name their limits. A host-level change (GLOSSARY.md): the container's tmpfs changes with the deploy, so the reboot rule of ADR-0018 applies. Device check, by hand, with the device-checks skill, after the owner's /deploy-device: (1) the supervisor's /tmp size: `scripts/dev/sd.sh measure tmpfs-size -- scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker exec unos-supervisor df -m /tmp'` shows a tmpfs of 192 MiB (the Size column), and `scripts/dev/sd.sh measure tmpfs-options -- scripts/dev/ssh.sh "docker inspect -f '{{json .HostConfig.Tmpfs}}' unos-supervisor"` shows /tmp with noexec,nosuid,nodev,size=192m, and `scripts/dev/sd.sh measure db-size -- scripts/dev/api.py GET /health/full` shows components.database.size_mb far below 48; (2) `scripts/dev/scenario.sh backups` and (3) `scripts/dev/scenario.sh restore` pass, each with its SD MiB (the checks' backups are a few MiB, within the limits); (4) after the owner's reboot, steps 1 to 3 again. Review (fresh context) findings: fixed the off-device copy's allowance in the tmpfs (80 MiB for restic's packs), the wrong api.py path, the archive headroom, the decrypt copies, the tests of the scheduled task and the configuration archive, the stale backup.upload step (ADR-0406), the test of file uploads of any size; left open, with the reason: the restic cache of an S3 store is unbounded in /tmp, so its copy fails with a full tmpfs instead of taking the board's memory (ADR-0406 says so; bounding it is a later entry). Not on the device: a database over the limit and a 1 GB board, which the backend tests show (test_backup_files.py, test_deploy_scripts.py TestTemporaryFiles). Device check of 09e792a on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB): the supervisor's /tmp is a tmpfs of 192 MiB (size=192m) and the backup's database size 0.19 MiB, below the 48 MiB limit, before and after a reboot from the API (15:07 UTC); the backups and restore scenarios passed under the new limits (0.469 and 7.887); deploy SD MiB sync 4.902, build-supervisor 15.219, build-webui 20.574, up 5.945, check.sh 0.844.

features.description: uninstall.sh restarts smbd once and restores smb.conf.original atomically
steps: With smb.conf.original present, uninstall.sh restarts smbd once
The restore writes a temporary file and moves it into place
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-10 (ADR-0322, which supersedes ADR-0180). Step 1: with smb.conf.original, remove_samba_passwords leaves the restart to restore_samba_config, whose restart of smbd and nmbd with the restored file also ends the removed passwords' connections; when the restore fails, it runs systemctl try-restart smbd instead (test_with_smb_conf_original_smbd_restarts_once, test_a_copy_that_fails_halfway_leaves_smb_conf_whole, test_a_rename_that_fails_leaves_smb_conf_whole), and a failed restart after the restore is reported (test_a_restart_that_fails_after_the_restore_is_reported). Step 2: the restore copies the file with cp -p to .smb.conf.unos-restore.unos-tmp in /etc/samba and renames it over smb.conf before Samba restarts (test_the_restore_copies_next_to_smb_conf_and_renames_before_samba_restarts); a copy or rename that fails leaves smb.conf as UNOS wrote it and no temporary file, and a removal of the temporary file that fails does not end the script (test_a_temporary_file_that_cannot_go_does_not_stop_the_uninstallation). The first three tests failed on the script before. Open: host-level (GLOSSARY.md: it restarts smbd and replaces /etc/samba/smb.conf), so the check on a host and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), by hand with the device-checks skill: uninstall.sh never runs on the dev device, as for deploy.uninstall-script.

features.description: install.sh and update.sh start UNOS without the compose down kept for networks of releases before the fixed subnet
steps: update.sh restarts with docker compose up -d, and the comment about releases without the fixed subnet is gone
install.sh starts UNOS without docker compose down --remove-orphans, and its comment about older installs is gone
tests/test_deploy_scripts.py checks both starts
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-10. Step 1: restart_services of update.sh runs docker compose up -d --no-build --remove-orphans alone, which recreates the containers of the new images and removes those of services that a release dropped or renamed, as the old down --remove-orphans did; the comment on the networks of releases without the fixed subnet is gone (TestUpdateScript test_builds_while_running_then_switches_and_prunes_after_health: no compose down in an update; test_every_compose_up_waits_for_the_supervisor_start_or_the_health_timeout: the exact up). Step 2: start_unos of install.sh runs docker compose up --remove-orphans without a compose down before it, and its comment on older installs is gone (TestInstallScript test_the_start_runs_no_compose_down_before_up, also that neither script mentions the fixed subnet; test_start_and_the_unit_wait_at_most_the_start_timeout: the exact up, and the unit's ExecStart unchanged). The no-down tests failed before the change. An interrupt of the restart now comes during its compose up (the docker stub's interrupt-at-up), and the rollback starts the previous version as before; the rollback itself still runs compose down first. A change of the subnet needs docker compose down by hand, as docs/INSTALL.md says (ADR-0048). Open: host-level (GLOSSARY.md, the host's containers), and neither script has run on a host in this phase (the dev device is deployed with scripts/dev/deploy.sh): a run of install.sh and of update.sh on a host, with the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), as for deploy.install-script and deploy.update-script.

Step 1: the copy in deploy/ is deleted, and webui/Caddyfile stays: webui/Dockerfile copies it into the image, and neither compose file mounts a Caddyfile. test_the_web_ui_has_one_caddyfile lists the repository's files named Caddyfile (two before the change) and checks the COPY line and the compose volumes. Step 2: git grep finds the copy's path only in this entry's steps (test_nothing_refers_to_a_copy_of_the_caddyfile_in_deploy, added after the review). The deploy component's runtime files of scripts/dev/tree.py, the copy's header check in test_standin.py, the web UI container of test_apps.py (a bind of the copy that the real container never had), the comment of webui/Caddyfile, deploy/AGENTS.md, webui/AGENTS.md and ADR-0025 (its decision unchanged, corrected in place) no longer name it. The device's checkout keeps the copy until the next sync of deploy.sh deletes it; nothing reads it there. make check passed; make e2e-local did not run: the stand-in serves the web UI through scripts/standin/front.mjs, never through webui/Caddyfile, whose headers test_standin.py compares, and the build does not read it. A fresh-context review found both steps met, step 2 without a test (added), and the record of the checks missing. Not host-level.

features.description: install.sh recognizes the smb.conf that UNOS wrote by its header line alone
steps: install.sh keeps an existing /etc/samba/smb.conf only when it starts with the line '# Generated by UNOS from its database.'
A file that only has server string = UNOS NAS is handled like any other smb.conf of the host
tests/test_deploy_scripts.py checks both cases
features.notes: Done in the code 2026-11-10 (ADR-0316). Step 1: configure_samba of deploy/install.sh keeps an existing /etc/samba/smb.conf only when its first two lines are the supervisor's header, which starts with '# Generated by UNOS from its database.' (TestInstallScript test_rerun_keeps_a_file_that_starts_with_the_unos_header, test_rerun_keeps_the_smb_conf_that_unos_generated). Step 2: a file that only has server string = UNOS NAS, a part of the header or the header below its first line is replaced by the file of render_config([]), like any other smb.conf of the host, and kept as smb.conf.original only when there is none yet (test_a_file_that_does_not_start_with_the_unos_header_is_replaced, test_a_rerun_keeps_no_copy_of_a_file_it_replaces). The tests failed before the change, but for the header below the first line, which the old check replaced too. Open: host-level (GLOSSARY.md: Samba's smb.conf on the host), and install.sh has not run on a host in this phase (the dev device is deployed with scripts/dev/deploy.sh): on a host, a second run of install.sh prints 'Keeping /etc/samba/smb.conf: it is already managed by UNOS' and leaves the file byte for byte, and a file with only the server string is replaced while smb.conf.original stays as it was, with the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), as for deploy.install-script.

features.description: The UNOS containers' logs no longer grow on the system disk with every request
steps: docker logs still shows the recent lines of unos-supervisor and unos-webui
On the dev device, 100 API calls with a cached token write at most 0.1 MiB to the SD card, measured with scripts/dev/sd.sh
features.notes: Built (ADR-0338, which supersedes ADR-0176): uvicorn's access log keeps only the requests that answered 400 or above (_RefusedOrFailedRequestFilter of supervisor/src/main.py); Caddy logs no requests. Step 1: test_only_refused_and_failed_requests_reach_the_access_log of test_authz.py, a real uvicorn server with requests answering 200 to 500, which failed before (every request but a successful health check was logged); docker logs keeps the supervisor's own lines, warnings and errors. Measured before the change on 2026-11-11 (main b290ada): 60 idle seconds wrote 0.000 MiB, 100 calls of GET /api/v1/auth/me with the cached token 0.105 MiB, and the supervisor's json-file log was the only container log that grew. After the deploy of main 96db310 (ADR-0338) at 15:16 UTC (SD MiB sync 1.129, build-supervisor 12.336, up 3.250, check.sh 0.016): 60 idle seconds 0.016 MiB, 100 calls of GET /api/v1/auth/me with the cached token 0.016 MiB (15:18 to 15:19 UTC), and docker logs unos-supervisor kept its start lines and no access line of the calls or of the health checks. After the reboot from the API at 19:25:58 UTC (the boot of 19:26:54) and the scenario checks of all areas, measured with scripts/dev/sd.sh at 19:34 to 19:36 UTC: 60 idle seconds 0.016 MiB, the 100 calls 0.000 MiB, all answered 200, and docker logs of the last 5 minutes held 9 lines of unos-supervisor, none of the calls; at 19:42 UTC docker logs unos-webui held 49 lines, 32 of the last 30 minutes, the newest Caddy's TLS lines of 19:27 UTC, both containers with json-file max-size 10m, max-file 3.

features.description: The device checks of the host-level entries are scripts in the repository that report their SD writes
steps: scripts/dev/ has a check per area (files, volumes, SMART, backups, the SMB flows with a temporary account and share) that cleans up after itself
Each check prints its results and the MiB it wrote to the SD card
The feature-pass skill names the check of each host-level entry
features.notes: Built (ADR-0304); before, the device checks of the slice 1 and slice 2 deploys were scratch scripts outside the repository. scripts/dev/scenario.sh [--pool NAME] AREA... (files, volumes, smart, backups, smb; all: every area) holds the device lock and runs scripts/dev/scenario.py once per area. Step 1: each check reads the device's state first and refuses to start beside names of an earlier check, makes a temporary user, share, volume and folders named unoscheck and six hex digits, and two backups, through the API, registers each clean-up before the call that makes its thing, removes them newest first, also after a FAIL, a lost answer or a signal, and compares the device with the state it read; files: New Folder and Upload (755 and 644 root:root), Download, Rename, Copy, Move, Delete into the pool's trash, Restore, a restore refused while the name is taken, Delete for good, a volume that Delete, Rename and Move refuse with 409 and Copy copies, the volume's own trash, a folder with a subvolume below it refused; volumes: a volume without a quota, one with a quota (refused while quotas are off, else its quota group's limit read with btrfs), the Delete refused while a share uses it; smart: the disks of Storage and Disk Health, their SMART data, the system disk, a partition and a name of no disk refused with 400, a short self-test; backups: a plain and an encrypted backup, the restores refused for a missing backup and without or with a wrong passphrase (never a restore), no passphrase in the logs; smb: the flows of ADR-0185 with a temporary account and share (the marked host account and Samba account, the folder's 2770 root:unos-smb, a signed session that writes, New Folder and Upload in the share's folder changed over SMB, the access lowered and removed during open sessions, a comment with the expected version and a stale one refused, a password change that ends the open session, the replaced password refused without a write to passdb.tdb, a wrong password and a null session refused, the [global] lines, Samba's log in /run/samba, no password of the check in an answer or a log, the share's Delete keeping its folder, the user's Delete removing its accounts), each session step naming Samba's NT_STATUS. Step 2: every step prints PASS or FAIL with the SD MiB written meanwhile, and scenario.sh prints SD writes scenario <area> for each check, also one that a signal ended. Step 3: the feature-pass skill's table names the check of each host-level entry (a scenario area, or by hand with the steps of the entry's notes) and what each scenario check leaves out; its test fails for an entry whose notes name the reboot rule of ADR-0018 and that the table lacks. Tests: test_dev_scenarios.py runs every area against a stand-in of the device in memory (each passes and leaves it as it was; a 500 at any API call of a step, before or after the call changed something, an interruption, an output that fails or a refusal of the device still removes everything, and a backup whose answer was lost is named; a signal waits for the clean-up and the device lock holds through it (test_dev_scripts.py); a failed clean-up and leftovers are reported; the defects each check exists for fail it; every call matches a route of the supervisor with a body its model accepts), runs the SMB helper's session and share-list protocol against a stand-in smbclient, the subvolume helper's path guard, scenario.sh's lock and SD lines, and the skill's table; test_dev_scripts.py the relay's upload and what the device-checks skill says about the lock and the SD writes. Reviewed twice in a fresh context (ADR-0017): the findings of both are fixed (PROGRESS.md, 2026-11-08). Device run 2026-11-08 before the reboot (scripts/dev/scenario.sh all, the pool data): every step passed, and each check left the device as it found it; SD writes files 0.418 MiB (16 steps), volumes 0.938 (7), smart 0.098 (5), backups 0.512 (8), smb 3.980 (27), 5.946 MiB in all. Run again after the deploy of main 78769b4 (22:33 UTC, still before the reboot): every step passed, 5.259 MiB. After the owner's reboot (the boot of 22:59:48 UTC, ADR-0018), 23:02 to 23:05 UTC: every step of the five areas passed again, 5.393 MiB (files 0.441, volumes 0.734, smart 0.105, backups 0.449, smb 3.664). Area smbconf (ADR-0309, 2026-11-09), also in all: the SMB steps that had been checked by hand (smb.conf edited by hand and named before an apply, the copy byte for byte in smb.conf.unos-replaced and its problem, a comment with the expected version and a stale one refused, a share not served through a symbolic link that gets access only with a new folder, Delete keeping the folder, a restart of the supervisor that writes no file in /etc/samba); its hand edit runs without the read-only namespace, and it restarts the supervisor once. It takes the device's first regular user for an access entry (a temporary one without SMB only when there is none), refuses to start beside a section that UNOS did not write, and waits for the startup reconcile after the restart. Device runs 2026-11-09: 13:22 UTC, 15 steps passed, 2.621 MiB; after the review's fixes 13:46 UTC, 15 steps passed, 2.391 MiB; the device as found each time. The area scrub (ADR-0314, 2026-11-09) runs the scrub steps that were checked by hand that day.

features.description: Each backend test run, and each worker of a parallel run, uses temporary paths of its own, so test runs can go in parallel
steps: tests/conftest.py sets no fixed /tmp path (test_smb.conf, test_exports, test_pools): each pytest process, a run's or a worker's, gets a temporary folder of its own for them, removed at its end, and every other file of a test is in its tmp_path
Two runs of make test at once, in two worktrees, both pass
features.notes: Built 2026-11-17 (ADR-0383). Step 1: supervisor/tests/conftest.py makes a temporary folder per pytest process (tempfile.mkdtemp, prefix unos-tests-, in TMPDIR) for UNOS_SMB_CONF_PATH, UNOS_NFS_EXPORTS_PATH and UNOS_POOLS_BASE_PATH, and removes it in pytest_unconfigure, or at the process's exit after a usage error; a probe fixture run over the whole suite found nothing in that folder before or after any test, so one folder per process suffices. test_test_paths.py: the settings point into the process's folder, and two pytest runs started at once each get a folder of their own and remove it. Step 2: make test ran in this worktree and in a second checkout of the branch at the same time, beside another worktree's make test of the old suite under the lock, on 2026-11-17: both passed (8096 passed, 118 skipped, 1 xfailed each, in 187 s and 200 s). A first such pair failed one test of test_dev_scenarios.py, whose fake balance paused 0.25 s after the check's wait ended; its margins are now a second on each side. make test runs the tests in pytest-xdist workers (TEST_WORKERS, default auto) and takes no machine-wide lock any more (test_repo_tooling.py test_the_test_targets_run_in_parallel_without_a_machine_wide_lock, test_the_tests_run_in_workers_with_pytest_xdist_and_in_one_process_without). Fixed for parallel runs, no assertion changed: test_totp_once.py (the ids of cases with a secret drawn at random in each process), test_dev_scenarios.py (the clean-up's SIGINT sent to the main thread, which an xdist worker's own threads took otherwise; the offsite poll set in the fixture without pauses, which had slept about 150 s in one test), test_dev_scripts.py (the holder of the device lock works until the test has looked at the lock, not 2 s, which a busy machine used up in one run of make check-fast beside the other runs). Measured on the workstation (10 cores, other worktrees' runs beside), before and after: the backend tests 719 s and 112 s (8048 passed before; the same tests and the new ones after), make check 746 s and 132 s (996 s before with its 250 s wait for the lock), make check-fast 324 s and 60 s (it had waited 409 s for the lock), make smoke 3.1 s and 2.1 s (it had waited 891 s). Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017); its findings were fixed but one, which is the lead's: whether ADR-0383 supersedes ADR-0210 and ADR-0216, whose statements on the lock it replaces. Not host-level.

features.description: The compose test stack runs once per worktree, with its own project name, ports and subnet
steps: The project name, the ports and the subnet of deploy/docker-compose.test.yml come from settings that scripts/test-cycle.sh derives from the worktree
Two worktrees run scripts/test-cycle.sh at once
Its down -v removes only its own project
features.notes: Built 2026-11-21 (ADR-0439). Step 1: deploy/docker-compose.test.yml takes its name:, container names, UNOS_WEBUI_CONTAINER, published ports, subnet, gateway, addresses and FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS from UNOS_TEST_PROJECT, UNOS_TEST_HTTP_PORT, UNOS_TEST_HTTPS_PORT and UNOS_TEST_SUBNET_PREFIX, with the old values as defaults; scripts/test-cycle.sh derives the project from the cksum of the checkout's physical path (unos-test-<8 hex>) and, after the build, the first of 100 slots from the path's own whose 172.31.(100+n).0/24 no Docker network has (HTTP 13080+n, HTTPS 13443+n). test_deploy_scripts.py: TestTestStack (the file read with and without the settings, as Compose interpolates it; docker compose config gave the same), TestTestStackPerWorktree (two checkouts of one name get two projects; a held slot moves a second worktree to the next free one; all 100 held stops before up; no project without a hash; the slot is chosen after the build). Step 2: this worktree and a temporary second one ran scripts/test-cycle.sh --quick at the same time, as unos-test-c31cae12 (13533, 172.31.190.0/24) and unos-test-e8769e4a (13525, 172.31.182.0/24): both stacks built, ran side by side and exited 0 (53 passed, 1 flaky, 18 skipped each); the held-slot path also ran against real Docker with a network on the slot's subnet. Step 3: every compose call passes -p, ahead of COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME (TestTestStackPerWorktree, with COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=deploy), and no volume or network of the file is external or named; in the run, the first stack's down -v removed its 2 containers, network and 6 volumes while the other's stayed, and nothing was left after both. features.description: On the compose test stack, auth.spec.ts's test of invalid credentials passes every run
steps: Every spec of a test-cycle.sh run reaches the supervisor from the stack network's gateway, so the sign-in rate limit counts the whole run as one client; the specs pass without the limit refusing a sign-in
auth.spec.ts 'should show error on invalid credentials' passes in three runs of scripts/test-cycle.sh in a row
features.notes: Seen 2026-11-21 by the builder of testing.compose-stack-per-worktree, on its stacks and on the base code's: the test fails when the run's earlier sign-ins used up the limit. The stand-in does not show it. Built 2026-11-22 (ADR-0452). The cause: scripts/test-cycle.sh runs Playwright on the test machine against the ports Docker publishes on 127.0.0.1, so the stack's Caddy sees every connection from the network's gateway and forwards it in X-Forwarded-For, which uvicorn --proxy-headers believes from FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=<prefix>.2, the web UI (ADR-0048); slowapi's get_remote_address of src/auth/limits.py then counts the whole run as one client of 5 a minute (ADR-0010). Shown on the base code's stack (unos-test-bd5b4f50, 172.31.104.0/24): test-cycle.sh --quick failed 'should show error on invalid credentials' in all 3 tries (52 passed, 1 failed, 1 flaky, 18 skipped), the supervisor logging '172.31.104.1:0 - POST /api/v1/auth/login 429'. The fix: supervisor/Dockerfile.test copies supervisor/tests/fixtures/stack_app.py and runs uvicorn stack_app:app, the app of src.main with the limiter of src/auth/limits.py off, as the stand-in turns it off (sign-in, first-run setup, own SMB access, security keys); supervisor/Dockerfile still copies only requirements.txt and src/ and runs src.main:app, and the trust rules are unchanged. Every limiter of supervisor/src now comes from client_limiter() of src/rate_limits.py, which gives the storage memory:// and sets enabled after building it: slowapi took RATELIMIT_ENABLED and RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URL from the environment or a .env file, which would have turned a limit off on a NAS too. Tests (test_authz.py TestTestStackSignInLimit): the sign-ins of a run forwarded from the gateway get 429 from the sixth on from src.main's app and are all answered by stack_app's, whose next right password gets 200 and whose login history holds the gateway; only the test image runs stack_app and no production file names it; Limiter is built only in rate_limits.py and no code of supervisor/src turns a limiter off; RATELIMIT_ENABLED=false and another RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URL leave a limiter on and in memory. test_auth.py and test_request_limits.py expect stack_app:app in the test image. Step 1: no sign-in refused in any run below (no 429 in the supervisor's log, which keeps every answer of 400 or more; the 401 of the invalid-credentials test came from 172.31.104.1, the gateway); a test-cycle.sh --e2e run on the code before the review's fixes (the same switch) was stopped after 446 of about 1185 tests to save time: 416 passed, 26 skipped, 4 failed attempts, all of them retried apps-stacks, apps-update and logs specs under the machine's load, none at a sign-in, and no 429. Step 2: on the final code, three scripts/test-cycle.sh --quick runs in a row (auth.spec.ts and api.spec.ts; unos-test-bd5b4f50, slot 4: 13447, 13084, 172.31.104.0/24) each passed the test at its first try: 54 passed, 18 skipped, none failed or flaky, exit 0; three earlier --quick runs before the review's fixes gave the same. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): test_request_limits.py still expected src.main:app in the test image (fixed); the six other limiters still took RATELIMIT_ENABLED from the environment (fixed with client_limiter) and the static check missed exempt routes and request filters (added); the gateway clause of step 1 needed a real stack's evidence (the supervisor logs above); stack_app imported src.auth.limits before src.main's logging setup (swapped); the docs named only the sign-in of the limiter's routes and the published port, not the test-runner (fixed); the production COPY check missed ADD, JSON form and '.' (fixed). Left, with the reason: RATELIMIT_HEADERS_ENABLED and RATELIMIT_SWALLOW_ERRORS are still read by slowapi (headers on would break the setup route with 500, swallowing needs a failing storage, which memory:// is not; neither turns a limit off, and production's compose file sets neither); root could point docker compose at the test stack's file through /etc/unos/secrets.env (that runs the unprivileged loopback-only test stack instead of UNOS, no setting of UNOS); uvicorn reads UVICORN_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS from its environment (pre-existing, reachable only by editing the tracked deploy/docker-compose.yml, which update.sh refuses): a feature-list entry for the lead to decide. Not host-level.

features.description: make check reports the backend's line coverage and fails below an agreed floor

features.notes: The February 2026 roadmap aimed at 80 percent; the owner left the floor to the agents ("decide yourself"), and it is the measure of 2026-11-21 rounded down (ADR-0442). Built 2026-11-21: make test, when TESTS names every test (tests/, as make check runs it; PYTEST_ARGS do not turn it off), adds pytest-cov's --cov=src --cov-report= over the workers of pytest-xdist and prints the total; each run's data is .coverage.run<pid>, renamed to the git-ignored supervisor/.coverage at its end. The floor is the one setting of supervisor/.coveragerc beside its precision of two decimals, and only rises (test_repo_tooling.py refuses one below a floor committed in HEAD's history, other settings and pragma: no cover in src). A part named in TESTS, make test-fast, make smoke and the hooks measure nothing. Measured on macOS, where make check runs and the Linux-only tests skip: 91.40% of 32879 statements, so the floor is 91; Linux measures more. coverage 7.17.2 is pinned beside pytest-cov 7.1.0 in supervisor/requirements-dev.txt; scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh bundles neither, and the coverage tests skip in its chroot. Step 1: test_coverage_floor.py (make test's own command, with two workers that each run one test, prints the total of a throwaway package, the sum of both workers) and test_repo_tooling.py (the coverage options on make test and make check over every test, also with PYTEST_ARGS, and on no part or other target). Step 2: test_coverage_floor.py (the same run fails at a floor of 86 over 85.71% with both tests passed, at two decimals, passes at 85, and leaves another run's data in the folder alone) and test_repo_tooling.py (the floor a whole percent in supervisor/.coveragerc alone, as coverage reads it, never below a committed one, the coverage data git-ignored). Review (ADR-0017, a fresh subagent), all fixed: the floor read with configparser, which a [coverage:report] section could disable unseen (now coverage's own reading); make check PYTEST_ARGS=-x passing without the floor (now measured whatever PYTEST_ARGS); a lowering through omit, exclusions or pragma: no cover (now refused, and an ADR's); worker summing untested (each worker now runs one test); the times missing from these notes; the measure written into docs/TESTING.md (now a form); the coverage tests erroring in the device's chroot (now skipped without git, make or pytest-cov); two runs in one checkout erasing or adding each other's data (now a data file per run). Gates on 2026-11-21, TEST_WORKERS=3 on the 10-core workstation beside other worktrees' runs: make check exited 0 in 1807 s at a load of 50 to 60, with 10771 passed, 124 skipped, 1 xfailed and "Required test coverage of 91.0% reached. Total coverage: 91.40%"; before this change it took 1079 s at a load of about 14 (its tests 867 s against 1687 s), so the loads, not the tracer, set most of the difference. make test with the floor raised to 92 failed with every test passed (10771): "Coverage failure: total of 91.40 is less than fail-under=92.00"; the floor is back at 91. Not host-level.

features.notes: Passed 2026-11-10, with its description and step 2 reworded by ADR-0317. Step 1: 2e4306d removed both skips of the SMB API's specs for a supervisor without that API, and the early return of their afterAll; no skip of webui/tests names a version of the supervisor. Step 2: test_standin.py reads every file of webui/tests and its folders that Playwright may load with TypeScript's parser (SKIP_SCAN, run by node with webui/node_modules/typescript) and reports every token whose text is one of the names, an identifier, a string, a template or a part of one; the member of a call on any object, also inside parentheses, a non-null assertion or a cast, gives its condition and reason, and a skip of test.describe or test.step gives (a title). A file that does not parse or holds JSX fails the check (test_a_file_that_typescript_cannot_parse_fails_the_check, test_jsx_in_a_spec_fails_the_check). test_every_skip_form_in_every_spec_file_is_seen holds 53 uses in six files: each detector before missed some of them, the last one the names in keys, declarations, enum members and class fields. test_specs_skip_only_on_the_listed_conditions refuses all of them but a skip on a listed condition, and every test.fixme, test.fail and expectedStatus (test_an_expected_failure_is_refused_on_any_condition); in a manual run, a skip of the SMB API on E2E_OLD_SUPERVISOR in a copy of webui/tests was found. test_every_skip_gives_its_reason and test_a_skip_without_its_reason_is_refused fail on a skip without a reason and on a stand-in skip whose reason does not start with what the stand-in lacks or does not end with TEST_STACK_TOO. In the real specs it finds the 28 skips that git grep shows, all on listed conditions, and no other use of the names: the variable fail of health.spec.ts is listingFails, and the fake of logs.spec.ts names its method failWith. Not seen: a name that the code builds or reads from data, and modules outside webui/tests (ADR-0317). features.description: No E2E skip or check passes over an API that answers an error: a skip fires only on what the local target lacks
steps: The File Browser specs of files.spec.ts skip only when no folder of the pools takes a new one, and fail when POST /files/mkdir answers an error for another reason
The import-notes specs of shares.spec.ts fail on a fresh stand-in whose seeded share has no import notes, instead of skipping
The GET /files/list check of api.spec.ts expects 200, as files.spec.ts does, and no check of api.spec.ts accepts a 404 or a 500 where the stand-in answers otherwise
The IPv6 hints of shares.spec.ts skip only when the stand-in does not answer on [::1], not on any answer of /api/v1/health that is not OK
features.notes: Found by the fresh-context review of testing.no-compat-skips on 2026-11-09: files.spec.ts (scratch === null) skips the whole describe whenever POST /files/mkdir fails, 404 and 5xx included; shares.spec.ts (notes.length === 0) names an earlier run that dismissed the notes, which never applies on a stand-in that e2e.sh starts fresh, so the skip fires only when the import stops writing notes; api.spec.ts accepts a 404 for GET /files/list. The review of 2026-11-10 added: api.spec.ts accepts a 500 (two checks) and a 404 (one more), and shares.spec.ts's !reachable is only that /api/v1/health answered OK. Passed 2026-11-10. Step 1: the beforeEach of the File Browser specs takes the first folder of the pools that takes a new folder and expects 403 "Permission denied" from each folder before it (an unmounted pool's mountpoint is immutable: EPERM); any other answer, a 403 for another reason included, fails the test with its status and text, and NO_POOL_FOLDER skips only when every folder refused so. Step 2: expectNotes fails without import notes; the Seeded specs run twice on one stand-in (--repeat-each 2) failed both notes specs in the second round, where the old skip passed over them; on the test stack a second run fails them until down -v (docs/TESTING.md). Step 3: GET /files/list expects 200, and GET /snapshots/?subvolume=<pools>/testpool 200 with no snapshots; GET /containers/images and GET /snapshots/subvolumes, which the stand-in answers with 500 (no Docker; no findmnt), skip on E2E_STAND_IN=1, which both local targets set, with their reasons (NO_DOCKER, NO_MOUNTED_POOLS); the backend tests hold their answers (test_containers.py: the images listed, no container route takes the name images; test_snapshots.py). Step 4: the IPv6 hints skip only when the request to [::1] is refused or this machine has no IPv6 loopback (health === null); any other failure of the request, and an answer that is not OK, fails the test. SKIP_CONDITIONS of test_standin.py lists health === null in place of !reachable, and notes.length === 0 no more, as ADR-0317 foresaw. Not host-level.
