features.notes: Built 2026-11-21 (ADR-0449): eslint 10.15.0, @eslint/js 10.0.1, typescript-eslint 8.72.2, eslint-plugin-svelte 3.24.1, prettier 3.10.1 and prettier-plugin-svelte 4.1.1, exact dev dependencies of webui/package.json. make frontend runs frontend-lint (npm run lint: eslint --max-warnings 0 src, with webui/eslint.config.js: the recommended rules of the three, five rules off with their reasons) and frontend-format (npm run format-check: prettier --check src, with webui/prettier.config.js: tabs, single quotes, no trailing commas, 120 columns), also when another part fails; the CI workflow's Frontend job runs make frontend. The base tree's 172 findings were resolved without a change of behaviour, and src/ was formatted once. Step 1: test_webui_lint.py (a finding of each set of rules, a warning and an unused exemption fail ESLint; a file that Prettier would change fails its check; Prettier's settings), test_targets_run_the_agreed_commands and test_lint_and_frontend_run_every_part_even_when_one_fails of test_repo_tooling.py, and make frontend itself. Step 2: test_frontend_checks of test_deploy_scripts.py shows that the Frontend job runs make frontend with lint and format-check; that the job fails on a finding is not seen: the workflow is off on GitHub (ADR-0230), so passes stays false until it runs there once with a finding. Review in a fresh context (ADR-0017): 2 should-fix and 7 nits, fixed but one nit and two parts, recorded in PROGRESS.md. Not a host-level change: no device check.

features.description: Every tool the checks install is pinned
steps: pip-audit's own environment gets pinned pip, setuptools and wheel, with hashes
scripts/test-cycle.sh runs Playwright from webui/node_modules, not through npx
pip installs prefer wheels (--only-binary) where they exist
features.notes: Built 2026-11-19 (ADR-0423). Step 1: pip-audit -r cannot be given pinned tools: it runs pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools in its own venv, and a PIP_CONSTRAINT file with hashes turns on hash-checking for the requirements too, which pip 24.0 (and 26.2.1) then refuse without hashes (tried offline with local wheels). So scripts/audit-python.sh makes the environment: a venv of Python 3.11 (another version is refused), .github/audit-env-requirements.txt installed with --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: (pip 26.3, setuptools 84.2.1, wheel 0.48.0 and packaging 26.3, which wheel needs; the sha256 of each wheel from PyPI's JSON API on 2026-11-19; pip and packaging as in lint-requirements.txt, whose hashes the test compares), then pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --no-build-isolation --only-binary=:all: --no-binary=nut2 --report of supervisor/requirements.txt (the pinned setuptools builds nut2's sdist), then pip-audit --disable-pip --no-deps --strict on the resolved name==version list; an empty resolution fails. make audit, the lint job of test.yml and the python job of audit.yml run it (TestAuditEnvironment: the pins, the commands with stub tools, a failed step, an empty resolution, a finding, another Python; the make and workflow tests of test_repo_tooling.py). Not run against the network: pip on this workstation cannot reach the index (the real script with Python 3.11 made its venv and stopped at the first download, as expected), and pip-audit --disable-pip --no-deps read the list and stopped at the vulnerability service; make audit on the owner's machine is the first real run. Step 2: scripts/test-cycle.sh runs ./node_modules/.bin/playwright in webui/ for the browser install, the E2E run and the quick test (test_playwright_runs_from_the_web_uis_node_modules_never_through_npx). Step 3: --only-binary=:all: in scripts/setup.sh for both venvs, the pip installs of both workflows, supervisor/Dockerfile.test and the audit; where they install or resolve supervisor/requirements.txt (or requirements-dev.txt, which includes it) the command line adds --no-binary=nut2 after it, since nut2 2.1.1 publishes only its sdist (TestWheelsOnly, with test_pip_takes_nut2_as_its_sdist_and_every_other_package_as_a_wheel, which runs this Python's pip offline on a local folder of wheels and sdists with the real requirement files' option lines and the command line's --only-binary=:all: --no-binary=nut2, so that the order of pip's format-control options and nut2's build without isolation are checked; the setup tests). supervisor/Dockerfile and supervisor/requirements.txt are as on origin/main (test_the_image_keeps_its_pip_layer_and_pips_default, and test_the_pip_layer_builds_on_riscv64_and_keeps_no_toolchain_there as it was): an option in either would rebuild the image's pip layer, about a hundred MB of writes on the dev device's SD card (ADR-0214), and change no wheel it installs, since pip's default with exact pins takes a wheel wherever the pinned version has one, which meets the step's "where they exist" there (ADR-0423, at the lead's request). Outside the audit, nut2's sdist is still built with the newest setuptools from the index (pip's build isolation). Wheels read from PyPI on 2026-11-19 for the resolved tree of requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt on CPython 3.11: every package but nut2 has one for linux/amd64, linux/arm64 and macOS arm64 (cryptography 50 none for macOS x86_64); on linux/riscv64 bcrypt, cffi, cryptography, psutil, PyYAML and uvloop have none, which the riscv64 build compiles (ADR-0373); every package of lint-requirements.txt has wheels for all of these platforms. The supervisor image's pip layer does not change. With --only-binary, an unpinned dependency whose newest version has no wheel resolves to an older one in make setup, CI and the audit, while the image builds the newer sdist: the audit can then check another version than the image's. Not built: no image was built here. Review in a fresh context (2026-11-19): nothing blocking. Fixed: ADR-0423 now supersedes, in part, the audit and install commands of ADR-0190, ADR-0216 and ADR-0218; the docs no longer claim that the checks run only pinned code (nut2's sdist is built with the newest setuptools from the index outside the audit); the ADR says that an unpinned dependency without a wheel resolves to an older version rather than stopping; pip-audit runs with --strict; an offline test of pip's own format control and of --no-build-isolation; the Intel Mac limit in docs/TESTING.md and setup.sh's message. Left: scripts/standin/e2e.sh's comment that `npx playwright install chromium` downloads the browser predates this change and names no command that runs.

features.description: CI runs make setup on a clean checkout, so that the bootstrap cannot break unnoticed
steps: A CI workflow, on a schedule and on demand, runs make setup on a fresh ubuntu-latest runner
The same job then runs make check-fast and make smoke, and fails when the setup or either of them fails
features.notes: Built 2026-11-22. Where: the job bootstrap (Bootstrap (make setup)) of .github/workflows/audit.yml, the weekly workflow that stays on (ADR-0230), not test.yml, which is off and has no schedule, and not a workflow of its own: one more job of at most 30 minutes a week, about 2 hours a month at most of the Free plan's minutes, and no pull request runs it. Step 1: every Monday at 06:17 UTC and on demand (workflow_dispatch), no push or pull_request trigger; ubuntu-latest; a checkout with the whole history (fetch-depth: 0, as a clone has it, for test_the_floor_only_rises and the ledger's merge base with origin/main) and persist-credentials: false; actions/setup-python 3.11 and actions/setup-node 22, the prerequisites that scripts/setup.sh checks, without their caches; then make setup. The actions have the pins of the other jobs (ADR-0423). Step 2: make setup ends with its own baseline, make check-fast and then make smoke (ADR-0217), and exits 1 when a prerequisite is missing, an install fails or either target fails, which fails the step and the run; the job does not run the two targets a second time in steps of their own, which would check nothing new and cost the minutes of make check-fast again. The job has no if, needs, continue-on-error, env, defaults or strategy, its steps no if, continue-on-error, env, shell or working-directory. Tests: test_the_audit_workflow_runs_make_setup_on_a_fresh_runner of test_repo_tooling.py reads the job (failed before the job existed); the stub runs of scripts/setup.sh show the baseline last (test_setup_bootstraps_a_checkout_and_a_rerun_changes_nothing), a red baseline (test_a_red_baseline_is_named), a failed pip install, npm ci or Chromium install (test_a_failed_install_fails_the_setup_before_the_baseline, new; it passed on the old code, since setup.sh already stopped there) and a missing prerequisite each exiting 1. Open: passes stays false until the job has run on GitHub: a dispatch of audit.yml on this branch's ref once it is pushed (gh workflow run audit.yml --ref ci.bootstrap-in-ci, which runs all six jobs of the workflow), or the Monday schedule once main has the job; make check-fast then runs on Linux as the runner's user, where no workstation runs it, so a test that fails only there fails the job too. Chromium is installed but not started (no playwright install-deps). Review in a fresh context (ADR-0017): nothing blocking; fixed: the note's claim that only a run after the merge can show the job, a dispatch's cost (all six jobs), the ADR's link to ADR-0230's rules (the job checks no pull request and extends no test.yml; the tests that skip on macOS run on the runner), the overclaim of a runner with only Python and Node.js (its image has git, make, Docker and most of Chromium's libraries) and the reason for fetch-depth: 0. Left: the reviewer asked that the job's comment and the tests cite it as the other jobs cite theirs, left out because the batch's rule cites a new ADR only in the ADR, its README row, the entry's adr field, CHANGELOG.md and the docs; a PROGRESS.md line for the owner that a weekly job that may go red was added is the lead's (builders do not edit PROGRESS.md). Not host-level: no device check.

features.description: CI scans the whole git history for credentials with a pinned secret scanner
steps: A CI job checks out the full history and runs a secret scanner, pinned by its commit SHA or image digest, over every commit
A commit that adds a credential fails the job
The job passes on main with the passwords once published in CLAUDE.md, rotated (ADR-0226) and kept in the history (ADR-0208), allowed by commit and path with the reason (ADR-0445)
features.notes: make secret-scan (scripts/secret-scan.sh) and the Secret Scan job of the CI workflow run gitleaks v8.30.1, pinned by digest, with .gitleaks.toml, and scripts/published-passwords.py over every commit, merges by their remerge-diff (ADR-0445). On 2026-11-21 both passed locally: gitleaks read 635 commits, its 55 findings in 23 pairs of commit and file allowed by commit and path; the digest check read 839. Waits while the CI workflow is off on GitHub (ADR-0230): passes stays false until the job has run there.

features.description: A small database change, such as a sign-in's login-history row, writes at most 0.1 MiB to the system disk in the middle of SQLite's write-ahead log, instead of 0.156 to 0.168 MiB with the rollback journal
steps: Measure one sign-in's SD writes on the dev device with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure, and the SQLite part of them
An ADR decides the journal mode and synchronous level (for example WAL with synchronous NORMAL) against the power-cut window of ADR-0078 and the backups of the database
A sign-in in the middle of the write-ahead log writes at most 0.1 MiB to the SD card, measured before and after with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure (0.156 to 0.168 MiB with the rollback journal)
features.notes: On 2026-11-07 a sign-in wrote about 0.16 MiB, mostly the login history's commit (rollback journal, synchronous FULL). Since ADR-0306 (2026-11-08) unos.db uses SQLite's write-ahead log with synchronous NORMAL: a sign-in's commit in the middle of the log appends 3 pages (12.4 KB) to unos.db-wal and changes 3 pages of unos.db-shm, syncs nothing and creates or deletes no file; backups stay one file with the rollback journal. Device check of 2026-11-09 (main 12483dd, deployed at 07:41 UTC), with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure, one run each, each sign-in after scripts/dev/api.py --forget-token: a sign-in right after the start, which starts the log, 0.145 MiB; one in the middle of the log 0.082 MiB, against 0.156 to 0.168 MiB before; the two sign-ins grew unos.db-wal by 6 frames, 3 pages each; a call with a cached token 0.020 MiB; a restart of the supervisor up to healthy 1.125 MiB in all, Docker's own writes among them, so it does not isolate the 0.05 MiB of ADR-0306's exception. Steps 1 and 2 hold, and step 3 as ADR-0308 reworded it (at most 0.1 MiB in the middle of the log): 0.082 MiB. Not a host-level change (GLOSSARY.md): the journal mode stays inside the supervisor's data volume, so no re-check after a reboot applies, and the feature-pass skill's table does not list the entry.

features.description: The dev device admits inbound IPv6 to its services only from the LAN, unless the owner wants remote access
steps: The owner says whether the services are used from outside over IPv6

Without remote use: SSH, the web UI, Samba and transmission's web port answer only LAN, unique-local and link-local addresses over IPv6, Docker's published ports included; the BitTorrent port stays open
A check from another network shows the service ports closed and the BitTorrent port open
features.notes: Device check on 2026-11-08 (ADR-0301): the owner chose the filter ("Yes, turn it on"). scripts/dev/ipv6-filter.sh install loaded the table ip6 unos_ipv6_inbound from /etc/unos-dev/ipv6-inbound.nft, with the LAN's global prefix read on the device, and enabled unos-ipv6-inbound.service (0.133 MiB written; a rerun 0 MiB). From the workstation, on the LAN, SSH 22, the web UI 80 and 443 (docker-proxy), Samba 445, transmission's web port 9091 and 51413 answer over both global and both unique-local addresses and the link-local one, and 22, 443 and 445 over IPv4; Bonjour still lists the SMB service. From a network outside the LAN, a network namespace on the device with the source 2001:db8:6::2 routed to the device's global address, 22, 80, 443, 445, 5355 and 9091 are closed, 51413 is open and ping answers; before the filter every port answered. The router over link-local and outbound IPv6 (https://deb.debian.org, 200) work. After two reboots from the API the unit is active before systemd-networkd, the table is loaded, the probes answer the same and check.sh, which now reports the filter, is OK. supervisor/tests/test_dev_scripts.py pins the ruleset and the unit and runs the installer's and remove's device side with stand-ins. The router's own inbound filtering was not probed from the internet: the filter decides by source address, so a datagram from outside that forges a unique-local or LAN source is stopped only by the router's ingress filtering (the UDP services).

features.description: scripts/dev/check.sh checks the SMB services that UNOS runs: smbd, wsdd2 and avahi-daemon, with nmbd off
steps: check.sh reports a problem unless smbd, wsdd2 and avahi-daemon are active
check.sh reports a problem while nmbd is active or enabled
The deploy-device and device-checks skills get check: OK on the dev device once the owner has set up network discovery and turned nmbd off
features.notes: Found by the review of shares.smb-discovery: check.sh loops over smbd and nmbd and marks the device unhealthy unless both are active, so once nmbd is off (ADR-0275) the deploy-device skill stops at its step 3, deploy.sh all ends with check.sh's failure, and every device check reports the device unhealthy. scripts/dev/ was off limits for that branch. The new check.sh passes on the dev device only after the owner's setup of shares.smb-discovery (avahi-daemon and wsdd2 installed and running, nmbd off): it lands between that setup and the device check of shares.smb-discovery. Built 2026-11-09: check.sh's section "samba and network discovery" requires smbd, wsdd2 and avahi-daemon active and reports nmbd while it is active or enabled (enabled or enabled-runtime), whatever smb.conf says: UNOS always renders NetBIOS off (ADR-0275), so the branch for an smb.conf with NetBIOS on went (ADR-0207). Steps 1 and 2: test_dev_scripts.py (test_check_sh_reports_samba_and_network_discovery_problems for each service and for nmbd active or enabled, and test_check_sh_shows_every_containers_log_configuration for the lines of a healthy device, with a systemctl stub per unit). Step 3 on the dev device, 2026-11-09: the first run found nmbd inactive but enabled (Debian's nmbd.service skips its start through its ExecCondition /usr/share/samba/is-configured nmb while NetBIOS is off, so it never ran, but install.sh disables it); the session ran systemctl disable nmbd at 14:02 UTC on the owner's word "I allow everything" (a change of the device's services is the owner's, ADR-0211; it is the end state of install.sh's line, as nmbd was not running; 0.680 MiB), and check.sh answered check: OK (0.016 MiB).

features.description: An app of several containers installs as one app, with pinned images, generated secrets and a port check before anything is pulled
steps: Install an app of several containers (Immich: its server, database, Redis and machine learning) as one app: the Apps page lists it once, and start, stop, restart and uninstall act on all its containers in order
Its secrets are generated and kept on its pool, its images pinned by tag and digest, and its ports checked for conflicts before anything is pulled
An install that fails leaves no container or network behind and keeps the data folders and secrets; nothing of the app but its images, container records and logs is written to the system disk
features.notes: Built (ADR-0381, ADR-0382); host-level, as an app's containers, its network and its mounts are made on the host's Docker and its data and password on the pool (ADR-0018). An app is its main container and its companions (AppTemplate.companions, src/apps/catalog.py): every container carries the label unos.app=<id>, a companion also unos.app.companion=<name> and the name <id>-<name>, and they share the network unos-app-<id>, on which each companion answers to its name; one instance per template (the install request takes no name). The install, under a lock per app, checks before any pull that the app, its names and its network are free, its host ports against every container's port bindings and ss on the host, the system disk's free space (2 GiB must stay free after the pinned images' estimated sizes; df through src/host.py) and the password file and its database's folder; then pulls by digest, checks that every VOLUME of a pinned image is bound to the pool or a tmpfs, makes the folders and the password file (64 hexadecimal digits, root, 0600, linked from a temporary file after an fsync), the network and the containers, and starts the containers in the same order, the main container last, each companion that it depends on ready (within 180 s) before the next container starts, so that a later failure meets the database set up. A failure after the pull stops what it started, each container with its stop timeout, removes the containers and the network it made and keeps the folders, the password and the images, and names a database folder that was empty before the install, which may now hold a database that was not finished; only a clean-up that fails is audited. Start, stop (in reverse order, with each container's stop timeout), restart (stop all, then start all) and uninstall act on every container; an app that lacks a container is incomplete (start refused, uninstall allowed). Immich: its server immich (port 2283, /data on the pool, RK3588_VIDEO), database (Immich's Postgres, DB_STORAGE_TYPE=HDD, stop timeout 60 s), redis (Valkey, /data on the pool) and machine-learning (models in /cache on the pool; RK3588_NPU and the -rknn image where it applies, apps.rk3588-hardware-acceleration), its images pinned by tag and digest at v3.4.1 (PINNED_IMAGES; the templates in UNPINNED_TEMPLATES only shrink); BookStack, Paperless-ngx and Linkwarden are left to apps.catalog-companions. Tests: test_app_stacks.py (StackDocker, a strict fake of docker-py), test_apps.py (TestPortCheck, TestSystemDiskSpace, TestStackCatalog), apps-stacks.spec.ts. Costs (ADR-0381): about 3.6 GB of images on the SD card once per version of Immich, and the pool's hard disk stays awake while Immich runs. Device check, before and after a reboot, each command wrapped in scripts/dev/sd.sh measure <label> -- and its SD MiB reported; the agent only reads, and the deploy, the pulls, the installs and uninstalls, the app actions, Immich's administrator and the reboot are the owner's (ADR-0211): (1) before the deploy, scripts/dev/check.sh and scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker info --format "{{.DockerRootDir}} {{.Driver}}"; df -B1M --output=target,avail / /var/lib/docker /var/lib/containerd /mnt/pools/data; free -m; docker ps -a --format "{{.Names}} {{.Status}}"; docker network ls --format "{{.Name}}"; docker volume ls -q | wc -l; ss -Hltn "( sport = :2283 )"': at least 6000 MiB free on the system disk, otherwise stop and ask the owner, port 2283 free, and the count of Docker volumes recorded; (2) after the owner's deploy, scripts/dev/api.py GET /apps/catalog/immich and scripts/dev/scenario.sh hardware (the notes of apps.rk3588-hardware-acceleration); (3) optionally, to measure the pull alone, the owner pulls the four images that the RK3588 runs by name@digest (PINNED_IMAGES: the server, the -rknn machine learning, Postgres, Valkey) under scripts/dev/sd.sh measure immich-pull: about 3400 MiB; (4) the owner installs Immich on the pool data, in the App Store or with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure immich-install -- sh -c 'echo "{\"template_id\": \"immich\", \"pool\": \"data\"}" | scripts/dev/api.py --timeout 3600 POST /apps/install -': 200 with the companions database, redis and machine-learning, under 30 MiB of SD writes when the images were there; then opens Immich on port 2283 of the device and registers its administrator at once; (5) scripts/dev/api.py GET /apps/installed lists one Immich with its three companions running; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker inspect -f "{{.State.Health.Status}}" immich' until healthy (minutes at the first start), then scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'curl -s http://127.0.0.1:2283/api/server/ping; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:2283/api/server/version' answers pong and 3.4.1; for each of immich, immich-database, immich-redis and immich-machine-learning, docker inspect's Config.Image, HostConfig.Privileged, Devices, MaskedPaths, SecurityOpt, Tmpfs, LogConfig, Config.StopTimeout, RestartCount and Mounts: the images by digest, no privileged mode, binds only below /mnt/pools/data/apps/immich and /etc/localtime, the tmpfs of the catalog, Docker's json-file log capped, StopTimeout 60 on the database, and no new Docker volume; the password file, read without showing it: scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker inspect immich immich-database immich-redis immich-machine-learning | grep -c -F -f /mnt/pools/data/apps/immich/postgres/password; stat -c "%a %U %s" /mnt/pools/data/apps/immich/postgres/password' prints 0 and 600 root 64, and no container has a DB_PASSWORD or POSTGRES_PASSWORD variable; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker network inspect unos-app-immich -f "{{json .IPAM.Config}} {{len .Containers}}"; ss -Hltn' gives a subnet outside 172.31.254.0/24 (unos-net, ADR-0048), 4 containers, and no listener on 3003, 5432 or 6379; docker diff of each container names only mount points and what a start makes (anything else gets a tmpfs); docker logs immich has no 'password authentication failed'; (6) the owner uninstalls Immich: scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker ps -a --filter label=unos.app=immich -q | wc -l; docker network ls --filter label=unos.app=immich -q | wc -l; ls /mnt/pools/data/apps/immich /mnt/pools/data/apps/immich/postgres; stat -c "%a %U %s" /mnt/pools/data/apps/immich/postgres/password' prints 0, 0, its folders library, model-cache, postgres and redis, the database's data and the password file in postgres, and 600 root 64; the owner installs it again and the administrator still signs in (the database and its password were kept); (7) scripts/dev/sd.sh measure immich-idle -- sleep 1800 with Immich idle: at most 1 MiB; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'cat /sys/block/sda/stat; sleep 600; cat /sys/block/sda/stat; hdparm -C /dev/sda' after the pool disk's idle timeout (ADR-0378): record whether it sleeps (expected: it does not); scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker stats --no-stream --format "{{.Name}} {{.MemUsage}} {{.CPUPerc}}"' while Immich's jobs run and idle, whose peaks go to apps.container-resource-limits; (8) the owner stops, starts and restarts Immich on the Apps page: scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker events --since 15m --until "$(date +%s)" --filter label=unos.app=immich --format "{{.Time}} {{.Actor.Attributes.name}} {{.Action}}" | grep -E " (start|die)$"' shows the starts database, redis, machine-learning, immich and the stops in reverse, scripts/dev/api.py GET /audit/logs --param limit=10 the entries, and the apps installed before still list and run; (9) after the owner's reboot, scripts/dev/check.sh, GET /apps/installed with all four containers running, and scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker inspect -f "{{.Name}} {{.RestartCount}}" immich immich-database immich-redis immich-machine-learning' (the server may restart a few times, as the start at boot is unordered: ADR-0381). Immich stays installed and its models on the pool. Device check on 2026-11-16 (UTC; the dev device, a BPI-W3 with kernel 6.1.172 and the pool data on sda; the SD MiB of each step in PROGRESS.md's Log), the pulls, the installs, the uninstall, the app actions and the reboot at the owner's word, run by the agent through the API: (1) on 2625f84 at 20:07, check.sh OK, 24206 MiB free on the system disk, port 2283 free, 3 Docker volumes; (2) after the deploy of 41ad495 (this branch with main ce5f86c) at 21:38 to 21:40, GET /apps/catalog/immich gave the server rk3588-video and the machine learning rk3588-npu with the -rknn image, and scripts/dev/scenario.sh hardware passed its 7 steps; (3) not run on its own: the install measured the pull with it; (4) the install answered 200 in 299 s with the companions database, redis and machine-learning, 3661.938 MiB of SD writes with the four images' pull, and the second install of (6), with the images there, 6.059 MiB; no administrator was registered (isInitialized false at 21:52 and 21:53): the owner's; (5) GET /apps/installed listed Immich running and healthy, its log cut at 1500 characters after the companion database (running, healthy) and before redis and machine-learning, and the check asserted only that the list held Immich, not one Immich with its three companions running; all four containers running by 21:46:24, healthy where they have a health check; pong and 3.4.1; docker inspect: every image by digest, none privileged, binds only below /mnt/pools/data/apps/immich and /etc/localtime, the catalog's tmpfs, json-file capped (10m, 3 files), StopTimeout 60 on the database, no Docker volume mounted and still 3 volumes; the password file 600 root 64 and in no container's configuration, no DB_PASSWORD or POSTGRES_PASSWORD variable; the network unos-app-immich on 172.18.0.0/16 with 4 containers, no listener on 3003, 5432 or 6379; docker diff named only mount points (/data, /run/secrets and its file in the server, /run/secrets and its file in the database, /cache in the machine learning) and their parent /run, nothing in redis; no 'password authentication failed'; (6) the uninstall answered 200 and left no container or network of Immich, the folders library, model-cache, postgres and redis, postgres/data and postgres/password, 600 root 64; the second install answered 200, healthy, pong, no 'password authentication failed', and the same database: its version_history's first record (2026-11-16 21:46:29 UTC, 3.4.1) and its administrator state (none) as before; with no administrator registered, that record stands for (6)'s sign-in; (7) 30 minutes of an idle Immich (21:53 to 22:24): 0.547 MiB; docker stats then: immich 577 MiB and 0.06% of a core, machine-learning 144.9 MiB and 0.41%, redis 5.664 MiB and 0.92%, database 70.42 MiB and 0.00%; sda with UNOS's shortest idle timeout (5 minutes) from 22:28 while Immich ran: 40 reads 30 s apart until 22:48, active/idle at each, its count of completed writes up between every two reads (112 to 467) and of reads not (2490), so that no stretch without I/O came near the 5 minutes: it did not sleep, as ADR-0381 expects; features.description: An installed app updates in place to the catalog's newer pinned images, keeps its data and can be rolled back
steps: Updating an installed app to the newer images of the catalog keeps its data folders, its generated secrets and its settings
Before the new version migrates the app's database, UNOS copies the database; a rollback returns to the earlier image digests and that copy
The update first shows what it writes to the system disk, then runs as a background job that reports its progress over /ws/v1/events
features.notes: Split from apps.compose-stacks (ADR-0381). Immich migrates its database at the server's start and refuses a downgrade, so the earlier digests alone cannot roll it back; Immich's own dumps go to its library's backups folder daily and not before an update. Built 2026-11-18 on the workstation (ADR-0408); host-level, as it changes Docker's containers and the pool's folders, so it passes only after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). GET /apps/installed adds version (label unos.app.version, null for containers made before it), update_to (the catalog's version when every image of the template is pinned and the catalog pins another index digest for a container than the one it was created from, its own or a hardware profile's) and previous (the earlier containers <name>.previous, their images and the copies that are there). GET /apps/installed/{id}/update answers the plan: each container's image before and after, read for the host's platform from the registry anonymously (index, platform manifest, configuration, each checked against its digest); an image must be built after the one that runs (409 otherwise, also when either time is unknown); download_bytes are the compressed layers whose chain id Docker's store lacks, system_disk_bytes that share of the PinnedImage's disk_bytes, with the system disk's free space (409 below 2 GiB after it); the copies of the copy_before_update folders (Immich's postgres/data) with their size and the pool's free space (409 below size + 1 GiB, and while a .previous or .rolled-back folder is there). Refusals: floating tag, nothing to update, an earlier version still kept, incomplete app, platform, registry (503). POST .../update (202) is a job of install_jobs (kind update; one install, update or rollback at a time; the app's lock): checks, pulls by digest, stops the app in reverse with stop timeouts, copies each marked folder with cp -a --reflink=auto to <folder>.copying then <folder>.previous, renames the earlier containers <name>.previous, recreates every container from the template with the kept binds, password files, editable variables, group option, ports, limits and hardware, starts in order and waits up to 900 s for the main container (unhealthy does not fail it before then). A failure or a cancel after the stop removes the new containers, puts the copy back (the newer folder deleted once the earlier version runs) or deletes it when no new container started, renames the earlier containers back and starts them; a copy that cannot be put back leaves them stopped. A stop of the supervisor leaves the state as it is (503). POST .../rollback (202, kind rollback, not cancellable) and DELETE .../previous. Audited: app_updated, app_rolled_back, app_earlier_version_removed; an uninstall removes the earlier containers and keeps the copy. The Containers page refuses to start or restart an earlier container and to start, restart or remove an app's container while a change of the app holds its lock. Tested on the workstation: test_app_updates.py (the strict fake Docker with images' Created and RootFS, rename and images.list, a fake registry transport, cp done by copytree; the plan and its refusals, the same image under another index, the update, a failure, a new version that does not start, a cancel during a pull and after the stop, a stop of the supervisor after the stop and after the renames with the rollback from there, a copy that cannot be put back, one job at a time, the Containers page's guards, the rollback, the removal and its refusal, the uninstall), apps-update.spec.ts and the update dialog in mobile-layout.spec.ts on the stand-in with route fakes. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): fixed the earlier containers startable from the Containers page beside the newer ones, a copy that could not be put back leaving an ordinary stopped app, the containerd store's image ids, a rollback from a half-renamed state, the rollback's and the removal's preconditions, an unexpected error skipping the restore and the restore's selection by label; left: the device check cannot run an update or a rollback while no pinned app other than Immich is installed there (transmission floats; the update on real Docker and a real pool is unverified until one is), the rollback finds the copies through the current catalog's marks (a template change that drops one is to be reviewed with that), the registry reads have a 30 s timeout per read and no bound in total, cp takes the folder's path after a walk without links, and an image with a fixed build time is never newer. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), on the dev device (Immich and transmission installed), each command under scripts/dev/sd.sh measure <label> -- with its SD MiB reported. Immich is never updated, rolled back or pulled: no POST to /apps/installed/immich/update or /rollback and no DELETE of /apps/installed/immich/previous. (1) After the deploy: scripts/dev/check.sh OK; scripts/dev/api.py GET /apps/installed lists immich with update_to null and previous null (the catalog pins its installed digests; version null, since its containers predate the label), and transmission with update_to null and previous null (its image floats on latest); scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker ps -a --format {{.Names}}' lists no name ending in .previous. Expected SD writes: about 0 MiB. (2) Read-only and refusal paths: GET /apps/installed/immich/update answers 409 'Immich runs the images that the catalog pins: there is nothing to update' (Docker reads only; no registry read, no pull); GET /apps/installed/transmission/update answers 409 "Transmission's image floats on a tag (lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:latest): UNOS updates only an app whose catalog pins its images by digest"; POST /apps/installed/transmission/update answers 202 with a job of kind update, and scripts/dev/api.py --timeout 120 GET /apps/install/jobs/<id> --param wait=60 shows it failed with error_status 409 and that text; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker events --since <the POST> --until <now>' shows no pull, stop, rename or create, and GET /audit/logs has no app_updated; POST /apps/installed/transmission/rollback answers 409 'Transmission has no earlier version to roll back to' and DELETE /apps/installed/transmission/previous 409 'Transmission has no earlier version to remove'. Expected SD writes: about 0 MiB (nothing is audited for a refusal). (3) Only if the deployed catalog pins a newer image for transmission than its installed one (GET /apps/installed lists transmission with update_to set; not so on 2026-11-18, since transmission's template floats on latest until apps.pinned-catalog-images pins it), once: GET /apps/installed/transmission/update and record system_disk_bytes; scripts/dev/sd.sh measure update -- scripts/dev/api.py POST /apps/installed/transmission/update -, then scripts/dev/api.py --timeout 3660 GET /apps/install/jobs/<id> --param wait=3600 ends succeeded; report system_disk_bytes in MiB beside the measured SD MiB of the update; docker ps -a shows transmission running the new digest and transmission.previous exited, docker inspect transmission shows the binds of /config, /downloads and /watch and the port bindings as before, its web login takes its old USER and PASS, and GET /audit/logs shows app_updated. Then scripts/dev/sd.sh measure rollback -- POST /apps/installed/transmission/rollback with the waiting GET ends succeeded: transmission runs its earlier image again, no .previous container is left, app_rolled_back is audited. (Transmission has no copy_before_update folder: the database copy is the backend tests'.) (4) After the owner's reboot: check.sh OK, and (1) and (2) answer as before; after (3), transmission still runs the earlier image and no .previous container is there. Device check of 09e792a on 2026-11-18, the refusal paths only, before and after a reboot (0.031 SD MiB a run): both update plans answered 409 with their texts, POST update answered 202 and its job ended failed with 409, docker events showed no container change, app_updated was not audited, rollback and DELETE previous answered 409, and no .previous container exists. Step (3), a real update and rollback, waits for apps.pinned-catalog-images: transmission's image floats on latest, so nothing is newer. Immich was not touched. Since apps.pinned-catalog-images (ADR-0410) the catalog pins transmission at lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:4.1.4-r0-ls370@sha256:5baf08cd73a566699f35baad3c4a84ba7d7057220566c5fb29969bf2292dc2ff: once that is deployed, (1) lists transmission with update_to 4.1.4-r0-ls370 and (2)'s refusals of transmission's floating tag no longer apply; its POST /apps/installed/transmission/update starts a real update, so it is run only as (3), once, and not as part of (2). Device check of e5d531a on 2026-11-18: with transmission pinned, GET .../transmission/update planned 134.5 MiB, and the update was tried twice (19:07 and 19:10 UTC); both jobs failed at the pull with Docker's 'timeout awaiting response headers' on lscr.io's blobs while lscr.io answered curl, so the device's network, not UNOS: transmission was never stopped, no .previous container was made, it ran on its old image after a reboot, and the two partial pulls cost 63.582 and 14.516 SD MiB. The real update and rollback are still to see on a network that completes the pull. Device check of cbe437c on 2026-11-18: a third try, after lscr.io's blob answered a HEAD in 0.30 s, planned 134.5 MiB and failed at the pull the same way (55.539 of partial layers); transmission was never stopped, docker images unchanged. 2026-11-19 (main 9061fb0): a fourth try, after a HEAD of one of the pinned image's blobs answered 200 in 0.29 s from the device: the update planned 134.5 MiB and failed at Docker's pull of an lscr.io blob ('timeout awaiting response headers', 148.309 SD MiB of partial layers); transmission running on its old image with no .previous. lscr.io has no IPv6 address and Docker has no proxy or daemon.json: the cause lies in Docker's downloads from lscr.io on this network, not in UNOS. 2026-11-19 (apps.linuxserver-images-from-ghcr's device check of fc42813): transmission updated in place to the catalog's pin on ghcr.io, kept its data, binds, ports and login, was rolled back to its earlier container and updated again, before a reboot; after the reboot it ran the pin, offered nothing. The pulls that failed from lscr.io (four times) were LinuxServer's redirector's: from ghcr.io the same image came in 10 s (ADR-0426).

features.description: BookStack, Paperless-ngx and Linkwarden are back in the catalog as apps with the companion containers they need
steps: BookStack installs with its MariaDB, Paperless-ngx with its Redis broker and Linkwarden with its PostgreSQL, each as a companion container; UNOS generates the password of each database (BookStack's MariaDB and Linkwarden's PostgreSQL) on the pool, and the broker, like Immich's Valkey, has none
Each app starts after its install and serves its web page, with all its data on the pool
features.notes: ADR-0381 removed the three templates: each needs a database or a broker that a one-container template never gave it. BookStack's named its database's host (DB_HOST=bookstack-db); Paperless-ngx's named no broker (PAPERLESS_REDIS) and Linkwarden's no database (DATABASE_URL). Related apps that need another container or the host: open-webui reaches Ollama at host.docker.internal, which does not resolve on Linux without a host-gateway entry, and zigbee2mqtt needs an MQTT broker (the mosquitto app) that its template does not name. Built 2026-11-18 on the workstation (ADR-0415); host-level, as the apps' containers, networks and mounts are made on the host's Docker and their data and generated files on the pool, so it passes only after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Step 1: bookstack (lscr.io/linuxserver/bookstack:v26.09.3-ls299@sha256:c741211356966fd38f8fea10483f341ca29c41cdd1b96b5cfcdd4312f26d7f97, port 6875) with the companion database (mariadb:11.8.9@sha256:d36f18d65a0459510b8b0f643b226a6d299e3206486e2b64ff20754a6d291707); paperless-ngx (ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx:3.5.1@sha256:8508853b8a0f8394074260957d0be186c8c64f346973b24a7583de4580f306b9, port 8010) with the companion redis (docker.io/valkey/valkey:9.1.3-alpine@sha256:bf09d58e96d6b4524a15396b65b242bbe18beebbcc15a04d8ee75ddac62fae0b, as Paperless-ngx's own docker-compose.sqlite.yml names Valkey 9 on Alpine; its database is SQLite in its data folder); linkwarden (ghcr.io/linkwarden/linkwarden:v2.17.0@sha256:7c11fde57d1a0c819b6de0079966eba3a33584d718464af7dacde22bd470ae46, port 3010, since 3000 is Open WebUI's) with the companion database (postgres:16.16-alpine@sha256:81e77a4833487b8132fe4b00bedd39dc3f74b8641e387f19312a48f7de218c2e), read anonymously from the registries (no pull), each with its estimate (four times the larger compressed image of arm64 and amd64: 385, 425, 3282, 77, 2283 and 465 MB), its VOLUMEs and its platforms (image_platforms.json; all six have linux/arm64 and linux/amd64, none of the three apps linux/riscv64). UNOS generates every password and key as a file on the pool (root, 0600, never shown): BookStack's database/password, database/root-password and app-key (32 hexadecimal digits: Laravel takes a key without base64: as its 32 bytes; VolumeMapping.secret_digits), Paperless-ngx's secret-key, Linkwarden's database/password and nextauth-secret, each refused when missing beside the data it opens (secret_for); they reach the containers through MariaDB's, PostgreSQL's and Paperless-ngx's *_FILE variables, LinuxServer's FILE__ ones and, for Linkwarden, which takes its password only in DATABASE_URL, its command (catalog.LINKWARDEN_COMMAND: sh -c reads both files into DATABASE_URL and NEXTAUTH_SECRET, then runs the pinned image's CMD, LINKWARDEN_START). The broker has no password. Each database is awaited by its ready command (ContainerSpec.ready_command, only on a companion of depends_on: MariaDB's timeout 10 healthcheck.sh --connect --innodb_initialized, PostgreSQL's pg_isready -t 5 -h 127.0.0.1, each bounded by its own timeout since docker-py reads an exec's output without one), run with Docker's exec every 2 s at the install, at each start and at an update, no run after 180 s, never a Docker health check, which would write the container's state to the system disk at each probe; the broker is ready after 2 s of running. Paperless-ngx and Linkwarden run without their images' 30-s health checks for the same reason (ContainerSpec.image_healthcheck, Docker's NONE). Step 2: every data folder is under {pool}/apps/<id>/ (BookStack's config, its database's data; Paperless-ngx's data, media, export, consume, scratch with TMPDIR, redis; Linkwarden's data, its Next.js image cache, its database's data); in RAM: s6's /run (exec) and /tmp of BookStack (256 MB, an upload's two copies) and Paperless-ngx, MariaDB's /run/mysqld and /tmp, PostgreSQL's /var/run/postgresql, Linkwarden's /tmp with XDG_CACHE_HOME; Paperless-ngx's S6_READ_ONLY_ROOT=1 keeps it from compiling bytecode into the container's layer; each database folder is copied before an update (ADR-0408). BookStack's install requires APP_URL; Linkwarden's NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_REGISTRATION (false, as its image's default, so that its first account can register) can be set true at a reinstall. Linkwarden's CMD is recorded in its pin (PinnedImage.cmd), which its command runs. The App Store's details show the estimate of an app's images on the system disk (system_disk_bytes of the catalog API), and the three apps the hint that they keep the pool's disks awake; the install notice asks to change BookStack's built-in admin@admin.com account (password 'password') and to create Paperless-ngx's and Linkwarden's first account at once. Related gaps fixed: Open WebUI and Zigbee2MQTT get host.docker.internal:host-gateway (AppTemplate.host_gateway), and Zigbee2MQTT's ZIGBEE2MQTT_CONFIG_MQTT_SERVER names the Mosquitto app (mqtt://host.docker.internal:1883, editable). Left: Mosquitto's template binds an empty folder over the mosquitto.conf that its command reads, so Mosquitto needs a mosquitto.conf with a listener and its authentication before Zigbee2MQTT can reach it (a new entry for the lead); with the firewall on, Docker's networks must be allowed to those ports. Tested on the workstation: test_app_companions.py (each app's install on the strict fake Docker: its order, the ready command until it answers, the rollback when it never does, when its runs are slow, when the database keeps restarting and when Docker fails the exec, a start of the installed app, the environment, mounts, tmpfs, the generated files and their absence from every call, answer, audit entry and log; the host gateway; the catalog's system_disk_bytes), test_apps.py (TestStackCatalog), test_app_updates.py (an update creates the containers with the command, the host gateway, no health check and the ready command), test_catalog_platforms_script.py, apps-companions.spec.ts on the stand-in. DEVICE CHECK, read-only (the dev device's SD card has no room for these images: nothing is installed, pulled or changed), each command under scripts/dev/sd.sh measure <label> -- with its SD MiB, after the owner's /deploy-device: (1) scripts/dev/check.sh OK; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker images --format "{{.Repository}}@{{.Digest}}" | sort; docker ps -a --format "{{.Names}} {{.Status}}"; docker network ls --format "{{.Name}}"; docker volume ls -q | wc -l' recorded as before. (2) scripts/dev/api.py GET /api/v1/apps/catalog: bookstack, paperless-ngx and linkwarden with host_platform linux/arm64 and available true, image and companions' images equal to the pins above, companions database, redis and database, depends_on as their companions, ready_command on the two databases, system_disk_bytes 810000000, 3359000000 and 2748000000; open-webui and zigbee2mqtt with host_gateway true and zigbee2mqtt's ZIGBEE2MQTT_CONFIG_MQTT_SERVER mqtt://host.docker.internal:1883; GET /api/v1/apps/catalog/immich with system_disk_bytes 3597000000 (its -rknn machine learning on the RK3588). (3) (1)'s ssh reads again: unchanged, and docker events --since <start of (2)> --until now shows no pull, create or network event. (4) After the owner's reboot, (1) to (3) answer the same. Expected SD writes about 0 MiB (reads; no log line, no audit entry). THE OWNER'S REAL INSTALL, of each app in turn, on a host with room for it (the system disk keeps 2 GiB free after its estimate; df -B1M of / and /var/lib/docker) and its port free (ss -Hltn), each step's SD MiB where it is the dev device: (a) install it in the App Store on a pool (BookStack with APP_URL http://<address>:6875); the job ends succeeded with its companion; (b) GET /api/v1/apps/installed lists it once with its companion running; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -L of http://127.0.0.1:6875/login, :8010/ and :3010/login answers 200; open the page in a browser at the host's address and make the first account (BookStack: sign in as admin@admin.com with 'password' and change both); (c) docker inspect of each container: Config.Image by digest, no privileged mode, binds only below <pool>/apps/<id> (and the secret files read-only), the tmpfs above, the json-file log capped, StopTimeout 60 on the databases, Linkwarden's Config.Cmd LINKWARDEN_COMMAND, no new Docker volume; docker diff of each names only mount points and what a start makes (anything else gets a tmpfs: report it); (d) stat -c '%a %U %s' of the generated files prints 600 root 64 (app-key 32), and docker inspect and docker logs of the app's containers piped to grep -c -F -f <each file> print 0, without showing the files; (e) Stop, Start and Restart on the Apps page: docker events shows the database's start, the exec of its ready command, then the app's start, and the stops in reverse; (f) after a reboot, both containers run again and the page answers; (g) uninstall: no container or network of the app left, its folders and generated files kept; install again and sign in with (b)'s account (the same database); (h) uninstall and remove its images on Containers > Images to free the system disk. passes stays false until the owner's real install of each app, (a) to (g), shows step 2 (each app starts after its install and serves its web page with all its data on the pool), which neither the read-only device check nor the fake Docker can show: the FILE__ and *_FILE reads, the ready commands against the first start's temporary servers and BookStack's 32-digit APP_KEY are proved only there. Open WebUI and Zigbee2MQTT on such a host: docker inspect -f '{{.HostConfig.ExtraHosts}}' prints [host.docker.internal:host-gateway]. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): fixed the ready command that could hang an install's worker (docker-py reads an exec's output without a timeout: each command now carries its own, and no run starts after 180 s), the Russian text that the test of old wording refuses, Paperless-ngx's and Linkwarden's health checks every 30 s (now off), BookStack's /tmp too small for an upload's two copies (256 MB), Linkwarden's open registration (a variable, and the guide), the update path (a test), Linkwarden's CMD (recorded in its pin), a ready command off depends_on (refused), the 409 that dropped the last output, the CHANGELOG's claim for installed Open WebUI and Zigbee2MQTT, the guide's sizes, and the absence of every generated value from every call, log line, audit entry and answer for all three apps; this entry's passes waits for the owner's install (above). Left: small writes into the containers' layers at a start (LinuxServer's init rewrites /etc/passwd for PUID 1000; Paperless-ngx's HOME caches if its AI features are turned on; Chromium's ~/.pki in Linkwarden), which (c)'s docker diff shows; a password file that someone gave a final newline passes UNOS's check (ADR-0381) but would give BookStack a 33-byte APP_KEY; Mosquitto's empty config folder (a new entry). Device check of cbe437c on 2026-11-18, read-only: GET /apps/catalog's BookStack, Paperless-ngx and Linkwarden name their pins, companions, ready commands and system_disk_bytes as expected, open-webui and zigbee2mqtt have the host gateway, Immich 3597000000; docker's images, containers, networks and volumes unchanged, no pull, create or network event (0.016); the same after a reboot. Not run: an install of the three apps (the owner's). Device check 2026-11-19 (main 9061fb0): Paperless-ngx and Linkwarden installed through the API on the pool data with their companions (pulls and first starts 3524.414 and 3029.160 SD MiB; images 3308.3 and 2857.8 MiB): every container running and healthy, every mount under /mnt/pools/data/apps/<app>/, no named volume, images by digest, not privileged; the generated files mode 600, root, 64 bytes, in no docker inspect or log; Paperless-ngx's Valkey without a password; Paperless-ngx's page 302 to its login, Linkwarden's 200; the same after the reboot from the API at 05:57:39 UTC; then both uninstalled with their data kept and their images removed. Found and fixed (3ab6dde): Linkwarden's start wrote Prisma's cache to /root/.cache/prisma in its container's layer whatever XDG_CACHE_HOME says (a tmpfs now), and the estimates of the system disk were 3% and 8% short (raised to the measured sizes plus about 5%). Open: BookStack, whose install failed at Docker's pull of an lscr.io blob ('timeout awaiting response headers', 587.672 SD MiB of partial layers, its MariaDB image removed after), while curl on the device fetched the same blob in 0.3 s. 2026-11-19 (ADR-0426's device check): BookStack installed from ghcr.io with its MariaDB on the pool, both containers running with every bind on the pool and its generated files 600 root, then uninstalled with its data kept; its login page was not read, by a fault of the check's script, and a second install (about 1 GB on the SD card) was not run. features.description: Every image of the catalog is pinned by tag and digest, and a weekly audit finds tags that moved
steps: UNPINNED_TEMPLATES of supervisor/src/apps/catalog.py is empty: every template's image is name:tag@sha256:<index digest>
A weekly audit compares each pinned tag with its registry and reports the templates whose tag points to another digest
features.notes: ADR-0381 pins the images of apps with companions and keeps the templates that still use a floating tag in UNPINNED_TEMPLATES, which may only shrink. The weekly audit overlaps the one of apps.catalog-platforms, which compares the recorded platforms with the registries (ADR-0218). Built 2026-11-18 on the workstation (ADR-0410); host-level, as it changes the images that Docker pulls on the host for every app, so it passes only after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Step 1: every image of the catalog is a PinnedImage of PINNED_IMAGES (APP_IMAGES by template id for the 65 apps of one container, Immich's five), name:tag@sha256 of the index that the template's floating tag named on 2026-11-18, read anonymously from the registries (HEAD and GET of manifests, indexes and configurations, no pull), with the publisher's most specific tag (a version, LinuxServer's <version>-ls<build>), template.version that tag, disk_bytes four times the compressed layers of the larger linux/arm64 or linux/amd64 image, and the VOLUMEs of its configuration. UNPINNED_TEMPLATES is removed rather than left empty (ADR-0207). Where no fixed tag named that index: Open WebUI v0.13.4 (main is its branch), Netdata v2.12.3 (latest was edge), Glances 4.5.9-full, LocalAI v3.12.1-aio-cpu, Uptime Kuma 2.5.12; Traefik pins its line v3.7, since v3.7.19's index lacks the riscv64 image; Trilium is triliumnext/trilium:v0.107.0, the index that zadam/trilium:latest mirrors. transmission: lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:4.1.4-r0-ls370@sha256:5baf08cd73a566699f35baad3c4a84ba7d7057220566c5fb29969bf2292dc2ff (built 2026-11-17). Immich's five digests are unchanged; only Valkey's tag text moved from 9 (which names another index since 2026-10-27) to 9.1.2, which names the pinned sha256:418652cfb58ef879d4978c33553735d7147016032d5aefaa14c828e611eb9dfd, so the device's Immich is offered no update (stacks.update_to compares digests). Homarr's /data and LocalAI's /backends and /configuration, VOLUMEs of their images, are now bound to the pool; a test fails for a VOLUME that is not at or under a pool bind or a tmpfs. Step 2: scripts/catalog-platforms.py tags (make catalog-tags, the tags job of .github/workflows/audit.yml) asks each registry with HEAD, anonymously, which index the pinned tag names, and exits 1 with MOVED <templates>: <name:tag> names <digest>, not the pinned <digest>, saying when the pinned index is gone; an unpinned image or an unreadable tag is an ERROR.
