features.description: Every account's own settings are on the Account page, System holds the NAS's, and each setting, action and fact of the menus has one place
steps: The account block at the foot of the sidebar (a regular account's Account link) opens /account, whose tabs Sign-in and security (#security), File sharing (#sharing, regular accounts only) and Appearance and language (#appearance) hold the password, two-factor authentication, API tokens and own login history, the own SMB access, and the theme and language

System is an administrator's: its tabs are grouped as Settings (General, Network, Remote Access, Security, Notifications), Monitoring (Resource Monitor, System Logs, Disk Health) and Maintenance (Updates, Backup & Restore, Scheduler, Power Management), and Security holds only the NAS's two-factor requirement, firewall and certificates

An administrator's login history on the Account page lists only the administrator's own sign-ins; every account's are in the Audit Log, which records each wrong password and each refused second step (two-factor code, recovery code, security key) as a failed sign-in

No setting, action or fact has a second place: the dashboard has no Quick Actions, General shows no version, signed-in account or second host name, /settings is gone, and the command palette has one entry per place and changes nothing itself
Every text is in English and Russian, and the Account page and its tabs fit a 375 px phone in both languages
features.notes: Built on main 89ca9fc. The ADR's number is 0431, after the ADR of the boot screen and the loaders (another branch), which takes 0430; while that one is not on this branch the ADR tests refuse the gap, so this branch numbers its ADR 0430, and the merge after the boot screen renames the file and its citations to 0431. The ADR lists every move and each removed duplicate with the place it keeps (38, from an inventory of every menu item and place). The specs that reached a moved setting open its new place and assert what they did; where a page's structure changed, the page-ready marker follows it (the h2 Security Settings became Sign-in and security, Security of the NAS or File sharing), and where an element was removed as a duplicate the spec checks its one place (monitor.spec.ts and network.spec.ts the sidebar's connection line for the Live badges, files.spec.ts the sidebar's Files for the Trash's button, containers.spec.ts that the drawer has no actions, dashboard-layout.spec.ts 8 widgets without Quick Actions). account-smb.spec.ts's canned-answer tests sign in as a regular account, since an administrator has no File sharing tab. Step 3: the login audits each refused second step (test_totp_once.py, test_recovery_codes.py, test_security_keys.py), mine=true limits an administrator's history as a user's (test_authz.py TestLoginHistory), information-architecture.spec.ts finds another account's failed sign-in in the Audit Log and not in the own history. Fresh-context review (17 findings): all BLOCKING and RISK fixed; left, a nit: with three wide widgets the dashboard's last one is half a row wide, as when a user hid one of four before; the layout is each user's (ADR-0395). Web UI and a supervisor query parameter plus audit lines of failed sign-ins: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md).

features.description: The data pages (Dashboard, Storage, Snapshots, Files, Trash) say only what is true, count every issue once and keep one primary action each, with the rarer actions behind More
steps: With a pool degraded and the socket reporting no problem, the dashboard's banner under its header lists "Pool <name> is degraded" as a link to /storage, the header's chip reads "1 issue" and "No problems" is nowhere; a disk to replace soon is an issue linked to Disk Health with the server's reasons
The dashboard's header says "Live" with the last update's time in its tooltip, nothing on it ticks, and the Containers widget's counts add up to the total

Each pool card shows Volumes and Scrub (Mount when not mounted) and a More that holds Balance…, Add disk…, Remove disk…, Unmount… and Remove pool…; a disabled action says why, and Remove pool is one dialog whose typed name starts empty
At 375 px no snapshot or trash name breaks one letter per line, and Snapshots has no About card, its picker in the header and Restore… in words

The sidebar lists Trash under Files and marks it alone on its page; Files' header has Upload as its one primary and New folder in words, and the selection's actions show only while something is selected
Every new or changed text is in English and Russian, in sentence case
features.notes: Chunk 2 of the UX audit's order of work, built from mvp.batch-18 (69dfae5) beside the design-system foundations (chunk 1). The ADR is 0434: 0432 on its branch, renumbered when it was merged into mvp.batch-18. Places that switch to a foundations component once it lands: PoolActions' More (ActionMenu), SelectionBar (BulkBar), DeletePoolDialog (ConfirmDialog), the disabled reasons of Create pool, Scrub and More's actions (Button disabledReason), the empty states (EmptyState action), Create pool's dialog (Modal size), the snapshot dates (nasTime), the storage page's unreadable lists (ErrorState with Retry; the header's Refresh reads them again meanwhile). Fresh-context review (10 findings): fixed the BLOCKING one (a pool's low-space problem hid its degraded health on the dashboard: only a socket problem of the same sense hides the dashboard's issue, and a disk the socket reports failing is not listed again as replace soon) and the RISK ones (the empty storage card's second link to Storage, Create snapshot's reason while the pools load, a disk that a new list no longer offers left in Create pool's selection, the empty state's free-disk count now shares the dialog's rule, Enter submitting Remove pool twice, the temporary screenshot spec removed); the nits too (a paused balance asks to be resumed or cancelled, a dead helper and a stale comment removed; the snapshot name prefixes stay, test_snapshots.py keeps them as the page's constants). Web UI only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md).

features.description: The share dialog's Access is a table of who and level, and Shares, Users and groups, the Audit Log and the sign-in pages say each state once, beside what it concerns
steps: The Add and Edit share dialogs show Access as one row per user and group, each with its kind or SMB state and a None / Read / Read & write choice, an All users row, and at 375 px the choice under the name, nothing wider than the screen

Saving a served share that lowers access, turns guest access off, requires encryption or turns Previous Versions off first asks "Close open connections?", listing each change; giving access saves at once

Shares shows each tab's Add button in the page header (Add target too), says under a disabled one why, and names a share's problem once, on its card; features are neutral chips and users whose SMB is off are muted with a tag, never struck through
Users shows an error with Retry when the list cannot be read, never "No users found"; at 375 px every user's role, 2FA, SMB and actions are on screen, and Delete names what it removes

The Audit Log heads an API token's entry by what it did, shows the browser in a few words and folds its filters on a phone; first-run setup shows its rules and errors under the fields, and the forced two-factor setup is a sign-in card without the menu
Every new text is in English and Russian
features.notes: Chunk 3 of the web UI's UX work, built on mvp.batch-18 69dfae5 beside chunk 1 (the design foundations), which owns lib/components/ui, app.css and the common and ui catalogs. The ADR is 0435: 0432 on its branch, renumbered when it was merged into mvp.batch-18. The pages use the ui components that exist now; the places that switch to chunk 1's ConfirmDialog, Sheet, Menu and Toast are listed in the ADR's consequences. NFS exports still have no Edit: the API has none. The Save question counts only what smb.conf has (a user whose SMB is active, a group with such a member, a guest access or Previous Versions that smb.conf did not leave out, on a share someone can connect to), as smbconf.shrunk_shares closes connections only then. Fresh-context review (10 findings): fixed the BLOCKING one (the Save question listed users not in smb.conf) and the RISKs: the header Add target said no volume while the paths loaded or failed; the access table links lost the open form (now a new tab) and /users#groups did not reach the Groups card (scrolled to after the load); a failed copy of a Connect address said nothing (now said, also to screen readers); a failed critical audit entry lost Critical; the specs did not cover setup validation, Show, the users load error, the audit entry words or the forced setup card (tests added in first-run, auth, users, audit and mandatory-two-factor specs). Left: a disabled Save with nothing to change (Edit user, SMB interfaces) and Export after a failed audit load give their reason as hover text only, until chunk 1 adds Button disabledReason (a one-line change each); the users page hides the groups while the users cannot be read, and a groups load error has no Retry of its own (Retry of the page reads both); UsersCard formats its dates itself instead of lib/time (chunk 1 owns it).

features.description: The System tabs other than Security show status before settings, one primary action, one time zone and one pattern per job, and offer only settings that work
steps: System > Power Management shows a Status card first (pending action, next shutdown, next wake, idle shutdown), then Reboot, Shut down and Suspend as secondary buttons, then the schedule's three on/off rows whose fields stand in one column, every time on the NAS's clock, whose zone the tab names once

When the host's power state cannot be read, Power says so once with Retry, the cards say they wait and the actions are disabled with the reason; a shutdown's reasons to wait show only while it is on, each once with its count
System > Notifications has one Add channel whose dialog asks for the kind and offers no events, tabs for Channels and History, no stat tiles, and an on/off per channel

Backup & Restore's off-device copy shows its state and snapshots in one card and its settings in another, with Snapshots to keep and Integrity check as compact fields on one line and a disabled Save that says what it waits for

Scheduler, Disk Health, System Logs, Resource Monitor, Network, Remote Access and Updates use page tabs, neutral icon actions with tooltips, one badge that reads alone, charts with a scale and a time axis, and sentence case, in English and Russian, at 375 px too
features.notes: Chunk 5 of the web UI's UX work, built on mvp.batch-18 69dfae5 beside chunk 1 (the design foundations), which builds the shared Switch, FieldGroup, ActionMenu, ConfirmDialog, Toast and Tabs: until then checkboxes, legends, secondary buttons and the hand-made restore and delete dialogs stand in for them, each a one-line swap; the window.confirm and alert() calls of these tabs are left for chunk 1, which replaces them all. A peer gets no Show config: its private key is shown once (ADR-0420). The ADR is 0436: 0432 on its branch, renumbered when it was merged into mvp.batch-18. E2E of the area (25 specs with mobile-layout, command-palette, navigation and roles): 619 of 625 passed in one run under load, the three timing failures (command-palette Reboot, backup upload button, network gone interface) passed on a rerun and the three spec misses were fixed and pass. Review: this builder's session had no subagent tool, so the review was the builder's own pass over the diff's risky parts (alert routing, channel and task on/off, the power form's Save, the copy's Save gating); it found offsite snapshot sizes of 1 TiB and more shown as "1 undefined" (fixed: TB and the largest unit for larger sizes). Not host-level: the web UI only. Fresh-context review of f3c9e7c (1 blocking, 6 risks, 5 minor), all taken: (1) offsite.spec checks the state and settings cards and, by positions at 1440 and 375 px, Daily, Weekly and Monthly on one line in columns of one width (they wrapped at 375 px: now a grid of three), Integrity check beside them at 1440 and below at 375, and Still needed beside the disabled Save; (2) Power's actions wait only for the reason said once with Retry: a pending action that alone failed has its own Retry in the Status card and leaves them usable; (3) a task's on/off, and a channel's alike, shows the new state at once, is disabled until the answer and puts the stored state back on a refusal; (4) specs click the task's and the channel's checkboxes and check Paused, Last run failed, the charts' scale and time axis and Remote access's Connected, and the ADR names them; (5) Disk Health's skeleton is the list's flush card of rows, where the list appears; (6) the copy's settings card has its skeleton; (7) the restore's warning is a warning Alert again and the filename is no longer select-all; (8) TestTheWebUI checked only the EVENTS map that the page no longer has: the events kept on save are in notifications.spec, the routing to every enabled channel in test_alert_events.py, and no doc claims a backend change; (9) Scheduler names only a zone the browser knows; (10) the power schedule checks only the fields shown (a hidden one keeps the stored value), and the RTC caveat behind More shows, checked, only for an RTC that takes the alarm; (11) a disabled Add channel or Save changes says what it waits for; (12) the API gives no handshake age, so Connected ages on the NAS's clock (the offset of the answer's Date header) and is read again every 15 s without asking the API; formatBytes of lib/api/backup.ts serves Backup, the off-device copy and Remote access only (Storage and Network have their own), and remote-access.spec checks a size beyond TB. After the fixes: make check passed (10716 tests); E2E of power, offsite, backup, scheduler, health, monitor, remote-access, notifications, loading and mobile-layout: 397 of 397 passed.

features.description: Containers and the App Store get one state filter that adds up, quiet actions, plain states and errors, and an app's container is removed only with its app
steps: On /containers the state filter is one segmented control All, Running, Stopped and Other, each with its count; the counts follow the search and add up to All, and there are no count cards and no state menu

A container row's buttons stay on one line as icon buttons with their names as tooltips; below 640 px the list is cards with Restart unless the table was chosen; the selection's bar shows only while a container is selected

A container with the label unos.app links to its app on the App Store and offers no Remove; when Docker does not answer (its 503), Containers and the App Store say so with Docker's reason and Retry, any other failed load says plainly that the list could not be loaded, and nothing offers Install while the installed apps are not known

A catalog card has no Install button of its own (the card opens the details), sources and categories are neutral badges, and an app's details lead with its memory in the page's units, its system disk and its containers

An installed app's actions are secondary buttons and a quiet red Uninstall button with its word that names the app, its resources are one table per container that says once what is not read yet, an install shows one bar for the whole download in which each image is an equal share, without layers, and the update dialog opens with a summary and keeps each container's images in a disclosure
Every new text is in English and Russian, and Containers, the App Store and their dialogs fit a 375 px phone in both languages, where the first load's skeletons have the phone's layout
features.notes: Chunk 4 of the web UI's UX work, built on mvp.batch-18 69dfae5 while chunk 1 (the design-system foundations) builds the shared components; its ADR is 0437: 0432 on its branch, renumbered when it was merged into mvp.batch-18. Left for chunk 1's components, each a one-line swap listed in the ADR: confirm() for the window.confirm of the App Store and the Containers page, ActionMenu, BulkBar, Segmented/Tabs, ErrorState/LoadState, Button disabledReason, Sheet and Toast. The fresh-context review (ADR-0017) could not run in the builder's session (no subagent, and the claude CLI was not signed in): the builder reviewed the diff against the audit itself, so the merge's review covers it. A fresh-context review after the build (ADR-0017) found 12 findings, all fixed: (1, blocking) the App Store's first-load skeleton drew the categories card at every width, so a phone's and a tablet's page jumped: it now has the category menu beside the search below lg (loading.spec.ts measures the first card against its skeleton at 375 px); (2) the Containers phone skeleton lacked Select all shown and the filter wrapped to two lines at 375 px in Russian with Other: both fixed and measured the same way; (3) the whole-download bar summed bytes_total, which counts only the layers reported so far (ADR-0384), so it neared 100% and dropped: each image is now an equal share of the bar, and the summed bytes line is gone; (4) every failed load said Docker is not answering: only Docker's 503 does, any other failure says the list could not be loaded; (5) Install showed while the installed apps still loaded past the grace period: the catalog and the details follow installedKnown; (6) Uninstall was an icon-only bin like Remove earlier version: it is a quiet red button with its word, its own glyph and the app in its name; (7) apps-limits.spec.ts gained the positive one-note test; (8) the docs said no status colours on an action while Remove and Uninstall are ghost-danger: the ADR and the changelog now say that a delete is the quiet red of webui/AGENTS.md; (9) mobile-layout.spec.ts fakes an app's container (the link and the drawer's facts) and ends the drawer at its labels' disclosure; (10) ADR-0437 supersedes ADR-0384 and ADR-0431 in part, noted in both; (11) appUpdates.changedCount takes its plural from the changed count; (12) Enter in the create dialog did nothing, since its form had no submit button: Create is now the form's submit button and the form novalidate, so Enter shows the inline messages. Web UI only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md).

features.description: CI runs the storage scenarios against real btrfs on loop devices in a privileged container
steps: A CI job creates loop devices, makes pools, volumes and snapshots through the API and checks the results
The job runs on every pull request that changes supervisor/src/storage
features.notes: Waits while the CI workflow is off on GitHub (ADR-0230).

features.description: A commit of a working tree that make check or make check-fast has just passed does not run make check-fast again
steps: make check and make check-fast record the state of the working tree when they pass, and record nothing for a dry run, a run of a part of their checks, or a tree that changed during the run
The pre-commit hook skips make check-fast for a tree in the recorded state, runs it for any other, and says in one line which it did
The Stop hook skips make check-fast for a tree in the recorded state
features.notes: Built 2026-11-17 (ADR-0383). Step 1: make check and make check-fast record the state of the working tree (scripts/green-run.py, the Stop hook's SHA-256 of HEAD, git status, the diffs staged and not, without external diff drivers or textconv, and the untracked files) in tmp/stop-check/green when they pass and the tree is still in that state, and forget it when they fail; nothing is recorded for make -n, -t, -q, -i or -e (also through MAKEFLAGS), a variable on the command line other than PYTHON, RUFF, NPM, PIP_AUDIT, TEST_WORKERS (one word) and E2E_ARGS, TESTS or PYTEST_ARGS from the environment, PYTEST_ADDOPTS or MAKE from the environment. Step 2: the pre-commit hook skips make check-fast for a tree in the recorded state, with git commit and git commit -a, and runs it after a change of a tracked file, of the index, of an untracked file or of HEAD, saying which in one line. Step 3: the Stop hook skips it for the recorded state and no longer records one itself. The guard's rule skip-hooks refuses green-run.py record and writes to tmp/stop-check/green (test_agent_guard.py). All in test_repo_tooling.py, with real git commits through the hook and the real Makefile with stub tools. A commit of a tree that make check-fast had just passed spent 0.16 s in the pre-commit hook. A second review in a fresh context (2026-11-17) recorded a failing tree as green through a TEST_WORKERS of 0;true, 0||true or 0$$IFS--co, another makefile (-f, MAKEFILES, an ignored GNUmakefile), the tools given to make, PYTHONPATH, PYTEST_PLUGINS and PYTHONHOME, writes into tmp/stop-check that the guard missed (the folder as a target, cp -t, tar -C, sed -i, python code, the Write and Edit tools) and a commit that held less than the green tree (an unstaged change, an untracked file, a commit of paths, another GIT_INDEX_FILE): make now refuses such a TEST_WORKERS and records nothing for the others, the guard and .claude/settings.json refuse those writes, and the pre-commit hook skips only a commit that holds all of the green tree (green-run.py check-commit); each case is a test. Accepted and named in ADR-0383: ignored files the checks read, untracked files' modes, symbolic links' targets and nested repositories. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): its findings (make -i, other variables and PYTEST_ADDOPTS that narrowed a run, the Stop hook's own record, git's external diff drivers, no forget on a failure, a record by hand) were fixed. Not host-level.

features.description: An administrator imports a btrfs pool that already exists on the host's disks, without formatting them
steps: Attach the disks of an existing btrfs filesystem: the Storage page offers to import it
After the import the pool is mounted by UUID, survives a reboot and keeps its data
features.notes: Built 2026-11-08 (ADR-0283, which superseded ADR-0282 after the fresh-context review). The pool of a name is the btrfs filesystem labelled with it, or of several with one label, the one mounted or managed under it: GET /api/v1/storage/pools lists those, and Mount imports a pool found on the disks (its dialog says the disks are not formatted). Any other btrfs filesystem that is neither the host's system filesystem nor mounted is listed by GET /api/v1/storage/filesystems/importable and under Found on the disks; POST /api/v1/storage/filesystems/{uuid}/import mounts it by UUID at /mnt/pools/<name>, checks that the mount shows the top level, sets the name as its label through the mount, has udev read its devices again and writes the managed fstab entry. Filesystems on boot or virtual devices (the SD card, the eMMC, loop and RAM disks) or on the system disk are neither offered nor listed, and Mount and Import refuse them; an import under a name that SMB shares, NFS exports or containers of an earlier pool still use is refused. A refused or failed import leaves no mountpoint, fstab line or label behind, and Mount, Import and Create undo a mount that shows another subvolume than the top level. Asserted on fakes: step 1 by test_pool_import.py (what is offered: labels, duplicates, boot, virtual and system devices) and storage.spec.ts (Pool import: the offer, the dialog, the refusals, two filesystems with one label, Mount of a found pool); step 2 by test_pool_import.py (the fstab entry by UUID, the mount from it after a reboot, the used bytes kept, no mkfs, the refusals and what an undo leaves), test_pool_persistence.py (TestMountPool) and test_smb_integration.py (an import under the name of a removed pool serves none of its shares). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214); it needs a spare disk, which the dev device does not have. On it: (1) read only, first: GET /api/v1/storage/pools and GET /api/v1/storage/filesystems/importable list nothing on mmcblk0 (the eMMC) or mmcblk1 (the SD card); nothing is ever imported or mounted there (ADR-0225). (2) A btrfs filesystem without a label (mkfs.btrfs without -L) that holds a few files, not mounted: Storage lists it under Found on the disks with its UUID and size; Import as importtest mounts it at /mnt/pools/importtest by UUID (findmnt), /etc/fstab holds the marker and the UUID entry, btrfs filesystem show and lsblk show the label importtest, and the files are there; after a reboot it is mounted again with its files. (3) An SMB share on importtest, then Remove Pool: the files stay on the disk. Clear the label while it is unmounted (btrfs filesystem label <device> ''): Import as importtest answers 409 and names the share, and nothing changes; after the share is deleted, the import succeeds. (4) Remove Pool, then label the filesystem with a pool name: it is listed as Not mounted, and Mount imports it. (5) Remove Pool, clear the label, mount it by hand, run btrfs subvolume set-default with another subvolume and unmount it: Import as importtest answers 409 with the subvolume message, findmnt shows nothing at /mnt/pools/importtest, that directory does not exist, btrfs filesystem show prints no label, and /etc/fstab is unchanged; labelled with a pool name, Mount answers 409, it stays unmounted and /etc/fstab is unchanged.

features.description: UNOS installs and runs on a Banana Pi BPI-F3 (SpacemiT K1, linux/riscv64) with Debian 13, as on amd64 and arm64 hosts
steps: install.sh on a riscv64 host with Debian 13 or Ubuntu 24.04 installs the distribution's Docker Engine, Compose v2 and buildx, without Docker's repository

The supervisor image builds on the board, and the web UI's image, which Node.js cannot build there, comes from another machine: install.sh and update.sh build only the supervisor on a K1 and start the web UI from the image deploy-webui:latest that is there
On the K1 install.sh adds the udev rule that turns off the APST and ASPM L1 of NVMe drives as they appear, and leaves the power management of SATA and USB disks and fstrim.timer as they are
On the K1 a pool on SATA disks behind an M.2-to-SATA adapter is made and mounted with TRIM as on every host, fstrim.timer trims it, and it is mounted again after a reboot
The dashboard shows the temperature of the K1's CPU (cluster0_thermal), not that of the first sensor psutil lists
scripts/dev/scenario.sh all passes on the board before and after a reboot
features.notes: Built 2026-11-13 from the stack that runs on the owner's BPI-F3 (Armbian 26.8, Debian 13, kernel 6.18.45-current-spacemit, 4 GB), published as https://github.com/und3f1ned/bpi-f3-frigate-ha. That evening ADR-0370 superseded ADR-0369: the board's NVMe drive (Patriot P300, MAXIO MAP1202) hung under load and did not come back after a warm reboot (CSTS=0x0), so the owner moved it to two SATA SSDs in an md RAID1 behind a JMB582 M.2-to-SATA adapter (JMB585 197b:0585, AHCI), where TRIM works and fstrim.timer is on, and the K1's workarounds now apply to NVMe drives only. What UNOS does with an NVMe drive on a K1 (the udev rule's effect, mkfs.btrfs --nodiscard, nodiscard and X-fstrim.notrim for a pool with one) is shown by the backend tests only: the board has no NVMe drive any more, and the one it had did not come back after a reboot. Checked off the board: on the workstation, docker buildx built both images for linux/riscv64 under QEMU from the pinned bases (the pip layer about 25 minutes: bcrypt, cryptography, psutil, cffi and uvloop compiled, cargo and rustc removed again in the same layer), and the riscv64 supervisor image imported src.main, round-tripped bcrypt and cryptography (OpenSSL 3.5) and answered GET /api/v1/health with 200 under uvicorn; the riscv64 web UI image ran npm ci and the build in the emulated builder and its Caddyfile validated; the arm64 images built as well. The udev rule passed udevadm verify of systemd 257, Debian 13's. Read on the board over ssh, without changing it: its device tree's compatible is spacemit,k1-x; its zones and hwmon groups are top_thermal, gpu_thermal, cluster0_thermal and cluster1_thermal after the NVMe drive's nvme group; Debian's docker.io 26.1.5, docker-compose 2.26.1 and docker-buildx 0.13.1; the NVMe drive's disk appeared after the controller's identify, and in one boot 63 ms before local-fs-pre.target; util-linux 2.41's fstrim knows X-fstrim.notrim. Open: every step on the board itself (it runs another stack; making it a device for UNOS is the owner's call), and the device check and the reboot check of ADR-0018. The next supervisor build on the dev device runs its pip layer again (tell the owner first, deploy/AGENTS.md). Device run on the owner's BPI-F3 on 2026-11-13 (ADR-0372): install.sh from a bundle of this branch installed the packages, kept the distribution's Docker that was there (26.1.5, Compose 2.26.1 with its warning), added the K1's udev rule, set up Samba and network discovery and built the supervisor on the board in about 35 minutes; the web UI's build crashed in Node.js twice (ADR-0373), so its image was made from static files built off the board, as ADR-0184 does, and install.sh's own functions started UNOS and its unit. The md RAID1 of the two SATA SSDs was taken apart after a checked copy to a USB disk, and UNOS's create_pool made the pool data, a btrfs RAID1, mounted with discard=async; fstrim trimmed it and fstrim.timer stays on. Docker's data root and the data of Home Assistant, Frigate, its detector and mosquitto moved to the pool (the subvolume .docker, apps/), and all of them ran again (Frigate's detector on the NPU about 24 ms). After a reboot from ssh at 16:43 MSK the pool was mounted 203 s into the boot, Docker started at 220 s, UNOS answered /api/v1/health with 200, every container ran, and 3.2 MiB had been written to the microSD card; cpu_temperature gave cluster0_thermal. At 17:37 MSK install.sh of 6007166 ran on the board to its end with the loaded web UI image: it built only the supervisor, from the build cache, and started UNOS and its unit. Step 1 is shown only in part there: Docker came from the distribution before UNOS, so install.sh kept it. Open: scripts/dev/scenario.sh all before and after a reboot, which needs the owner's administrator account of UNOS on the board and a dev.env for it (UNOS_DEV_ENV_FILE); the root key of scripts/dev/ is in place. 2026-11-19: ADR-0429 (storage.nvme-trim-on-k1) removed the NVMe no-TRIM rule (mkfs.btrfs --nodiscard, nodiscard, X-fstrim.notrim, NVME_NO_TRIM_SOCS): a pool on an NVMe drive of a K1 gets TRIM like every other pool; the udev rule of NVMe power saving stays.

features.description: UNOS installs and runs on a Banana Pi BPI-W3 (ArmSoM W3, Rockchip RK3588, linux/arm64) with Debian 13, with no code of its own for the board
steps: install.sh on a BPI-W3 with Armbian's Debian 13 or Ubuntu 24.04 image for armsom-w3 installs Docker from Docker's repository and builds both images on the board
The eMMC, its boot partitions, the microSD card and zram are neither listed on the Storage page nor accepted for a pool

A pool on a SATA disk behind an AHCI controller, or on an NVMe drive in the M.2 Key M slot, is made and mounted with the options of every host, without the K1's nodiscard and X-fstrim.notrim, and is mounted again after a reboot
The dashboard shows the temperature of the whole chip (soc_thermal), and scripts/dev/check.sh shows every thermal zone and fails within 5 C of soc-thermal's passive trip at 75 C
scripts/dev/scenario.sh all passes on the board before and after a reboot
features.notes: The dev device is this board (the owner, 2026-11-15; the UGREEN firmware on its eMMC is the owner's and has nothing to do with the board). Read on it: device tree model armsom w3, compatible rockchip,rk3588-armsom-w3 and rockchip,rk3588; Armbian 26.2.0-trunk.151 (community, BOARD=armsom-w3), Debian 13, kernel 6.1.115-vendor-rk35xx, 7927 MiB; Docker 29.1.5 from Docker's repository (upgraded on 2026-11-15, see below), set up by hand and kept up with scripts/dev/deploy.sh, which builds the web UI off the board (ADR-0184); the system on the microSD card mmcblk1; the eMMC mmcblk0 (nine partitions) beside mmcblk0boot0 and mmcblk0boot1, never written (ADR-0225); the pool data on a hard disk (sda, WDC WD6400AACS, no TRIM) behind a JMicron JMB58x AHCI controller (197b:0585) on pcie@fe170000, a PCIe 2.0 x1 link; the M.2 Key M slot (pcie@fe150000, PCIe 3.0 x4) empty; an RTL8125 on pcie@fe190000 at 2.5 Gb/s with r8169; /boot/armbianEnv.txt also loads an extra overlay of the owner's, which turns on pcie@fe160000 and pcie@fe180000, where nothing is; thermal zones soc-thermal (passive 75 and 85 C, critical 115 C) and bigcore0, bigcore1, littlecore, center, gpu and npu (critical 115 C alone); cooling devices cpufreq-cpu0, cpu4, cpu6 and the GPU's devfreq, no fan; fstrim.timer enabled. The backend tests show steps 2 to 4 on the board's facts (ADR-0376). The device check and the reboot check of ADR-0018, by hand on top of scenario.sh all: (1) scripts/dev/api.py GET /storage/disks lists no mmcblk or zram device; (2) findmnt and the fstab entry of the pool show UNOS's options without nodiscard or X-fstrim.notrim; (3) scripts/dev/check.sh shows soc-thermal with its passive trip of 75 C; (4) the dashboard's cpu_temperature of GET /system/stats equals soc-thermal's /sys/class/thermal temp. On 2026-11-15, main e80e2d5 deployed (its pip layer built again, 440.9 MiB on the card): scenario.sh all passed before and after a reboot from the API at 13:39:55 UTC (the boot of 13:40:11, both containers healthy by 13:40:40), 10 areas, 156 steps, one skipped for want of setfacl, 20.1 MiB on the card each time. The checks by hand before and after a second reboot from the API (the boot of 14:21:23 UTC, both containers healthy by 14:21:51), the same each time: (1) only sda, the pool data mounted at /mnt/pools/data (0.000 MiB before, 0.133 MiB after); (2) rw,noatime,space_cache=v2 and the fstab entry defaults,noatime,nofail,x-systemd.device-timeout=15s,x-systemd.before=docker.service (0.000 MiB); (3) soc-thermal 39 C before and 40 C after, first passive trip 75 C, check.sh OK, unos-supervisor at 0.4 and 0.2% of a core (0.016 MiB each); (4) cpu_temperature 39.769 C before, 41.615 C after, each equal to soc-thermal's temp read with it (0.000 MiB). Later on 2026-11-15 the owner had Armbian upgraded with apt on the same repository (beta.armbian.com, nightly) and kernel branch: 26.11.0-trunk.133, kernel 6.1.172-vendor-rk35xx, Docker 29.9.3, Samba 4.22.11 (apt update 166.5 MiB and the upgrade 3155.2 MiB on the card); the owner's overlay copied into the new kernel's dtb directory; after a reboot from the API (the boot of 16:03:11 UTC) check.sh passed, and after hdparm, nvme-cli and acl were installed (63.1 MiB), scenario.sh all passed, 157 steps without a skip (20.0 MiB). scenario.sh all makes no pool and reads no temperature: steps 3 and 4 rest on the by-hand checks and the backend tests. Open: step 1, install.sh on a fresh microSD card of the board (a second card, an owner action); a pool made on the board, which needs a spare disk; an NVMe pool in the M.2 Key M slot (a drive, an owner action); the pool's TRIM on an SSD.

features.description: The App Store shows which apps have an image for the host's platform and refuses the others before any pull
steps: Every catalog template lists the platforms its image publishes, and a test fails for a template without them
On a host whose platform an app's image lacks, Apps marks the app as not available for that platform and disables Install
POST /api/v1/apps/install answers 409 for such an app without pulling an image
The weekly audit workflow compares the recorded platforms with the registries and fails when they differ
features.notes: Found with deploy.riscv64-bpi-f3: on riscv64, 6 of the 70 catalog images publish a linux/riscv64 build (docs/research/riscv64-support-2026-11-07.md, area 6), and the install of any other fails at the pull with Docker's error as a 500. Built (ADR-0403): supervisor/src/apps/image_platforms.json records the Linux platforms of all 71 image references of the catalog (its 67 templates, the companions' and the RKNN machine-learning image; the research counted 70 templates before three left the catalog), read from the registries' manifest lists of the pinned tag or digest with scripts/catalog-platforms.py (`record`; `check` or `make catalog-platforms` is the audit, also the `platforms` job of the weekly audit.yml). The recorded riscv64 images are exactly the 6 of the research: navidrome, prometheus, zigbee2mqtt, pihole, traefik and gitea. Readarr's tag has an empty index (no platform at all), recorded as none: it is not available on any host, as its pull never worked. The catalog API adds host_platform and available; POST /api/v1/apps/install answers 409 before the request's other checks, any Docker read and the job. Checked only by tests and the stand-in (ADR-0215): the backend tests for linux/arm64, linux/amd64 and linux/riscv64 hosts (the catalog marks exactly the recorded riscv64 apps, the install of any other app answers 409 with no Docker call, also when one companion lacks the platform), and an E2E spec that answers the catalog as a riscv64 host (Install disabled with the reason in English and Russian, the six apps stay installable); no riscv64 host was used. The script ran against the live registries (anonymous curl, no pull) and `check` passed on 2026-11-18. Floating tags: the record is the tag's of that day. DEVICE CHECK on the arm64 dev device (the owner's /deploy-device; host-level, ADR-0018), nothing is changed there: 1) after the deploy, `scripts/dev/api.py GET /api/v1/apps/catalog` (read-only): every template has host_platform linux/arm64, and the apps with available false are exactly those whose `platforms` lack linux/arm64 (today only Readarr, whose image publishes none); count them and compare with `python3 -c` over supervisor/src/apps/image_platforms.json (an app is available when all its images list linux/arm64). 2) The App Store (Catalog tab) shows 'Not available for linux/arm64' on the same apps only. 3) POST /api/v1/apps/install for `readarr` (the one app not available for linux/arm64; if the catalog has no other by then, this is it; with an `{"template_id":"readarr"}` body, scripts/dev/api.py POST) answers 409 'Readarr is not available for linux/arm64: ...' within a second, while `docker images` on the device and `docker events --since <start>` show no pull, no container and no network, and /api/v1/apps/install/jobs stays empty. 4) A reboot check changes nothing (the record is in the image). SD MiB of each step: 0 expected (reads only; no new log lines). BPI-F3 (riscv64, deploy.riscv64-bpi-f3) is the owner's to check, with the same read-only steps: GET /api/v1/apps/catalog says host_platform linux/riscv64 and available true for exactly navidrome, prometheus, zigbee2mqtt, pihole, traefik and gitea (6 of 67 apps), the App Store shows 'Not available for linux/riscv64' on the other 61, and one refused install (for example plex) answers 409 with no pull in `docker images` and the Docker events. Device check of f281749 on 2026-11-18 (SD MiB 0.020): host_platform linux/arm64, readarr alone unavailable (its develop tag publishes an empty index) and 66 of 67 apps available; POST /apps/install for readarr 409 in 0.02 s with 11 images before and after, no pull, create or network event and no install job; the same answer after a reboot from the API (0.000). The BPI-F3 steps above stay the owner's.

features.description: Apps use the SpacemiT K1's hardware: Frigate decodes camera streams on the VPU and detects objects on the NPU
steps: Install Frigate on a BPI-F3: it decodes an H.264 camera stream on the VPU
Its object detection runs on the K1's NPU
features.notes: Like apps.rk3588-hardware-acceleration for the RK3588. Waits for riscv64 images of Frigate and of a detector: neither Frigate nor Home Assistant publishes one, and UNOS takes app images from their publishers. What such apps need, from the stack that runs Home Assistant and Frigate on the owner's BPI-F3 with Armbian's current-spacemit kernel 6.18, published as https://github.com/und3f1ned/bpi-f3-frigate-ha (November 2026): the VPU's firmware (Bianbu's package k1x-vpu-firmware 0.1.0) and its driver amvx, which does not load by itself (modules-load.d), with /dev/video0; for the decoders of Bianbu's ffmpeg (h264_stcodec, hevc_stcodec) the CMA heap /dev/dma_heap/linux,cma; for the NPU /dev/tcm and /dev/udma (spacemit-tcm); udev rules that give those devices to the group video; onnxruntime 1.24.2+spacemit with spacemit-ort 2.0.6 from SpacemiT's package index, imported before spacemit_ort, on cores 0 to 3, where YOLOv8n INT8 took about 10 ms; Frigate's zmq detector reaches it. stcodec hangs at the end of a stream (files loop through go2rtc), its -scale option corrupts frames, and the MPP library prints to stdout, which corrupts the raw frames ffmpeg writes there unless it is sent to stderr. The kernel's packages are held: the mainline kernel has neither the VPU nor the TCM driver.

features.description: install.sh installs no package that UNOS does not use, mdadm first, so that the disks of an old NAS are not assembled into md arrays
steps: install.sh installs no mdadm, which no code of UNOS runs, or docs/INSTALL.md says what it is for
On a host whose disks carry the md superblocks of an old NAS, the installation adds no ARRAY line to /etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf and no array to the initramfs, and Storage lists those disks
features.notes: Found with deploy.riscv64-bpi-f3 (ADR-0370) on 2026-11-13: install_dependencies of install.sh installs mdadm, which nothing in supervisor/src runs. On the owner's BPI-F3, installing Debian's mdadm wrote ARRAY lines for the arrays of old NAS disks into /etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf, which the initramfs carries; the stack there now removes them and rebuilds the initramfs. Not checked for UNOS: what Storage shows for such disks once their arrays are assembled. Built 2026-11-18 (ADR-0413): install.sh and docs/INSTALL.md drop mdadm, parted, nvme-cli, lm-sensors, net-tools and wget, none of which supervisor/src, deploy/ or the docs run (checked against HOST_TOOLS, OPTIONAL_HOST_TOOLS, the host commands of the routers and the scripts); smartmontools stays because uninstall.sh runs the host smartctl. update.sh removes nothing: a host with mdadm keeps it. Step 2 answered from the code: a disk or partition that lsblk shows with a child of type raid* is in use (reason: Used by md127 (raid1)); the Storage page shows that reason and offers it for no pool, and create_pool refuses it with force too; an unassembled linux_raid_member is free but holds data and needs force. Tests: test_deploy_scripts.py (the package list, the HOST_TOOLS packages installed, update.sh removes none) and test_disk_safety.py (the partition case, the refusal with force, the unassembled member). Device check, read-only (the dev device already has its packages and install.sh is not run on it): with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure, scripts/dev/ssh.sh runs cat /proc/mdstat and lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,FSTYPE, and scripts/dev/api.py GET /api/v1/storage/disks lists the disks: no raid* row below a data disk unless the owner made one, and each disk's in_use and in_use_reason agree with lsblk. Review (fresh context): no BLOCKING; RISK left: ADR-0002 still says install.sh installs lm-sensors (an accepted ADR is not rewritten; ADR-0413 names the change), and docs/research/riscv64-support-2026-11-07.md lists the old packages as a dated record; the vacuous update.sh test was widened to uninstall.sh. Not checked on hardware: a fresh install.sh run on a host with old md disks; the stub apt-get test shows the package is not installed, and without it nothing writes ARRAY lines. Device check of e5d531a on 2026-11-18, read-only, before and after a reboot (0.000 and 0.145 SD MiB): /proc/mdstat holds no array, lsblk no raid* row, and GET /storage/disks shows /dev/sda in use (mounted at the pool) as lsblk does. A fresh install.sh on a host whose disks carry an old NAS's md superblocks (the owner's BPI-F3) is open.

features.description: A release publishes linux/riscv64 images of the supervisor and the web UI next to amd64 and arm64
steps: The release workflow of deploy.release-images also builds linux/riscv64, under QEMU with a pinned binfmt image or on a native riscv64 runner
The riscv64 wheels of the supervisor's compiled packages are built once per change of requirements.txt and reused from a cache
A SpacemiT K1 pulls both images of a tag, and install.sh and update.sh build nothing there
features.notes: Proposed by docs/research/riscv64-support-2026-11-07.md. Found again with deploy.riscv64-bpi-f3: Node.js crashes on the K1 in the web UI's build, so a K1 cannot install or update UNOS alone (ADR-0373), and update.sh compiles the supervisor's Rust and C packages on the board for about 35 minutes each time.

features.description: UNOS keeps its idle load within a budget on a slow board, also with a dashboard open, and the device check reports load and heat
steps: Every socket of /ws/v1/events gets the same stats sample, taken at most once per interval in a worker thread, and the process list in it at most every 10 seconds, reading the ten processes it shows in full only
The supervisor's healthcheck asks for the health with bash, not with a Python
The check for leftovers of uploads leaves out Docker's data root on a pool

scripts/dev/check.sh shows each container's CPU and the temperatures, and fails for a container of UNOS above 15% of a core or a thermal zone that slows a processor within 5 C of its first passive trip
On the BPI-F3, with a dashboard open in two tabs, unos-supervisor stays below 15% of a core on average
features.notes: Found on the owner's BPI-F3 on 2026-11-13 (deploy.riscv64-bpi-f3): an open dashboard cost the supervisor 25 to 64% of a core, one sample 0.4 s of the K1's CPU, and the walk for upload leftovers went through Docker's data root on the pool. After ADR-0375 (07f9c47) on the board: unos-supervisor 3.5% of a core with no dashboard open, 5.6% with two simulated tabs (threads calling shared_system_stats every 2 s); with two real tabs not yet measured (needs the owner's sign-in). Builder pass 2026-11-18 (ADR-0412): steps 1 to 4 are met by the code of ADR-0374 and ADR-0375 and asserted: step 1 by test_ws_stats.py (one sample per interval, the process list every 10 s, ten processes in full) and TestSharedStatsSample of test_ws_auth.py (two sockets, one sample, taken off the event loop); step 2 by test_supervisor_is_healthy_only_while_the_api_answers of test_deploy_scripts.py; step 3 by test_upload_leftovers.py; step 4 by the check_sh tests of test_dev_scripts.py (CPU of each container averaged over five readings, the 15% and 5 C boundaries, a UNOS container without a reading, unreadable zones, K1 and RK3588 zones, and a reading that writes nothing). Step 5 is the owner's, on the BPI-F3 (passes stays false until then): open the dashboard signed in as an administrator in two browser tabs for 10 minutes, then run scripts/dev/check.sh (its CPU line for unos-supervisor is an average of five readings over about ten seconds; take it three times, a minute apart) and read `docker stats --no-stream` for unos-supervisor in the same minutes; the average must stay below 15% of a core, and the check must say check: OK. Record the figures in PROGRESS.md. Device check of e5d531a on 2026-11-18 (BPI-W3): check.sh OK with its CPU lines (unos-supervisor 0.3 to 0.4% of a core, unos-webui 0.0, Immich's machine learning 12.6 before and 0.2 after a reboot) and thermal lines (soc 40 to 42 C, first passive trip 75 C), each run 0.016 to 0.066 SD MiB. Step 5, two real dashboard tabs on the BPI-F3, is the owner's. 2026-11-19: on the owner's BPI-F3 check.sh warned of top_thermal and gpu_thermal near their first passive trip of 40 C, which drives the fan (top_thermal) or is bound to nothing (gpu_thermal): the kernel slows no processor there. ADR-0421 supersedes ADR-0374 and counts only the zones that bind a processor's clock (step 4 reworded by it); the BPI-W3's soc-thermal counts as before.

features.description: The catalog's LinuxServer images are pinned and pulled as ghcr.io/linuxserver/<name>, with the digests of their lscr.io pins
steps: Every LinuxServer image of the catalog is pinned and pulled as ghcr.io/linuxserver/<name>:<tag>@<digest>, with the index digest that ghcr.io names for its tag, and no image of the catalog names lscr.io
An installed app created from lscr.io is still its template's app: one created from a tag is offered the ghcr.io pin as its update, and its rollback returns it to the image it ran
On the dev device BookStack installs with its MariaDB on the pool and serves its page, and transmission updates to the ghcr.io pin and rolls back, with pulls that complete
features.notes: Found with apps.catalog-companions and apps.update-in-place (PROGRESS.md's open owner action 19): on the dev device's network every Docker pull from lscr.io failed (four times since 2026-11-18, a blob's download ending with 'timeout awaiting response headers' after 55 to 590 MiB of partial layers), while on 2026-11-19 docker pull ghcr.io/linuxserver/transmission@sha256:5baf08cd73a566699f35baad3c4a84ba7d7057220566c5fb29969bf2292dc2ff, the image of the catalog's transmission pin, completed in 10 s. lscr.io is LinuxServer's redirector to ghcr.io, which serves the same indexes. Built 2026-11-19 on the workstation (ADR-0426); host-level, as Docker's containers and the images it pulls on the host change, so it passes only after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Step 1: the 22 LinuxServer pins of supervisor/src/apps/catalog.py (BookStack's and 21 of APP_IMAGES) are ghcr.io/linuxserver/<name>:<tag>@<digest> with the tags, digests, estimates and VOLUMEs they had: on 2026-11-19 GHCR's anonymous token and a HEAD of each tag's manifest, with curl from the workstation, named the pinned index digest for all 22, so none changed. The install pulls ghcr.io/linuxserver/<name> by digest, creates the container from <name>@<digest> and tags <name>:<tag>; the space check finds a pin by that name and digest (an image that Docker has only under an lscr.io name counts its estimate again, which errs high); image_platforms.json's 22 keys are renamed (make catalog-platforms passed on 2026-11-19, 76 images); the update's registry reads, the tags audit and the OpenAPI examples name ghcr.io; the lscr.io aliases of supervisor/src/apps/registry.py and scripts/catalog-platforms.py are removed (ADR-0207). make catalog-tags on 2026-11-19 reported none of the 22, but two other pins whose tags moved: traefik:v3.7 and Linkwarden's postgres:16.16-alpine (a re-pin for the lead, outside this entry). Step 2: an app is its containers' unos.app label, so a container created from lscr.io is listed, started, stopped and uninstalled as before; one created from a tag (the dev device's transmission, from lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:latest, without a version label) is offered 4.1.4-r0-ls370, its update creates it from the GHCR pin and keeps transmission.previous on its image, and the rollback gives that container its name back: the image it ran, by Docker's id, under its lscr.io name, with no pull; one created from an lscr.io pin's name@digest runs the same image and is offered nothing (ADR-0408 compares digests). Custom containers and the Images tab take any registry, lscr.io too (the user guide names GHCR as the same image). Tested on the workstation: test_linuxserver_ghcr.py (no image of the catalog on lscr.io, the 22 tags and digests on ghcr.io, the platforms under the GHCR names, transmission's install pulled and created by GHCR's digest, an image pulled by its digest alone taking no room and no pull and one Docker lacks counting its estimate; the dev device's transmission against GHCR's recorded answers of 2026-11-19, fixtures/ghcr_transmission.json, behind its token handshake and CDN: listed with its template and offered the pin, its plan read from ghcr.io alone with 0 bytes to pull when Docker has the image, its update to the pin and its rollback to the lscr.io image with the same binds and variables and no pull, without the image a pull from ghcr.io by digest, and one created from the lscr.io pin's name@digest offered nothing and its update refused with 409, with no registry read), test_catalog_platforms.py, test_catalog_platforms_script.py, test_openapi.py. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): fixed the device check's piped body, which sd.sh's own ssh would read first, the trailing - of the POSTs without a body, the docker reads outside scripts/dev/ssh.sh, the two sizes of 134.5 MiB and 33.5 MiB, and the docs' claim of 'some networks'; added the tests of an app created from the lscr.io pin's digest and of the removed aliases, and the ADR's reason why ADR-0410 and ADR-0415 are not superseded. Left: LINUXSERVER_PINS is the record of what ghcr.io named on 2026-11-19, which the gate cannot read (make catalog-tags reads it again); the space check counts an image that Docker holds only under an lscr.io name again (it errs high, ADR-0426); the listing and rollback tests also pass on the earlier code, as guards. The notes of apps.pinned-catalog-images, apps.update-in-place and apps.catalog-companions name the lscr.io references of their day; their digests are unchanged. Before the device check, on the workstation (network, anonymous HEAD and GET, no pull): make catalog-tags reports none of the 22 LinuxServer pins, and make catalog-platforms passes. DEVICE CHECK on the dev device after the deploy of this branch (/deploy-device), through UNOS's API, which pulls; no docker pull, run or prune by hand; each command under scripts/dev/sd.sh measure <label> -- <command> with its SD MiB; Immich is never updated, rolled back or pulled. (1) scripts/dev/check.sh OK; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker images --digests --format "{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.Digest}} {{.ID}}"; docker ps -a --format "{{.Names}} {{.Image}} {{.Status}}"; docker network ls --format "{{.Name}}"; df -B1M / /var/lib/docker; ss -Hltn sport = :6875' recorded: transmission Up on lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:latest, ghcr.io/linuxserver/transmission with sha256:5baf08cd73a566699f35baad3c4a84ba7d7057220566c5fb29969bf2292dc2ff (the diagnosis' pull; without it (5) pulls it: download_bytes about 33.5 MiB, system_disk_bytes about 134.5 MiB), no bookstack container, port 6875 free, and the system disk with at least 2 GiB plus 773 MiB free. (2) scripts/dev/api.py GET /apps/catalog: no image of any template, companion or hardware profile starts with lscr.io; bookstack's image ghcr.io/linuxserver/bookstack:v26.09.3-ls299@sha256:c741211356966fd38f8fea10483f341ca29c41cdd1b96b5cfcdd4312f26d7f97 and transmission's ghcr.io/linuxserver/transmission:4.1.4-r0-ls370@sha256:5baf08cd73a566699f35baad3c4a84ba7d7057220566c5fb29969bf2292dc2ff, both available on linux/arm64. (3) BookStack's install: scripts/dev/sd.sh measure bookstack-install -- sh -c 'echo "{\"template_id\": \"bookstack\", \"pool\": \"data\", \"env_overrides\": {\"APP_URL\": \"http://<LAN address>:6875\"}}" | scripts/dev/api.py POST /apps/install -' (the pipe inside the measured command: sd.sh's own ssh would read it first) answers 202 with its job; record the POST's time (date -u); scripts/dev/sd.sh measure bookstack-wait -- scripts/dev/api.py --timeout 3660 GET /apps/install/jobs/<id> --param wait=3600 ends succeeded with bookstack and its companion database running; report the two SD MiB beside the catalog's system_disk_bytes (810000000, 773 MiB). Then: GET /apps/installed lists bookstack once, pool data, its database running; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker inspect -f "{{.Name}} {{.Config.Image}} {{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}" bookstack bookstack-database' shows ghcr.io/linuxserver/bookstack@sha256:c741211356966fd38f8fea10483f341ca29c41cdd1b96b5cfcdd4312f26d7f97 and mariadb@sha256:d36f18d65a0459510b8b0f643b226a6d299e3206486e2b64ff20754a6d291707, every source under /mnt/pools/data/apps/bookstack/; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker events --since <the POST> --until <now> --filter type=image' shows the pull of ghcr.io/linuxserver/bookstack and none of lscr.io; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -L http://127.0.0.1:6875/login' prints 200 (BookStack's page from its database; nobody signs in, and (4) follows at once, since its built-in admin@admin.com account has the password 'password' while it runs). (4) scripts/dev/sd.sh measure bookstack-uninstall -- scripts/dev/api.py DELETE /apps/installed/bookstack answers 200 with its data kept (on purpose: an uninstall keeps an app's data, ADR-0256; the folders hold BookStack's database with its built-in account and its generated passwords, on the pool, not the SD card, and a reinstall uses them; their removal is the owner's choice); GET /containers/images, then for each image that (1) did not list (ghcr.io/linuxserver/bookstack:v26.09.3-ls299, and mariadb:11.8.9 unless (1) had it) scripts/dev/sd.sh measure bookstack-image -- scripts/dev/api.py DELETE /containers/images/<its id> answers removed; (1)'s ssh reads show no bookstack container, no network unos-app-bookstack and the images of (1), and scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'ls -A /mnt/pools/data/apps/bookstack /mnt/pools/data/apps/bookstack/database' lists its config, app-key and database (data, password, root-password), kept. (5) Transmission's update: GET /apps/installed lists transmission with version null, update_to 4.1.4-r0-ls370 and previous null; GET /apps/installed/transmission/update answers 200 with image_from lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:latest, image_to ghcr.io/linuxserver/transmission:4.1.4-r0-ls370@sha256:5baf08cd73a566699f35baad3c4a84ba7d7057220566c5fb29969bf2292dc2ff, changed true, and download_bytes 0 and system_disk_bytes 0 with (1)'s image (else about 33.5 and 134.5 MiB); scripts/dev/sd.sh measure transmission-update -- scripts/dev/api.py POST /apps/installed/transmission/update (no body) answers 202 (record its time) and scripts/dev/sd.sh measure transmission-update-wait -- scripts/dev/api.py --timeout 3660 GET /apps/install/jobs/<id> --param wait=3600 ends succeeded; report both SD MiB beside system_disk_bytes. Then docker ps -a shows transmission Up on ghcr.io/linuxserver/transmission@sha256:5baf08cd73a566699f35baad3c4a84ba7d7057220566c5fb29969bf2292dc2ff and transmission.previous Exited on lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:latest; scripts/dev/ssh.sh "docker inspect -f '{{json .Mounts}} {{json .HostConfig.PortBindings}}' transmission transmission.previous" shows the same binds (/config, /downloads, /watch under the pool) and ports (9091, 51413); scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:9091/transmission/web/' prints 401 (its login is kept); GET /apps/installed: version 4.1.4-r0-ls370, update_to null, previous with transmission.previous; GET /audit/logs --param limit=5 has app_updated; scripts/dev/ssh.sh 'docker events --since <the POST> --until <now> --filter type=image' shows no pull of lscr.io (and none at all with (1)'s image). (6) The rollback: scripts/dev/sd.sh measure transmission-rollback -- scripts/dev/api.py POST /apps/installed/transmission/rollback (no body) answers 202 (record its time) and its waiting GET (as in (5)) ends succeeded: docker ps -a shows transmission Up on lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:latest and no transmission.previous, curl of 9091 prints 401, GET /apps/installed lists version null, update_to 4.1.4-r0-ls370 and previous null, the audit log has app_rolled_back, and the docker events of (5) since the rollback's POST show no pull. The GHCR image stays, for the next update. (7) After a reboot from the API (scripts/dev/api.py POST /power/reboot, which reboots a minute later): check.sh OK, (2) answers as before, GET /apps/installed lists transmission running lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:latest with update_to 4.1.4-r0-ls370 and previous null and no bookstack, and (4)'s ls lists BookStack's folders. Expected SD writes: about the images' size for (3) (BookStack's two pulls and its first start), small for (4), (5) and (6) with (1)'s image (container changes and audit entries), about 0 for (1), (2) and (7)'s reads. Device check 2026-11-19 of fc42813 (mvp.batch-17's backend, deployed 17:3x UTC: sync 9.027, build-supervisor 18.461, up 3.293 SD MiB; check.sh OK), before and after the reboot from the API at 18:10:24 UTC: make catalog-tags reported none of the 22 LinuxServer pins moved (traefik:v3.7 and Linkwarden's postgres:16.16-alpine did: their re-pin is open), make catalog-platforms passed for 76 images; GET /apps/catalog named no lscr.io image and 22 ghcr.io/linuxserver ones. Its login page was not read (the check's own script failed before it). transmission, created from lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:latest: offered the ghcr.io pin with download_bytes 0 (the image was there from the diagnosis), updated (5.203), rolled back to its own container on lscr.io:latest with no .previous (3.258), updated again (5.094): binds, ports and its login kept, 9091 answering 401, app_updated and app_rolled_back audited. After the reboot transmission ran the pin, offered nothing, and BookStack's folders were still on the pool. Docker 29's containerd store logged no pull events, so the registry is shown by the job and the images' names.

features.description: A pool on an NVMe drive of a SpacemiT K1 gets TRIM like every other pool
steps: On a SpacemiT K1 a pool with an NVMe drive is made without --nodiscard, mounted with noatime alone (btrfs's default discard=async) and kept in fstab without nodiscard or X-fstrim.notrim, so that fstrim.timer trims it, as on every host and without a read of the board's device tree, also when it is imported or mounted again after a busy unmount

On a SpacemiT K1 Add Disk adds an NVMe drive to a pool, and any disk to a pool on an NVMe drive, without --nodiscard and without a read of the board's device tree, and refuses no disk for being an NVMe drive

On a BPI-F3 with a pool on an NVMe drive, the pool's fstab entry has neither nodiscard nor X-fstrim.notrim, its mount shows discard=async, fstrim trims it without an NVMe timeout, reset or error in the kernel's log, and after a warm reboot it is mounted again from that entry
features.notes: Built 2026-11-19 (ADR-0429, which supersedes the TRIM rule of ADR-0370 and the refusal and --nodiscard of ADR-0411 that followed from it; host-level, so the device check and the reboot check of ADR-0018 apply). supervisor/src/storage/pools.py loses NVME_NO_TRIM_SOCS, DEVICE_TREE_COMPATIBLE, NO_TRIM_MOUNT_OPTIONS, NO_TRIM_FSTAB_OPTIONS, pool_is_trimmed, _remount_is_trimmed and the trimmed and devices parameters; supervisor/src/storage/devices.py loses the 409 for an NVMe drive into a pool with TRIM and --nodiscard; no compatibility kept (ADR-0207). The udev rule 60-unos-k1-nvme.rules of deploy/install.sh (APST and ASPM L1 off) stays. Tests: test_disk_safety.py (Create on a K1 under the vendor's and the mainline kernel, NVMe, SATA and both, and on a BPI-W3's own layout, SATA and NVMe: mkfs.btrfs without --nodiscard, mount -o noatime, the plain fstab entry, no read of /proc/device-tree/compatible), test_pool_persistence.py (Mount of an NVMe and a SATA pool on a K1 and of NVMe pools on the RK3588, the mount again after a busy unmount), test_pool_import.py (an NVMe filesystem imported on a K1) and test_pool_disks.py (an NVMe drive into a SATA pool and a SATA disk into an NVMe pool on a K1); docs/INSTALL.md no longer advises against NVMe on the K1: it lists NVMe drives among the K1's disks for pools, keeps the udev rule and the kernel parameters that the board does not boot with, and says to replace a drive that still hangs in the slot; USER_GUIDE.md drops Add Disk's NVMe refusal. Device evidence, before this change, on the owner's BPI-F3 (SpacemiT K1, Armbian kernel 6.18.45-current-spacemit) on 2026-11-19, whose pool data is now one Kingston A1000 (SA1000M8240G, Phison controller) on PCIe Gen2 x2: fstrim of 256 MiB and then of all free space (210.8 GiB in 8 s, 6.3 GiB in 5 s), a 4 GiB write with a parallel fstrim and its read-back, then the pool mounted with discard=async and a warm reboot: no NVMe timeout, reset, abort or error in the kernel's log, the drive back after the reboot, the pool mounted by its fstab entry. The drive that hung under ADR-0370 was a Patriot P300 (MAXIO MAP1202), which also hung under load and never came back after a warm reboot. Open: the device check on the dev device is not possible (a BPI-W3 without an NVMe drive, not a K1), and the BPI-F3 runs an older UNOS, so step 3 waits for this tree there; mkfs.btrfs and btrfs device add on a K1's NVMe drive are the backend tests' only (the F3's one NVMe drive holds its pool). Device check on the BPI-F3 after this tree is deployed there (the owner's board, by hand with the device-checks skill): (1) Mount of the pool through the API (POST /api/v1/storage/pools/data/mount, which rewrites an older managed entry), then grep -A1 'unos-pool:data' /etc/fstab shows defaults,noatime,nofail,x-systemd.device-timeout=15s,x-systemd.before=docker.service and neither nodiscard nor X-fstrim.notrim; (2) findmnt -no OPTIONS /mnt/pools/data shows discard=async and no nodiscard (a mount with nodiscard from before keeps it until the reboot of step 5); (3) sudo fstrim --listed-in /etc/fstab --dry-run --verbose names /mnt/pools/data, and systemctl is-enabled fstrim.timer answers enabled; (4) sudo fstrim -v /mnt/pools/data trims, and journalctl -k -b | grep -iE 'nvme.*(timeout|reset|abort|error)' prints nothing; (5) a warm reboot, then findmnt -no OPTIONS /mnt/pools/data shows discard=async, the pool is listed mounted by GET /api/v1/storage/pools, and step 4's grep prints nothing for the new boot. Review (fresh context, 2026-11-19): BLOCKING, the supersession texts named only ADR-0370's TRIM rule while docs/INSTALL.md also dropped its advice against NVMe: both ADRs now name that advice. RISKs fixed: the evidence wording (the P300 worked in a USB enclosure, so the docs say to replace a drive that hangs in the slot, not that it was faulty), ADR-0429's fstab consequence (an older entry with nodiscard,X-fstrim.notrim stays across reboots until a Mount through UNOS rewrites it; the device check's step 1 does), the BPI-W3 test back on the board's own layout, "for being an NVMe drive" instead of "for its kind", ADR-0429 in the adr lists of the two entries whose notes cite it. RISKs left, with the reason: ADR-0370 was proposed and is now superseded only in part, as the brief asked (its supersession line says its other rules stay proposed until deploy.riscv64-bpi-f3 passes) instead of a new ADR that restates them all; no per-pool way to keep TRIM off a drive that hangs on it (ADR-0429, Considered options: the drive is replaced); the owner's BPI-F3 now keeps its pool data on the A1000, so docs/INSTALL.md's Home Assistant section (ADR-0372: a RAID1 on two SATA SSDs), deploy.riscv64-bpi-f3's SATA-pool step and its feature-pass row describe a setup the board no longer has, which is ADR-0372's and deploy.riscv64-bpi-f3's to update, not this entry's. NIT left: deploy.arm64-bpi-w3 step 3 still says "without the K1's nodiscard and X-fstrim.notrim", still true, and a step changes only with an ADR that names its entry.

features.description: The web UI's shared components carry its loads, confirmations, toasts, menus, form controls and tables, and the design check keeps pages on them
steps: A destructive action asks in a confirmation of the page, never the browser's dialog: the question as its title, what happens, Cancel and the action named by its verb and object; Escape answers no and gives the focus back, and a pending question is answered no when the page changes; the outcome of a backup's deletion and of the Scheduler's actions comes as a toast in a live region, in English and Russian
A load that fails says so in place of its list, with the server's reason (a technical one folded under Technical details with Copy) and Retry, never as an empty list

A row's actions stay on one line, at most edit and delete as icons and the rest in a ⋯ menu that the arrow keys, Home, End and Escape work; at 375 px System > Backup & Restore's list is cards with each fact labelled, and no page scrolls sideways

A disabled button says why on hover and focus and as its description; a number field shows its unit and bounds and has steppers, related fields line up in a group, an on/off setting is a switch, and a dialog's header and buttons stay in view
The Scheduler shows every time on the NAS's clock and names the zone once; badges are in sentence case

The design check fails for window.confirm, alert, prompt, the class uppercase, a raw checkbox or radio and a filled primary button in a card's header or a table's row, and (ADR-0438) for a success Alert, a hand-made spinner and a raw details element outside the shared components, each unless a design-ignore comment gives its reason
features.notes: Built 2026-11-20 on mvp.batch-18 (69dfae5), chunk 1 of the UX work after the owner's "the design is slapdash, the UX limps". Not host-level: only the web UI's image rebuilds on the dev device; no new dependency. Decisions in ADR-0432, which supersedes ADR-0266 and ADR-0401 in part (the Scheduler's times on the NAS's clock). Chunks 2 to 5 adopt the components on their pages and empty scripts/design-baseline.json (41 uses in 26 files when the rules came); once they had, ADR-0438 removed the baseline and added the rules on success alerts, spinners and raw details elements.
